title: César Vallejo: Heraldo del dolor humano
body:
Publicado en Español, Inglés y Portugués.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRVzLediv8d5bB9RJtjpkGfQfbXcfGs9MosGULjbhVMVw/1776737026722.jpg) *Editado en PhotoCollage*


Buenas noches, buena lectura y dulces sueños.

Hoy me reto a mi misma por atreverme a hanlar de uno de los poetas mas relevantes de Latinoamerica. Nuestro enorme Cesar Vallejo. De él, un libro y el poema que le da nombre. Un poema que definitivamnete amo.

Los heraldos negros, libro del autor y tambien título del poema que le da el nombre al libro es lectura obligatoria de los amantes de la poesía o de los que la escribe.

Este libro supone una ruptura sutil pero decisiva con el Modernismo imperante en ese momento, anunciando ya la voz inconfundible que culminaría en obras posteriores como Trilce o Poemas humanos .

Los heraldos negros no es un libro desesperanzado. Frente a ese dolor universal, Vallejo despliega una profunda solidaridad piadosa con el hombre sufriente. El poeta se siente fraternalmente unido a todas las víctimas de este \
y experimenta incluso un sentimiento de culpa por ocupar un lugar que podría corresponder a otro . En poemas como \

, esta culpa se transforma en un impulso de entrega y de compartir, anticipando entonces la dimensión política y colectiva tambien, que alcanzaría su poesía posterior en España, aparta de mí este cáliz .

Nos encontramos ante una obra fundacional donde ya están presentes las grandes obsesiones vallejianas asi como: la muerte, el desasosiego, la búsqueda de Dios, la memoria de la infancia y la compasión por el hombre pobre y golpeado por un destino que no comprende . Un libro que, desde su título mismo, convierte al poeta en mensajero, heraldo del dolor humano, pero también de la fraternidad que ese dolor despierta.


Aca les dejo el poema y un pequeño análisis, creo que asi le podemos decir.

---
---


>**Los heraldos negros**

>Hay golpes en la vida, tan fuertes... Yo no sé!Golpes como del odio de Dios; como si ante ellos,la resaca de todo lo sufridose empozara en el alma... Yo no sé!

>Son pocos, pero son... Abren zanjas oscurasen el rostro más fiero y en el lomo más fuerte.Serán tal vez los potros de bárbaros atilas;o los heraldos negros que nos manda la Muerte.

>Son las caídas hondas de los Cristos del alma,de alguna fe adorable que el Destino blasfema.Esos golpes sangrientos son las crepitacionesde algún pan que en la puerta del horno se nos quema.

>Y el hombre... Pobre...pobre! Vuelve los ojos, comocuando por sobre el hombro nos llama una palmada;vuelve los ojos locos, y todo lo vividose empoza, como charco de culpa, en la mirada.

>Hay golpes en la vida, tan fuertes... Yo no sé!

---
---

Este poema inaugural de César Vallejo funciona como una declaración poética y existencial. El título mismo presenta una metáfora centra pues los heraldos negros son mensajeros funestos que la Muerte envía para golpear al vivo, anunciándole su destino de sufrimiento.

El poema explora la naturaleza de esos golpes. Vallejo los describe con imágenes violentas y contrastantes asi como: abren zanjas en el rostro más fiero, golpean el lomo más fuerte. Los compara con \
poniéndolos como una fuerza destructiva externa y con \
el mismísimo designio inexorable. Pero luego introduce una imagen sorprendente: \

. Aquí el dolor no viene de fuera, sino que es una crucifixión íntima, una traición de la propia fe por parte del Destino.

La metáfora del pan que se quema en la puerta del horno es particularmente reveladora. El pan representa la vida, es el alimento cotidiano, lo que debería nutrir; pero el sufrimiento lo quema justo antes de estar listo, en el umbral mismo de su realización.

Vallejo retrata la reacción del hombre y dice: vuelve los ojos como si alguien le tocara el hombro, un gesto de sorpresa, de espera de consuelo, pero lo que encuentra es el charco de culpa en su mirada. No hay consuelo, solo la memoria de todo lo sufrido empozada. El poema propone así una visión trágica mostrando el dolor inevitable, incomprensible, y deja al hombre solo con su culpa sin causa.

---
---

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUCA7PAJsTmKRaYQj9RPiuJkiUiZVpZnudAqyGen3GQpZ/1758337351123.jpg)


---
---

# *ENGLISH*

---
---

Good evening, happy reading, and sweet dreams.

Today I challenge myself by daring to speak about one of the most relevant poets in Latin America. Our great César Vallejo. About him, a book and the poem that gives it its title. A poem that I definitely love.

Los heraldos negros (The Black Heralds), a book by the author and also the title of the poem that names the book, is required reading for lovers of poetry or for those who write it.

This book represents a subtle but decisive break with the prevailing Modernism of its time, already announcing the unmistakable voice that would culminate in later works such as Trilce or Poemas humanos (Human Poems).

The Black Heralds is not a hopeless book. Faced with that universal pain, Vallejo displays a profound, compassionate solidarity with the suffering man. The poet feels fraternally united with all the victims of this \
and even experiences a feeling of guilt for occupying a place that might belong to someone else. In poems such as \

), this guilt transforms into an impulse to give and to share, thus anticipating the political and collective dimension that his later poetry would achieve in Spain, Take This Cup from Me.

We are faced with a foundational work in which the great Vallejian obsessions are already present: death, restlessness, the search for God, the memory of childhood, and compassion for the poor man beaten by a destiny he does not understand. A book that, from its very title, turns the poet into a messenger, a herald of human pain, but also of the fraternity that this pain awakens.

Here I leave you the poem and a small analysis, we could say.

---

>**The Black Heralds**

>There are blows in life, so hard... I don't know!
Blows as if from God's hatred; as if before them,
the backlash of all that has been suffered
pooled in the soul... I don't know!

>They are few, but they are... They open dark trenches
in the fiercest face and in the strongest back.
Perhaps they are the steeds of barbarian Atillas,
or the black heralds that Death sends us.

>They are the deep falls of the Christs of the soul,
of some adorable faith that Destiny blasphemes.
Those bloody blows are the cracklings
of some bread that burns at the oven door.

>And man... Poor... poor! He turns his eyes, as
when a pat on the shoulder calls us from behind;
he turns his mad eyes, and everything lived
pools, like a puddle of guilt, in his gaze.

>There are blows in life, so hard... I don't know!

---

This inaugural poem by César Vallejo functions as a poetic and existential declaration. The title itself presents a central metaphor: the black heralds are fateful messengers that Death sends to strike the living, announcing their destiny of suffering.

The poem explores the nature of those blows. Vallejo describes them with violent and contrasting images: they open trenches in the fiercest face, they strike the strongest back. He compares them to \
presenting them as an external destructive force, and to \
as inexorable destiny itself. But then he introduces a surprising image: \

Here, pain does not come from outside, but is an intimate crucifixion, a betrayal of one's own faith by Destiny.

The metaphor of the bread that burns at the oven door is particularly revealing. Bread represents life, daily sustenance, what should nourish; but suffering burns it just before it is ready, on the very threshold of its fulfillment.

Vallejo portrays man's reaction and says: he turns his eyes as if someone touched his shoulder — a gesture of surprise, of waiting for comfort — but what he finds is the puddle of guilt in his gaze. There is no comfort, only the memory of everything suffered, pooled. The poem thus proposes a tragic vision, showing pain as inevitable and incomprehensible, and leaves man alone with his causeless guilt.

---
---


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUCA7PAJsTmKRaYQj9RPiuJkiUiZVpZnudAqyGen3GQpZ/1758337351123.jpg)


---
---

# *PORTUGUÉS*

---
---


Boa noite, boa leitura e doces sonhos.

Hoje me desafio a ousar falar de um dos poetas mais relevantes da América Latina. Nosso enorme César Vallejo. Dele, um livro e o poema que dá nome a ele. Um poema que eu definitivamente amo.

Los heraldos negros (Os arautos negros), livro do autor e também título do poema que dá nome à obra, é leitura obrigatória para os amantes da poesia ou para aqueles que a escrevem.

Este livro representa uma ruptura sutil, mas decisiva, com o Modernismo vigente na época, anunciando já a voz inconfundível que culminaria em obras posteriores como Trilce ou Poemas humanos.

Os arautos negros não é um livro desesperançado. Diante dessa dor universal, Vallejo desdobra uma profunda solidariedade piedosa com o homem sofredor. O poeta sente-se fraternalmente unido a todas as vítimas desse \
e experimenta até mesmo um sentimento de culpa por ocupar um lugar que poderia pertencer a outro. Em poemas como \

, essa culpa se transforma num impulso de entrega e de partilha, antecipando então a dimensão política e coletiva que sua poesia posterior alcançaria em Espanha, aparta de mim este cálice.

Estamos diante de uma obra fundacional onde já estão presentes as grandes obsessões vallejianas: a morte, o desassossego, a busca por Deus, a memória da infância e a compaixão pelo homem pobre e golpeado por um destino que não compreende. Um livro que, desde seu próprio título, converte o poeta em mensageiro, arauto da dor humana, mas também da fraternidade que essa dor desperta.

Aqui lhes deixo o poema e uma pequena análise, podemos dizer.

---

>**Os arautos negros**

>Há golpes na vida, tão fortes... Eu não sei!
Golpes como do ódio de Deus; como se ante eles,
a ressaca de tudo o que foi sofrido
se empocasse na alma... Eu não sei!

>São poucos, mas são... Abrem valas escuras
no rosto mais feroz e no lombo mais forte.
Serão talvez os potros de bárbaros Átilas,
ou os arautos negros que a Morte nos manda.

>São as quedas fundas dos Cristos da alma,
de alguma fé adorável que o Destino blasfema.
Esses golpes sangrentos são as crepitações
de algum pão que na porta do forno se nos queima.

>E o homem... Pobre... pobre! Vira os olhos, como
quando por sobre o ombro nos chama uma palmada;
vira os olhos loucos, e tudo o que foi vivido
se empoca, como poça de culpa, no olhar.

>Há golpes na vida, tão fortes... Eu não sei!

---

Este poema inaugural de César Vallejo funciona como uma declaração poética e existencial. O título em si apresenta uma metáfora central: os arautos negros são mensageiros funestos que a Morte envia para golpear o vivo, anunciando-lhe seu destino de sofrimento.

O poema explora a natureza desses golpes. Vallejo os descreve com imagens violentas e contrastantes: abrem valas no rosto mais feroz, golpeiam o lombo mais forte. Compara-os com \
apresentando-os como uma força destrutiva externa, e com \
como o próprio desígnio inexorável. Mas logo introduz uma imagem surpreendente: \

. Aqui a dor não vem de fora, mas é uma crucificação íntima, uma traição da própria fé por parte do Destino.

A metáfora do pão que se queima na porta do forno é particularmente reveladora. O pão representa a vida, é o alimento cotidiano, o que deveria nutrir; mas o sofrimento o queima justo antes de ficar pronto, no limiar mesmo de sua realização.

Vallejo retrata a reação do homem e diz: vira os olhos como se alguém lhe tocasse o ombro — um gesto de surpresa, de espera de consolo —, mas o que encontra é a poça de culpa em seu olhar. Não há consolo, apenas a memória de tudo o que foi sofrido, empocada. O poema propõe assim uma visão trágica, mostrando a dor inevitável, incompreensível, e deixa o homem sozinho com sua culpa sem causa.

---
---


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcAhAKwyNZZUJMUA7vdruF54aTShX8Mq1ZCs7xYD3C5Sp/1758337351053.jpg)

---

title: A Saturday spent celebrating with the family ✨ (EN/ES)
body:
> I hope you’re all doing well; I’m fine, thank God. Last Saturday was a day that started off quietly but ended up being a celebration. Making the most of the wonderful occasion that was the publication of my dad’s book—which I told you about in my previous post—we decided to have a small family get-together. We met up in San Felipe, in Yaracuy, and the venue we chose was Bokata, which I’ve mentioned before because it’s practically become one of those regular spots for family get-togethers (especially after that dinner in December). This time was no exception. I’d come from Barquisimeto, my sister had left work that very day to make it there, and my parents were already in the mood to go out that evening. The atmosphere was quite lively because there was live music that very night. And here comes the funny bit: it was vallenato. And well, to be honest with you, I don’t like vallenato, ha ha ha. But never mind, most of us were enjoying ourselves, singing along, getting into the spirit of things, so I had to adapt and go with the flow a bit. That said, one thing that didn’t let us down was the food. I ate plenty, without a shred of guilt, because that’s what these outings are for too – to enjoy yourself without overthinking things. Amidst laughter, conversations and the odd comment about my dad’s book, the evening flew by. In the end, beyond the music (well, that’s that, ha ha ha), what mattered was that family moment. Being able to share, celebrate achievements and simply be together. Anyway, I hope you’re having moments like that too, the ones that seem small but last a lifetime. See you in the next post 💜

https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/omarqm/23yU8Zfg24LstJWiiJHyvYoWwxmTc5uBuGGdwuDb2EeUUqfSD6aLWz7DAeJdRrtGejw6g.png **

Versión en Español

** **
¡Saludos comunidad de Hive!
** Espero que se encuentren muy bien, yo bien gracias a Dios. El sábado pasado fue un día que se siente sencillo, pero que termina siendo de celebración. Aprovechando todo lo bonito que ha sido la publicación del libro de mi papá, que ya les conté en el post anterior, decidimos hacer una pequeña celebración familiar. Nos reunimos en San Felipe, en Yaracuy, y el lugar elegido fue Bokata, que ya lo he mencionado antes porque prácticamente se ha vuelto de esos sitios fijos para compartir en familia (sobre todo después de aquella cena de diciembre). Esta vez no era la excepción. Yo venía desde Barquisimeto, mi hermana salió del trabajo ese mismo día para poder llegar, y mis padres ya estaban animados por salir ese día. El ambiente estaba bastante movido porque justo esa noche había talento en vivo. Y aquí viene la parte graciosa, era de vallenato. Y bueno, siendo sincero con ustedes, el vallenato no me gusta jajaja. Pero nada, la mayoría estaba disfrutando, cantando, metidos en el ambiente, así que tocó adaptarse y dejarse llevar un poco. Eso sí, algo que no falló fue la comida. Comí bastante, sin ningún tipo de culpa, porque para eso también son estas salidas, para disfrutar sin estar pensando mucho. Entre risas, conversaciones y uno que otro comentario sobre el libro de mi papá, la noche se fue pasando súper rápido. Al final, más allá de la música (que bueno, ahí quedó jajaja), lo importante fue ese momento en familia. Poder compartir, celebrar logros y simplemente estar juntos. Y nada, espero que ustedes también estén teniendo momentos así, de esos que parecen pequeños pero perduran en el tiempo. Nos leemos en el próximo post 💜

title: The Root and the Silence || Review [Eng/Esp]
body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPz19ByqZXCfz62kqiSw4xiz5i2BRShyfL4JNFUBGwpgD/1776737333391.jpg)


***
***
When in 2024 they announced that Han Kang had won the Nobel, something clicked inside me. It was not just surprise but that visceral certainty that I had to read her immediately, so I quickly went to get The Vegetarian. I devoured it in two nights, and of course it startled me as if someone had opened a door that I myself kept locked, and suddenly all the air had escaped.

The novel is short, but each page weighs like a slab. Yeong hye, an ordinary woman, insignificant to her family, decides one night to stop eating meat. She does not give grand speeches, she does not become an activist, she simply says no, and her family reacts as if she had announced an unforgivable betrayal. Her father slaps her at a dinner, her husband, a gray and petty man, is ashamed of her in front of his colleagues, while I, reading, thought: this is not about vegetarianism, this is a radical refusal of the violence that sustains everyday life.
***


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcyhcLXEAw85zTe4TA5rSnQ6uUhzLaASPFYfq9YtDDyAH/1776737168920.jpg)


***
What fascinated me most was the structure: three parts, three voices, three gazes that never quite let us into Yeong hye's head. First the husband, who sees her as a nuisance to his orderly life, then the artist brother in law, an obsessed and pathetic being who wants to paint her body covered in flowers, taking her to a morbid limit, and finally the sister, who witnesses Yeong hye's silent collapse while trying to hold herself and her son together.

Han Kang forces us to see the protagonist through the distorted reflections she provokes in others, and this gamble that she put on paper worked perfectly because Yeong hye becomes more real the more unreachable she is.
***

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmW1UNk8Ypqeifp5mFHFzfLb1iYbiNB4kyoAax29ZZPEiK/1776737261936.jpg)

***

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmf5DYHEAKWLeVP4rcRX6NY8eejnKGBEVKCMjSmJzeBrU4/1776737262081.jpg)

***
I remember reading the forest scene with a physical tightness in my chest. I closed the book and stared at the wall for a good while because it is definitely a novel that offers neither comfort nor answers; it is one of those that hurt because you recognize yourself in the secondary characters: in the sister's contained rage, in the husband's utilitarian cowardice, and in the almost unbearable need to say no even if it costs you everything you have.

What makes The Vegetarian great? For me it was the tremor it leaves after closing it, and because days later, I still saw Yeong hye standing on the ground, choosing the root and the silence over the insatiable hunger of others.
***


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmShk45zT4ZmddwdWRxrGTX5GJe6Mjm8TosRYEWLLrFAzU/1776737302938.jpg)


***
I do not know if Han Kang wrote the best novel of the year she won the Nobel, but she certainly wrote one that changed the way I sit down to eat, and the way I look at those who refuse to swallow the world as it comes.

### <center>VERSIÓN EN ESPAÑOL</center>

![cinti 800x20 - copia.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWKGeMBmj14VqKn8xBrmpFM3RYVcgmAXX6bGnGwuNWEnc/cinti%20800x20%20-%20copia.jpg) 

## <center> La raíz y el silencio || Reseña</center>



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVpcGaAmP352mBtn26G1ZV8cSVbmheZYVX6XR3ugT1pLb/1776737352971.jpg)



***
***



Cuando en 2024 anunciaron que Han Kang ganó el Nobel, algo hizo clic dentro de mí. No era solo la sorpresa sino esa certeza visceral de que debía leerla de inmediato, así que fui rápido a por La Vegetariana. La devoré en dos noches, y claro, me sobresaltó como si alguien hubiera abierto una puerta que yo misma mantenía cerrada con llave, y de repente todo el aire se hubiera escapado.

La novela es corta, pero cada página pesa como una losa. Yeong hye, una mujer corriente, insignificante para su familia, decide una noche dejar de comer carne. Ella no da grandes discursos, no se vuelve activista, simplemente dice no, y su familia reacciona como si hubiera anunciado una traición imperdonable. El padre la abofetea en una cena, el esposo, un hombre gris y mezquino, se avergüenza de ella ante sus colegas mientras que yo, leyendo, pensé: esto no va de vegetarianismo, esto es una negativa radical a la violencia que sostiene el mundo cotidiano.
***


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcyhcLXEAw85zTe4TA5rSnQ6uUhzLaASPFYfq9YtDDyAH/1776737168920.jpg)


***
Lo que más me fascinó fue la estructura: tres partes, tres voces, tres miradas que nunca nos dejan entrar del todo en la cabeza de Yeong hye. Primero el marido, que la ve como un estorbo para su vida ordenada, luego el cuñado artista, un ser obsesionado y patético que quiere pintar su cuerpo cubierto de flores, hasta llevarla a un límite enfermizo, y finalmente la hermana, que asiste al derrumbe silencioso de Yeong hye mientras intenta sostenerse a sí misma y a su hijo.

Han Kang nos obliga a ver a la protagonista a través de los reflejos deformados que provoca en los demás, y esta apuesta que puso en papel funcionó a la perfección pues Yeong hye se vuelve más real cuanto más inalcanzable está.
***


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmW1UNk8Ypqeifp5mFHFzfLb1iYbiNB4kyoAax29ZZPEiK/1776737261936.jpg)


***


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmf5DYHEAKWLeVP4rcRX6NY8eejnKGBEVKCMjSmJzeBrU4/1776737262081.jpg)


***
Recuerdo leer la escena del bosque con una opresión física en el pecho. Cerré el libro y me quedé mirando la pared un buen rato pues definitivamente es una novela que no da consuelo ni respuestas, es de las que duelen porque te reconoces en los personajes secundarios: en la rabia contenida de la hermana, en la cobardía utilitaria del marido y en la necesidad casi insoportable de decir no aunque te cueste todo lo que tienes.

¿Qué hace grande a La Vegetariana? Para mí fue el temblor que deja después de cerrarla y porque días más tarde, yo seguía viendo a Yeong hye plantada en el suelo, eligiendo la raíz y el silencio antes que el hambre insaciable de los otros.
***


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmShk45zT4ZmddwdWRxrGTX5GJe6Mjm8TosRYEWLLrFAzU/1776737302938.jpg)


***
No sé si Han Kang escribió la mejor novela del año que ganó el Nobel, pero desde luego escribió una que me cambió el gesto al sentarme a comer, y la forma en que miro a quienes se niegan a tragarse el mundo tal como viene.

title: The Gray Man (2022) - Big Budgets Broken Script - REVIEW
body:
https://i.postimg.cc/nr5rfjHR/The-Secret-Agent-(2022)-REVIEW-000.gif
[Source](https://www.netflix.com/title/81160697/)

https://i.imgur.com/PGNq5Ek.png

Two hundred million dollars is a number that should buy you a lot of things, a real script, a reason to care about the person on screen, maybe even one line of dialogue that does not sound like it was generated from a list of things action heroes say in trailers, and yet here is The Gray Man spending every cent of that Netflix check on bullets and drone shots while the actual human beings stuck inside the movie look around confused about what movie they are supposed to be making. I decided to give it a try after watching Gosling latest movie Project Hail Mary since this was describe as one of his best work and its not true at all, he has way better movies than this, this was a under the table Netflix failure if not very meh. The Russo brothers have been riding the Avengers goodwill for years now but the further they get from Marvel money and Marvel infrastructure the clearer it becomes that a lot of what worked in those movies was not them, it was the machine, and The Gray Man is the kind of movie that shows you the difference real fast. Ryan Gosling is a legitimately capable actor who has done some of the most interesting work of his generation in movies like Drive and Blade Runner 2049, and watching him play Sierra Six, who is essentially a walking empty vessel with good reflexes, feels like a quiet waste of a very expensive talent, the character doesnt have that momentum, no point of view, no reason to be interesting beyond the fact that Gosling is doing probably his best that cant even be notice. The movie opens with a textbook setup where Six is recruited out of a prison cell by a government guy named Fitzroy, played by Billy Bob Thornton who is doing his low key southern charmer thing, and the deal is simple, you work for us or you rot in here and then you just almost stand by for aabout twenty minutes of setup before the movie finally admits what it actually is.

- IMDB: https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1649418/
- Platform: [NETFLIX](https://www.netflix.com/title/81160697/)

https://t6.picb.cc/2026/04/21/uXqM20.png
<div style=\

>Rottentomatoes Rating https://i.imgur.com/uwwnjtd.png https://t6.picb.cc/2026/04/21/uXqO11.png [Source](https://www.netflix.com/title/81160697/) Chris Evans is basically the only thing stopping this movie from becoming pure second monitor entertaiment, Chris is the one that goes all in as Lloyd Hansen, who is a completely ridiculous villain and that full commitment is easily the most fun thing in the movie. The mustache, the sweaters, the total lack of redeeming qualities, Evans knows exactly what kind of character he is playing and you can tell the guy is just having a good time at it. The action looks impressive in a technical sense too, especially the Prague fountain sequence where the drone shots and the stunt work actually have some style and purpose behind them, you can respect the effort even when the rest of the movie is kinda meh. There is also a part of the movie where Six becomes a protector for Claire, Fitzroy’s niece, and that could have added some real emotion to the story. It is not a bad idea at all but very average movie for the amount of marketing the put into it. The problem is the movie gives it almost no room to breathe before moving on, Ana de Armas also does what she can with her role and looks like a star every time she is on screen, she is great in the action but she also gives off the energy of someone who knows she is too good for this movie. https://t6.picb.cc/2026/04/21/uXqWad.png [Source](https://www.netflix.com/title/81160697/) https://t6.picb.cc/2026/04/21/uXqqEa.png [Source](https://www.netflix.com/title/81160697/) There is this airplane scene where they just going at each other throwing hands while the entire fuselage is almost comming apart around them, that is when the movie goes full CGI overload and just start becoming bloaded, ngl it does looks expensive but its more like trying to get your attention rathern than earning your attention, like the production knew the story was not doing the job so it kept turning up the spectacle hoping nobody would notice the reason behind all the flashy CGI. The whole thing has this strange washed out colors too, like someone in post forgot to turn the saturation up and every city they blow through, Bangkok, Prague, London, looks equally flat and equally fake. Rege Jean Page shows up as the antagonist and I hate to say it because the guy has charisma in other things but every scene where he is supposed to feel menacing just sits there not doing anything, flat delivery in a flat role and the movie tries to add some actual weight to Six through flashbacks about abuse and trauma that feel like they were dropped in because someone looked at the script and said this character needs a backstory, not because anyone actually figured out what that backstory should do for the movie. The moment where Six gets a blade through his hand and keeps fighting like he caught a splinter tells you everything about the movie not really taking in consideration concequences or at least trying to stay close to reality. Gosling and Evans have exactly one scene that actually hits and it was expected to happen, its when they finally clash with eacy other, and all of the sudden it feels like this was the right direction of the movie, this is the movie that could have been made with these two if anyone had bothered to write it right. https://t6.picb.cc/2026/04/21/uXqheu.png [Source](https://www.netflix.com/title/81160697/) https://t6.picb.cc/2026/04/21/uXqv7D.png [Source](https://www.netflix.com/title/81160697/) Compared to how much Netflix spent on it against something like other Netflix originals, for example Red Notice at least knew it was empty nonsense and had a little fun with that. The Gray Man is more annoying because it takes itself way too seriously, always reaching for depth and seriousness that it never actually earns. Other similar failures like Six Underground that kinda makes me mad almost immediately with how aggressively Michael Bay was throwing chaos at the screen, so The Gray Man is better than that at least but fits just in the same hype train that never really deliver. It is more coherent got to give it, but getting over that very low bar does not automatically make it a movie I would tell anyone to watch, it remains in the lower meh range. The stunt and action work is clearly being done by people who know exactly what they are doing, and you can feel the skill in some of the fight scenes even when the story around them is completely empty. The problem is that good craft without a story behind it will always feel empty like they just doing the action scenes for the show but you really dont care about the characters and it takes the sense of danger out of it, and that is basically what this movie turns into. It is a very long, very polished vague content that somehow cost two hundred million dollars. The movie keeps piling on new cities, new characters, and new threats, but none of it really builds into anything with actual weight. By the time its past half mark of the movie, you can feel the whole thing starting to fall flat even with all the action and spectable that it kept pumping, like it kept adding more and more on top to see if it clicks or get some dopamine into your brain so you look the other side. https://i.imgur.com/uwwnjtd.png

> https://i.imgur.com/r0yj9oi.png I walked out of this thing feeling like I had been handed a very expensive gift in a box that turned out to be completely empty, the production quality is not a problem at all and Evans alone is worth at least watching the movie once but only if you go in with total transparency about what you are getting into, but there is nothing, nothing that grabs you and keeps you interested into the movie, there is that drama and sense of character building missing as in any good action movie, you cant be in between, either you are all show or you put some intention behind it but the problem is that when they try they just make things too complicated. Evans makes Lloyd Hansen the kind of villain you want to see get his own movie where he is still a total bastard but at least he is the center of something, because watching him chew through this script is the only time The Gray Man feels like it has actual life in it. If you get to watch this movie just be aware that it feels fancy, its loud, got action into it, but its not as good as it seems, you for sure have seen worst movie so its not like its the worst movie any of this actors have done. This one lands at a 6/10 from me, my post probably feels like a rant but its just that after watching Project Hail Mary I took some interest into Gosling work, specially for any action movies he has done and it has been mention how this movie compares but it was just total bs and pure marketing hype because its been about 10 years since Blade Runner 2049 and First Man came out, yes it is watchable streaming content that you will have forgotten entirely after a week, go in with zero expectations and the Evans factor might just be enough to carry you through it. Yes this was a delayed rant on a movie from 4 years ago that I regret watching comparing to the recent highs of Gosling with Project Hail Mary. https://i.imgur.com/uwwnjtd.png https://i.imgur.com/AbuDA6i.png

title: Emotional Intelligence Taught Me Patience And Gentility (#285)
body:
What is one book, YouTube video, movie, or life lesson on self-development that has truly impacted you? It could be about skills, money, purpose, relationships, health, or personal growth. Share what it taught you and why you would recommend it to others. Hello #ladiesofhive, happy new week.
I have read several books in search of self-awareness and development in both normal life and professional development. However, this video on \

by Oluyemi Adeosun has helped broaden my scope on people management.

https://youtu.be/2qPoqHbVNN4?si=g0nx0Ey0XRN1kwjw

[Oluyemi Adeosun](https://youtu.be/2qPoqHbVNN4?si=Y9rFXe1l_fa2dDCV)
I encountered the video through a post on our professional forum to his YouTube page. That day, I just hovered it.Afterwards, I had a challenge that bothered  on emotional intelligence and people management at the workplace. This, took me back to the link to watch the full video.

Emotional intelligence is defined as the ability to recognise, understand, and control my and other people's emotions to bring out their best. Mismanagement of emotions can lead to a chaotic relationship and environment, which may affect productivity. When people are happy, motivated, and healthy, productivity increases, otherwise, it decrease when the environment is toxic and chaotic. 

This video has impacted me positively with skills and competencies to engage and manage my emotions even in the face of provocation. Recently, an employee had an issue of forgery which attracts a summary dismissal according to the company's policy and a weighty penalty according to my country's labour law. The individual was issued a forty eight hours in a query to come up with reasons for such behaviour. Rather than obeying instructions, the individual was going around and seeking the union's intervention until the time elapsed without a esponse to the query.

A disciplinary meeting was called, and right before me, the individual became abusive and full of threats. During the turmoil, the individual was still giving more days after the intervention of some top management staff to come up with a response to the queey, which never happened. Eventually, the arms of law took its weight upon the employee.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmT5YXDJZir8MdYk4FGpkMcekupiqpxRZnGagQoYkQJgRm/1776736289104.jpg)

 Before, more time  wouldn’t  have been given to the employee for being abusive which is a gross misconduct automatically. But with my present learning and unlearning from the video, I allowed more time. Therefore, I would recommend the video to everyone, because it helped me develop patience and emotional intelligence in people management. Not only at my workplace but in my side hustle, client management, and at home as well. 

This video will help individuals to understand their emotions,  manage them, and eqquip them with the ability to depict other people's emotions and manage them. This will help us build good relationships, understand people better, and treat them well. It will also assist us in providing the support needed to people around us to bring out their shine.

Feel free to join [here](https://ecency.com/hive-124452/@ladiesofhive/ladies-of-hive-community-contest-285)

title: A butterfly with polka dots on its wings [Eng/Esp]
body:
>

Butterflies are my favorite insects to photograph because I always find them beautiful, whether it’s the color of their wings, the patterns they often display, the shape of their wings, or the subtle beauty they exude when they land on flowers. That’s why I’m sharing some photos with you today; I hope you enjoy them.

Las mariposas son los insectos que más disfruto fotografiar, porque se me hacen siempre bonitos, ya sea por el color de sus alas, los patrones que suelen tener, la forma de sus alas o la sutil belleza cuando se posan en las flores; por eso el día de hoy les comparto algunas fotografías; espero que las disfruten.


https://images.ecency.com/DQmcgm5Lis5T7JSkqMgYkuYz97zkxCP9J4zeY58GoQKn5bW/dsc05159.jpg

https://images.ecency.com/DQmSKevtwEeA3VPjAv5Mt3aJjobAYvWGSugPqjoB7fCKtZG/dsc05190.jpg

https://images.ecency.com/DQmew9kXpZLH33ReQVJrzeuwFKFEVR3W8Fb2q9MN493dDTx/dsc05205.jpg

>

There are butterflies of many colors, no doubt about that, but I rarely come across white butterflies with black spots, or perhaps they’re black butterflies with white spots; I suppose it all depends on how you look at it, but the point is that I find this pattern really beautiful.

Existen mariposas de muchos colores, de eso no hay duda, pero son pocas las veces que me cruzo con mariposas blancas que tienen lunares negros o quizás sean mariposas negras con lunares blancos; supongo que todo depende de la perspectiva que se le quiera dar, pero el punto es que se me hace muy bonito este patrón.


https://images.ecency.com/DQmUJQqEkZUUhze2Dhs3MLUg2ERmE3L3fN3cZbmo335uPQq/dsc05217.jpg

https://images.ecency.com/DQmb5q7ox7U4Y1AjXVrLHiJMB6CNRp4MwQh7ESmXpZWHATA/dsc05232.jpg

https://images.ecency.com/DQmPoJ9n7B32PZisM89heLYw6Qkmjg9iFHWkkRZ4PXvaRch/dsc05235.jpg

>

What isn't so great is the process of taking the photos, because they're obviously always on the move, which means you have to keep moving from one spot to another, and that's assuming they stay on nearby flowers and don't just decide to fly away and never come back, but it's still fun to do.

Lo que no es tan bonito es el proceso de hacer las fotografías, porque es evidente que están en constante movimiento, lo cual te hace tener que moverte de un lugar a otro, y eso teniendo suerte de que se mantengan en flores cercanas y no decidan irse simplemente y no volver, pero aun así resulta divertido de hacer.


https://images.ecency.com/DQmSmvaekuSGZc7d5EaSNZ7rYLGmt3pEB98wxS1TNDwafPo/dsc05237.jpg

https://images.ecency.com/DQmf28YjnEG1ANiTwS79spUQrXBuEtXMA5BVoLyiwTADSZA/dsc05245.jpg

https://images.ecency.com/DQmX86d5ZmKtepkQxjAEqJxuoq2bXkrDAb5Bc9HE2pZMmQb/dsc05247o.jpg

>

That's all for today; I hope you enjoyed these nature photos. Thank you so much for taking the time to look at my photos. Until next time, dear friends in the community and photography lovers. Have a great day!

Esto es todo por el día de hoy; espero que disfrutaran de estas fotografías en la naturaleza. Muchas gracias por tomarse el tiempo de ver mis fotografías. Hasta la próxima, queridos amigos de la comunidad y amantes de la fotografía. ¡Feliz día!

/>

title: Enunciada mujer /   Enunciated woman [ES /EN]
body:
Hola Hivers, es un gusto estar de vuelta por el blog. Hoy quiero compartir un poema que nace desde la tensión entre lo terrenal y lo sagrado, entre el cuerpo y aquello que lo desborda. Enunciada mujer es una aproximación a esa fuerza que funda, desordena y vuelve a crear: la mujer como origen, como lenguaje y como misterio. Aquí no hay respuestas, solo una búsqueda: la del instante en que la palabra intenta nombrar lo inabarcable. Les comparto este poema.
ENUNCIADA MUJER En los ardores del día se levantan las espumas de tu mar lo sabes y mueves el eje de las risas. Temo que temblará la tierra bajo mis pies, mientras andamos sobre la zanja donde han caído las flores que ayer eran coronas de las fiestas. Tú has detenido el reloj sin que se quiebre el eje de la tierra. Aprecio la circunstancia terrenal que funda: me hace naufragar en el oleaje de tu ser. Tu voz. Todas las voces vinieron a anunciar un temblor de pálpitos un huracán de primaveras que se instaura. Precipitas las manzanas de las Evas y fecundas el día con corceles asomados, iluminando el espectáculo del alba. Inundas mis venas, de hombre traslúcido, con la savia de tu policromía. Cercas el vientre con una miel próxima, como eximiéndome de las lanzas que el día instaura. Un aleteo contra el fusil de la noche se avecina, lava la desidia, los malditos contratiempos. Quedaremos —cercados— a expensas de tu faro en la tormenta: tu mano de seda que sabe de corazones duros. Descenderemos desde la altura conmovida a la noche con pechos al frente y caderas al filo de la rosa, hasta la frontera de nuestra desolación de sustantivo. Sigo ávido de tu agua, del duelo que sugieres contra el desnivel de los odios. Debajo de tu párpado: miel de frutas, amargo combativo. Por allí quiero escudriñar los derroteros, acaso el sendero por donde Dios dejó escondido el paraíso, o —entre amargos presentimientos — dejó el molde olvidado con que te hizo ser y espíritu. —PoetaFrankoo 🌿

> ----

ENGLISH - ENGLISH - ENGLISH - ENGLISH - ENGLISH

Hello Hivers, it’s a pleasure to be back on the blog. Today I want to share a poem that emerges from the tension between the earthly and the sacred, between the body and that which overflows it. Enunciated Woman is an approach to that force which founds, disrupts, and recreates: woman as origin, as language, and as mystery. There are no answers here, only a search: the moment in which the word attempts to name the ungraspable. I share this poem with you. ENUNCIATED WOMAN In the ardors of the day, the foams of your sea rise, you know it, and you move the axis of laughter. I fear the earth will tremble beneath my feet, as we walk along the trench where have fallen the flowers that yesterday were crowns of festivity. You have stopped the clock without the axis of the earth breaking. I cherish the earthly circumstance that founds: it makes me shipwreck in the surge of your being. Your voice. All voices came to announce a trembling of heartbeats, a hurricane of springs that takes hold. You precipitate the apples of the Eves and fertilize the day with emerging steeds, illuminating the spectacle of dawn. You flood my veins—of a translucent man— with the sap of your polychromy. You encircle the womb with a near honey, as if releasing me from the spears that the day establishes. A flutter against the rifle of the night approaches, washing away indolence, the cursed setbacks. We will remain—besieged—at the mercy of your beacon in the storm: your silk hand that knows of hardened hearts. We will descend from the moved height into the night, with chests forward and hips at the edge of the rose, to the frontier of our desolation of noun. I remain thirsty for your water, for the duel you suggest against the unevenness of hatred. Beneath your eyelid: fruit-honey, combative bitterness. There I want to search the routes, perhaps the path through which God left paradise hidden, or—amid bitter forebodings— left the forgotten mold with which He made you being and spirit. **—PoetaFrankoo 🌿**

title: Harmony.
body:
<center>![image](https://pixabay.com/get/g99d234c3c047f09a7e3a380ac320260e141e62b219ab61f879a002f0ed44e8ff7d0005801386a4b036c4bb8998f5a80c453e2f79415fbefa4f23883619e6aa2e_640.jpg)</center>

***

# The Tale of the Harmony Tree

Once upon a time, in a vibrant village nestled between two mountains, there stood a magnificent tree known as the Harmony Tree. This tree was unlike any other; its branches intertwined with those of its neighboring trees, creating a beautiful canopy that provided shade and shelter to all who sought it. The villagers believed that the tree possessed the power to bring peace and unity to their community.

## The Gift of Harmony

Every spring, the villagers would gather around the Harmony Tree to celebrate the Festival of Unity. They would sing, dance, and share stories, each person contributing their unique voice to the chorus of life. The tree thrived in this atmosphere of love and togetherness, its blossoms more vibrant each year.

However, as time passed, the village began to change. New families moved in, each bringing their own customs and traditions. At first, the villagers welcomed these newcomers, eager to learn and grow together. But as differences began to surface, misunderstandings arose. The once harmonious gatherings dwindled, and the villagers became divided.

## The Warning Ignored

One fateful day, an elder of the village, wise and weathered, called for a meeting beneath the Harmony Tree. \
she said, her voice steady yet filled with concern. \

The villagers nodded, but their hearts were heavy with resentment. They were too focused on their grievances to heed her warning. Instead of working together, they began to isolate themselves, each group clinging to their own beliefs and traditions.

## The Withering Tree

As the years passed, the Harmony Tree began to show signs of distress. Its once-lush leaves turned brittle, and its vibrant blossoms faded into dull shades. The villagers, now entrenched in their divisions, no longer gathered beneath its branches. They had forgotten the joy of unity and the strength that came from their diversity.

One day, a young girl named Lila, who had grown up hearing tales of the tree's former glory, decided to take action. She invited children from all groups to come together and share their stories, songs, and games. Slowly, the children began to play, laugh, and learn from one another, rekindling the spirit of unity that had once thrived in the village.

## The Restoration of Harmony

Inspired by the children's joy, the villagers began to join in. They remembered the elder's words and realized that harmony required effort, empathy, and an openness to learn from one another. They came together once more, sharing their traditions and creating new ones that honored their differences.

As the villagers worked to restore their sense of community, the Harmony Tree responded. Its leaves grew green and lush again, and blossoms returned, more vibrant than ever. The tree became a symbol of their renewed commitment to understanding and celebrating their differences.

## The Lesson Learned

The tale of the Harmony Tree teaches us that:

- **Harmony is an active pursuit**: It requires effort, empathy, and a willingness to listen.
- **Diversity is a strength**: Embracing our differences can lead to richer experiences and deeper connections.
- **Unity is fragile**: It can wither if neglected, but with care and commitment, it can flourish once more.

In the end, the villagers learned that true harmony is not about erasing differences but about weaving them into a beautiful tapestry of community. And so, the Harmony Tree stood tall, a testament to the power of understanding and the beauty of unity in diversity.

武汉花博汇的花在四月悉数绽放了，最引人注目的是那一大片蝴蝶造型的花海。不过若是从正门进入，平视的视角很难看清它的全貌，唯有换个角度才能感受到它的宏大。
 
周末和朋友去打卡时，他特意带了无人机航拍。从高空俯视下去，那只巨大的蝴蝶造型瞬间清晰起来，立体的视觉效果确实比站在地上看震撼得多。
 
半个月前种下的花苗都如期盛开了。虽然期间经历了几场春雨，花期受到些许影响，但花海依然保持着85%以上的完整度，大部分花朵都还挺立着，没有大面积凋谢。
 
除了蝴蝶花海，园区内另外一边也已是繁花似锦。反观三月份我们看到的那片虞美人花海，如今花期已过，大半都已凋零，剩下的不足三成，呈现出另一番景象。
 
春天的花季本就是此起彼伏、轮番登场，这边是盛极一时的蝴蝶花海，那边是谢幕退场的虞美人。这种更迭感，让整个春天都充满了循环往复的生机。
 
眼下武汉的气温正经历一波低温，但下周到了五一，天气会迅速进入夏季模式。是时候把短袖全部拿出来了，毕竟在武汉，春秋十分短暂，漫长的盛夏即将开启。

title: Ed's Story, Arriving at the musical destination
body:
Good afternoon, friends. Today I've written a new story for each of you. This one is about Ed, who works in the music industry. You'll see how he and the band face certain difficulties. You'll see how they overcome them. I hope you enjoy it.

> Buenas tardes amigos, Pues hoy he escrito una nueva historia para cada uno de ustedes. Esta la hice sobre Ed, el es una persona que trabaja en el sector de la música. Ya verán como tiene que enfrentarse junto a la banda a ciertas dificultades. Ya verán como salen de ellas. Espero que les guste.

<div class=\

> ![1776596025907.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/omztech/23yJCXAhSqMJ3G5yTcjpqWbx28CrgdVyuxMcMqE4yjji3qGS4V14YQdzubfBiEC84x2MV.jpg) Image created by me in canva Finally, what they had been waiting for so long had happened. They had been invited to the biggest show in the province. This show was the most prestigious musical event in the entire state of Buskeria. They would be the featured guests and the main act of the day. They were none other than the band TAW. This band had been trying for years to be part of this show because it gave a lot of exposure to emerging singers. In fact, everyone who went through it received a great boost to their future career. That's why TAW so desperately wanted to participate and sing at the big concert. Since the organizers of the event saw that they had stood out and were very good, even better than several singers in the area, they chose them to represent the province, and that was a great privilege. The show would be on a Monday at 2 p.m. It would start at that time and end well into the night. It would be great for anyone who could go; the best of the best would be there. This is where our friend Ed comes into the picture. He is the band's personal driver and the one in charge of taking them to the big concert that day. > Por fin había ocurrido lo que llevaban ya mucho tiempo esperando. Habían sido invitados al mayor show de la provincia. Ese show era el mayor exponente musical de todo el estado de Buskeria. En el show ellos serían las estrellas invitadas y los principales exponentes del día. Ellos eran nada más y nada menos que la banda llamada TAW. Esta banda llevaba años intentado ser parte de este show porque les daba mucha visibilidad a los cantantes emergentes. De hecho todo el que pasaba por el tenía un gran impulso en su carrera futura. Por eso TAW deseaba tanto poder participar y cantar en el gran concierto asociado. > Como los organizadores de ese evento vieron que ellos se habían destacado mucho y eran muy buenos, incluso más que varios cantantes de la zona los eligieron para representar la provincia, y eso era un gran privilegio. El show sería un lunes a las 2 de la tarde. A esa hora comenzaría y terminaría bien adentrada la noche. Sería genial para todo el que pudiera ir, estaría lo mejor de lo mejor. Aquí es donde entra nuestro amigo Ed en escena. El es el conductor personal de la banda y el encargado de llevarlos ese día al gran concierto.

> ![tony-sebastian-5j_X8XaaUSM-unsplash.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/omztech/23wqik4apUAk6yjhpx1epbypmh1iWDaGNrAbT31ruZrZCJzeyurTqY9nnf4TZM8eg9hn3.jpg) [Source](www.pexels.com) The big day arrived; it was early Monday morning. Ed got up and prepared the band's official van. He filled the gas tank and inflated the tires. He also checked the engine for any problems. It was a little noisy, but that was normal; it was a classic van. He suggested the band leave earlier to be prepared for any unexpected issues, because you never know. And since the concert was so important to them, it was essential to arrive on time and without delays. But the band couldn't leave at the time he suggested. They needed to do a few final rehearsals before going on stage for the audience. Since Ed had no authority over the band, he was just their driver, he couldn't tell them anything more. He simply parked the van outside the hotel where they were staying and waited. Several hours passed, but then they got in and left. The delay didn't really bother them much because it was only noon and the concert wasn't until 2 p.m. And since the truck was quite fast despite being old, they were all super confident, including Ed, that they would arrive on time. But they hadn't taken into account that it was rush hour. Thousands of people were leaving work for lunch, and the traffic was horrendous at that time. As a result, they could barely move because of the number of cars in front and behind them. They couldn't believe it; even though the truck was fast, it was impossible to go fast. > El gran día llegó, era lunes bien temprano por la mañana. Ed se levantó y preparó la camioneta oficial de la banda. Le llenó el tanque de combustible y llenó de aire los neumáticos. También revisó el motor para ver si había problemas. Hacía un poco de ruido pero eso era normal, era una camioneta clásica. El le sugirió a la banda salir más temprano para poder hacer frente a imprevistos, porque nunca se sabe. Y como el concierto era tan importante para ellos era necesario llegar a tiempo y sin demoras. Pero la banda no pudo salir en el horario que el les sugirió. Es que necesitaban hacer unos últimos ensayos antes de salir y hacer en vivo para el publico. Como Ed no tenía poder alguno sobre la banda, solo era su conductor no pudo decirles nada más. Solo aparcó la camioneta fuera del hotel en donde estaban y espero. > Se demoraron varias horas, pero luego se montaron y salieron. La verdad el retraso no los afectaba mucho porque aún eran las 12 del mediodía y el concierto no era hasta las 2 de la tarde. Y como la camioneta era bastante rápida a pesar de ser vieja estaban súper confiados incluido Ed de que llegarían a tiempo. Pero no tuvieron en cuenta que ha esa hora es el horario pico. Miles de personas salen de sus trabajos para almorzar. Y el tráfico es horrible a esa hora. Las consecuencias fueron que no podían avanzar casi por la cantidad de autos detrás y delante. No lo podían creer, aunque la camioneta era rápida no era posible ir rápido.

> ![nao-takabayashi-XgsrzJhJulI-unsplash.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/omztech/243BRSv41PJsWHS2YrYaa1MeLzyZN5kWZDSnwUh569tw2mecccbPpenWV9ZaGjxDMFf6B.jpg) [Source](www.pexels.com) Because they were going so slowly, they lost a lot of time and became extremely worried. If they were late, the concert would start without them, and that would be disastrous for their careers and everything that meant to them. They regretted not listening to Ed and leaving when he told them to. But there was nothing they could do except ask the traffic to move quickly. However, going so slowly created an even bigger problem. Because the van was going so slowly, it overheated. The old engine couldn't withstand the pressure and broke down. They all had to get out and push the van to the side of the road so it could be checked. Nervousness and worry turned into panic. The big concert—they wouldn't make it on time. Their only hope was that Ed, who knew the van best, could do something. Luckily for them, he was able to check the engine and repair it, and they were able to continue. The time they lost helped clear the traffic jam. When they could finally proceed without traffic, Ed floored the van. They arrived on time and were able to be the stars of the concert that day. But they will never forget the lesson; they will never again leave just in time. They will always follow Ed's foresighted example. > Como iban tan lento perdieron mucho tiempo así que se preocuparon muchísimo. Si llegaban tarde el concierto empezaría sin ellos y eso sería fatal para sus carreras y lo que eso significaba para ellos. Se lamentaron de no hacerle caso a Ed y haber salido cuando el les había dicho. Pero ya no había nada que pudieran hacer salvo pedir que aquel trafico pasara rápido. Pero ir tan lento creó otro problema aún más grave. Como la camioneta iba tan lento se sobrecalentó. El viejo motor no resistió esa presión y se averío. Todos tuvieron que bajarse y empujar la camioneta hacia a un lado de la carretera para poder revisarla. El nerviosismo y la preocupación se transformaron en pánico. El gran concierto, no llegarían a tiempo. Su única esperanza era que Ed pudiera hacer algo que era quien mejor conocía a la camioneta. > Por suerte para todos ellos el pudo revisar el motor y repararlo y pudieron continuar. El tiempo que perdieron sirvió para que el atasco de vehículos se disipara. Cuando por fin pudieron seguir sin trafico Ed aceleró a todo lo que daba la camioneta. Llegaron a tiempo y pudieron ser las estrellas del concierto ese día. Pero nunca olvidarán la lección, no volverán a salir con el tiempo justo. Seguirán siempre el ejemplo previsor de Ed.

> ![Captura de pantalla (2600).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/omztech/EoK5sQdsXsUS7ZLcAZYBEe5GmHFAebHJrsUXiga5KPPcj6usByoTjcdxkNe1VdxsUCo.png) # [Join](https://risingstargame.com) hive's most incredible game, Rising Star , today. **Don't miss the opportunity to become a Rising Star**.

Yesterday, when I was out walking in nature to take pictures, I suddenly saw this blue butterfly, the butterfly caught my eye at first sight. Sitting on the green grass, its soft blue wings looked so beautiful that it was almost eye-catching.

Although this butterfly is small, its blue wings and black color at the end of the wings made it look incredibly beautiful. Although it is impossible to capture all the beauty if you want, you can capture this beauty of nature with your camera.

I stood there for a while and watched it, occasionally spreading its wings and then standing still. When I took the picture, it was sunny, so its blue color stood out even clearer and brighter.

These small moments with nature are what really make our day different.

title: Exploring the sacred art museum inside. | Explorando el museo de artesacro en su interior.
body:
> **Gratos saludos tengan todos mis queridos amigos viajeros del mundo desde sus distintas partes hoy quiero seguirle mostrando este hermoso lugar el Museo de arte sacro de mi ciudad.** **Warm greetings to all my dear fellow travellers from all corners of the world. Today, I’d like to continue showing you this beautiful place: my city’s Museum of Sacred Art.** El museo de alta sacro es un lugar fantástico, ya que posee diversas partes en un poco anterior, conocimos toda su fachada externa y ahora vamos a conocer cada una de su lugares internos, los detalles interesantes e históricos que posee es un lugar enmarcado por galerías fotográficas de fotos antiguas, así como también retratos artisticos, elaborados por artistas de la localidad que tienden a ser bastante hermosos, así como también los detalles antiguos que posee su edificación que forma parte de la identidad propia del lugar, al ser un lugar histórico con más de 100 años antigüedad, donde residió, el obispo Lasso ofrece mucho más que historia a cada una de las personas que le visitan. >The Sacred Art Museum is a fantastic place, as it comprises several sections. Earlier, we explored its entire exterior façade, and now we are going to take a look at each of its interior spaces, The interesting and historical details it contains are framed by galleries of old photographs, as well as artistic portraits created by local artists, which tend to be quite beautiful. There are also the ancient architectural details of the building itself, which form part of the place’s unique identity, as it is a historic site over 100 years old where Bishop Lasso once resided. Bishop Lasso offers much more than just history to every visitor. ![Uploading image #1...]() Ahora bien, al entrar al lugar uno de los detalles más interesantes, es su techo en alturas, ya que a diferencia de los otros techos característicos de la ciudad, estas casas antiguas se distinguían, por tener un techo en altura, ya que más ya que permitía tener mayor paso del aire permitía una ventilación dentro de las casas totalmente natural, ya que Maracaibo tienende hacer una ciudad caliente, esto permitía que tuviera mayor fluidez del fresco de adentro hacia afuera, es por eso que podemos evidenciar que los techos son sumamente altos para permitir la facilidad de la distribución del viento a lo largo de toda la fachada interna de la casa, así como sus enormes pasillos. >Now, upon entering the building, one of the most interesting features is its high ceiling; unlike the other roofs typical of the city, these old houses stood out for having a high ceiling, as this not only allowed for greater airflow but also enabled completely natural ventilation inside the houses, given that Maracaibo is a hot city, This allowed for a greater flow of cool air from inside to outside, which is why we can see that the ceilings are extremely high to facilitate the circulation of air throughout the entire interior façade of the house, as well as its enormous corridors. Porque va a lo mejor el techo es totalmente machenbrado techo de madera, fabricado en roble, ya que anteriormente se tendía a elaborar los techos de esta manera para así también garantizar una excelente climatización del lugar también uno de los detalles interesantes de este lugar es su hermoso piso que este es de cerámica con distintas formas, así como también posee distintos tipos de candelabros, característico también de estas edificaciones antiguas ya que en muchos lugares históricos como la catedral entre otras iglesias anteriormente en el siglo pasado se tenía a colocar estos tipos de candelabros. >Perhaps the ceiling is a fully carved wooden ceiling, made of oak, as ceilings were traditionally constructed in this way to ensure excellent temperature control within the building; another interesting feature of this place is its beautiful floor, which is made of ceramic tiles in various shapes, as well as various types of chandeliers, which are also characteristic of these old buildings, as in many historic sites such as the cathedral and other churches in the last century, it was customary to install these types of chandeliers. Chiquinquirá y también del Sagrado Corazón de Jesús, ya que estaban en el marco de las obras Chiquinquireñas, haciendo referencia a los días patronales de la virgen de Chiquinquira, estaba totalmente fascinada, con toda la expresión artística de los distintos lienzos que se encontraban plasmados dentro de cada una de esas obras plásticas y artísticas sin duda algunas fantásticas rindiendo homenaje especial a nuestra madre del cielo, patrona de los zulianos la virgen de Chiquinquirá. >And on its main walls, right in the centre, we can find various types of portraits and artistic works painted by hand with a brush by artists from our city; we can see Catholic paintings such as the image of Our Lady of Chiquinquirá and also of the Sacred Heart of Jesus, as they were part of the Chiquinquirá works, referring to the patronal days of the Virgin of Chiquinquirá. I was completely fascinated, by all the artistic expression in the various canvases captured within each of these visual and artistic works—undoubtedly some fantastic ones—paying special homage to our Mother in Heaven, the patron saint of the people of Zulia: the Virgin of Chiquinquirá. ![20251217_101607.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdMa8hgTtbPR94pwLu9E32icgg5D6N1Nqi1TRCRx14zGM/20251217_101607.jpg) ![20251217_101619.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVNHAvcqaAGVLMfRSj7UBJ7UcRvzUPkN2boGBgqCiJxra/20251217_101619.jpg) ![20251217_102623.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSDu5pzU2aHeMxrR82P5Ehx4eTekgdjks2vqfJaTXvr8p/20251217_102623.jpg) ![20251217_103055.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmREVwUouExNZfn9mPq6j8joJFg2KykmJSVffP4eWjTVvc/20251217_103055.jpg) ![20251217_103058.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcMPFk6bAu5yr6q2kr7JYgo7XbCj8TQ8HE1K6FPZ2G1yw/20251217_103058.jpg) --- No mostraron el área de la sala donde se encuentran los baños desde este punto hay distintas fotografías de lo que ha sido el clero de Maracaibo a lo largo de los años cuando digo clero, refiero a los distintos sacerdotes que han pasado por cada una de las iglesias que conforman la arquidiócesis de Maracaibo, es decir, cada una de esas iglesias que forman parte de la iglesia de nuestra ciudad entre ellos, podemos ver imágenes importantes del monseñor Ubaldo Santana, quien fue nuestro obispo durante muchos años, así como también de otros insignes importantes que estuvieron anteriormente presentes frente a nuestra iglesia, así como también podemos ver retratos de algunos papas entre ellos, nuestro querido papa Francisco, incluyendo al obispo esta ciudad a quien le debemos el nombre de este museo y de su carretera de en frente. >They did not show the part of the hall where the toilets are; from this point onwards, there are various photographs depicting the clergy of Maracaibo over the years. When I say ‘clergy’, I am referring to the various priests who have served in each of the churches that make up the Archdiocese of Maracaibo; that is to say, each of those churches that form part of our city’s church. Among them, we can see important images of Monsignor Ubaldo Santana, who was our bishop for many years, as well as other distinguished figures who previously served our church. We can also see portraits of several popes, including our beloved Pope Francis, and the bishop of this city to whom we owe the name of this museum and the road in front of it. ![20251217_103247.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUs846dEWCC3eLHvVm18rtzpva9Bpn4ZW2tKtXbYNdNjD/20251217_103247.jpg) ![20251217_103254.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmU4AKg8zYtPM2c2enJdMD7FcGZr2QBpc3QEaMSUv3DFbE/20251217_103254.jpg) ![20251217_103257.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYiBgU8kJyqJBL26L64C5ViyH3XGdCTMgppuyPXVbuw6b/20251217_103257.jpg) ![20251217_103304.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNfBqt1GkALmQu3XWKupTnDcV1gKKsF9CjWzqp9z7Wv9n/20251217_103304.jpg) ![20251217_103903.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZmh5GvNyJGvfLK7nxtbu6FhtJHnGv5AizXCY1rMbWQQA/20251217_103903.jpg) ![20251217_103913.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRNyUxt32AXR7UMM9E3A62tmHfrDJDQjRp1cWJaH7kGXf/20251217_103913.jpg) ![20251217_103917.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTMnvDJN1S5hKayXhmtfqJy41YB1NSbz8tugTAgNy5Eg1/20251217_103917.jpg) ![20251217_103920.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXpbiWB7WTH8FCFSSQg7G8YDqqtwFpWHHeBFLSGWTe6df/20251217_103920.jpg) ![20251217_103925.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRq1m4cmWBgCdSdYe1fc8hTtGfNCNmUfdKYyr4SU8xbbn/20251217_103925.jpg) ![20251217_103934.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmduazMh16Bn3saQsxJcg4ats3CxAngpHkDFu6JaLbUCeZ/20251217_103934.jpg) ![20251217_103951.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noelyss/241tb7CX9DuDRwyRNACmxC2U39bxLW9s5ZC2gmi4Ci6cywK3ZQwzW8mwTD97Hby8ZAWQe.jpg) ![20251217_103937.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noelyss/23xAgVLRHYRbBTXFeF8RTJvMmH7gmYQJpqoNCT59tsm8kDnxTrxh3KdLvToJe8RdWD4Kr.jpg) ![20251217_104520.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noelyss/23vsUmNpDvfcfSdj6Frqcsd3nySbucEDYpstSPKTMnKbZkx3M1wA7dDhWZ1CZeeuNR7EX.jpg) --- En esta en esta área, la directora que nos permitió dar ese recorrido nos explicó varios elementos interesantes de la época en ese entonces plasmado, en unos cuadros, Maracaibo anteriormente tenía pocas carreteras, esta carretera representaban una única entrada y una única salida, es decir, por dónde entrabas tenían que salir pero a medida, que la ciudad se fue modernizando. Ciertamente esta infraestructura se fueron perdiendo modificando cada una de esas calles bien, en estos retratos fotográficos, podemos ver cómo vestían las personas de la época cabe destacar que la señora nos manifestó que aquellos jóvenes hasta los 16 años utilizaban el pantalón totalmente corto, haciendo referencia de que eran personas jóvenes cuando esto alcanzaban la mayoría de edad, utilizaban pantalón de vestir totalmente largo, cubriendo más allá de sus tobillos In this area, the director who gave us the tour explained several interesting aspects of the period, which were depicted in a series of paintings. Maracaibo used to have very few roads; this road was the only entrance and the only exit in other words, you had to leave the city the same way you entered it but as the city modernised, certainly, this infrastructure was gradually lost as each of those streets was altered in these photographs, we can see how people dressed at the time. It is worth noting that the lady told us that young people up to the age of 16 wore very short trousers, pointing out that once they reached the age of majority, they wore full-length trousers, covering well beyond their ankles. ![20251217_103719.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noelyss/23tveWQ1qy2YE5cVLnq3C7BbPCpxjsjRY5oTs4RcEZV9SL5nayHkGBqRz3E4NUG6VmPqy.jpg) ![20251217_103637.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noelyss/23uQpVW5rqqTfb5Yu9yzeviJjMsRAja16FSvFz4bJ7Lm1ysoVZjnnJxt1zzkRch3rKte7.jpg) --- También nos explicaron el área de la cocina y nos dijeron que en esta en este sitio en particular se grabó una de las partes de la película de Bolívar, ya que se adaptaba perfectamente a la época colonial que querían expresar en la cinta ahora bien, podemos ver que la cocina anteriormente eran elaboradas completamente en ladrillo y esta poseían una chimenea que iba directamente hacia los techos, a pesar de que esta cocina ha sufrido ciertas modificaciones en el tiempo o adaptaciones conserva cierta esencia de cómo eran las cocinas antiguas anteriormente en nuestra ciudad, podemos ver el emarcado de distintas formas de la puerta así como también la estatua, del Obispo Lasso. >They also showed us the kitchen area and told us that a scene from the film about Bolívar was shot at this particular location, as it perfectly suited the colonial era they wanted to portray in the film. Now, we can see that kitchens used to be built entirely of brick and featured a chimney that led directly up to the roof; although this kitchen has undergone certain modifications or adaptations over time, it retains a certain essence of what old kitchens in our city used to be like; we can see the distinctive archways of the doorway as well as the statue of Bishop Lasso. ![20251217_103224.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noelyss/23xedt7PziSk9pSWuq3Vq6ru99FMwwbAVdS2zEh4D57396Z8fCtyRNzw9nTvnnxSRWzZ7.jpg) ![20251217_104240.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noelyss/242DG4iEEceYTUd3JMA7EQMScFm8Mpaak9ZoK1g8TwL8dgBoiWAK5wQFuJpohW4gG1BVM.jpg) ![20251217_103220.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noelyss/23wMYDhQb18dgf8yG4EsVDeFE6kkuS8DpLy5qUZ5FS5H4jfGJ458zRR5HcnE9tULBMJqK.jpg) ![20251217_104218.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noelyss/23xozETXCoSr1AYSjd6iGQjiL2k3L1dpg78w1JHgn18BfDqC8W3Ad5Q4rJL6ojjgdvLru.jpg) ![20251217_104539.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noelyss/23t7mWDQDwLPXmbWLLzEutdgQFq382UPYUGAAUCmJXHum6AiR2ngE3fLQjGGRZF6ZANAp.jpg) ![20251217_103206.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noelyss/23wMWb96wVrb3KVcSj8tBwY1JGAAp9Gxz6EfKGBv9JWx6h3cMoqVnKLhFV2qH9m7WqevX.jpg) ![20251217_103210.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noelyss/23y96r1MdfG7Ev1t5uetv4JkV5HNFg97bJkgVUpPT9Nrs1UfxyGYDhjmBAeWZnnRgoAGj.jpg) --- Algunas se sus hermosas ventanas del lado de adentro se abren estas poseen unos puntos, que permiten abrirlas ya que estas ventanas son totalmente anchas y largas, estas ventanas también permiten el paso de la luz por lo que permiten también mayor iluminación del lugar, el paso del sol, en el lugar podemos ver a la virgen de la Inmaculada Concepción, en este lugar hay muchas imágenes de alta calidad en acabado español. >Some of the beautiful windows on the inside open; they have hinges that allow them to be opened, as these windows are very wide and tall. They also let in light, thereby brightening the space and allowing sunlight to enter. Inside, we can see the Virgin of the Immaculate Conception; the space features many high-quality images with a Spanish-style finish. ![20251217_104510.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noelyss/244xyuCZyFbJuGtpRvxgX1uXPxSuywFAFmTULaEu8cmkBMvsSw4LFGK3nJqLvrQcHzsva.jpg) ![20251217_104454.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noelyss/23uQkSMGWAKPFt8RLanppazTQYSXmmhRzoF3QsA5dvi5GFKUicVAFAvzQq11UyAq3zPpp.jpg) ![20251217_104506.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noelyss/23vhuAhASCJG5akkwzX4fEe81sNWPMBE2srqDTu1xj3UUmyZ1CmGG3yc6UJHMkrEijmTd.jpg) --- Por último podemos encontrar un lugar especial que permite el paso de la luz del sol, en donde también están las placas del lugar con su fecha de inauguración, esto le da un toque increíble al lugar y también de mucha claridad como también de cierta naturaleza es hermosso ver como este lugar conversa gran parte de nuestra esencia como marabino, como edificaciones de antaño, seguiré en otra publicación dando a conocer cada uno de los detalles. >Finally, there is a special spot where sunlight streams through, featuring plaques marking the date of its opening; this adds an incredible touch to the place, bringing plenty of light and a sense of nature. It is wonderful to see how this place captures so much of our essence as Marabinos, much like the buildings of yesteryear. I will continue in another post to share all the details. ![20251217_102614.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noelyss/23vi2Abbrw3Lrzw14f6DLwDfBHnn3fxifQEtSH6xiUbJm7q1WKuzxGssPQmjLEqLyYMXF.jpg) ![20251217_103108.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noelyss/23vsScZpqDQ1poUhCbk8RhDhLD6Jh2cAwNyHR3CmpLHd5jygND8cSpwx7aMzgbU8utZRU.jpg) ![20251217_103540.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noelyss/23vsQkW8nV6RqXuynK7TkVeziyhuPW7hN1MwT5RWkjUVb7GUAYD9whH5dUDEA4q9iqp1w.jpg) ![20251217_104404.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noelyss/23tbnc56oXDjKnb2hRqKfbMxFNGvutzx9KDnjhHLX9nwZDwNf1tVyKDnqwtiSQAZFHV1i.jpg) ![20251217_104653.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noelyss/23wCDwGg2hFRrygVHkWpSXsZ9rpGZYJiE8M9BPEuxwGUG3VKx1dDHQCsK4JhiqDcdSuXG.jpg) ![20251217_104356.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noelyss/23zGaZn4fekfpbAg7zRswjjfptdgAgJMbh5QPkfmcKL5hUyhKJYd2w1oEFdVCTkJShxFS.jpg) Me despido hasta una próxima, oportunidad mis queridos amigos viajeros hasta pronto. >I’ll say goodbye for now, my dear fellow travellers see you soon. ![20251217_103420.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noelyss/23wMeffeN4N8g5A6Y865G5LxQkL54okxb8cmACDLiFYEZRYhNZ776dXuBzYdfiAQu34Tr.jpg) [//]:# (!worldmappin 10.64296 lat -71.60700 long d3scr)

title: The Magic of Those Eyes: A Romantic Encounter
body:
Part-1
​It was the afternoon of Eid day. With mild sunshine and a gentle breeze, the atmosphere was perfectly romantic. At that time, three of us friends were sitting in a local shop, playing games. An auto-rickshaw came and stopped in front of the shop.
​I was still playing the game on my phone when a few people got down from the vehicle. Then, my eyes shifted from the phone screen toward the feet of those people. Among those pairs of feet, there was one particular pair that I couldn't take my eyes off. How can someone's feet be so beautiful? For the first time in life, a boy fell in love with someone's feet.
​Slowly, I began to raise my gaze upward. As soon as my eyes met hers, it felt like the shadow of dark clouds amidst the blue sky. I felt like I might die now, yet I couldn't look away. I can never explain to anyone just how magical those two eyes were.
​In the light breeze, her hair seemed to be playing with her eyes. Those eyes seemed to be staring right at me. A storm erupted inside my chest; for the first time in my life, I liked a girl so much that it felt like I could even give my life for her.
​I don't know who she is, where she lives, what her name is, what her lineage is, or what her religion is—I know nothing. Yet, I don't know why so much love awakened for her. Someone once said, \

Today, that became true; I too fell under the spell of a mysterious girl's enchanting eyes.
​While these thoughts were swirling inside me, the girl started walking slowly toward me. I don't know why, but my heart rate was increasing, yet I couldn't turn my gaze away. My eyes seemed to be locked onto hers. She kept coming forward...

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZHqQhkTNmB5NfaqTtrxS5nzNwUmmMkk7d2W5xuTuRe2f/1773998854436.png)
পার্ট-1 
ঈদের দিন বিকাল বেলা হালকা রোদ হালকা বাতাস একেবারে রোমান্টিক পরিবেশ,
তখন আমরা তিনজন বন্ধু মিলে আমাদের এলাকার এক দোকানে বসে গেম খেলছি  
দোকানের সামনে একটা অটো এসে থামলো 
তখনো আমি ফোনে গেম খেলছি তখন গাড়ি থেকে কয়েকজন নামলো ।
তখন আমার চোখটা ফোনের স্ক্রিন থেকে সরে 
সেই কয়েকজন লোকের পায়ের দিকে গেলো।

'পা' এত সুন্দর কী করে হতে পারে।
জীবনে প্রথম বার একটি ছেলে কারো 'পা ' এর 
প্রেমে পরলো ।
আমার চোখ  ধীরে ধীরে উপরের দিকে তুলতে লাগলাম তার চোখে চোখ পরতেই মনে হলো যেন 
নিল আকাশের মাঝে কালো মেঘের ছায়া। 
এবার মনে হয় মরেই যাবো তবু চোখ সরাতে পারবোনা।

হালকা বাতাসে তার চুল যেন চোখের সাথে খেলা করছে । চোখ দুটো যেন আমার দিকেই তাকিয়ে আছে । আমার বুকের ভেতরে তো টুফান ওঠে গেল, জীবনে প্রথম বার কোন মেয়েকে এত 
ভালো লাগলো যেন তার জন্য জীবনও দিতে

জানিনা সে কে, কোথায় থাকে, নাম কি, বংশ কি,

এসব কথা যখন আমার ভেতরে ঘুরপাক খাচ্ছে

¡Saludos, compañeros de ruta! Estoy de vuelta por estos lados en Liketu, ya que la otra herramienta me venía causando varios inconvenientes con la configuración; ojalá logre acostumbrarme rápido a este espacio. Este pasado fin de semana viví una verdadera “acción combinada” entre compromisos personales, obligaciones, distracción, entrenamiento y trabajo. En cuanto a lo deportivo, el entrenamiento no fue más allá de unos pocos kilómetros en la trotadora, adicionando luego unos minutos en la bicicleta estática, los cuales fueron excelentes para ejercitar las piernas, ya que no tuve oportunidad de salir a entrenar en la calle.
​Por otro lado, quería compartirles otro de mis momentos favoritos: disfrutar de una buena obra teatral o del espectáculo circense. Ante todo, me gusta apoyar a esos jóvenes emprendedores y talentosos que aman lo que hacen y lo ejecutan con excelencia. El riesgo se lo exige; son atletas, son gimnastas y profesionales que ejercen su labor con pasión, a pesar de ser un arte mayormente poco lucrativo. El sábado acudí a una función de circo en el bello Teatro Municipal, la “tacita de plata” del centro de Caracas; qué asombro ver lo bonito y elegante que está por dentro.
​La obra se tituló Rapsodia Circense, un espectáculo increíble de acrobacias, luces, drama, música de Queen y comedia. La entrada no fue costosa; más caros son los artistas reconocidos e igual se llenan las tribunas. Apoyemos lo nuestro y, a los que aman el circo sin animales como yo: ¡Feliz Día Internacional del Circo! Gracias a todos los que leyeron la publicación. Como es costumbre, aquí les regalo algunas fotografías de la jornada.
Traducido con Google traductor 

Greetings, fellow runners! I am back on this side of things in Liketu, as the other tool was causing me several configuration issues; I hope I can quickly get used to this space. This past weekend was a true \

of personal commitments, obligations, recreation, training, and work. Regarding sports, my workout didn't go beyond a few kilometers on the treadmill, followed by a few minutes on the stationary bike, which were excellent for exercising my legs since I didn't have the chance to go out and train on the streets.
On the other hand, I wanted to share another of my favorite moments: enjoying a good play or a circus performance. Above all, I like to support those young, talented entrepreneurs who love what they do and execute it with excellence. The risk demands it; they are athletes, gymnasts, and professionals who carry out their work with passion, despite it being a mostly unprofitable art form. On Saturday, I attended a circus performance at the beautiful Municipal Theater, the “tacita de plata” (silver cup) of downtown Caracas; I was so amazed to see how beautiful and elegant the structure is inside.
The show was titled Circus Rhapsody, an incredible spectacle of acrobatics, lights, drama, Queen's music, and comedy. The ticket was not expensive; famous artists are far more costly and the stands still fill up just the same. Let’s support our own, and to those who love the circus (without animals) like I do: Happy International Circus Day! Thank you to everyone who read the post. As is tradition, here are a few photographs of the day's journey.
Note: I kept the phrase \

in Spanish as it is a classic nickname for the theater, but included the literal translation so your English-speaking followers can appreciate the metaphor!
