json_metadata.title: Belleza desde mi ventana/ Beauty from My Window
json_metadata.body:
A veces pensamos que para disfrutar de una buena vista necesitamos paisajes perfectos o lugares extraordinarios pero hoy, desde la ventana de mi cuarto, encontré algo diferente.

No es la vista más bonita del mundo, hay paredes, techos y detalles simples del día a día. Sin embargo, el cielo se roba toda mi atención. Ese azul profundo acompañado de nubes que le da un toque especial a todo lo que lo rodea.

 Las plantas crecen sin pedir permiso, llenando el espacio de verde y frescura. En especial, la mata de plátano, que con el tiempo y paciencia nos regala nuevos racimos. Cada vez que aparece uno, no puedo evitar sentir una pequeña felicidad, como si la naturaleza me estuviera recordando lo generosa que puede ser.

Tal vez la vista no sea perfecta, pero tiene algo que muchas veces olvidamos valorar: autenticidad, vida y pequeños detalles que hacen el momento especial.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVBWRwHyPmmND9fRCP6hUQWyQBAnbfKkRPWMLymtPmhzX/1776716193771.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYDUQ75rdzuyXPFh5GjGTvCucc6tsRvcU2AZv3d9wH8mD/1776716194043.jpg)

-------
Sometimes we think that to enjoy a good view we need perfect landscapes or extraordinary places, but today, from my bedroom window, I found something different.

It’s not the most beautiful view in the world—there are walls, rooftops, and simple everyday details. However, the sky captures all my attention. That deep blue, accompanied by clouds, gives a special touch to everything around it.

Plants grow without asking for permission, filling the space with greenery and freshness. Especially the banana plant, which with time and patience gifts us new bunches. Every time one appears, I can’t help but feel a small sense of happiness, as if nature were reminding me how generous it can be.

Maybe the view isn’t perfect, but it has something we often forget to appreciate: authenticity, life, and small details that make the moment special.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVBWRwHyPmmND9fRCP6hUQWyQBAnbfKkRPWMLymtPmhzX/1776716193771.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYDUQ75rdzuyXPFh5GjGTvCucc6tsRvcU2AZv3d9wH8mD/1776716194043.jpg)

json_metadata.title: The Food I Never Ate at My Chilanga MuliloMy
json_metadata.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcX2NQATtkse8mwycfDZbwNS5Uf7h7jm3w6agcrame9XF/untitled_76_20_2_.jpg)

My Chilanga Mulilo was meant to be a celebration of food, culture, and family however, I ended up being the only one who didn’t eat. While everyone enjoyed the dishes prepared in my honor, I stepped out to go and meet my bride to be for a photo shot session, at her father’s place a 35 to 40 minutes drive from where my Chilanga Mulilo was hosted. I arrived at the place rushed to where the photo booth was setup; we started taking pictures with my fiancée (now my wife) smiling for the camera and completely unaware that my meal was slowly disappearing. 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeMGKvKz4eF1u6RaEnCnQouUSscQLieRkbiXG5qZ9WSEr/untitled_110_20_2_.jpg)

Chilanga Mulilo is a traditional pre-wedding ceremony practiced mainly among the Bemba people of Zambia. Though many other Zambian cultures now do it too. My wife and I are both Bemba’s so this ceremony was a must. The name (Chilanga Mulilo) literally means showing the fire. It’s a ceremony where the bride’s family demonstrates to the groom’s family how their daughter has been raised, particularly in terms of cooking skills, a variety of traditional dishes are prepared. The bride seldom prepares or presents food, and her family explains the meaning behind the dishes and customs.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPm7DebZHvUTmawmvJ427ap5LqQs6hJmZRaxkWMWS6XeE/untitled_104_20_3_.jpg)

The 9th of March 2026 was the day for my Chilanga Mulilo. I started the day with a lot of excitement and anxiety. I was anxious in the sense that the weather was not favorable because it was kind of rainy and cold in the morning. However everyone spoke highly of the dishes that were being prepared and the thought of it only made the wait more exciting. Though I hadn’t seen the food myself, I could already imagine the variety and effort behind it. The hour make was fast approaching my excitement had turned into real hunger, and I looked forward to finally testing the meal prepared in my honor.When the ceremony finally began the atmosphere quickly came alive the weather became bright. Guest arrived one after another, filling the space with laughter and celebration. As the groom, I was required to sit down and observe as the different dishes were presented and their meanings explained. Each meal carried a message about tradition, respect, and family values. Even though I tried to focus on everything being shared, I could not ignore the growing anticipation. I was eager for the moment I would finally get to taste the food that had been prepared in my respect. Just as I was about to settle down and finally taste the food, I was called to take pictures with my bride-to-be at her father’s place, which was about 35 to 40 minutes away from where I was being hosted. What I thought would be a quick trip turn into a long session of poses, adjustments and retakes. We moved from one spot to another, smiling and trying to capture every perfect moment. With the distance and time spent there, I completely lost track of everything, including the meal I had been eagerly waiting for. Meanwhile back at the ceremony, the celebration continued and so did the eating.By the time I returned, the celebration was still going but the food I had been looking forward to was gone. json_metadata.title: Love starts from within
json_metadata.body:
![F4099DE6-1FC9-4A52-BA29-20AA9DE132A1.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dwayne16/23yJCAP7mnqR625KtxuxE4zYGRpvt9qrahvingvJfEgxh5aiz7qtdophkUM2SwKWKxJVe.jpeg)
***

Before you love anyone else, be it your mother, friends, family or person your in a romantic relationship with, you must love yourself.

There is an irony in life that ceases to amaze me. We love others. We adore Influencers , celebrities, musicians, models. We look up to those who are in a higher sociable status than us. We gleefully observe those who seemingly have it all. The recognition and praise that others wish for. We love those who take care of us, those who keep us emotionally intact. But we don’t ever reflect on what love constitutes and how it must first start with ourselves.

Instead we bottle up our insecurities, eat ourselves away, tell ourselves all sought of things that scream pessimism. We tarnish our self esteem and kill our sense of belonging. We strive to meet up with the exaggerated expectations and self-proclaimed standards of today’s world. All to come to terms with the same unwavering disappointment. That we are not good enough. That we aren’t beautiful enough. There we aren’t academically sound or intelligent. That we lack talent, ambition and dreams that are far beyond attainable and in our reach.

The breaking reality is, is that we’ve streamed so far off into the unrealism of what we’re “expected” to be. With peer pressure on the rise, becoming a moving tyrant , turning our youths astray and making them prone to bad influence, habits and the likes it’s no surprise to say that our generation has been off to a bad start.

You need to love yourself. This isn’t some cliche anecdote on the negative side of not being an optimist or a rant-dump telling you why you need to feel good about yourself. It’s a progressive truth that isn’t typically revealed given today’s social atmosphere. Loving yourself isn’t for the sake of yourself per say. It holds the weight of your own self-worth, life perspective and overall judgement. If you do t love yourself you’ll find it hard to love someone who truly cares about you. You won’t believe what they say because if your insecurities. You won’t trust a word from the closest of friends because of your self doubt. You won’t see the world as it is as because your self- hatred and loathing. It’s a lot more to do with how it affects your external environment than your internal environment.

 Be kind to yourself and know your worth. Love starts from within.

json_metadata.title: The Things We Truly Value Never Stay Dirty
json_metadata.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmavhRK9FN4bvDZ2X6t4NwaYJZddfS2Mr5RKncPdJeo4GF/1776716286291.jpg)
https://shorturl.at/8Ilw2


I remember something from my childhood that still comes to my mind whenever I hear deep lines about life. In our village, people used to take great care of the things they truly loved. My father had a simple white shawl. It was not expensive, not something from a big brand, but he kept it very clean. He would fold it carefully after using it and keep it in a safe place. As a child I once asked him, “Why are you so careful with this old shawl?” He smiled and said something simple: “When something is dear to a person, they never let it become dirty.”
At that time I thought he was just talking about clothes. But as I grew older, I realized the meaning was much deeper. It was never really about the cloth.
In life, a person protects the things they truly value. When something has a place in someone’s heart, they try their best to keep it safe, clean, and respected. This does not only apply to objects. It applies to relationships, trust, respect, and even memories.
Sometimes we meet people who say many good words, but their actions show something different. If someone truly respects another person, their behavior will show it. They will not allow disrespect, neglect, or carelessness to damage that bond. Just like a favorite piece of clothing that someone keeps neat and clean, the relationships that matter most are handled with care.
I have seen this many times in everyday life. In villages, people may not have many things, but the few things they have are treated with love. A farmer may have only one pair of good shoes, but he keeps them safe because they matter to him. A mother may have an old cooking pot, but she washes it carefully every day because it is important in her life.
These small examples show a simple truth: what matters to a person is always protected.
The same principle works in human relationships. Respect, kindness, and honesty are like cleanliness for the heart. When a person truly values someone, they will protect their dignity and treat them with care. They will think before speaking, and they will avoid actions that could hurt or damage the connection.
But when something is not valued, it is often treated carelessly. It becomes easy to ignore, easy to disrespect, and easy to leave behind.
Life quietly teaches us these lessons through small moments. Sometimes a simple line, like the one in this post, carries a deep meaning. On the surface it talks about clothing, but in reality it speaks about value, respect, and responsibility.
In the end, the truth is very simple:
When something truly matters to a person, they protect it. They do not allow it to become “dirty” with disrespect or neglect.
And perhaps this line was never really about clothing at all. It was about the way a person chooses to value the people and things that are important in life.

json_metadata.title: Old Tyres - Waste management needs a big reconsider
json_metadata.body:
There are some products that are used heavily for one single time and then we don't have a facility to recycle them or they don't have a big value after that. Today I came across something like that. I had to change my car tyres. After 50k kilometres, looks like it is a good and safe practice to change tyres. Now I learnt a lot about all these things and I came to know that old tyres had no value in the market. Instead of leaving the tyre in the store itself, I brought it home. Every tyre costed about 70 dollars and I paid a total close to 300 dollars. 


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbsMpnxs22n25GrnqjxhTei2zQg4Jcx8oLRiV5dvhLbp8/1776715521941.webp)


Source - Sora

It was very sad to see that old tyres only go for scrap and nobody even busy old tyres. We pay close to 300 dollars for new tyres but the old tyres go for nothing. There are not enough attractive recycling options available with old tyres. That's when I was curious to read and understand about what happens to old tyres. Many countries dump then in a junkyard and there is no proper facility to recycle them. In some countries people make furniture out of old tyres and in some places people use old tyres in their garden. I also had a similar thought and that's why I also wanted to bring it home. Looks like it is very common that there is no facility to recycle old tyres. 

Some countries burn the old tyres to create tar from it and use the Tar for other purpose. Some people try to create cement from old tyres that can be used for constructing houses. Developing nations don't have any great solution yet for old tyres. The high chance is that it just goes as scrap and stays without destruction. The major reason why recycling is not a possibility for tyres is that it is a combination of materials that are not biodegradable. It makes it hard to dispose the tyres. Burning them can pollute the environment and people still do that. 

Hopefully some developed countries will come up with a facility to make use of old tyres properly and if that happens we should be able to handle that waste properly without polluting the environment. Let's hope for the best.

## <center>**<u>📣📢IMPORTANT ANNOUNCMENT📣📢</u>**</center>

We want to be fully transparent with our community, because you deserve honesty.
Since early this year, the WeAreAlive Tribe has been in the red on HIVE. We have been sending out significantly more than we receive, and sadly, our weekly HIVE income has dropped by more than 50%. For now, continuing with fixed rewards for all the activities is no longer something we can sustain.
So we are trying something new.
Going forward, rewards for the Monday activity will be based on post-earnings rather than fixed payouts. We know this is a change, and we know fixed rewards felt great, but this is what allows us to keep the challenge alive, keep the community going, and keep showing up for each other. We believe in this tribe, and we hope you do too.
Thank you for your understanding, your loyalty, and for being part of this. Let's keep thriving together. 💚

***A few important changes have been made to participation and rewards. Please review the rules and rewards sections of the post for complete details.***
# <center><u>**💚🌟PEACE BE UPON YOU ALL💚🌟**</u></center>

<center><u>**Welcome Back to @alive.chat Monday Challenge. Let’s share our goals, track our progress, and support each other.**</u></center>

<center>
![](https://media.tenor.com/Me82v-d-XDIAAAAC/welcome-back-wb.gif)
</center> 

I hope you are all doing great, healthy, and well. I’m happy to have you here and warmly welcome you all.

<center>
![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23swY1SiJNYXS5WrkQGHwUTqc8ovYW5dnPFQJstbWui91WWNjsSipwyPyZ5ZEqXFc6gRK.jpg)
</center>

You already know the purpose of this activity is simple: to share our goals, share our progress, and try to support each other in achieving them.

Everyone has goals, and the journey is not always easy. Here, we can motivate one another, learn from each other, and grow together. There is no pressure, just honest sharing, encouragement, and positive energy.

Feel free to share your goals, update your progress, and engage with others because when we support one another, success becomes more achievable for all.

<center>**<u>We are alive, we are growing, and we are moving forward together. 💪✨</u>**</center>

<center>![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tydynrain/23swY1SiJNYXS5WrkQGHwUTqc8ovYW5dnPFQJstbWui91WWNjsSipwyPyZ5ZEqXFc6gRK.jpg)</center>

# <center><u>**Challenge Task and Rules.**</u></center> 

<center>**<u>Kindly read the rules before participating in the challenge activity. You must follow all the rules mentioned below to be eligible for the Prizes.</u>**</center>

2. **<u>Sharing your weekly progress is an important part of this activity.</u>**
Please remember to include your progress along with your goals; without it, your entry won’t be eligible for the challenge.   
This requirement does not apply to first-time participants only.

3. <u>**Increased the time duration:**</u> This challenge will remain open for **<u>more than 48 hours, until Wednesday at 11:59 PM UTC</u>**.

4. We will post the participant list and the raffle results (if there are more than five participants) for last week’s challenge in the next post.

5. **<u>Using #alive tag is mandatory, addittionally you can use #aliveandthriving, and #AliveChat tags in your posts.</u>** 

6. Feel free to share your post and receive upvotes from the community.

7. **<u>It’s not mandatory, but we really appreciate it if you reblog the post and tag your friends in your posts and comments.</u>**

8. **<u>Engage with other participants and community members; don't forget the purpose of this activity is to encourage and support each other.</u>**

I had a meeting to attend, and my hair had grown too full. Wearing a wig wasn't even an option because of the unbearable heat lately, I needed something neat and stress free. So I stepped out to get a hair cut.

Immediately I stepped out, guess what? The sun greeted me, hmmmm, it was as if I'm stepping into an oven. I stated to look for a shield, I began scanning my surroundings, searching for any spot that could shield me from the sun.

json_metadata.title: Online Learning vs Offline Learning
json_metadata.body:
I hope that by the infinite grace of Allah, you are all doing well. Alhamdulillah, by the grace of Allah, the Creator, I am also doing well. I would like to discuss with you today online learning and offline learning and which one of them is more useful to our students and our society.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbrgWgCqRXZaWV3GZdX3LbzwNzuGPe5Rd2CviRhQpJapa/screenshot_2026_04_21_015805.png)
[Source](https://www.freepik.com/free-photo/student-online-cute-guy-checked-shirt-with-glasses-studying-computer-confused-writing_26220532.htm#fromView=search&page=1&position=12&uuid=786445be-7896-4d80-a4e0-0130559b7b71&query=Online+Learning+vs+Offline+Learning)

In essence, technology has developed significantly in the contemporary world. With this development of technology, online learning has gained popularity in our society. A lot of students are today completing their education in online activities. However, the question arises, whether online learning is superior to offline learning? Or is online learning still the optimal method to help a student in creating his future?

In essence, there are some merits of online learning. Online learning allows a student to study at the comfort of his home. There is no place he has to go. He is able to observe classes on his computer or smartphone. This is time and money saving to most families. Online learning can be a blessing to poor families especially those that live far apart and are unable to attend schools and colleges.

Nonetheless, there are numerous drawbacks of online learning too. The bottom line is that as a student spends several hours before a screen, his eyes become frail and his concentration is reduced. Besides, the internet has been used by most students not to study but to have fun. They watch movies and play games as opposed to studying. This is not at all true. A student should learn to use technology to study and not in case of entertainment.

On the other hand, offline learning is the traditional and most effective way of education. Once a student attends school on a daily basis and sits at the classroom, he gets to learn about discipline. He is taught to respect his teachers. He gets to know how to live in the society with his friends. Through online learning, one can never learn these things. Since in internet based learning a student sits on his or her own in their home and is not able to work on his or her social skills.

Essentially, a teacher can get to know the student in offline learning. In case a student fails to comprehend anything, the teacher could repeat it in person. But in online learning, this personal attention is very limited. And a student can never improve himself, without personal attention.

In addition, I have witnessed in a number of schools and colleges that students who go to school are far more successful in their performance as compared to those students who only study through the internet. Since attending school regularly develops a good habit of learning in a student.

So I think offline learning is much more important and beneficial than online learning. Online learning can be applied as the supplement tool but it cannot entirely substitute offline learning. In order to have a truly educated nation we must make sure that our children attend school on time.

And with that we must ensure that our children go to school day by day. We should not turn them into screen and phone addicts. Only in this case, we will be able to shape a beautiful and educated society in our future. I am very glad to see you here with the community of education.

json_metadata.title: 🌿✨ My Rosemary Plant – A Living Treasure Full of History and Healing ✨🌿
json_metadata.body:
></center>

Hello HiveGarden community! 🙌🌱

Today I want to share with you something that might look simple at first glance, but actually holds a lot of meaning in my daily life… my **rosemary plant** growing quietly in this corner of my home 🌞🏡

📸 In the photo, you can see how it stands close to the wall, receiving sunlight during the day and projecting those beautiful natural shadows 🌿✨. There’s something very calming about watching it grow slowly, adapting to its space without rushing.

Rosemary (_Rosmarinus officinalis_) is not just any plant. It’s a perennial aromatic shrub that comes from the rocky coasts of the Mediterranean and even parts of the Caucasus 🌍. Over time, it can grow quite tall—sometimes reaching up to 1.5 meters—with thin needle-like leaves and small flowers that may appear bluish, white, or even slightly pink 🌸

One of the things I enjoy the most is its **intense aroma** 🌬️. It has this unique blend of pine, camphor, nutmeg, and even a soft lavender note. Every time I touch the leaves, that scent stays on my hands and instantly makes me feel relaxed and refreshed 💆‍♂️🌿

In the kitchen 🍳, rosemary is incredibly powerful. It enhances flavors in a way that feels almost magical. It works beautifully with meats, light fish, vegetables, and traditional stews. Sometimes I imagine how many generations have used this same plant to give life to their meals 🍽️💚

What really amazes me are its **medicinal properties** 🌿💊. Rosemary has a strong connection with the digestive system. It helps stimulate the production of gastric juices, making digestion smoother and reducing discomfort like bloating, gas, and abdominal cramps. It also has a **carminative effect**, which helps reduce gas formation and improve overall digestive balance.

Additionally, it supports bile flow, which is important for proper digestion of fats. It also has **diuretic, anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and even antibacterial properties**. This makes it useful not only internally but also externally. For example, rosemary has been used to help with muscle pain, improve circulation, and even support skin healing 💪🌿

Some people use rosemary in different ways: as an infusion ☕, essential oil, or even in baths for relaxation and recovery. Personally, I like the idea of making a simple tea occasionally, especially after meals. It feels natural and comforting 💚

Of course, I always keep in mind that natural remedies should be used with awareness. Rosemary is powerful, and while it’s generally safe, it’s important not to overuse it and to respect proper guidance when needed ⚖️

Taking care of this plant has become a small ritual for me 💧☀️. I water it when the soil feels dry, make sure it gets enough sunlight, and just let it grow freely. No stress, no pressure—just nature doing its work 🌱

This rosemary plant reminds me that something so small can carry history, flavor, healing, and even emotion all at once 💫

Do you have rosemary or any medicinal plants at home? I’d love to hear your experience and how you use them 😊🌿

json_metadata.title: Television Review: Silver Spoon (Mazhor, Season 1, 2014)
json_metadata.body: ![(source:  tmdb.org)](https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/original/9CAZRRrdN4hcyNOozYlxI79tI7a.jpg)\n\nIn the golden age of television, given hyperproduction and until recently an unimaginably wide selection of content, it is increasingly difficult to find a police series that does not evoke a sort of \
. That does not mean the authors of the genre aren't trying. In that regard, lately few have gone as far as the creators of *Mazhor*, a Russian TV series whose title is best translated as \

. The series, which began in 2014 and whose initial plot in its idea is closer to parody or a Latin American telenovela, has managed to reach four seasons, three standalone feature films and South Korean remake *Flex X Cop*. That success has even reached Netflix, which has offered the series to an international audience under the English title \
.\n\nThe titular protagonist is Igor Vladimirovich Sokolovsky (Pavel Priluchny), a young member of Moscow's \

whose life revolves almost entirely around nightlife and who has absolutely no financial or other worries. However, his father, the influential oligarch Vladimir Yakovlevich Sokolovsky (Alexander Dyachenko), is increasingly dissatisfied with his son's lifestyle, and that dissatisfaction culminates when Igor, during a night-time race of furious cars, clashes with two policemen. The incident represents the last straw, and the father decides to teach his son a lesson, using a previously obtained law degree diploma. Igor is given an ultimatum – he must join the police and serve a year as a detective, otherwise he will be disinherited. Igor rather reluctantly agrees, and his suspicions that it might not be the best idea are confirmed when upon arriving at the station he discovers that his colleagues – Lieutenant Danila \

Oblasov (Alexander Oblasov) – are precisely the two policemen he had clashed with. A deep enmity immediately arises between them, which will be further fuelled by the fact that Korolyov is in a romantic relationship with Captain Viktoria \

Radionova (Karina Razumovskaya) and becomes pathologically jealous of the young man accustomed to solving all problems by reaching into his seemingly bottomless wallet. The investigative team, however, eventually does begin to do its proper work and Igor, over time, partly out of defiance, partly out of an effort to prove himself to his father, begins to turn into a more or less efficient policeman. His professional experience also prompts him to start investigating the death of his mother who, in the 1990s while he was a child, perished under suspicious circumstances linked to his father's shady dealings.\n\nScreenwriter Alexander Shcherbakov requires a considerable suspension of disbelief from the viewer, not only because there are rare cases in the real world where rich and influential fathers would try to discipline their profligate sons by shoving them into police offices. The amount of coincidence needed to create complications for the protagonist, which he tries to solve, usually with not the most impressive results, is such that the viewer will very quickly get the impression of watching an episode of a soap opera that the authors are trying to deliberately prolong with ever more bizarre subplots and new characters. That impression, admittedly, is partially offset by the narrative structure which combines individual criminal cases solved per episode with the main plot. That is also an opportunity for Shcherbakov to show some creativity in certain cases, creating one-off but in some instances quite memorable villains. The basic plot, however, develops in a way that seriously compromises the fundamental concept, turning the protagonist's father, who should be some kind of capable and cunning \

, into someone who neglected an important detail in the plan to discipline Igor. All this ultimately leads to a desperately melodramatic and rather predictable finale which, of course, comes in the form of an irritating cliffhanger.

That does not mean everything in *Silver Spoon* is bad. The direction by Konstantin Statsky skilfully overcomes budget limitations and creates a strong contrast between the world of the wealthy to which his protagonist belongs and the world of ordinary mortals like his colleagues. The acting is relatively good, even when it comes to thankless roles like that of the protagonist. Pavel Priluchny tries to give a convincing transformation from an arrogant spoiled brat to a more or less efficient policeman, although the screenwriter, who made his character largely unsympathetic, has created serious and often insurmountable obstacles in that regard. The same is true of Denis Shvedov as his rival, while Alexander Oblasov was unable to utilise the potential of his character, obviously conceived as a sort of comic relief. The only character viewers might truly sympathise with is Vika, but the performance of Karina Razumovskaya, who approaches it with deadly seriousness without almost ever smiling on screen, only emphasises the fundamental problem of *Silver Spoon*. The series had an original idea, but poor execution, or rather authors who were afraid that using humour would make the audience not take them seriously.

RATING: 4/10 (+)

*(Note: The text in the original Croatian version is available [here](https://draxblog.com/2020/04/02/recenzija-silver-spoon-%d0%bc%d0%b0%d0%b6%d0%be%d1%80-sezona-1-2014/).)*

#### <center>─── ❖ ── ✦ ── ❖ ───</center>  

 
 
# <center> ✦ ***The three magics*** ✦</center> 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaAke8qLu3FVxkXWoLGR2zL99NwG1kktyrfwREUesT9Pr/image_0wzyyov6z0l0fdkqukrs8.webp)


#### 📸https://raphael.app/es

Deep in the forest, where silences are shared with forgotten creatures, lived an old man. Wise, yet stubborn, and privy to secrets of bygone eras. The old man lit a candle with his fingertips, without tinder or rubbing. The flame danced in his weary eyes as the young apprentice sat at his feet, gazing wide-eyed as she had every evening since she could remember, yearning to one day master magic like her teacher.

\

he said, his voice echoing.

The girl nodded, though she had heard the story a hundred times. She knew this time would be different. The old man's hands trembled more than yesterday. And according to tradition, she would soon be the guardian of the forest, tasked with finding an apprentice to teach as she had been. The eternal cycle of guardians, an honor and a responsibility sometimes fraught with suffering.

\

Not simply naming things, but knowing the true name of all that exists. Whoever mastered this magic could whisper the secret name of fire and the fire would go out; could call the wind by its cradle name and the wind would cease to blow.

The old man took out an enormous book, one written by thousands of hands. In it were drawings of birds, animals, magical creatures, but also insects, leaves and flowers, simple rocks and rocks that shone. Alongside the drawings were all kinds of notes, all kinds of scribbles, all kinds of stories.

\
the old man said between sighs and sips of tea, while with a finger he pointed to his extensive and precise notes on how to make fire with light rocks.\n\n\
They say that when her time came, she simply said no, and death had to leave.\n\n\
the young woman asked, though she already knew the answer.\n\n\

The old man touched the earth, and the earth stirred barely, like a dog recognizing its master.

The second magic, he continued, was the magic of silence. In those times, the wise could hear what was left unsaid. A father didn't need to say, \
because his son heard love in the silence between words. Lovers didn't ask for forgiveness, because the silence after a fight already carried all the regret.\n\n\
the young woman asked, saddened by those words. She had never told the old man how much she respected and loved him.\n\n\

The candle flickered. Outside, the wind died down for a moment. A moment in which the forest became immense, infinite, and above all, unique.

The third magic, the most powerful, was the magic of memories. Whoever mastered it could walk through the memories of others as one strolls through a garden.

\

the young woman's voice was barely a whisper.

The old man smiled lovingly.

\

The old man stood with difficulty. He took a worn wooden chest and placed it in the young woman's hands.

\
she asked, though she already knew the answer.\n\n\

That night, the old man slept and didn't wake. The young woman opened the chest. Inside were a compass, a small ocarina, and an old pen stained with ink. She touched them one by one, and then she knew.

A small note confirmed what she had imagined:

\
\n\nThe young woman wept silently as she tidied the house, which was now hers. In the silence, she heard the old man's voice say: I love you, one last time.\
Magnol, like my teacher, unique plants grow in that stream.\

body.title: Pescando olas en el malecón, un ejercicio de paciencia/Fishing for Waves on the Malecón: An Exercise in Patience (Esp-Eng) \n
body.body:
> Hola, mis amigos. Que placer volver a saludarlos este lunes. Feliz semana para todos. Un nuevo día amanece en La Habana y el oleaje en el malecón simula estrellitas plateadas en el agua. A lo lejos, veo un barco guarda costas. El malecón habanero no es solo un muro de ocho kilómetros que desafía al estrecho de Florida. Aquí siempre voy a volver porque es mi sitio de meditación, es el sitio donde la ciudad se asoma al mar con la melancolía de quien sabe que el horizonte es un espejismo. Allí, al mediodía, cuando el sol se derrite sobre las losetas irregulares por la sal y el tiempo, cuando el mar no tiene ganas de estar en calma, ocurre un espectáculo único, las olas saltan y bailan para traspasar el muro. >Hello, my friends. What a pleasure to greet you again this Monday. Happy week to everyone. > >A new day dawns in Havana, and the waves on the Malecón mimic little silver stars in the water. In the distance, I see a coast guard boat. The Havana Malecón is not just an eight-kilometer wall defying the Florida Strait. I will always return here because it's my meditation spot, the place where the city peers out to sea with the melancholy of one who knows the horizon is a mirage. There, at midday, when the sun melts over the irregular flagstones worn by salt and time, when the sea has no desire to be calm, a unique spectacle unfolds: the waves leap and dance to cross over the wall.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmX6KuhqWx25Fn3M1Bbn91K3ToQgHfMK12Mi5izAn9sciD/1776714309768.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPmT4mEzxv5j8aYarpWMGVDzDM6ey14rdmpHSt8xQGEdH/1776714327876.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNhsTfNa9hckrZRj3eMWDauj4zhxhEzqYdWopfU8nGFKg/1776714327916.jpg)

> El Malecón tiene un ritmo propio, y hoy decidí seguirle el compás. Vine caminando sin prisa, con el sol cayéndome sobre los hombros y el salitre pegándose en mi piel. Pero no era solo un paseo, traía una misión entre manos. Sacar el móvil y capturar el momento exacto en que una ola rompe contra el muro, salta por encima y se estrella en la acera, a veces hasta la calle. >The Malecón has its own rhythm, and today I decided to follow its beat. I came walking unhurriedly, the sun falling on my shoulders and the sea salt sticking to my skin. But it wasn't just a stroll—I had a mission in hand. To take out my phone and capture the exact moment a wave breaks against the wall, jumps over, and crashes onto the sidewalk, sometimes even into the street.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUMMXyaBmH5RAYku5h5mreDkoADrMxXTWC8yiqyeb15ES/1776714398298.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYoxLFk6DFHuhYL7NLPBzSSMSyArucji57qJpdv8H5c73/1776714398474.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmR8DzPbbfu9K4LpHM5smVhx557eRYaQSV3MMm8Fau2k3c/1776714398631.jpg)

>





Pescar olas parece sencillo, pero no lo es. Requiere de tiempo y paciencia. Me paré en la acera de enfrente, porque no me quería mojar y apunté. La primera ola llegó imponente, blanca de espuma, pero mi dedo tembló y solo capturé un borrón azul. La segunda la preví demasiado pronto, el agua cayó pesada un segundo después de que yo ya había bajado el teléfono. Suspiré. Un  hombre al lado me miró con media sonrisa: “Hay que tener paciencia, muchacha”, me dijo.

>Fishing for waves seems simple, but it's not. It takes time and patience. I stopped on the opposite sidewalk because I didn't want to get wet, and I aimed. The first wave arrived, imposing, white with foam, but my finger trembled and I only captured a blue blur. The second I anticipated too soon; the water fell heavily a second after I had already lowered the phone. I sighed. A man next to me looked at me with a half-smile: \

> Cada ola es única. No viene cuando tú quieres, sino cuando la marea lo decide. Al principio, me desesperaba. Veía venir una grande, enfocaba, y… nada. Solo salpicaduras tímidas. Otras veces, cuando ya había bajado la guardia para revisar el encuadre, el mar me lanzaba un puñetazo de agua que salpicaba la cámara y me obligaba a limpiar la lente con el dobladillo de mi blusa. >Each wave is unique. It doesn't come when you want it to, but when the tide decides. At first, I got desperate. I'd see a big one coming, focus, and… nothing. Just timid splashes. Other times, when I'd let my guard down to check the framing, the sea would throw a punch of water at me, splashing the camera and forcing me to clean the lens with the hem of my blouse.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaXd57Jbx8aePRqAm5j5jCDHGDYBrv1ZPGUroPJJrKBcs/1776714542596.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeULNoT6o2C4t9ViBVLzQoSTfWbi1psLtygmmx3nq87p3/1776714542777.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbHN7MvZo9hbAazukgJrQy5bm92PnJzGpoLJ9UDcWTdkw/1776714542929.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWs5jiiUiHsAS31Mt8utk2X2nCz77zUxZ8m4d5d19qkAJ/1776714543073.jpg)

> Poco a poco fui encontrando el ritmo. Dejé de pelear contra el tiempo y empecé a observar. Noté cómo el viento precede a la ola más brava, cómo la espuma brilla justo antes de estallar. Aprendí a no disparar a la primera señal, sino a esperar ese instante de tensión máxima, cuando el agua se encrespa, se levanta y se lanza. La paciencia, descubrí, no es pasiva. Es estar alerta, con el dedo en el disparador, los ojos fijos, la respiración contenida. Es creer que la ola perfecta llegará, aunque las anteriores hayan fallado. >Little by little, I found the rhythm. I stopped fighting against time and started observing. I noticed how the wind precedes the fiercest wave, how the foam glitters just before it bursts. I learned not to shoot at the first sign, but to wait for that instant of maximum tension, when the water ruffles, rises, and launches itself. Patience, I discovered, is not passive. It's being alert, finger on the shutter, eyes fixed, breath held. It's believing that the perfect wave will come, even if the previous ones have failed.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRyLbJTGhyFT1c7wz7vPgahBGy9fBhGkum2ntSXasMJUo/1776714594590.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmX1exFVGDyBJ4cGyaz7krXtGQwqh3fteuaoUEfpSsmk21/1776714594672.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXWTZTQVH5rhrcbhsf5KcK7doWhDuEZ8AcV6NxeXAkVkZ/1776714594769.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbjaQpwSbkVsWQ2YxTqrbTVRAnvzRoiNd4mKozXprMz5v/1776714594926.jpg)

> Cuando por fin la atrapé, la ola justa, la que se alzó dos metros, besó el cielo y cayó con estruendo sobre la acera, regando hasta los coches, solté el aire que no sabía que tenía guardado. No era la foto más nítida del mundo, pero era mía, ganada a pulso. >When I finally caught it—the right wave, the one that rose two meters, kissed the sky, and crashed thunderously onto the sidewalk, spraying even the cars—I released the air I didn't know I'd been holding. It wasn't the sharpest photo in the world, but it was mine, hard-earned.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRC1UgzD6nbm29Cy5Cu1bveYivApapWmQo4JtkGJFFEU5/1776714626700.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmczt5M4m9x6nE2srzSDrFWQcVduA5yZk1qAjxLfKN3jBt/1776714626743.jpg)

> Seguí caminando, con el teléfono caliente entre las manos y la ropa salpicada. El Malecón seguía ahí, imparable. Y yo, más lenta, más atenta, agradecida de que el mar me hubiera recordado que algunas cosas bellas solo se alcanzan cuando uno aprende a esperarlas. Pescar olas en el malecón es un arte que no necesita carnada. Consiste en observar cómo el mar Caribe empuja su lengua salada contra el dique, cómo las olas se encrespan, se levantan un instante y se estrellan en un estallido blanco que moja a los transeúntes despistados. >I kept walking, the phone warm in my hands, my clothes splattered. The Malecón was still there, unstoppable. And me, slower, more attentive, grateful that the sea had reminded me that some beautiful things are only attained when you learn to wait for them. Fishing for waves on the Malecón is an art that needs no bait. It consists of observing how the Caribbean Sea pushes its salty tongue against the seawall, how the waves ripple, rise for an instant, and crash in a white burst that wets unsuspecting passersby.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQx7RYCs89kmvjFQ47SpVd3RgeG2FaF3ojcuEBt18VE9i/1776714688108.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZeXTEGqEUvviFf2J2jcEeGwnAmH3TsU5KfoBQJvVMTuU/1776714688282.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeUdiiBnyYpdkqdrYwcywneXao6BFqDtzWkkU4CCKzCDs/1776714688363.jpg)

> Como soy media poeta, pienso que cada ola es un verso, cada rompiente un estribillo. Creo además que pescar olas es una metáfora de la vida en esta isla. Se espera algo que nunca llega o al menos no se sabe cuando va a llegar, se sueña con lo que está más allá del muro, pero al final se aprende a disfrutar del golpe de agua en la cara. Hoy tengo la certeza de que, mientras el mar siga golpeando, La Habana seguirá viva. Porque pescar olas es, al fin y al cabo, una forma más hermosa de no sentirse solo frente al infinito. >Since I'm something of a poet, I think each wave is a verse, each breaker a chorus. I also believe that fishing for waves is a metaphor for life on this island. You wait for something that never arrives—or at least you never know when it will—you dream of what lies beyond the wall, but in the end, you learn to enjoy the splash of water in your face. Today I am certain that as long as the sea keeps pounding, Havana will stay alive. Because fishing for waves is, after all, one more beautiful way not to feel alone before the infinite.

body.title: Butcher, Baker, Candle Maker
body.body: >\n\nWhile Smallsteps was eating her night snack, she asked me what I found interesting, with the ulterior motive of asking a question she has been pondering, which is *how people have evolved from being primitive to what we are today.* We talked a bit about nature and nurture (with the latter being a new term for her) and intelligence and the general \

concept that affects our development. We also talked about survival of the fittest and how it isn't just the healthiest or strongest, but also the wisest that have the best chance of survival and of course, procreation. --- ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tarazkp/2458bBDUYCt5zcMS7b5yucrkYkJqKAHQFmWtLJZANJzuxJjZKVEJ2XtFgFhkVNsyRw4X9.png) --- But it was interesting as we were discussing the shift from tribal communities that provided for each other to farming, and no longer having to rely on each other Smallsteps found that sad. But as I started talking about swapping goods and the trouble with things not being one-for-one in value, she quickly realised that this is where money came in to play a part, and although we didn't go down that road today, it is another point of *sadness* for what humanity has done with it. What we did discuss was how once we settled down, the traditional tribal roles started to evolve, but more than that, *job roles* exploded in number and type. A tribe always on the move had hunters, gatherers, makers, shaman, etc. But a farm starts to specialise, and then there are specialised farms that require specialised skills, and then there are the markets of trade and sellers and buyers, and the many specialised services and the list just kept on growing. Perhaps the reason that we have been able to advance so rapidly as a species, is not because we are necessarily smarter, but because we are able to put the intelligence we have into specialised roles that complement and compound against each other. And while this has created many issues, it has also been pretty great, because it means that a massive range of skill could be leveraged and people were not automatically thrown into a very narrow set of options. Musicians and artists became careers, rather than hobbies. But I was thinking on this and was wondering what happens now with automation taking over, because we are going to lose the majority of roles that have been created and even the creative ones, like music and art are being replaced by AI generated versions. For a time there might be some new types of roles created, but for how long before human interaction is again obsolete in those? And this goes back to my [previous](https://peakd.com/hive-126152/@tarazkp/distributed-dumpsters) (and many others) article about meaning from activity and how once we become irrelevant, we tend to spiral. Forget about the economic implications of the economy fundamentally failing as it stands, because we need to think about how we are to survive as a species when nothing we do really matters to anyone else, and maybe not even to ourselves. This world is too small and resources to few for it all just to be a playground for our whims, and even if it wasn't, I do not believe we would adjust well as individuals or society. Like how my daughter found it sad that people no longer need to rely on each other like in tribal times, we are entering into a phase where we will be reliant on machines to keep everything going, from the back office to the front, from the first action of the supply chain to the last - it will become more and more automated and we will have no choice but to accept terms, because we as individuals can no longer fill any of the roles. And collectively, we will be even more useless. It seems to me that this technological drive has fractured the very conditions that have kept us evolving as a species. And while the technology created in the future will keep advancing, that no longer means that we as a species are advancing it. Instead, we become a beta species, unable to support or direct itself, continually degrading until our value is the same as soil. There are a lot of jobs that most people don't want to do, but what happens when there are no jobs anyone can do? And the problems will occur well before the final human job disappears, because the economic world we have created and the conditions we value and rely upon, are not built to withstand the pressure of even a quarter of the global population to be completely unproductive, let alone a half or more. Maybe the evolution of the human species is a circle, where we have gone from primitive to advanced, but once we become too advanced, we slide back to our primal roots. I suspect the back nine will play much faster than the front. body.body:
It is interesting to think of our ultimate past and future. Where did we come from and where are we headed.

I have my thoughts, which are held based on my current understanding and which I will change as new info comes in. I am always open to new ideas, even if, or especially if, they differ from mine. That's how I learn, and not simply confirm my existing biases.

## The Past

I think the universe has always been here, and no god created it. If one posits a creator god, where did this entity come from? If it was always there, then the universe could also have always been there.

I think the stuff in the universe acts upon itself according to patterns that we have come to discover and name things like physics and chemistry. Eventually physics and chemistry resulted in things that could self-replicate and then biology was born. Self-replicating biology is not exact replication so there is variety. Some of that variety does better in the environment it is in and becomes dominant in the competition for resources.

The biological entities develop information processing because those that do are better able to thrive in their environment. The information processing system becomes able to collect information about the fact that it is processing information and so becomes self aware, and so we have consciousness.

We also become aware of the fact that there are other information processing beings out there, some who want to cooperate with us and some who want to eat us.  The part of our brain that detects these other information processing agents becomes hyper vigilant over time because those that hear a rustling in the grass and do not notice become lunch for the lion. We're left with creatures that have a lot of false positives because we're quick to attribute agency where it may not be, but at least we avoid the true negatives and we live.

As these beings communicate, they realize they have similar things to talk about, and stories to answer questions arise. We think agents are behind everything - wind, lightning, thunder, heavenly objects, floods, etc.  These supernatural agents are worshiped to appease them so their abilities don't harm us. Finally a few thousand years ago, some people think it is just one Agent, not multiple ones. And we have God.

## The Future

I do see us changing into something we probably can't quite imagine now.

In the short term we'll still have individual people but they will be enhanced even further by tech. Maybe even becoming cyborg or fully robotic.  

I think robots will be able to grow and change and repair themselves and self-replicate. I think this happens by having the robots made of tiny cube shaped robots.  These cube bots can have computing ability as well as the ability to move. Each cute bot has the plan for the entire robot in its memory as well as its position in the robot, so it knows which of its 6 faces needs to be attached to its neighbor and which don't, in order for structural integrity and weight bearing.

There can be pathways in the robot that allows for the passage of the cube bots. If a cube bot fails, it marks itself as failed and moves to the passage for elimination. New unattached cube bots are also in the passage and the closest one will head to where the failed cube bot was, to replace it. Hence self-repair.

Any of the cube bots can be tasked with making a new copy of the robot.  It might make its way to an internal or external pool of unattached cube bots and grow into an exact copy of the robot by attaching new cube bots to the growing structure, telling each new cube bot the plan and its position in the plan so it knows which of its 6 faces need to bind with another cube bot.  Hence self-reproduction.

Growth and change of robot structure is simply broadcasting the new body plan to all the cube bots who then seek free cute bots to bind with according to the new plan.

This can all be done in the near future because it is becoming easier and easier to create smaller and smaller computers and actuators that will make up the cube bots. At first we'll have robots looking like Roblox, all jaggedy, just like early computer displays we jagged, and for the same reason - pixel (or voxel in the case of 3D cube bots) size starts off large and then keeps shrinking.  Regarding pixels, no one these days even realizes the screens they look at are just a matrix of very tiny individual elements.  Once we can make cube bots sufficiently small, the robots they form will look smooth.

Back to the idea of doing this in the near future - the fact that the cube bots are all identical will facilitate this. Mass production of just one thing is faster than making lots of individual things. The cube bots are all identical but their function will differ depending on what the plan calls for, for each cube bot to be.

I don't see people or anything becoming energy without matter. I'm not sure what that even means. I think energy depends on there being matter. I think energy without matter to contain it and do things for it will just expand and dissipate. 

But who knows!  We'll have to wait and see!

Thanks for the great article which got me thinking of the things I wrote about here.

Have a great week ahead!

body.title: Online or Physical, Bullying Should Not Be Tolerated
body.body: > In recent times, I've tried to make a comparative analysis of things with regard to physical and online, trying to ascertain or understand the level of impacts, challenges, benefits and more that come from both ends while exploring several matters and subjects of concern. Since the advent of the online world, where virtually everything has leaned towards, unlike the era when all was done physically and online wasn't even a thing. Talk of financial transactions, business, health care, entertainment, meetings, communication, work, learning and so on. However, if there's one thing I've come to realise about the wonderful and advantageous online space is that it brings a great amount of negative effects as much as the positive. It's like, there's a corresponding negative effect to every good thing the online world offers. We see scams, crimes, lies, deceits, infidelity and several other negative effects. These are all human actions by the way. For the sake of this prompt, one of such is the advent of online bullying, born from the online world which has affected many as much as the physical actions. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZT5bySHMBSpUMzdPrTj3QeEhooaKQd465vynN7FtBiZB/photo_1600433805982_4ceb4ccdcb26.jpeg) [Image Source.](https://unsplash.com/photos/white-and-red-car-illustration-GUQb38zj2_I) Online bullying against physical bullying, which is worse? I won't mince words while saying both shouldn't be tolerated in any way. But let's look at some of the reasons why both are unwelcome and should be treated likewise. Physical bullying, of course involves physical actions like slapping, poking, or even beating an individual. The point of concern about this is the abuse and its effect on the body, physically. Not far from the name. It could leave a person with bruises, wounds, injuries or even a permanent body disorder or deformity. It's a very disturbing act that should never have a place in society. It tends to take away one's self-esteem, confidence and focus in life. Not to forget the physical pain one would have to endure. On the other hand, online bullying as the name implies happens in the online world, where keyboards and words do the bullying. This is more of a psychological and mental effect. The physical body doesn't suffer in this case, but the mental aspect of a person suffers. Such kind of bullying could lead to depression, trauma, psychological illness and so on. I feel like this is actually not talked about much enough. The victims of such mostly suffer “behind the scenes” with little support to get over it. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfCw6mm2GDgUiqv2ajgzHePVNmM5SYKgWsAXoRDeFERyo/photo_1649389966541_12af5cb7efa0.jpeg) [Image Source.](https://unsplash.com/photos/a-red-sign-that-says-no-to-bullying-XUdthBA01CM) Looking at it and understanding the effects involved when a thing becomes psychological and mental, I feel moved to say that it's worse when bullying emanates from online. Yet, I also consider that victims of physical bullying aren't really free from mental effects, especially when it's a continuous action. Such can even lead to a person's demise. Well, both forms of bullying can lead to that, which is why I say let none be tolerated and both should be treated with grave consequences on the perpetrators－the bullies. --- ###### Thank you for body.title: Carved With Love… Just Like the Future We Dream For Our Children
body.body: /> At first, it looks like simple curves in stone. Soft. Gentle. Flowing. But when you look closer… you begin to feel something deeper. Care. Connection. Love. These sculptures were shaped by skilled hands — patiently, intentionally, with vision. Each curve did not happen by accident.

/> It was guided. Formed. Given purpose. As I stood there looking at them, I thought about our children. Children, too, need shaping. Not with tools… But with love. With care. With a safe place to grow.

/> In our school, we see this every day. Young lives full of potential. Bright minds waiting for opportunity. Hearts that only need stability to flourish. But love alone is not always enough. Love needs space to grow.
/> Some of these children walk long distances. Some return to uncertain homes. Some carry burdens beyond their age. And yet, just like these stones… They are still becoming something beautiful.

/> This is why we dream of building a dormitory. Not just walls and a roof… But a place of care. A place of rest. A place where love can take shape in a child’s life. Because when a child is given safety… Given support… Given love… They do not just survive. They grow. They shine. They become. Just like these curves in stone… Carefully shaped…

/>

With purpose…  
And with love.  
If this speaks to your heart, I invite you to walk this journey with us.  
Because sometimes…  
The greatest thing we can build…  
Is a place where love can live.

#art #love #charity #education #hope #life #africa

body.title: secreto de un buen sofrito: Mi receta paso a paso de Arroz con Pollo / The Secret of a Great Sauté: My Step-by-Step Chicken and Rice Recipe
body.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYooC7UGzd5UUYNUJhNEchG7vLc6xQ6rMUsUbMXNy41yv/1776712581021.jpg)


🥘 __________________________________ 🥘

(Español)

Hoy se cocina un clásico que nunca falla!  No hay nada como el aroma de un buen Arroz con Pollo casero preparándose en la cocina. Ingredientes frescos, mucho color y ese sazón que nos transporta a casa. ¿Cuál es tu truco secreto para que quede perfecto? 

Ingredientes:

Pollo: Pechuga (la de la foto) cortada en cubos.
Vegetales: 1 cebolla, 1 zanahoria, ajíes dulces (verdes y rojos), ajo y 1 trozo de puerro.
Hierbas: Hojas de culantro (recado) fresco.
Base: Arroz blanco (2 tazas), aceite de soya, y condimento en polvo (onoto/achiote para el color).
Líquido: 4 tazas de agua o caldo de pollo.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRRNdmYnEZ7o3c1G3TZC6Ht5iGZhyp3JK9TiZhg6FjPQv/1776713074452.jpg)

Instrucciones:

Sellar: Calienta el aceite y dora los cubos de pollo con un poco de sal y el condimento de color. Retira y reserva.

Sofrito: En la misma olla, sofríe la cebolla, el ajo, los ajíes, el puerro y la zanahoria picaditos hasta que estén suaves.

Arroz: Agrega el arroz y mezcla bien para que absorba los sabores.
Cocción: Regresa el pollo a la olla, añade el agua y las hojas de culantro enteras (para retirar después) o picaditas.
Finalizar: Cocina a fuego alto hasta que el agua evapore, luego tapa, baja el fuego al mínimo y cocina por 15-20 minutos.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmR2SBPkzq6oB94vB8oCfP1n69CCnjsG97HcBhoy4GyCbR/1776713382604.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmc3mEeUJ8tYwrXN5yND1zeqBdP9JNaMh7KtCtGbuUuNnd/1776713382893.jpg)


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbVf6Z5d3dNYHMA7WRPxWpeeTWpEzXdSyZXNCD4Pgc3BX/1776713515553.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeAWy42ivuQSRkdYJrfQDh7aNAcaHjNReHZFDR2wFFcP1/1776713515809.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUr4nXEDG1CUEfM8FoRbReReziNzExp73spXqDb4LFwhC/1776713515999.jpg)


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbFccEv7EjpFeHVxtLoa84cJjEkNzJehTbqiQvvzDxbHX/1776713583037.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYbYf25KHi4i2TjRFvCE4vAcYdW7vinxWofhWtdCsNEhA/1776713583255.jpg)

Este tipo de arroz es la opción ideal para un almuerzo completo o para compartir en familia. Es un plato que rinde muchísimo y que siempre evoca esos momentos especiales alrededor de la mesa con nuestros seres queridos. ¡No hay nada como un buen plato de arroz con pollo para alegrar el día!

​\

> (Photos by me, captured in my kitchen while preparing this special family lunch.)

​🥘 __________________________________ 🥘

(English)

Nothing beats a classic!  Today is all about that homemade Chicken and Rice (Arroz con Pollo) vibe. Fresh ingredients, vibrant colors, and that authentic flavor that feels like a warm hug. What’s your secret ingredient for the perfect rice?

Ingredientes:

Chicken: Breast (as shown) cut into cubes.
Vegetables: 1 onion, 1 carrot, sweet peppers (green and red), garlic, and a piece of leek.
Herbs: Fresh culantro (recao) leaves.
Base: White rice (2 cups), soybean oil, and seasoning powder (achiote/annatto for color).
Liquid: 4 cups of water or chicken broth.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRRNdmYnEZ7o3c1G3TZC6Ht5iGZhyp3JK9TiZhg6FjPQv/1776713244957.jpg)

Instructions:

Sear: Heat the oil and brown the chicken cubes with a pinch of salt and the coloring seasoning. Remove and set aside.

Sauté: In the same pot, sauté the finely chopped onion, garlic, peppers, leek, and carrot until soft.
Rice: Add the rice and stir well to coat it with the oils and flavors.

Simmer: Return the chicken to the pot, add water and the culantro leaves (whole to remove later, or chopped).

Finish: Cook over high heat until the water evaporates. Then, cover, reduce heat to low, and cook for 15-20 minutes


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmR2SBPkzq6oB94vB8oCfP1n69CCnjsG97HcBhoy4GyCbR/1776713410704.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmc3mEeUJ8tYwrXN5yND1zeqBdP9JNaMh7KtCtGbuUuNnd/1776713410952.jpg)


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbVf6Z5d3dNYHMA7WRPxWpeeTWpEzXdSyZXNCD4Pgc3BX/1776713478222.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeAWy42ivuQSRkdYJrfQDh7aNAcaHjNReHZFDR2wFFcP1/1776713478475.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUr4nXEDG1CUEfM8FoRbReReziNzExp73spXqDb4LFwhC/1776713478647.jpg)


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbFccEv7EjpFeHVxtLoa84cJjEkNzJehTbqiQvvzDxbHX/1776713560471.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYbYf25KHi4i2TjRFvCE4vAcYdW7vinxWofhWtdCsNEhA/1776713560731.jpg)

This type of rice is ideal for a complete lunch or for sharing with the family. It’s a hearty dish that goes a long way and always brings back memories of those special moments gathered around the table with loved ones. There’s nothing like a delicious plate of chicken and rice to brighten up the day!

\
> (Photos by me, captured in my kitchen while preparing this special family lunch.)

body.title: Entrada al Concurso \
| Lugares del Imperio Saturnino
body.body: <center>\n\n**Nota de la autora**: ¡Hola y bonito día a todos! Espero que se encuentren bien. El día de hoy les comparto mi participación al concurso *El tesoro de las palabras*, organizado por el equipo de @es-literatos . El tema que escogí fue \

, pero pensando no en las ciudades reales, sino en las ciudades imaginarias, las de los sueños, las de la imaginación. Me pareció una oportunidad perfecta para elaborar un pequeño diccionario de los lugares en donde se desarrollarán en un futuro algunas escenas de *Una terrícola en Titán*, la cual publico de vez en cuando en este espacio.

Si alguien gusta participar, pueden hacer [click aquí](https://peakd.com/hive-179291/@es-literatos/segundo-llamado-concurso-literario-el-tesoro-de-palabras) para participar. ¡Saludos y que tengan un bonito día!

![Hive Banners 2026 (50).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/vickaboleyn/48Qv2MAVRdAGfn67ZC9ZEAPSBRuDp2vR2K89WGNEFkuAp8uM782Py5aXJ3DBRhsLCz.png) **Banner elaborado con Canva**.
>\n\n* **Cara Cassiopea**. Ciudad capital de Plutón, conocida con el epíteto de \

por su puentes dorados que se extendían de un extremo a otro a lo largo de los pequeños islotes que conformaban la capital. Fue la última ciudad en caer ante el Imperio Saturnino a principios del reinado del emperador Ergane VII.

* **Convento de las Nornas**. Un convento ubicado en los confines del último anillo de Saturno. A diferencia de los conventos prisión, este lugar es refugio de aquellas mujeres que huyen de los matrimonios forzados.

* **Cronia**. Ciudad capital de Saturno. Centro político del Imperio, dividido en tres sectores: La Periferia, el Distrito Comercial y el Distrito Imperial.

* **Distrito Comercial**. Centro económico de la ciudad, y quizás de todo el imperio. En él se concentran tres grandes barrios: El Barrio de los Artesanos, el Barrio de los Joyeros y el Barrio de los Textiles.

* **Distrito Imperial**. Centro administrativo de Cronia y del imperio. En él se encuentran el Barrio Aristocrático, el Barrio de los Juristas y Administrativos, así como el Palacio Imperial.

* **El Agujero**. Mercado de esclavos, ubicado a doce kilómetros de Cronia.

* **Helospontos**. Puerto y capital de Neptuno, considerado el centro artístico más importante del Imperio Saturnino. También es conocida como \

debido a la amplia variedad de minaretes que se encuentran en cada templo dedicado a la Gran Madre.

* **Icsos**. Villa de Titán, capital de la tribu Meeka. Centro político, religioso y económico desde el cual gobierna la diarquía conformada por el Jefe Máximo y el Shaman Mayor. Se encuentra cerca del desierto titanio de Terssos.

* **Jardines Colgantes de Caliban**. Ubicados en la luna uraniana de Caliban, es un territorio neutral en donde se han llevado a cabo distintas firmas de tratados. En él crecen plantas de distintos puntos del sistema solar y es famoso por su flor de los 300 pétalos. Se dice que en el Templo de la Gran Madre de Caliban contrajeron matrimonio legal y vinculante el legendario general saturnino-neptuniano Hanis Bey y la terrícola Ceren antes de devolverla a la Tierra.

* **Jovia**. Capital de Júpiter, llamada también \

debido a que su estructura está compuesta de distintos recintos académicos con sus respectivas facultades.

* **La Periferia**. El distrito más pobre de Cronia, conocida por su concentración de artistas, ladrones, prostitutas, disidentes políticos, y republicanos. Se dice que es el centro de operaciones de la temida Hermandad del Cuchillo.

* **Oruz**. Villa de Titán, capital de la tribu V'adh. Tiene un sistema de gobierno parecido al de Icsos.

* **Puertas de Riothar**. De acuerdo con los nativos de Titán, estas puertas se encuentran escondidas en lo profundo de la selva. Se cree que es a través de estas puertas a donde se podría llegar a la Tierra.

* **Titán**. Una de las lunas más grandes del Imperio Saturnino. Al contrario de lo que se cree en la Tierra, Titán tiene un ecosistema propio de desiertos y selvas, así como comunidades nativas.

* **Templo de las Dunas de Júpiter**. Uno de los recintos religiosos más importantes del Imperio Saturnino y centro de peregrinación anual. Morada principal de la Santa Vidente Ilyame, a quien gente de distintos estratos sociales visitan durante la peregrinación para consultar el Oráculo de la Gran Madre.

* **Templo de la Gran Madre de Caliban**. Ubicado en el centro de los Jardines Colgantes de Caliban. Al ser considerado un territorio de neutralidad política, a este lugar acuden en secreto aquellas parejas de estratos sociales desiguales.

* **Templo de Nipur**. Uno de los recintos religiosos más importantes de Neptuno, el cual recibe la constante visita de la Santa Vidente Ilyame.

* **Terssos**. Desierto ubicado en Titán, considerado el más grande y peligroso del imperio.

* **Torre de Polos**. Torre ubicado en La Periferia utilizado para almacenar granos. Los vecinos de la zona creen que ahí se reúnen la temida Hermandad del Cuchillo, aunque las autoridades imperiales descartan la idea.

* **Ur**. Ciudad capital de Urano. También se le conoce bajo el epíteto de \

por la predominancia de dicho color en sus viviendas.

Сегодняшняя прогулка была просто замечательной! Я выбрал маршрут через лес и поднялся на одну из близлежащих гор. Я остановился, чтобы сделать несколько фотографий и насладиться свежим воздухом. Эта прогулка вновь напомнила мне о том, как важна природа и как здорово проводить время на свежем воздухе! _This report was published via Actifit app ([Android](https://bit.ly/actifit-app) | [iOS](https://bit.ly/actifit-ios)). body.body:
by Del Bigtree on The Highwire 
View my bio on Vigilante.TV: https://vigilante.tv/c/the_highwire [![Episode 470 - A Food Crisis, Autism Communication Rights, And Stem Cell Secrets](https://vigilante.tv/lazy-static/previews/43c3bd01-2184-40f9-be0a-5b0c99a08483.jpg)](https://vigilante.tv/w/m4SRSDQ2aruqr6LGrCzQgC) 
 
 Episode 470 | The HighWire with Del Bigtree delivers a powerful episode covering vaccine messaging, an impending global food crisis, autism communication rights, and cutting-edge stem cell science.

First, One of the most powerful human events The HighWire has covered centers on the film Spellers, and the communication method that allows non-speaking individuals with autism to express themselves through spelling. Dawnmarie Gaivin, AT-ACP, founder of the Spellers Freedom Foundation, joins Del, along with Spellers cast member Elizabeth Bonker, for an inspiring conversation exposing the growing battle over the right to communicate.

As Robert F. Kennedy Jr. works to reconstitute the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP), we examine the new media narrative being deployed against so-called anti-vaxxers and what it signals about the next phase of the public health debate.
Then, Jefferey Jaxen reports on the growing fertilizer supply crisis linked to instability around the Strait of Hormuz, a key global chokepoint through which roughly one-third of the world’s fertilizer ingredients move. What could this mean for food supply, energy, fuel prices, and the risk of a broader international food crisis?

Finally, Del sits down with Ed Clay, a former MMA fighter whose family health crisis led him deep into the world of stem cell therapies and cancer research. He now leads one of the biggest clinics in the world doing this work — in Mexico. It’s a jaw-dropping conversation about why this science is happening outside the United States and what it could mean for the future of medicine.

Guests: Dawnmarie Gaivin, AT-ACP, Elizabeth Bonker, Ginnie Breen, Ed Clay

Things change fast now, but I've always felt that tech added benefit, sure things are different, but better.

I suppose the key factor here is the potential speed of change. AI is cool tech, but it's only the latest layer on our tech stack, we've been adding complexity and efficiency in layers since we domesticated the horse.

There is an cool study on telephone switchboard operators in the early 1900's. Many genteel young ladies had access to ready employment on the switchboards, there were a significant portion of a certain demographic employed in that task.

Along comes a guy who invents the automatic switchboard and literally in a very few years, a large portion (almost all in fact) of this demographic became unemployed. I can't recall the results or conclusion, but the sky didn't fall down for sure, those young ladies found other avenues for gainful employment.

In front of him, the usual piano. It's the first time he has so many people watching, and he fears he won't be able to play a single key, a single note. But the eruption of the crowd at the moment the spotlights illuminate his face makes him regain his confidence. > El joven se para frente al escenario y la multitud, por un momento, hace silencio. Frente a él, el piano de siempre. Es la primera vez que tiene tanto público y teme no poder tocar una tecla, una nota. Pero el estallido del público en el momento que los reflectores iluminan su cara hace que recobre la confianza. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeF6U6NrABq9xCYCdwxr4Xq28j4NfJPUwPoRtsdJFotMn/273_sin_t_tulo_20260416203546.jpg) I started this drawing as everyone starts: with an idea, with inspiration, with the need to draw something. And there was Willis, a true professional. I decided to capture them with quick strokes and shaky strokes, with a brush that should not be used for this at all, but I want a drawing that has that personality of Willis. > Comencé este dibujo como comienzan todos: con una idea, con una inspiración, con la necesidad de dibujar algo. Y ahí estaba Willis, todo un profesional. Decidí plasmarlos con trazos rápidos y trazos temblorosos, con un pincel que para nada debería usarse para esto, pero quiero un dibujo que tenga esa personalidad de Willis. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmezswNwmg1ydQAx4hS1NnsewM9GiLHnPU99K6SRi926Ju/273_sin_t_tulo_20260416203551.jpg) First appeared the firm one, standing, with his hoodie and his jeans, with that attitude of challenging the music and the crowd. > Primero apareció el firme, de pie, con su sudadera y sus jeans, con esa actitud de desafiar la música y el público. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbWhkjQhNZgb9c8g2egAka2jLDuoLDvWxa5Y3rLh2uVzY/273_sin_t_tulo_20260416204058.jpg) In front of him appeared his keyboard, his piano, the most faithful companion for music, with twisted lines like those of the most surreal dreams. > Frente a él apareció su teclado, su piano, el compañero más fiel para la música, con líneas torcidas como las de los sueños más surrealistas. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfBEDscZeyQZuFUWoPirA6P6icgiyDPEDrVs7CPck2CyU/273_sin_t_tulo_20260416210052.png) Color arrived with lights and shadows as music arrives, sometimes easy and simple, sometimes deep and tangled, in notes and arpeggios, in complex melodies, but also in catchy little songs. > El color llegó con luces y sombras como llega la música, a veces fácil y simple, a veces profunda y enredada, en notas y arpegios, en melodías complejas, pero en cancioncillas pegajosas también. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmY1LDSskKPfN9ZJ6MJzcQfZKSJjnaTESyrwPBnYfFeB2A/273_sin_t_tulo_20260416211153.jpg) The crowd shouted with energy and cheered at the end of the first song. The lights of the phones shone, taking pictures of Willis, because Willis is a true star. What will be the next song? No one knows that. But for now, thank you for joining me one more day drawing. > La multitud gritó con energía y ovacionó al concluir la primera canción, las luces de los teléfonos brillaban tomando fotos de Willis, porque Willis es una verdadera estrella. ¿Cuál será la siguiente canción? Eso nadie lo sabe. Pero por ahora, gracias por acompañarme un día más dibujando. I made this drawing while looking at the Willis card from the Rising Star Game. > Hice este dibujo mientras miraba la carta Willis de Rising Star Game. --- ***About:*** ==*Sketchbook and Journal of a Learner*== **If you like my content, join my [Fanbase clicking here](https://hive.vote/dash.php?fan=nestodibuja&i=2)**
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmc31AecQSitU5xAjsqS4snajcWh6CMMyapx88itjomSah/thanks.png)
___ *All photos and images are created by me. These are pictures of my sketchbook. Many of my drawings are practice pieces rather than finished works. Images from the internet may or may not have been used as references, copies, or sources of inspiration as part of my learning process.*

body.title: Revolut UK Bank Account Will Be Open In May
body.body:
/></center>


I was informed today that within the next 4 weeks my current Revolut Bank account will transform into a fully fledged UK bank account. This was totally unexpected when they informed us a couple of months ago due to having my 30 plus year old HSBC account closed due to not residing in the UK. This is kind of crazy here I am having another UK based bank account and just hope I do not have to offer up proof like utility bills etc. I do not want to fly in to arrange that type of proof and my UK salary may be enough.

The aim has always been to have an external bank account outside of South Africa for obvious reasons. Having another currency like GBP, Euro or USD is a must have considering how quickly the local Rand has depreciated over the last 20 years. Any funds outside the borders of SA has to remain there and would never be crazy enough to consider bringing it here.

One of the biggest reasons having an off shore bank account besides the depreciating Rand is the all important crypto off ramp. I have already worked out a planned route which does not include SA banking and would also not include the Revolut bank account due to taxes which would now be whatever the UK taxes are on crypto. SA has a 18% - 40% tax rate on crypto and with the majority of my crypto having been earned could actually be as high as 45% which is utter madness.

The Dubai off ramp crypto route will work with either a Dubai Bank account or a Jersey Bank account and have been looking more closely at the APR being offered. A bank account in Jersey would offer in the region of 1% (100K GBP minimum) up to 3.6% if you had 3 million GBP or more. For some reason I did not check this APR out properly before and just presumed it was in the region of 3%. The bank I have lined up in Dubai offers an APR of 1.6% without the hassle of worrying if you have 100K GBP and is far far less that it is not even a concern.

The Dubai bank account will be finally sorted this year and will wait and see when it is best to travel. The good thing about the off ramp is it would work for both Dubai and Jersey. I did find another bank being Nat West International offering a minimum deposit of 25K GBP and had I known this I would have opted for this last year instead of Revolut. I can also see the rationale for having both the Dubai and Jersey bank accounts and not just the one.

With the SA government clamping down on foreign pensions and tried to implement this from March this year, but withdrew due to opposition. Still the idea to even consider this as an option should have raised alarm bells and they can never be trusted. Having multiple off shore bank accounts does give you options and the crypto off ramp in Dubai does keep you in the shadows knowing they cannot reveal your personal data due to Dubai's banking laws.
