title.title: ¿Qué estoy leyendo?||What am I reading?
title.body:
Ludwig Wittgenstein** Una frase citada por Arturo Uslar Pietri en un artículo titulado “El tamaño del mundo”. En su momento, la frase me impactó mucho por la realidad y verdad que encierra, porque aquello que no está dentro de mi léxico no lo puedo nombrar y no lo hago porque lo desconozco; es decir, el lenguaje se convierte en un límite para el conocimiento. Me gusta recordar esta frase; tenerla presente es una invitación a estar atento a las puertas del conocimiento. Cuando nos encontramos con una palabra cuyo significado desconocemos y nos disponemos a investigarla, nos estamos abriendo a lo desconocido y, aun cuando nuestra interpretación sea limitada, al prestarle atención, el cerebro la archiva, quedando como una huella (significante) por donde pueden transitar otros conocimientos. En las interacciones cotidianas, con nuestros grupos de allegados, difícilmente podemos aumentar el léxico, pues tendemos a hablar con las mismas palabras de uso común con las cuales nos entendemos muy bien y, aun cuando a esto lo llamamos comunicación efectiva, no deja de ser una realidad lo limitado que puede ser nuestro lenguaje y con ello nuestro mundo. Las cifras son un buen marco de referencia para darnos una idea de algún punto que nos interesa reforzar, por ejemplo: el español, según la Real Academia Española, cuenta con más de 112.000 palabras, incluyendo americanismos. De todo este universo, las personas con un nivel de educación básico utilizan en sus conversaciones diarias aproximadamente 300; los de educación superior y lectores pueden llegar a 500 y los escritores rondan las 3000 palabras. ¡Es asombroso! Estas cifras se convierten en un reto. El 23 de abril celebramos el Día del Idioma Español y la fecha se presta para comenzar llamando a los objetos y situaciones por su nombre y no apoyarnos tanto en esas muletillas que a los venezolanos nos encantan y que son válidas para nombrar casi todo, como pueden ser: vaina y cosa. ¿Te atreves a asumir el reto? ![untitled.gif](https://media.tenor.com/KJOdwcjIjCgAAAAC/padai-karna-rudra.gif) Ahora bien, una de las vías más ricas para “apropiarnos” de las palabras es la lectura, que, junto al Día del Idioma, también celebramos el Día del Libro, una excelente fecha para hablar de lo que estamos leyendo, un tema que me resulta bastante estimulante, así que te comento el libro que terminé de leer este fin de semana. 20 Pasos Hacia Delante de Jorge Bucay. Autor dedicado a la literatura del crecimiento personal, y para aquellos que disfrutamos de un cuento, en esta entrega, Bucay sigue su línea de acercamiento al lector a través de historias ilustrativas de cada punto que toca y en el que nos invita a reflexionar, no solo para crecer como persona, sino también como humanidad. El punto de partida es la invitación a conocerte a ti mismo y luego va desglosando cada aspecto de la vida que nos acerca al propósito, la realización y a la internalización de cómo me muevo en cada uno de estos veinte pasos que son pilares para una existencia de bienestar. En estos veinte pasos nos pasea por la libertad, el humor, el amor, la humildad, el orden interno y externo, la creatividad, el buen uso del tiempo, el saber escuchar, correr riesgos, el fracaso, entre otros, y cuando llegamos casi al final, nos deja la alentadora sugerencia de tener presente que siempre tenemos la oportunidad de volver a empezar. Si te gustan los libros de crecimiento personal, te lo recomiendo y aunque pareciera que son temas en los que hemos profundizado, la frescura y experiencia del autor como terapeuta nos abre hacia una visión más amplia del mundo en general y de nuestro mundo en particular. En mi próximo post te cuento del otro libro que estoy leyendo. Si lo deseas, puedes dejarme en los comentarios qué estás leyendo y por qué me lo recomiendas. Gracias de antemano. ![Separadores línea E.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/damarysvibra/23wgoDTwWybCs8NGLz569ehFUGAYLk5HWk4YMp6RA7hd35nfzosFnjqKnDfQWjPXrFTv9.jpg) ![Libertad.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/damarysvibra/AL5xmHBNLU8JYRc8o7d2j7WNHYRCdTT9ruVr2JjMoNDFV3vwGKK31GrBa14vUSw.jpg) Greetings, friends at @holos-lotus. >**“The limits of my language are the limits of my world” - Ludwig Wittgenstein** A quote cited by Arturo Uslar Pietri in an article titled “The Size of the World.” At the time, the quote had a profound impact on me because of the reality and truth it contains, for what is not within my lexicon I cannot name, and I do not name it because I am unaware of it; that is to say, language becomes a limit to knowledge. I like to recall this phrase; keeping it in mind is an invitation to remain attentive to the gates of knowledge. When we encounter a word whose meaning we do not know and set out to investigate it, we are opening ourselves to the unknown, and even when our interpretation is limited, by paying attention to it, the brain archives it, leaving a (significant) imprint through which other knowledge can pass. In everyday interactions with our close circles, we can hardly expand our vocabulary, as we tend to use the same common words with which we understand each other very well; and even though we call this effective communication, it remains a reality just how limited our language—and with it, our world—can be. Numbers provide a good frame of reference to give us an idea of a point we wish to emphasize; for example: Spanish, according to the Royal Spanish Academy, has more than 112,000 words, including Americanisms. Out of this entire universe, people with a basic level of education use approximately 300 words in their daily conversations; those with higher education and readers can reach 500, and writers use around 3,000 words. It’s amazing! These figures present a challenge. On April 23, we celebrate Spanish Language Day, and the date lends itself to starting by calling objects and situations by their proper names and not relying so heavily on those filler words that we Venezuelans love and that are valid for naming almost everything, such as “vaina” and “cosa.” Do you dare to take on the challenge? ![untitled.gif](https://media.tenor.com/KJOdwcjIjCgAAAAC/padai-karna-rudra.gif) Now, one of the richest ways to “make words our own” is through reading. Along with Spanish Language Day, we also celebrate Book Day—an excellent occasion to talk about what we’re reading, a topic I find quite stimulating. So, I’d like to tell you about the book I finished reading this weekend. 20 Steps Forward by Jorge Bucay. An author dedicated to personal growth literature, and for those of us who enjoy a good story, in this book, Bucay continues his approach of engaging the reader through illustrative stories for each point he addresses, inviting us to reflect—not only to grow as individuals but also as humanity. The starting point is an invitation to get to know yourself, and then he breaks down every aspect of life that brings us closer to purpose, fulfillment, and the internalization of how I navigate each of these twenty steps, which are pillars for a life of well-being. In these twenty steps, he takes us through freedom, humor, love, humility, internal and external order, creativity, the wise use of time, knowing how to listen, taking risks, and failure, among others, and when we reach the end, he leaves us with the encouraging suggestion to keep in mind that we always have the opportunity to start over. If you enjoy personal growth books, I recommend this one, and although it may seem like topics we’ve explored in depth, the author’s fresh perspective and experience as a therapist open us up to a broader view of the world in general and our own world in particular. In my next post, I’ll tell you about the other book I’m reading. If you’d like, you can leave a comment telling me what you’re reading and why you recommend it to me. Thanks in advance. ![Separadores línea E.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/damarysvibra/23wgoDTwWybCs8NGLz569ehFUGAYLk5HWk4YMp6RA7hd35nfzosFnjqKnDfQWjPXrFTv9.jpg) Translated with www.DeepL.com/Translator (free version) **Fuente de imágenes**: Portada: [1](https://libroshernandez.com/wp-content/uploads/9788498675153.jpg) - [2](https://www.garabatolibros.com/imagenes/9789585/978958511887.JPG) Gif: Recursos Peakd. ![separador-rojp-800x5.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcuEfbmsuYdBRfYDrQctCJfzA1A8kQT9hp6UYL5CdDCyq/separador-rojp-800x5.jpg) ![pie 800.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/irvinc/VilfkhTe-pie20800.jpg) ![separador-rojp-800x5.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcuEfbmsuYdBRfYDrQctCJfzA1A8kQT9hp6UYL5CdDCyq/separador-rojp-800x5.jpg)

It was a big vibe today on Splinterlands as I finally decided to win over 15 battles for the day. That’s a good start for a Monday morning and beginning of the week. It was a success and after a couple of weeks without my mobile phone, I have finally been able to get back on track with my best game at the moment. After winning all the battles, it was possible to claim the three sets of prizes which I’m supposed to claim for the day. To my greatest surprise, A LEGENDARY card, and 2 RARE cards were included in my set of prizes. The LEGENDARY card was LITTLE SISTER, while the two RARE cards were SCALES OF JUSTICE and FROSTGUARD WARRIOR. while the others were REGULAR cards. LITTLE SISTER is one of my favorite cards on Splinterlands and I use it when I wanna make sure to win a particular battle. It is a Level 1 Unit MAGIC card that has a special ability. It belongs to the FIEND bloodline and falls under the DEATH element category. The first RARE card was SCALES OF JUSTICE card which has no attack feature but possesses a special abilities making it possible for it to bring bonuses to the battle. It has two special abilities actually, belongs to the FIRE element category and the SAURIAN bloodline. It has a MANA of 5, 1 Armor stat, 4 health stat and 4 speed stat. It is a Level 1 unit card.

It is a RANGED Attack card I also use from time to time as it is under the MARLAI SINGARIEL Archon card. It falls under the WATER element category and has a MANA of 8, Armor Stat of 2, Health stat of 4 and Speed stat of 4. It is a Level 1 card and is capable of reducing the health of an opponent after it attacks by 2. The regular cards won for the day include the PORT GUARDIAN, COLOSSUS RAIDER and the FRANKARSGARD. These were the three regular cards I got for the day. Congratulations to me and more on the way. 😁 I’m still on the battles trying to see how many more games I can win for the day so my points can move up. It’s gonna be a splendid week on Splinterlands now that I’m fully back. Then I must tell you that you do not deserve to miss out on all the fun going on over there. Tap on my referral link which I’m gonna share below and join me in the battlefield. Let’s make magic together. Thanks a bunch guys for stopping over and see y’all again soon. Have a good one.

</center>
</liketuimages>


There’s nothing cuter in the animal kingdom than the looks on the faces of puppies or kittens, for in their eyes you can see their innocence and what sparks their curiosity. 

I have a few photos of that sort of gaze that I’m sharing today of my cat Hermosú when he was younger and liked to play hide-and-seek with Duke in one of my mum’s fern plants; she was, of course, annoyed, and I ended up paying the price. 

I also have some photos of Hermosú staring intently at my grandmother; he wouldn’t take his eyes off her and would often come right up to her feet to get a better look. He did this every morning when it was my turn to wake my grandmother up; he and Duke would pop into the room just to check if my grandmother was alright, then they’d leave, but Hermosú’s gaze was as lovely as he was. 😍

And to finish off, here’s a photo of the looks on both their faces. Every time I go to bed, Hermosú comes looking for me to lie down with me, even if it’s just in the corner of the bed 😁. That day he was annoyed because I wanted to put him down. 

* * *

## <center>Miradas que enamoran</center>

* * *

No hay nada más tierno en el reino animal que las miradas de los carrochorros de perros o gatos, pues en sus ojos se puede ver la inocencia y lo que les causa curiosidad. 

Sobre ese tipo de miradas tengo algunas fotos que hoy comparto de mi gato Hermosú cuando estaba más chiquito y le gustaba jugar al escondido con Duke en una de las plantas de helecho de mi mamá que por supuesto se molestaba y yo terminaba pagando los platos rotos. 

También tengo algunas fotos de Hermosú viendo fijamente a mi abuela, no le quitaba la mirada de encima e incluso muchas veces se acercaba a la altura de sus pies para mirar mejor. Eso lo hacía todas las mañana cuando me tocaba levantar a mi abuela, él junto a Duke se meten en la habitación solo para ver si mi abuela está bien, después se van, pero la mirada de Hermosú era tan linda como él. 😍

Y para finalizar la foto de las miradas de ambos, cada vez que me acuesto, Hermosú me busca para irse a recostar conmigo asi sea en la esquina de la cama se acuesta 😁 este día estaba molesto porque lo quería bajar. 


---

title.title: Mountain hike with creek and flowers
title.body:
In summer I like hiking and Austria has some really nice mountains to offer. Depending on my time this year I am going to do some hiking again, but I assume that I only make some easy hikes this year since I don't have the fitness anymore like some years ago, but I am working on it again so I hope I will be back on track soon. Back in 2020 I was really fit and the hike was not a problem for me. I really enjoyed the beuatiful nature up on the mountains and this is why I am already looking forward to to at least some easy hiks this year again. 

Creeks up on the mountains can be very beautiful but they carry really cold water and I went into the water once but really regreted it afterwards. Since the really cold water stole so much of my energy that it was really difficult to go back down the mountain. Eventhoug the weather was really hot I shouldn't have bathed in the water and only used it to cool a little down by spraying it on my body. 

Nature up on the mountains can be really beautiful, Flowers and landscapes with creeks and waterfalls are really beautiful, you can watch the water flowing down the mountain and watching a small flow getting bigger and bigger until it reaches the valley. Often with a lot of waterfalls and beuatiful basins before it reaches a river down in the valley.

title.title: Border Control: Fixing the Communal Garden with ChatGPT and the Case of the Missing Bin!
title.body:
https://images.hive.blog/DQmeThEFFbAMcmG6jCoea6WRQJ8RaNPYkuWWkhFb4hqPErv/InCollage_20260420_175035559~2.jpg

I’ve been on holiday, so I haven’t done much gardening for a couple of weeks. 

https://images.hive.blog/DQmQW8X7nYTRRTfKThhZabmZG4FE9hEeq8Quq1eZFfPry55/4579~2.jpg

Over the weekend, I carried on putting down some membrane to stop the weeds growing through. I then popped down to the retail park to buy more plum slates to cover the membrane.  Unfortunately, I didn’t have quite enough to finish one side of the flats where I live.

https://images.hive.blog/DQmRnkCgx9WmcKYrwwZtLTHnzcoiBsy3uNMQgBcrgcP3K35/20260420_111813.jpg

https://images.hive.blog/DQmQUFVQujYjbSQAHNLhoYzDWWUXC9pvcaXpcKKKqiN861s/87c27a67-106e-4cfe-a58b-0f3b65f7e145.jpeg

I didn’t want to carry on spending money doing all of the outskirts of the flats, as my neighbours just aren’t interested. They won’t want to pay for any more slates. The job looked unfinished, so I asked ChatGPT what I could do to make it look better. This was what it came up with, and I’m going to do it, as it looks better than it does at the moment.  I might not bother with any plants though, as it will be me who has to tend to them, and I'm trying to make my life easier. I will go up to the derelict factory tomorrow that used to sell stone.  There are still some stones there that have been left behind, so they will be good enough for the border. 

https://images.hive.blog/DQmXJNinWy2C2uYVch7kqUVoU6uC7KRwBWkzeUxT8qjMUqA/4571~2.jpg

https://images.hive.blog/DQmQkSrHrdcL2pNcgtozSpSZJeq6DosMZDS3K2pkn2GYrCE/4572~2.jpg

In the meantime, the red flowers on the Japenese Quince and the Escallonia Rubra have come out more, and they look really vibrant.  The communal garden isn't very interesting, so any colour is a bonus.  Unfortunately, the Lucky Clover, and Triteleia that I sowed have done bugger all!

https://images.hive.blog/DQmZoe8xuf2MqdFkFRzmEaPjXgxVHxYtJan2voHVs22ei3i/4577~3.jpg

https://images.hive.blog/DQmRo352i8JpnjHW9s6eusanYyKXRd7mKWTBMEbbmBKCtNR/4576~2.jpg

At least we have some white bluebells and a few remaining daffodils.

https://images.hive.blog/DQmZUSNKA4c1zqFSsQZACatz6nKVU3xraDwvqQiT2voNCWD/4570.jpg
I swept up the moss that the blackbirds have thrown off the roof. This is an ongoing battle. The only problem is, that while I was away, the garden recycling bin we have to put our garden waste in, has disappeared. I’m hoping nobody has taken it. I think what has happened is that sometimes, when they mechanically empty the bin, it gets thrown into the back of the dustbin cart instead of just being emptied. Anyway, I’ve ordered another one, so until it arrives, I’m a bit limited in what I can do.  Until next time ...


![PaRgthAvamAmR7uZi4RENh3BWaKjnQbhHtF9iaSV1cVaeSir8SCZYpmzMLvBrDLdiD44L3w4RUXvxqnkBg2eqoHbbUCFgVMLCokxymJ6uR...g2EUvmwMbS8rDTmwiZZiXJVfaSEG5zu7KhSz75fp2aWUpTTXMModEMjmcJDocpskjENinHpDX2Xfhqs6PzWxPZxGDEgVmqwVo162Vb1AHTA1YxrG6iGLyJ3Dqw.gif](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTQF6wQW4xj6B6wQh99WqmNgkL1JrpKsWChsLv5k5Lq4b/PaRgthAvamAmR7uZi4RENh3BWaKjnQbhHtF9iaSV1cVaeSir8SCZYpmzMLvBrDLdiD44L3w4RUXvxqnkBg2eqoHbbUCFgVMLCokxymJ6uR...g2EUvmwMbS8rDTmwiZZiXJVfaSEG5zu7KhSz75fp2aWUpTTXMModEMjmcJDocpskjENinHpDX2Xfhqs6PzWxPZxGDEgVmqwVo162Vb1AHTA1YxrG6iGLyJ3Dqw.gif)

title.title: Repensar la Historia [ESP][ENG]
title.body:
Hace unos días tras mirar un podcast sobre la historia de México, comencé a hacerme varias preguntas con respecto a la historia de Venezuela, y caí en cuenta que en el sistema educativo venezolano (como todo sistema educativo) no enseña la historia con neutralidad y sentido crítico. Sino, que hay un profundo sentido ideológico como móvil de la enseñanza histórica. 

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmZsymWjehVQPspPjf1Twy8GPJ7Y8bV9vYBFzWBFCPSuT2/repensarlahistoria.png 

*Fuente[Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/es-es/foto/rojo-gente-azul-cartel-27857253/)*

Por mencionar un ejemplo, hoy en Venezuela no hay quien pueda cuestionar el movimiento de Bolívar y en ese sentido cabe la pregunta: ¿realmente fue un movimiento independentista? Precisamente ayer, 19 de abril se celebraba la efeméride venezolana, de la proclamación del acta de la independencia que ocurrió en 1810.  Por lo que podríamos afirmar que en ese año comenzó la “independencia de Venezuela”. 

*¿Alguien sobre el suelo venezolano se atreve a cuestionar la moralidad de dicho proceso?*

Suena bastante contradictorio que un venezolano pueda someter a juicio su historia, y este es precisamente el punto. La historia no es un conglomerado de hechos históricos, sino que la historia viene a ser la narración e interpretación de los hechos. Así que, realmente entiendo que la historia es como es, pero, no es como nos la han contado y las narrativas son precisamente lo que pretendo poner en tensión. 

Volviendo la mirada sobre lo enseñado en las aulas de clase,  cuando se nos menciona la historia de Venezuela se habla del tercer viaje de Colón por allá en el 1498 cuando llega a lo que viene a ser Venezuela, después de eso no se menciona mucho sino hasta el nacimiento de Simón Bolívar en 1783, luego continua la historia a partir de 1810.  Pero desde la llegada de Cristóbal Colón hasta Bolívar hay casi 300 años. ¿Algo debió haber ocurrido en esos casi 3 siglos? ¿Qué ocurrió? 

Lo cierto es que eso no nos lo cuentan en el sistema educativo, por lo que he comenzado un proceso de investigación y documentación para posteriormente crear contenido sobre la historia de Venezuela sin ideologizar los procesos históricos o ensalzar personajes que no son tan heroicos como creemos. 

Como recordatorio personal debo tener presente que cuando se estudia y profundiza en temas sobre los cuales recae mucha emocionalidad hablar con criterio se convierte en casi un ataque contra lo que las personas creen, de modo que antes de comenzar a desentramar personajes históricos me gustaría que las personas que se acerquen a estas líneas puedan entender que casi todo lo que creen saber de la historia no es estrictamente una narración de hechos de manera cronológica con sentido crítico, es una narración profundamente sesgada y con intencionalidad previa para identificarse personalmente con la historia. 

*¿Te has preguntado cómo se construyen los proyectos de nacionalidad?*

**A mis compatriotas: ¿Eres Venezolano porque naciste en Venezuela o por que te sientes identificado emocionalmente con Venezuela?**

No hay cosa con la que esté en más  profundo desacuerdo que con la identidad nacional como la hemos construido durante los últimos 50 años. Soy Venezolano porque nací en este pedazo de tierra, pero, estoy en profundo desacuerdo con que debemos identificarnos con una historia de Venezuela que nació a fuerza de bayonetas y cañonazos.  

Siento que podemos edificar otra narrativa de nuestra historia mucho más civilizada, pero, hay que aceptar que no somos infalibles y que en la historia nos hemos equivocado. Para ello, habría que redescubrir la historia y crear nuevas narrativas, menos emocionales. ¿Seremos capaces de desmontar a Bolívar del pedestal en donde está? Y no porque no haya sido importante, porque decir eso sería una estupidez. Bolívar claro que fue importante, pero, habría que preguntarnos ¿Es cierto todo lo que sabemos de él? 

*¿Te atreves a cuestionar todo lo que sabes?*

***Si te gustaría redescubrir la historia conmigo, acompáñame en esta aventura humanista.*** 






*Fotografía @filoriologo Redmi Note 14*
*Edición: Adobe Photoshop Lightroom*


***

---

##  ENGLISH VERSION

# Rethinking History 

A few days ago, after listening to a podcast about the history of Mexico, I began to ask myself several questions about the history of Venezuela, and I realized that the Venezuelan educational system (like any educational system) does not teach history with neutrality and a critical eye. Rather, there is a deep ideological agenda driving the teaching of history. 

https://img.leopedia.io/DQmZsymWjehVQPspPjf1Twy8GPJ7Y8bV9vYBFzWBFCPSuT2/repensarlahistoria.png 

*Fuente[Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/es-es/foto/rojo-gente-azul-cartel-27857253/)*

To give an example, today in Venezuela no one can question Bolívar’s movement, and in that sense the question arises: was it really an independence movement? Just yesterday, April 19, Venezuela celebrated the anniversary of the proclamation of the Declaration of Independence, which took place in 1810.  So we could say that “Venezuela’s independence” began that year. 

***Does anyone on Venezuelan soil dare to question the morality of that process?*** 

It sounds quite contradictory that a Venezuelan could subject their history to scrutiny, and this is precisely the point. History is not a collection of historical facts; rather, history is the narration and interpretation of those facts. So, I truly understand that history is what it is, but it is not what we have been told, and it is precisely these narratives that I intend to challenge. 

Looking back at what we were taught in the classroom, whenever the history of Venezuela is mentioned, the focus is on Columbus’s third voyage back in 1498, when he arrived in what would become Venezuela. After that, not much is mentioned until the birth of Simón Bolívar in 1783, and then the story continues starting in 1810.  But there are nearly 300 years between Christopher Columbus’s arrival and Bolívar. Must something have happened during those nearly three centuries? What happened? 

The truth is that the education system doesn’t teach us about this, so I’ve begun a process of research and documentation to later create content on the history of Venezuela without politicizing historical events or glorifying figures who aren’t as heroic as we believe them to be. 

As a personal reminder, I must keep in mind that when studying and delving into topics that evoke strong emotions, speaking with discernment can almost feel like an attack on what people believe, so before I begin to unravel historical figures, I would like those who read these lines to understand that almost everything they think they know about history is not strictly a chronological account of events with a critical perspective; it is a deeply biased narrative with a premeditated intent to personally identify with history. 

*Have you ever wondered how concepts of nationality are constructed?*

To my fellow countrymen: Are you Venezuelan because you were born in Venezuela, or because you feel an emotional connection to Venezuela?

There is nothing I disagree with more deeply than the national identity as we have constructed it over the past 50 years. I am Venezuelan because I was born on this piece of land, but I strongly disagree that we should identify with a history of Venezuela that was born through the force of bayonets and cannon fire.  

I feel that we can build a much more civilized narrative of our history, but we must accept that we are not infallible and that we have made mistakes throughout history. To do so, we would have to rediscover history and create new, less emotionally charged narratives. Will we be able to take Bolívar down from the pedestal where he stands? And not because he wasn’t important—because saying that would be foolish. Bolívar was certainly important, but we must ask ourselves: Is everything we know about him true? 

*Do you dare to question everything you know?*

***If you’d like to rediscover history with me, join me on this humanistic adventure. ***

title.title: Consistency is The Best Medicine
title.body: As a medical student, I am trained to look beyond surface symptoms to find the root cause of an illness. Of recent,i  applied this same logic to my finances after watching a YouTube series that deeply impacted me: \
adapted from the novel by Arese Ugwu.\n\n​The series follows Zuri, a young, stylish woman who seems to have it all. Following a messy breakup, she travels abroad to \

a move strongly advised by her friends. However, Zuri returns to Lagos only to face a harsh clinical reality: she is drowning in debt. With her landlord on her neck for the houserent, she is left with debt beyond her salary amount. she realizes her impulsive spending has left her financially unstable.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWTLCPxxsVxXpa45fwi69yPkQCqzb7bfYUnaNswBSJ4JL/1776702368598.jpg)

​**Diagnosing the Problem**

​Zuri’s struggle taught me a vital lesson: never try to impress others at the expense of your own stability. In my own life, there are times I feel the urge to show off, but I am reminded that \
myself a lifestyle I cannot afford will only lead to long-term complications. We must \

regardless of the social pressure to do otherwise.
 **All pics were screenshoted from Azuea Studio on YouTube**
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmajVG1curdzS9oCKo4nqCcUqgqTNkLh6eK2g1CUzo7JKg/1776704748362.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTUEAoboeYL3jqofLhLcknspHTAHVsLcwjGkeuTZZ4HDP/1776704748419.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVyaFTk3Nk1RebEgYBfq8fC5A8dfEbSCQ2TLux3527Fn5/1776704748457.jpg)



​**The Emergency Fund: A Financial Vaccine**

​One of the most profound lessons involves the Emergency Fund. In medicine, we know that urgent care doesn't wait for a convenient time. If a loved one falls ill, you don't want to be forced to borrow money just to provide them with basic care.

​As the series says:


*​\

*



​This was evident when Zuri’s mother fell ill, and Zuri had to take on even more debt to pay for her treatment. Saving for a \
is the only way to break the \

cycle.


**​Consistency is the Best Medicine**

​You don’t need millions to start. Whether it is a hundred Naira or a hundred dollars, the amount matters less than the habit. Nothing stunts growth more than inconsistency.

​I highly recommend this series to anyone looking to reshape their financial perspective and to change the way they view money in genral.You can find it on the Azuwa Studios channel on YouTube.

title.body:
>

___feliz lunes y feliz comienzo de semana queridos amigos DIYHUB, deseo que esta semana venga cargada de energías y bendiciones para que logren todos sus proyectos___ ☺️❤️

Antes de comenzar mi publicación, quiero agradecerle al equipo de @diyhub por el apoyo, recibido y por el premio obtenido, de mi parte les agradezco de todo corazón ❤️, ahora sí, comencemos con mi primera Participación para el Concurso: 🌴 2026 Apr-May Contest: DIY Summer Vibes 🏖️, y el día de hoy quiero mostrarles una idea para hacer un sombrero ideal para la playa, hecho con material de reciclaje, acompáñame y te comparto el paso a paso:

> Happy Monday and happy start to the week, dear DIYHUB friends! I hope this week is filled with energy and blessings so you can achieve all your projects ☺️❤️
>
> Before starting my post, I want to thank the @diyhub team for their support and the prize I received. I thank them from the bottom of my heart ❤️. Now, let's begin with my first entry for the contest: 🌴 2026 Apr-May Contest: DIY Summer Vibes 🏖️. Today I want to show you an idea for making a perfect beach hat using recycled materials. Join me and I'll share the step-by-step instructions:

<div class=\

> ___MATERIALES___ > MATERIALS Este tipo de sombrero en tela me gusta mucho, ya que en lo personal sudo mucho y éste me permite estar más fresca, aparte que su modelo es ideal para taparnos gran parte de nuestro rostro del sol y proteger nuestra piel, para la confección de este gorro utilizaré un viejo pantalón, la tela de este, está un poco gastada y también mi hijo dejó de usarlo ya que se rompió, pero éste tiene gran parte de la tela en buen estado, así que decidí convertirlo en algo útil y darle una segunda oportunidad, aquí les dejo la lista de materiales a utilizar: - Puedes utilizar la tela de tu preferencia, y también puedes utilizar esos viejos Jeans, que ya no usas o que están deteriorados - Cinta métrica - Tisa, para marcar la tela - Tijeras - Molde para el sombrero - Hilo - Máquina de coser, en caso de no tener puedes hacerlo a mano, ya que su confección es bastante sencilla > I really like this type of fabric hat because I tend to sweat a lot, and this one keeps me cooler. Plus, its design is perfect for covering most of my face from the sun and protecting my skin. To make this hat, I'll be using an old pair of pants. The fabric is a bit worn, and my son stopped wearing them because they ripped. But most of the fabric is still in good condition, so I decided to repurpose them and give them a second life. Here's the list of materials you'll need: > - You can use any fabric you like, or even those old jeans you no longer wear or that are worn out. > - Measuring tape > - Chalk for marking the fabric > - Scissors > - Hat pattern > - Thread > - Sewing machine. If you don't have one, you can sew it by hand, as it's quite easy to make.

> ___PASO A PASO___ > STEP BY STEP Para nuestro primer paso, vamos a comenzar sacando las partes de nuestro gorro, me voy a guiar por un gorro de mis hijas, este es un poco pequeño para mí, así que me gustó la idea de hacer uno con el tamaño ideal para mi cabeza, este gorro consta de 3 partes, dibujamos la orilla inferior, cortaremos cuatro piezas en total de esta parte del gorro. ahora cortaremos la segunda parte, esta es el centro del gorro, dibujo un aproximado del modelo y luego corrijo con las medidas, al momento de cortar, dobló a la mitad la tela para que me queden iguales ambas piezas. De esta cortaremos 2 piezas y por último vamos a hacer el círculo que lleva en la parte superior de la cabeza, dibujamos guiándonos con el gorro modelo, dejamos un excedente para la costura comparamos con las piezas del Centro de nuestro gorro y luego cortamos > For our first step, we'll start by cutting out the pieces for our hat. I'm going to use one of my daughters' hats as a guide. It's a little small for me, so I liked the idea of ​​making one the perfect size for my head. This hat has three parts. We'll draw the bottom edge; we'll cut four pieces in total from this part of the hat. > > Now we'll cut the second part, which is the center of the hat. I'll draw a rough outline of the pattern and then adjust it with the measurements. When cutting, I fold the fabric in half so that both pieces are the same size. We'll cut two pieces from this. Finally, we'll make the circle that goes on top of the head. We'll draw it using the pattern hat as a guide, leaving a seam allowance. We'll compare it to the pieces from the center of our hat and then cut it out.

> |![IMG_9168.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmX7uCWZuyhaUg2HEZYrFjB4ZkH8VwtmB9ggqpMV8wESXY/IMG_9168.jpeg)|![IMG_9173.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRnxeLoxqGsdcnE2g122W7MBkMFMTtKkSq91hY6tdsqFs/IMG_9173.jpeg)| |---|---| |![IMG_9180.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUH6xERkD3fBJbnPKrvhcsjRKtsohYmDL1GoSg34BNu4F/IMG_9180.jpeg)|![IMG_9184.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTieY7MJrCPx8h2atwQ9yokMdAXjbR6f6yVctgN57tb6t/IMG_9184.jpeg)| Para nuestro segundo paso, vamos a comenzar con las costuras, primero unimos las dos piezas centrales de nuestro gorro por los lados, luego unimos la parte superior, la que es una circunferencia, hacemos pequeños piquetes a la mitad de esta figura, fijamos con alfileres, y luego vamos pasando costura por toda la orilla, uniendo ambas piezas > For our second step, we'll start with the stitching. First, we join the two center pieces of our hat along the sides. Then, we join the top part, which is a circle. We make small notches in the middle of this shape, secure it with pins, and then sew along the entire edge, joining both pieces.

> |![IMG_9185.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQma2xu161zopvbB9QEY9USK6uLr1qm6cRyuhBxJFCqjwyX/IMG_9185.jpeg)|![IMG_9187.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNitfftMJ9doupmGb9WR2ZbWnjJZNWJQto65XCiKaVx6L/IMG_9187.jpeg)| |---|---| |![IMG_9190.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVw8oxmCXt83HJJ72sxhiNWK4kZFxQSh1nLwrac8FzYzm/IMG_9190.jpeg)|![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTXeau7piV2CDBq156xxkfeB9dtpZJqB7HW1m4oRp74hy/img_9194.jpg) I| Para el tercer paso, vamos a unir las piezas de la orilla inferior de nuestro gorro, unimos dos de las piezas por los lados y luego las otras dos y luego las unimos entre sí por toda la orilla, luego volteamos y le pasamos costuras por el lado derecho podemos pasarle varias costuras decorativas. Según nuestro gusto, yo le pasé dos hileras de costura. > For the third step, we'll join the pieces of the bottom edge of our hat. We'll join two of the pieces along the sides, then the other two, and finally join them together all along the edge. Then we'll turn it right side out and sew along the right side. We can add several decorative stitches, depending on our preference. I sewed two rows of stitching.

> |![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdatShej2jppQaiECzEVAEr6ptSxuL2Z8wuTQ7FYgmevf/img_9197.jpg)|![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmW9ZJVSwyhs8P1duDvJ9oRbBaxnRxVMqv4tGy5BCPvKhr/img_9200.jpg)| |---|---| |![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXEKaQANfqMY5itzXses2CfLvgedFJFq164jnKjVWqHSB/img_9201.jpg)|![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbwQWDtFTN7CweiBkfpBHzet8scmugh8JNEMuGgPfoo5g/img_9203.jpg)| Para el cuarto y último paso vamos a unir todas las piezas de nuestro gorro, aquí tuve una pequeña complicación, la parte del centro me quedó mucho más ancha que la de la orilla y no me coincidió, pero por suerte, esto no fue tanto problema, le hice unas pinzas y le metí un poco en la costura de los lados, y así me cuadró perfecto con la orilla inferior, fijé con alfileres y luego pasé costura y así ya está listo este lindo gorro, ideal para esos días soleados o para un día especial en la playa, espero les haya gustado esta idea > For the fourth and final step, we'll join all the pieces of our hat. Here I ran into a small problem: the center part ended up being much wider than the edge and didn't line up. But luckily, it wasn't too much of a problem. I made some darts and tucked it in a little at the side seams, and that's how it lined up perfectly with the bottom edge. I pinned it in place and then sewed it closed, and there you have it! This cute hat is ready, perfect for sunny days or a special day at the beach. I hope you liked this idea.

title.title: Experience is the Best Teacher - Ladies of Hive 285
title.body:
There are movies that feel entertaining and there are movies that stay as a lesson after watching them. For me, one that really impacted how I think is Slumdog Millionaire. The show is not just about winning the money but about how life random life facts and experiences can shape and help you in unexpected ways.

https://img.leopedia.io/DQmWW9hB1G3fW73ndZbrR4cDMUPCWkCLbE3TFAAePWE5sNR/Cover.jpg 

The Lesson That Stayed With Me

The biggest lesson I learned from this movie is that you never know when random knowledge and experience will help you. Jamal Malik, an 18 year old from the Juhu slum, was not educated in a formal way but he knew the answers because of what he lived through. The police even arrested him at one point because they thought he was cheating but it's actually just from his own experiences and being observant. Every question in the game show connected to a memory from his past. It made me realize that learning does not only come from school but also in everyday life and every simple things you experience.

One scene I remember is the answer to question, \

A tourist gave him a $100 bill (or he encountered it, I forgot which) and he remembered the face from that real-life interaction. It's part luck but also part experience. You may know this person because you're an American and encounter this in your everyday life or simply because you saw an image on the internet. Regardless of how you know this, it would still be a random knowledge that you don't know when it would help you in life.\n\nBut not all the questions are can be known and sometimes, luck plays a huge part. In the last question, \

Jamal answers based on emotion. He didn't know the answer and it all comes to luck.

This movie made me think about my own life. Sometimes, I feel like small things I learn or experience are not important. But this movie showed me that everything can have value someday. Even random moments or struggles can help in ways I cannot see yet.

https://img.leopedia.io/DQmVibgqv2j6LpvvXzC87dXWmzEaJehyYMBumEYjfTpmDJw/paris_0244828284.png 

I would recommend this movie because it gives a simple but good message. You do not need to have a perfect path to succeed. Life teaches you in different ways and those lessons stay with you. You just have to trust that what you are going through now can help you later.

Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@aiko2ne1/experience-is-the-best-teacher-ladies-of-hive-285-8um)

Para culminar el segundo momento del año escolar los niños presentaron su proyecto de ciencias. Se organizaron seis grupo y cada dos equipos tenían un tema en específico. 

Al los equipos 3 y 4 les tocó fuerza y energía. Mi hija era del equipo 4 y elegimos energía magnética. 

*El avión magnético*

Este experimento demostraba como se creaba un campo magnético debido a la atracción de los imanes permitiendo mantener en equilibrio y flotando el avión de papel. Este se sostenía de un hilo que impedía que ambos imanes se juntaran. 

Los materiales súper sencillo:

- cartón
- silicón 
- hilo
- hija de papel 
- imanes

Es fácil de hacer en casa y una buena manera de enseñar a los más chiquitos sobre las leyes de atracción y repulsión. 

Los niños se divirtieron mucho y explicaron a sus compañeros cada experimento. 

Este tipo de trabajos los incentiva y motiva a descubrir el mundo y amar la ciencia. 

Lo incómodo es que los papás estuvimos de pie todo el tiempo ya que no se cuenta con espacio ni sillas para este tipo de actividades. 

Cada momento de ahora en adelante dice la maestra que harán un proyecto de ciencias.

body.title: Cycling ChitChat – Week 16: Fresh ideas and Highlights
body.body:
>Photo by @vesytz
Hey folks,
I’ve been thinking about ways to spice up this initiative post — something that keeps us motivated, gives us new vibes, and helps us grow. Usually, when we’re out on our bikes we just enjoy the ride, training at our own pace and fitness level. But here we’re also sharing content, and an idea that’s been buzzing in my head for a while is about photography. So, how about this: once the Cycling ChitChat week wraps up, we run a poll with selected photos from your posts, and the winner gets a little prize? That way, even those posting through #Strava2Hive who are still a bit shy about writing route descriptions can join in. All they’d need to do is mention in the description that their photo is part of our Cycling‑Photography Challenge — and add a short caption for the pic, of course.
Ride it, snap it, share it!
 👆 (That this could be the title of that poll) 😄 Easy peasy — just nick the Monomad trick: 🤓 paste This is my entry for the Cycling‑Photography Challenge or drop the tag #CPC. I’d like to know what you guys think — drop your thoughts in the comments! Funny thing: one opinion I thought was spot‑on actually changed the name of the initiative. It used to be Sunday ChitChat, and now it’s got a better vibe, right? Alright, time to give a shout‑out to the posts from these past days! Right after we dropped the Week 15 initiative about the Hell of the North and its riders. Some jumped in, some didn’t — but the cool thing is our community keeps buzzing more and more, and that’s worth a big round of applause.

>Getting from blogging to vlogging... sharing my first cycling video! - So here’s the deal — this guy’s a bit scatter‑brained, but we’ll let him off since the initiative was already rolling… hahaha… we’re always messing around here. The cool bit? We’ve got ourselves a brand‑new influencer! Go check out his vids on YouTube!\n\n

>Paris, Jr Bloomsday, 20 Mile Ride, Mileage Goals, Gear, Robin Nest - Sunday - Apart from blue eggs and fresh kit (bib shorts and jerseys), this post — if you peek at it — has something kinda creepy: a pic! And the guy behind it never skips a cycling event.
>Cycling Community Weekly Milage Update: Another Bad Weather Week! - Speaking of photographs, Brutus sometimes shows up in some really good views.\n\n
>Cycling Chit Chat - This was the post that flipped history’s script! 🤣\n\n
>Lunch Ride 13.82km 48min54sec - Mate, you always drop awesome pics! Love seeing the spots you pedal through — told you that loads of times!\n\n
>Cycling #ChitChat – Life’s Better on Two Wheels - A post that digs into the stories and what fires up the athletes behind the races!

>Pollen, Camino, Boy's Dental, PDC, 35 Mile Zone 2 Trainer Ride PR, Sun, Soak, Driving - Thursday - That forest with the sun shining out loud… pure magic! Thanks a ton for all your posts here. You can tell you’re having a blast sharing your rides with us — and that’s awesome. Big shout‑out to your wonderful family!\n\n
>Right before the getaway - All I can say is she loves hanging out here with this crew and enjoying everyone’s company!\n\n
>Shit Sleep, Spokane Bike Swap, 23.85 Mile Ride, Grilling - Saturday - Some folks are having rough dreams lately. Guess we just need to ride harder — that might fix it, lol\n\n
>Back on the bicycle - So happy about your recovery and that you’re enjoying your bike again… your pics are always awesome, and I bet they’ll spark loads of inspiration round here!\n\n
, lol… just a joke from one of the lads riding along!\n\n<a href=\

>Sunday afternoon ride: Three climbs and some flower fields - Flower fields are spot‑on perfect! Dutch views always blow you away. Looks like our peloton leader is chilling for a few days after those massive climbs. 😁

> Hey, I didn’t forget the ChitChat question! Actually sneaked it into one of my posts, haha.
I also kept thinking about the whole debate around equipment and technological advances in sport — the pros and the cons. It’s not just a technical issue anymore, but also a philosophical and ethical one. This could be another post, or maybe part of next week’s initiative. What do you think?
Alright then, here we go!
How far do tech upgrades in sports gear change the game — making it richer or messing it up?
I cheekily used one of @vesytz’s pics for this post’s cover — hope that’s cool! And hey, with the idea we mentioned earlier, your shot could be the cover for the next #CyclingChitChat! ... Remember to use the hashtag #CyclingChitChat, and feel free to invite a friend to join in. That will help us connect with more people. You can reply in the comments on this post or even write a whole post about it… it’s your choice. We’ll be waiting for you. Catch you soon.

body.body: 1/4 🧵 The Giants trading Dexter Lawrence didn’t make a Kayvon Thibodeaux deal more likely — it did the opposite. If your defensive identity is the pass rush, gutting two core pieces at once would be absurd. Right now, Thibodeaux looks more likely to stay than go.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 2/4 🧵 The front office’s logic is pretty straightforward: they spent three years building the pass rush into the team’s backbone, and they’re not eager to blow it up overnight. Even with Abdul Carter and Brian Burns projecting as the starting edge duo, the Giants have reportedly been reluctant to move Thibodeaux. Teams have called since last season, but interest alone isn’t the same as a real offer.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 3/4 🧵 The contract piece matters here. Thibodeaux is on his fifth-year option and carries a $14.75 million cap hit for 2026, so this is basically a walk-year decision point. The Giants reportedly want at least a third-round pick, and that seems to be the sticking point — there’s no sign anyone has actually paid that price. Translation: they’ll listen, but they’re not in a rush to sell low.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body:
4/4 🧵 Performance is the reason this is even a conversation. He missed the final seven games last season with a shoulder injury, and after posting 11.5 sacks in 2023, he has just eight sacks across his last 22 games. Still, the article notes he’s become a better edge-setting run defender over time, so this isn’t a player whose value is only tied to sack totals. Bottom line: the Giants appear open to calls, but unless someone meets their price, Thibodeaux is staying put. 📎 Source

📎 [Source](https://nypost.com/2026/04/20/sports/where-giants-stand-on-potential-kayvon-thibodeaux-trade/)

body.title: Refreshing pineapple peel drink/ Bebida refrescante de cáscara de piña. [Eng/Esp]
body.body:
>


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRXNRB2Uc1YK6z5Sx5d7wS2YEiRakgPJXZ2BeEjfQjfCY/1776704226521.png)


**English:**


Hello friends of the Hive blockchain, I hope you're having a lovely weekend and that happiness smiles upon you all.

These days, with such hot weather and intense sun, we usually drink refreshing, pleasant, and cold beverages, but nothing beats natural juices, which provide the most benefits to the body.

To quench my thirst, I decided to make a refreshing \

which is made with pineapples—one or several, depending on what you have and how you plan to use the pulp.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUcEjzTeDTkNBsyYFdqcSDcVJknvoa9LHwKGf67dNUEAd/1776689736984.jpg)

This drink only requires water and the pineapple peels. Some people add raw rice, but I prefer its natural taste.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcvcARFaGynBNLfWZV3aK72bgVfxFhgghKt5kQan9a5XQ/1776689737178.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQk2XkcywZuqPKa3jj8TFBtLfncZLvs4SMGBfWzsTyCZX/1776689737290.jpg)

Place the peels in a pitcher or pot, add water until they are covered, then cover with a thin cloth or gauze and leave it outside the refrigerator for one day.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTjqvZnB24ebEYoxoFhWEbELUs37M6ujVPJ2RbhUxGpZw/1776689737452.jpg)

The next day, strain it, add sugar to taste, and chill it. You can garnish it with pineapple slices or simply drink it as is—very cold—it's very refreshing.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmW8BrdgyJwb8jED62HswajYDtqFWqpduCttvDVwp3PEv5/1776689779143.jpg)


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfAxZ25vsGChLipfmKMT9xumHrQqS1heHr19iDhGuf1ji/1776689779301.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWS957ashboW56D6jUXke4gzQuRhJioHFz6KtnHTAAezh/1776689779379.jpg)


According to taste, more water is added because sometimes it turns out too strong.

In other countries, this drink has other names, which I'm not familiar with.

I hope you really liked this recipe and that you feel encouraged to make it—you'll see how delicious it is. A hug to everyone. 🤗

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZujxZ54tbLuW2XMw6AjtMuk6XHRedpazdHrFETKKDLcJ/1776689779522.jpg)

° Text by me.
° Translation performed by DeepSeek.
° Photos taken with my Honor Play 10.

# Pineapple 


**Español:**


>Hola amigos de la blockchain Hive, espero que hoy estén pasando un lindo fin de semana y que la dicha les sonría a todos.

>En estos días tan caluroso y de intenso sol acostumbramos a tomar bebidas refrescantes, agradables y frías, pero nada como los jugos naturales que son los que más beneficios le aportan al organismo.

>Para calmar la sed me propuse hacer una refrescante garapiña, que se confecciona con piñas, ya sea una o varias, según lo que tengan y el uso que le dé a la pulpa.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUcEjzTeDTkNBsyYFdqcSDcVJknvoa9LHwKGf67dNUEAd/1776689736984.jpg)


>Esta bebida solo lleva agua y las cáscaras de la fruta, hay quienes le adicionan arroz crudo pero a mí me gusta más su sabor natural.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcvcARFaGynBNLfWZV3aK72bgVfxFhgghKt5kQan9a5XQ/1776689737178.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQk2XkcywZuqPKa3jj8TFBtLfncZLvs4SMGBfWzsTyCZX/1776689737290.jpg)


>Se ponen las cáscaras en una jarra o en una olla y se le adiciona agua hasta que las cubran, luego ponemos un paño fino o gasa encima y lo dejamos por un día fuera del refrigerador.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTjqvZnB24ebEYoxoFhWEbELUs37M6ujVPJ2RbhUxGpZw/1776689737452.jpg)


>Al día siguiente lo colamos, adicionamos azúcar al gusto y ponemos a enfriar. Puedes adornar con rodajas de piña o simplemente tomarlo así, bien frío, es muy refrescante.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmW8BrdgyJwb8jED62HswajYDtqFWqpduCttvDVwp3PEv5/1776689779143.jpg)


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfAxZ25vsGChLipfmKMT9xumHrQqS1heHr19iDhGuf1ji/1776689779301.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWS957ashboW56D6jUXke4gzQuRhJioHFz6KtnHTAAezh/1776689779379.jpg)


>Según el gusto se le adiciona más agua porque a veces queda muy fuerte.

>En otros países esta bebida tiene otros nombres, que yo no conozco.
Espero que esta receta les haya gustado mucho y que se animen a hacerla, verán que deliciosa. Un abrazo para todos 🤗

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZujxZ54tbLuW2XMw6AjtMuk6XHRedpazdHrFETKKDLcJ/1776689779522.jpg)

body.title: Online or Offline, Pain is Real: A Wake-Up Call on Bullying
body.body:
Bullying isn't something new it's been going on for a long time. It used to happen in different ways, but now the method has changed. Earlier, things used to happen mostly offline, but now everything is online. This is the big difference. See, many things change with time and this too has changed. Earlier, when I was in school, we used to hear that there is a lot of bowling in colleges and people are ragged. Sometimes children even commit suicide due to depression because they could not tolerate every situation and some people used to make them do such things for their entertainment which they had never even imagined. And this happens everywhere. You must have seen in many movies how some people make fun of those who are physically smaller than them. The movies we watch, the entertainment we see in our lives, in some way or another, reflect the society around us.



![bullying.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bhattg/23vsBVHCgZsXn9JwJRaQfgPfdUvfTiFbrBFq4Jf7GCU9EfDN2zRsK74t5rRD5GwG5KXaG.png)



[ImgSrc](ChatGpt.com)

Look, offline bullying used to happen a lot earlier or it still happens, it is not like that, many times we bully someone a lot just in fun and we do not even realize it. There are many platforms online where people bully each other or even bully a particular person. Many times it happens that a particular person is targeted and there have been many cases where people have committed suicide online due to being upset with all these things, it all starts with a joke and the FIR takes a much more serious form.



Whether it is any kind of exploitation, online or offline, it should not happen and strict action should be taken against both because see, today's generation spends a lot of their time in online things. Due to which they share a lot of their information online, in this way many people get harassed online or many friends are also made, some people maintain a very cigarette lifestyle and some people are not able to do so. People who keep their life very public face a lot of problems because sometimes they share some private moments, sometimes by mistake and sometimes their intention is such that they do so and after that people start following them.



![bullying  1.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bhattg/23u5ZPnNZwM6RfYmPM7AzcAJXdjWirG52gWkxY5TBQUerM28AecvztRbWiw8vrJQYccXd.png)



[ImgSrc](ChatGpt.com)

Look, they are popular faces, people consider them to be too ideal and no one wants them to get involved in all these things. Everyone has a private life and everyone has private moments, if they get exposed to the world then it creates a very wrong impact. And there should be rules for all these things as well. Because now harassment and other things have started happening a lot online due to which it is very important to make rules about what the police can do. If this is not done then it may cause a lot of trouble for the coming generation and the current youth.



See, troubling someone, be it online or offline, is not a good thing at all and you should keep all these things in mind and this is a serious crime in a way because you are troubling someone about their looks or anything else, which is not a good thing. If you are also involved in these things, then you should be a little cautious because it is possible that the same thing may be done to you someday, so you should be prepared for all these things. 
***You should treat people the way you want to be treated.***

body.body: I got lucky with a couple of the power down weeks crossing with close to highs, but truth is all I did was start a power down when we were spiking to a ridiculous high that made no logical sense. On average since I sold a lot and powered down for many weeks, the average both in late 2021 & January 2025, were well below the tops,  so maybe lucky on some level, but the move to sell was just common sense.  We were never going to stay above a dollar in 2021, & that pump to .68 15 months back had so many red flags it was artificial and not going to last.  I think many people just loose sight and get hype vibes and ignore doing what makes sense.  The signs were there.  We could have gone higher than .68 cents maybe for a week or so, but we were never going to sustained highs.  If we triple from here, start a power down immediately, because unless major changes happen, no way we sustain it!  That’s how u match what I did.

body.title: Pamilacan Uncovered: Part II 🌿
body.body:
![Blue and Beige Playful Beach Photo Collage (Portrait)_20260414_184133_0000.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jessmcwhite/23wqyUJGMhWGN4T6g8oTdE1x4CphXSCFFqTHRfihMn5TbmtJHgnAtc1P2d6xHSMY9Hc85.png)
**Hey guys, this will be the second part of my story and experience at Pamilacan, Island.**

![IMG_20260410_225229.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jessmcwhite/Eou6rqnubsSbgBqHwsbq3f8TTQwLX3ygAKmjY89cL6SArNhcUM5PkRGNLcTeUDjJgbk.jpg)
**It was around 3pm when we reached this hidden paradise of Pamilacan Island**, and the sunset is waving urging us to seize the moment, enjoy the time and chase the beautiful sunset soon.



![Messenger_creation_D17B8418-FE80-446E-8F5F-80458340D6B8.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jessmcwhite/Eptb4KBxvfAsd9Wdp5ccjs7kTJr3YDYgBXSqmYRa2GscDKSe8zFzSAQcjmE46HGRTde.jpeg)
*This photo was taken by Rachel I don't know what was the name of the camera she used but it looks like a digiCam.* **The capture looks good on me, just so beautiful!**

![Messenger_creation_C98662F8-EFA0-453F-BCB3-F490F3737DE9.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jessmcwhite/23uQvjzUpo4LcG8CD58JR2dZxtxtcmAbLy2LsPDukfyY5uFicN3ivoMnFzE9J5J1PFJXy.jpeg)
*If you can still remember I had my menstruation that very day so after a while of walk and exploring around the very long shore I got tired a bit and* **just wanted to sit down by the sand and just listen purely to the sound of the waves** but Rachel had my attention and took a photo of me while resting and so I give the best smile I can offer.

![IMG_20260414_130304.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jessmcwhite/245cWLYF46hy8g1wEWyDt8fTqqXtFbPkfTQPYNajNFRHKqdhPfKUQGpT5cvFaoGvtqRGE.jpg)
**Walking around was so fun, what we did is that we just walked on the shoreline to go back to our rented room and the very front or entrance of the Island what makes it interesting is that since it is low-tide that very moment we we're able to walk by the beach and the sunset was really stunning**.

![IMG_20260414_123157.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jessmcwhite/EpJZ9VfzEVoVozXYtugAT8G7a8KGEzKvJfnNvCCnyMh1McQWSF94vS9JF6rxykESVhU.jpg)
*Anddd we're almost there, the most awaited moment of chasing sunset my favorite moment.*

![IMG_20260414_130237.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jessmcwhite/EoyR13fWAXgvBJFvzVZ9fTyfWW83RQKYqThiH641eaBrT72s8j7QGXYqmEtDBmZmL9A.jpg)
After a long walk and amazing journey **I wanted to sit down here and feel the moment, the sound of the waves, the birds chirping** *and the sound of the surrounding as the day is about to end.*


![IMG_2260414_123016.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jessmcwhite/EpEHGxF63LcsPVFxKZpniC1VtvfuxF43xh3bE7RcKCJyzqZiL2HxhX4AfwN9g88qwfW.jpg)
**We have reached finally the beautiful spot of where the sun is setting.**

body.title: A BULLY IS A BULLY
body.body: When it comes to bullying I do not take it lightly, whether it is online or offline, I believe that everyone has the right to live freely without experiencing any form of bullying whether online or offline. I also believe that damages done emotionally take longer time to heal than some of the ones done physically. It is not easy enduring bullies and whenever I see someone using the power or position to intimidate others especially to the point of depriving them of their fundamental human right just because they feel that they can do it and get away with it, it gets me pissed off to my bones. I don’t just hate bullying, I hate everything bullies stand for, I even have the tendency to hate them and whenever I come across them, I do not avoid them, rather I find ways to make them suffer the same thing they do to others.\n\n

/> [Image by freepik](https://www.freepik.com/free-vector/stop-bullying-concept_9005183.htm#fromView=search&page=1&position=7&uuid=0d5b58e5-2719-4728-85dd-0bedc3099aaa&query=BULLYING) I remember one time back in school, I had a roommate who was very muscular and because he was in the military he was always trying to intimidate everyone in the hostel. For this reason I started making sure I dealt with him in ways he never saw coming. I really brought out the petty side of me as I would do everything to frustrate him especially when we had tests or exams. I would take his pen in the exam hall, make him go find or buy another one then drop it where he can see it, or take his fullscap sheet and make him right before a test starts and make him beg others only for him to find it afterwards. Sometimes when he cooks and tries to hide it I will intentionally find ways to let people know and before you know it, the hungry students are begging him. At a point I reported his theft to the school authorities anonymously after which he was expelled. For him I do not feel any regrets because he was one to beat up anyone who annoys him. One time he almost beat me if not for the fact that he knew I had connections in school. He preys on the weak, steals from almost everyone including the needy without remorse so yeah, he does deserve everything he got. When it comes to the online space however, it’s worse especially when the bully becomes a troll or has lots of followers and decides that they can ride on the weak. I hate these kinds of things, especially in a time when people use social media as a means of earning. You can not tell others to report a particular account because you do not like the owner of the account and you have your followers to back you up. Any form of bullying should be fought against, so long it preys on the weak, it should not be accepted. If we say cyber bullying isn’t physical, you will be surprised the number of people that have committed suicide because they could not take the toxicity of others. > THIS IS MY RESPONSE TO HIVE LEARNER'S > [PROMPT](https://discord.com/channels/928986840747372636/929001473231183873/1493873099085578271) FOR WEEK 214 EPISODE 1

body.title: A view from the top of a hill.
body.body:
A view from the top of a hill.

It's nice to stand on top of a hill and admire the beautiful scenery.

Living on a hill has many advantages, for one thing, the best views of sunrises and sunsets.

But that's not the only advantage of living on a hill. The cleanest water is usually found there, but you have to put up with some things, like the heat and winds.

Yes, sometimes, standing on my hill, where my plot is, at the top, sometimes I find a positive aspect of living in the floodplain of the river that flows at the foot of the hill, but far away. People there have more opportunities to raise waterfowl, and there's plenty of free pasture for livestock with lush meadow grass, something that's not available on the top of the hill.

But where there's no quacking, there might be gurgling grape juice, and I'm thinking of planting table grapes

![DSC01793.JPG](https://cdn.steemitimages.com/DQmV4EJHsZQbQcbsmVog78oJsgdCFnDZN934zwmuno88jzy/DSC01793.JPG)

Almost everything has its pros and cons, but even the cons can be turned into pros if I want. At the very least, living on a hilltop and unable to raise geese, I'll be able to sleep soundly and not worry about the floods one day inundating my entire yard, as happens periodically to those who live in river valleys.

![DSC01785.JPG](https://cdn.steemitimages.com/DQmUNDpQpzCJdBKeo214pyXjguhV1CHfycosS2TrP2cn5UH/DSC01785.JPG)

I once learned about some Koreans who leased orchards in Kazakhstan and planted carrots between the rows. These carrots, sliced ​​into thin noodles and seasoned with spices, became very popular and became known as \

These guys used the land very efficiently. I was curious about what could grow next to grapes and hoped that raspberry bushes could grow next to them and climb up a chain-link fence. But no, you can't plant raspberries next to grapes; they'll crowd each other out. But you can plant strawberries next to grapes; it's even beneficial, and the proximity improves the grapes' flavor. Now I'm thinking about how to implement this in practice :) ![DSC01688.JPG](https://cdn.steemitimages.com/DQmVopGLCy3byjWhgeRJqREM9z1ZhuJCGYqeye3FBrkkk9V/DSC01688.JPG) --- Below you can see my containers with data that I collect in INLEO and always have quick access to them it is very convenient. links.title: Part 2: A Coffee with a View and My Honest Food Review in Mecca
links.body:
After my first few days of prayer and reflection in Mecca, I started to discover the daily life around the Holy Mosque. Many people focus only on the religious side, but there is also a very modern and social side to Mecca that I found very interesting. I want to tell you about two specific experiences: a beautiful cafe visit and my dinner at the most famous fast-food chain in the country.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcevHwYh8eFFqUfkALcvhzxXJ8kTVGv9E62XTPyqZ6aSE/img_0493.jpg)


**A Sanctuary with a View: The Holy Cafe**

In Mecca, the heat and the crowds can be very intense. Sometimes, you need a place to sit quietly and just process everything you are seeing. I found a cafe that felt like a hidden gem. It was located very close to the Masjid al-Haram. In fact, it was so close that when I sat down at my table, I was looking directly at the walls of the Kaaba.
The interior of the cafe was very modern and stylish. It had large glass windows that offered a panoramic view of the holy area. Sitting there with a hot drink in my hand, watching the thousands of people circling the Kaaba, was a very emotional experience. It made me realize how small we are in this world, yet how connected we all are.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWu6MfUjoFXJ1CorgypAV9goysYFbvorfsj3c9hrDHopo/img_0183.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZwQwFX2nfZyeGBeGho9NiqrPVjzn46mhkuWfSfBTWmn1/img_0184.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfHZq6EMj7gULuikBdfMDc2JHn31wX59SGCMok3YfEryg/img_0185.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbtorwavhjJTz9kmX6pGA64KA4VCU6jwYuUjuBdPtxRoC/img_0197.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUwYNtZqPLT1cov5n7V5DadxuQx2rNytX5FL3iv8ZQMcA/img_0199.jpg)


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTTePwnxPHo3XJ3BoRh4QnyeBQYwXpckG4rz5o6NTvyQd/img_0485.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQma3XHnqyBrY1quV523Dy2DaYkG29TZHreWegG6NGTAF7z/img_0486.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmY1d3vyvkTiqyFKCkjEB8caBM6yLLofbGEAZxdnF1nTCC/img_0487.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWpzLgzm5RvLh5mEPoFxZWTrphmkTeX9xDWToq3hcRDio/img_0488.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVkM1hNcHUAPprBu3Fhd6w6BLrgP7Zc8jGxbdFAUoSs6g/img_0489.jpg)


One of the best things about this cafe was the price. Usually, when you go to a place with the \

you expect to pay a lot of money. However, in this cafe, the prices were very reasonable. I shared some photos of the menu so you can see for yourselves. It wasn't just a place to drink coffee; it was a place to find peace while staying connected to the heart of the city. I spent a long time there, just observing the architecture and the movement of the crowd. It was much better than staying in the hotel room because even while resting, I was still part of the atmosphere.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQme6J89swfD29isj1MEgewuSpoe8m78qDLqLaejWd5GboQ/img_0188.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXZwDwSTrrN3Rn4Luovgqe2HRis8HEjPCzqYUXupYiBqe/img_0190.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRVreLywbTkXwXp8jDNSEcBsd8JQhEk3MjiyEVfumQm3S/img_0191.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmefoJPtmdf7ew29kdKCFkSPTGkLzv4tSfjkx5Ye9rDWpD/img_0186.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeaZhfMEZ1zau1N8xVeBueuHNiRhgVRtMRaGeKoSGqS18/img_0195.jpg)


**The Al Baik Mystery: Is It Really That Good?**

If you ask anyone in Saudi Arabia where to eat, they will tell you \

It is a legendary fast-food brand here. People wait in long lines, and everyone talks about it like it is the best chicken in the world. Naturally, I was very curious. I had to try it.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmafHEg598bqhc99ggZjWiGWXsCHtwqECzA1wpkTejxpMX/img_0349.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQM6tVXiBDPDvKSH6V6dUZDyyidRjReLWVFipAhxeExzQ/img_0350.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNYcNydcvPkjbPGzzDfn5oG62DbSV4aNcnCW2mvGDP8dR/img_0351.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNad1Jja138ewKnS5HKPzmrc2FNY3suqaXLwtGqcSo3Z4/img_0352.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZRpJoNZu6Y7QK8bj5v1FYVY13epCuwHSGE3RRwnFaUhn/img_0354.jpg)


When I arrived at the Al Baik branch, the first thing I noticed was the organization. The culture here is very different from Turkey or Europe. There are completely separate sections for men and women to order. As a woman, I went to the ladies' section to get my food. It was very crowded, which made me think, \

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNM4PzaFD6zYRACcMifkDKYX7qrTABFeWgA6iEQUfGEA8/img_0373.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRwwED1wFo6DubWCprxwQ4reK5N8pkJT2EYEAnbxSgNJQ/img_0374.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfLDsizrhY2k6TQyWEHpB5kzW5Ku8A6TwoqGYwcAYKcx5/img_0372.jpg)


However, when I finally got my food, I was a little disappointed. To be very honest with you, it tasted like a normal chicken nugget. It was good and fresh, but it wasn't the \

taste I was expecting. I think it might be a bit overrated because of the fame.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNVFhh9G65p8CSqAVrNwToPYgEXb4DBeBH4kfmpr1ZoUv/img_0673.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVJt6ZNDsioZH95P5dTTYG1LCW2VMXycuqxSnvbdQEpxG/img_0672.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmesZcfzoEjs1td7PetNEHjFJVxpgz4j5kmaGDdZoz4Gn6/img_0671.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcNxSkBZpk6WwfTS7iKJEBbCkyhxne59hEzcEqGHumTp6/img_0678.jpg)


The way they serve the food was the most interesting part for me. In most places, if you order a meal, it comes as a sandwich or everything is in one box. At Al Baik, they give you everything separately. They give you the chicken nuggets in one package, the bread rolls in another, the French fries in another, and the garlic sauce in a separate container. It’s like a DIY (Do It Yourself) meal. You have to put it together or eat them one by one. It was a very different fast-food experience. While I didn't find the taste to be life-changing, I'm glad I tried it because it is such a huge part of the local culture in Mecca and Medina.

**Reflections on Local Life**

Being in Mecca taught me that life there is a balance. You have the most sacred place on Earth at the center, but right next to it, you have modern cafes, shopping malls, and busy restaurants.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYFZo9kgcdLMDxKW5FNdi7ddmWDjpLTC1RJzCEY26o7MW/img_0375.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRvPxZnS7AzpakdseAx9t2UKXyHG4zf7x8opfTBDsx8u8/img_0363.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZkpaMd7rzBBuehoZ8bz8dekHEEqnkjjokhkzR8QWX3Tj/img_0358.jpg)


I preferred spending my time in these public spaces rather than sitting in the hotel. Even though the hotels are very nice and comfortable, they feel isolated. By sitting in that cafe or visiting a local restaurant like Al Baik, I felt more connected to the people. I enjoyed watching families from different countries eating together and pilgrims from all over the world taking a break.

Mecca is a city that never sleeps. Whether it is 3:00 AM or 3:00 PM, the streets are full, the cafes are open, and the energy is high. This energy is what allowed me to survive on only 3 or 4 hours of sleep. You don't want to miss a single moment.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmU7gW2thjWPsrgvr9iuFSqEDmRE8PBSXoGQEjvJuTWt8R/img_0273.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXtdKWHTdV4vtEZ3DkdEatQJrqLWWR66fLPyYNXdrCDup/img_0532.jpg)


In my next post, I will take you with me to Medina. The vibe there is completely different—much more quiet and peaceful. But for now, I will cherish these memories of the busy, magnificent, and surprising streets of Mecca. Thank you for following my journey!

links.title: MOVIE REVIEW - BEHIND THE SCENES
links.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWuJd9cCX8P4CCwp4CEdPH3MVSGKvPUAptA8Z7B3SY48D/1776702566475.jpg)


‎In some lands, it is viewed that when one of the family members is wealthy he or she MUST carry all the problems \

in the family and such a person MUST help every member of the family. 
‎

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcakF21HGKhoTVXe1seR2KRKpHrZviofNUnxU8oyfGYkL/1776702619177.jpg)

‎Behind The Scene is a story of a successful real estate entrepreneur and widow Aderonke \

Faniran, also a mother of two (Tife and Tola), with her Elder Adetutu,  young brother Adewale (His wife Segilola), her friends Mariam, Wendy and her bestie & Lawyer Victor.
‎

‎Ronke is her family’s financial backbone  she is selfless and generous that she put everyone else’s needs above her own. She funded her siblings’ education, supports her father and nieces.
‎
‎Aderonke supported her sister Adetutu who was so loud, manipulative, and dependent. Years earlier, Ronke deferred her own education so Adetutu could attend school, only for Adetutu to get pregnant and abandon it, leaving Ronke to carry the responsibilities. Aderonke always gives Adetutu money for her business and twins school fees. 
‎
‎
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQQ843q9EK8W7GC3kSeR2WpW6uzoYGTdeB3fM1sLgZYwv/1776702652401.jpg)

‎
‎Adetutu squandered the money meant for her twins Taiwo and Kehinde school fees at her bestie party Alero and was arrested by FCTF for abuse and mutilation of national currency.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdC4nfcGCyWWbsep9c3okHYT1pcTKqy2TkjZov2MdweiD/1776702687394.jpg)


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmP8pWDkeZRpb6MR9kfx6pkNxr7GXmaNtE5t6XrhvuquLW/1776702724685.jpg)

‎
‎Her brother Adewale, is also exploitative. He takes advantage of Ronke's generosity to extort money from her. Adewale always squanders the money at the clubhouse. Ronke given Adewale money more than 4 times for his business (content creator) yet he squandered it. Adewale' wife Segilola who begged for everything equally uses her son Diola to extort money from Ronke. Yet she is willing to give.
‎

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQLASKUmvNiKCR4MLqTWd43mTYHbjN2zgTYLx8amREzvf/1776702766364.jpg)


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUpf4czorpg9jfeJTqxyTYNvQYhp3SNHAhU59kPQ6Su1L/1776702787497.jpg)


‎Ronke even covered salaries for employees at a friend’s struggling company (Mariam) who always wants to be like Ronke. To the extent Mariam arranged with the local people to extort money from Ronke by placing died bodies in one of her site which cost Aderonke a lot of money (N220 million).


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaN1nK1FLWAe7ff2V8pCmEqn6B9KYCXmbcgu6MiA8s8QK/1776702848398.jpg)


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNSn21Um7ZKnJ3JP23vkToCmNVFcb7eyhPDBvsKaEBqz7/1776702953009.jpg)

‎
‎As Ronke extends her generosity to family members, friends, employees, and even strangers, the stress begins to accumulate. She gradually realizes that those she has supported may not reciprocate the same loyalty. A personal tragedy (when she was diagnosed with lupus) makes her confront the emotional and financial act of her selflessness. This crucial moment triggers a long-overdue judgement that changes how she sees the people around her.
‎

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdqaruEP2JNW2RzH81FnPptJk9FgVTGxvvo4AUSJ3ef2Y/1776702995756.jpg)


‎Ronke faked her death with her bestie Victor and his wife. She placed CCTV in all corners of her house. With her bestie Victor and his wife she was able to accomplish her plains.


![](Uploading... 1776703182113.jpg)


 It was then she realized that her sister Adetutu was only after her wealth. While her brother Adewale realizes how important his sister is to the family vow to look after his sister's children and to protect their mothers wealth for them. And her friends Wendy and Mariam do not care about their friends children.  
‎

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXvnX7ZzPufgW3sGezeJ4Eok4kZk8bqaMpDCYyfQChGsy/1776703058196.jpg)


‎Johnson her cook and children's nanny Oluchi never for once forgot their boss children. She was able to know those who truly appreciate her generosity, and willing to look after her children when she is no more. 

‎
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYuVM94zHZN4Hj6PnjXKskCeDVWcua55xR68ET35opQaq/1776703223908.jpg)
(All pix were taken with my phone)

‎Johnson her cook and Oluchi her children's nanny and her brother Adewale were the ones who never forgot her generosity. 
‎
‎Adetutu and her children along with Segilola Adewale's wife and her driver were only after Ronke's wealth. 
‎
‎What is your view. Do well to watch this movie and write your review.
‎
‎
‎
‎

links.title: My Actifit Report Card: April 19 2026
links.body:
It was a hoo hum sort of day as we are just a week away from our drive back up to South Dakota for the volunteer season. A nice 4 miles on my local trails route early in the day to avoid the increasingly warm weather for a start. ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/b3709325-2c49-44da-b6cb-103f525f1ea0.jpg) Always so much better when my feet are on the dirt and soon enough I'll be trotting along on the soft dirt around Spearfish. Lots of small wildflowers are popping up taking advantage of the mild Spring days before the serious summer heat arrives and I am also happy to take advantage of these conditions while I'm here- makes my running a lot better. ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/18dd673b-e0ef-4aae-8777-a04bb23086c5.jpg) Later in the afternoon I drove a bit up into the foothills for a very nice 4 mile trail loop with just myself and Mother Nature. Nothing like a relaxed but somewhat tough hike along these dusty trails. ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/d3aea691-d4da-4dbf-9a8f-54904cecf046.jpg) ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/30c3c10f-7b82-4ede-b96a-191515c2d90c.jpg) While my pace was only around 3 mph (the narrow and often rocky route can be a bit tricky) my heart rate was consistently in a good cardio range and I was working up a decent sweat. Wide open vistas and wonderful scenery makes these trails really great although I like the more forested trails around Prescott and Flagstaff a lot more. ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/382c7383-6860-47d6-b6cf-b51124f54e34.jpg) Time to pack up some more. See you all tomorrow.
