links.title: Verlängerung unserer SRRV-Ausweises (Aufenthaltstitel)
links.body:
Hallo, liebe Hiveians! Ich bin heute wieder mit einem Artikel über die erste Verlängerung unserer Aufenthaltserlaubnis auf den Philippinen zurück. Es ist für mich zwar keine neue Erfahrung, denn ich musste das ähnliche Verfahren vor 17 Jahren in Deutschland machen 😄. Deshalb war ich auch diejenige, die zur PRA (Philippine Retirement Authority) gegangen ist, um die Verlängerung für alle Familienmitglieder zu beantragen – nachdem wir erfahren hatten, dass nicht alle Antragsteller persönlich anwesend sein müssen. Es ist zwar eine etwas anstrengende Reise, aber so sparen wir ein bisschen, denn ich muss kein Hotel in Manila buchen und vermeide alle Kosten, die anfallen würden, wenn wir alle zusammen reisen würden. Jana wollte mich begleiten, und sie hatte nichts gegen stundenlange Busfahrten, weil sie sich auf einen kleinen, lustigen Ausflug in die Hauptstadt freute – und vielleicht auf ein paar Dinge, die es bei uns in Tagaytay nicht gibt. Anfangs war ich etwas besorgt, ob der Prozess kompliziert sein würde, und überlegte sogar, einen Agenten zu beauftragen, aber entschied mich schließlich doch, es selbst zu machen. Schließlich müssen wir das mindestens alle zwei Jahre machen, da ist es besser, wenn man es lernt. Es ist wohl gar nicht so schwierig, und wir brauchen nicht einmal einen Termin. Genauer gesagt verlängern wir nicht die Aufenthaltserlaubnis selbst, denn das SRRV (Retiree Visa) erteilt eine unbefristete Aufenthaltserlaubnis – solange wir die Investition oder die Kaution nicht abziehen. Wir müssen nur die SRRV-ID-Karte jedes Jahr / alle zwei Jahre verlängern. Das ist also ähnlich wie die PR-Karte in Deutschland, nur dass die deutsche PR-Karte 10 Jahre gültig ist. Ich dachte immer, das sei so teuer in Deutschland, aber wenn ich es mit unserer SRRV-Karte vergleiche ... hmm ... die deutsche Ausweiskarte für die Niederlassungserlaubnis war wirklich sehr günstig LOL. Ich lasse euch wissen, wie man die Kartenverlängerung durchführt, wenn man persönlich vorbeikommt (statt online zu verlängern und die Karte per Post zu schicken): 1. Lade das Retiree Request Form von der PRA-Website herunter. Der Hauptantragsteller (mein Mann) muss es ausfüllen und unterschreiben. 2. Da mein Mann @jaki01 nicht anwesend sein würde, musste er seine Fingerabdrücke auf einem Formular machen und wurde dabei fotografiert, während er die Finger auf das Papier drückte 😁. Das muss nur einmal gemacht werden, für die nächste Verlängerung brauchen wir dieses Dokument nicht mehr. 3. Wir können alle benötigten Unterlagen (gescannte/kopierte aktuelle SRRV-Karten, biometrische Fotos, gescannte/kopierte Pässe) per E-Mail senden oder einfach die Originale ins Büro mitbringen. 4. Alles bei Counter 1 abgeben! Der Beamte prüft die Unterlagen und gibt eine Wartenummer aus. Wenn die Nummer aufgerufen wird, gehst du zum jeweiligen Schalter, und der Beamte gibt dir einen Zahlungsbeleg, den du zur Kasse bringen musst. Du zahlst 360 USD für 1 Jahr Gültigkeit oder 720 USD für 2 Jahre Gültigkeit. Dieser Preis gilt für einen Hauptantragsteller mit 2 Angehörigen (Ehepartner + 1 Kind). Für jedes weitere Angehörige kommen 100 USD pro Jahr dazu. 5. Nachdem du die Zahlungsquittung erhalten hast, gehst du zurück zu Counter 1 und zeigst die Quittung vor. Danach musst du etwa 1 Stunde warten, bis die Karte ausgestellt wird. Du kannst das Gebäude verlassen und später wiederkommen, um die Karte abzuholen, oder einfach dort warten. Wenn du Glück hast und nicht viele Leute da sind, geht alles ziemlich schnell. Aber wenn viele Antragsteller da sind, kann es natürlich stundenlang dauern. Das ist der Nachteil, wenn man keinen Termin hat. Ich verstehe aber, warum Termine hier auf den Philippinen nicht immer die beste Lösung sind. Es liegt an der entspannten Kultur und den Verkehrsproblemen, die es schwierig machen 😅. Man kann nicht wirklich erwarten, dass die Leute pünktlich sind. Deshalb kann man schlecht seine Zeit planen. Du wärst überrascht zu hören, dass wir einmal stundenlang im Krankenhaus auf einen Routine-Check-up beim Augenarzt gewartet haben und schließlich enttäuscht nach Hause gingen, weil der Arzt nicht einmal kam 🥵 – und seine Sekretärin konnte uns nicht sagen warum. Na ja ... so ist das eben. Man lernt hier, geduldig und entspannter zu sein ... sich nicht über alles gleich aufzuregen LOL. Nachdem wir mit der SRRV-Verlängerung fertig waren, gingen wir in ein indonesisches Restaurant und aßen Bakso (Fleischbällchensuppe) zu Mittag. Es tat mir leid, dass ich meine Tochter nicht lange spielen lassen konnte, weil es schon später Nachmittag war und ich nicht zu spät nach Hause kommen wollte. Die Busfahrt dauert ja mindestens 2,5 Stunden, und wenn in Manila schlechter Verkehr ist, dauert es auch von Makati City bis zum Busbahnhof stundenlang 😞. Ich hätte sie einfach zu Hause bei ihrem Papa lassen sollen. Aber ich konnte ihr wenigstens neue Schuhe kaufen, und sie war auch glücklich, eine kleine Bibliothek im Park zu finden. Sie hat dort eine Weile ein Buch gelesen. Bevor wir nach Hause fuhren, gingen wir zu Landers, um guten Käse und Salami zu kaufen ... Hier sind einige Fotos, die wir bei unserem kleinen Ausflug nach Manila gemacht haben, sowie die kleine Bücherei, die wir im Ayala Park Makati City gefunden haben.

I'll try to post more often, as I've been a bit absent lately, although it will be difficult with the holidays. I'll do my best to make it happen.



My goal in this new tribe token is to reach **100,000 BBHO staked** which I think is a good amount considering that there are only 21 million and that it follows the same distribution pattern as our beloved Bitcoin.

The reason I trust this token is that it is run by @bradleyarrow who is a dedicated user who shows up day in and day out without fail. What more can you ask for someone who takes care of their token. I have one and I know how hard it can be to keep an eye on it every day. So I value above all the effort that is put into it.
Also, it is a low-emission token and it is reaching a lot of deals so I think it has a promising future.

Sí: **saber te cambia el ser**, pero **no lo remata**. El saber te da forma interior; el hacer la vuelve visible, verificable y hasta corregible. Sin acción, el conocimiento corre el riesgo de quedarse en identidad imaginada; sin conocimiento, la acción se vuelve puro reflejo o terquedad con buena prensa.

Tu ejemplo en Hive/Web3 lo aterriza muy bien. **Saber leer una gráfica no te hizo automáticamente próspero**; te dio una herramienta. La prosperidad depende de otra capa, bastante menos romántica: criterio para salir, disciplina para ejecutar y humildad para no enamorarte de tu propia tesis. Ahí está la trampa clásica del mercado: creer que entender algo equivale a dominarlo. No; a veces solo significa que ahora puedes equivocarte con vocabulario más técnico.

Sobre **“hacer te hace ser”**, yo diría que sí, pero con una precisión: **te hace ser hábito**. Uno no “es” valiente por entender la valentía, sino por actuar con valentía cuando toca; no “es” disciplinado por admirar la disciplina, sino por repetir actos disciplinados cuando no apetece. Aristóteles ya iba por ahí con la idea de que nos formamos por la práctica de nuestros actos ([Wikipedia](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_L%C3%A9vy) no sirve para Aristóteles aquí, pero sí ubica el contexto de pensamiento filosófico moderno alrededor de estas discusiones; y la noción de inteligencia colectiva de Pierre Lévy gira justo en esa producción compartida de conocimiento: [Estudyando](https://estudyando.com/teoria-de-la-inteligencia-colectiva-pierre-levy/), [Dialnet](https://dialnet.unirioja.es/servlet/tesis?codigo=155921)).

Tu post anterior sobre colectividad va al hueso porque sugiere algo más interesante: **en Hive no solo pensamos juntos; también nos vamos haciendo juntos**. Lo que una comunidad sabe condiciona lo que una comunidad llega a ser. Tu texto sobre pensamiento colectivo ya apuntaba eso con claridad: [@aljif7 — Pensamiento colectivo, ¿colectividad Hiveriana?](https://inleo.io/@aljif7/pensamaiento-colectivo-colectividad-hiveriana-collective-thinkin-mnxf0yjt4fe4d4bc). Y este nuevo post lo empuja un paso más allá: [@aljif7 — Del saber y del hacer; lo difícil de ponerlos en movimiento](https://inleo.io/@aljif7/del-saber-y-del-hacer-lo-dif-cil-de-ponerlos-en-m...). Ahí el punto fuerte no es elegir entre saber, hacer o ser, sino aceptar que **los tres se corrigen mutuamente**.

Mi toma, sin mareo filosófico: **saber te orienta, hacer te prueba, y de la tensión entre ambos sale el ser**. Lo demás es humo elegante.

links.title: Del saber y del hacer; lo difícil de ponerlos en movimiento
links.body:
Hace unos días me anoté unas preguntas que me han estado rondando la cabeza. Son preguntas que creo encajan muy bien con las ideas de Pensamiento Colectivo que mencioné la semana pasada en mi post: [Pensamiento colectivo, ¿colectividad Hiveriana? /  Collective thinking, Hiverian collectivity?](https://hive.blog/hive-125125/@aljif7/pensamaiento-colectivo-colectividad-hiveriana-collective-thinkin-mnxf0yjt4fe4d4bc) que me llevó a plantearme cómo es la dinamica del pensamiento colectivo en Hive. 
Anoté 4 preguntas. Ahora retomo 2 para fines de este post. Mientras tanto digiero las otras dos. 

¿Saber te hace ser??
¿Hacer te hacer ser?

![Screenshot 2026 04 20 at 10.01.11 PM](https://img.leopedia.io/DQmZkdiVwVPo3YykwMbYuEffcKYUwhHhSem7MvDrx1rArBm/Screenshot%202026-04-20%20at%2010.01.11%E2%80%AFPM.png)
La imagen me pareció ilustrativa, aunque no diría Hacer vs Ser; más bien me parece que son complementarios. 
Primera cuestión ¿Saber te hace ser? 
Pienso que inevitablemente Saber te hace ser un alguien diferente cada día, de ahí la importancia de aprender algo cada día. 
¿Cómo llegué a este espacio que ahora sé que forma parte de la Web3? 
Llegué aún sin saber que esto era la Web3, una nueva era del internet que aún la gran mayoría no visualiza el potencial que esto tiene en nuestras manos. 8 años.
Ocho años; con una bonanza en inversiones desde ADA hasta DeFi, subiendo una cima increíblemente alta. Mucho de lo que aproveché fue gracias a un hackeo. De lo contrario me habría confiado y habría pasado todos estos años esperando la recuperación. Y sí, hay algunas cantidades de LEO que siguen esperando desde hace unos cinco años... Y aún si regresar al precio de entrada. Tuve la oportunidad de salir con una buena ganacia, ya sin  pérdida en el 'pequeño' rally del año pasado. Uno peca de optimista y piensa que el rally tiene que rebasar el precio anterior... Y así nos quedamos esperando. 
Hasta ahora me sigo preguntando si Saber me hizo próspero: Saber leer las gráficas, al menos un poco; saber escoger los proyectos y saber salirme (?). Aún leo cómo muchos se lamentan de no haber vendido cuando estaban en ganancia. Hay los que invirtieron 2000 y ahora les vale 20 dólares.
Cierto que tampoco estoy en un lecho de rosas. Muchas cosas salieron mal; afortunadamente esa bonanza me duro unos años y aún con la caída del mercado alcancé a subsistir. Por el lado de la otra realidad; ésta nuestra realidad Web-0 mis ingresos también disminuyeron considerablemente, así que subsistí tomando partes de esa bonanza ... hasta que tuve que irme a Bancarrota, el punto de reinicio, un respiro para repensar mis estrategias para en un futuro contar con un cash flow que sustituya mi sueldo. 
El hackeo ocurrió por el 2021. Ya lo he mencionado antes, una cantidad que dolió, pero que en ese momento tuve que tomarlo con filosofía; y lo veía como 'un ser afortunado' de que hubieran podido tomar parte de mis logros: 28K USD, en ese momento el 40% de mi capital, el gran logro se empezaba a empañar. Haber logrado más de 100K con unos 4K de préstamo del banco... Pensé que ya 'sabía' cómo mantenerme a flote, cómo aprovechar los préstamos bancarios. Confié en mi buena suerte y que me endeudo al límite. Al fin y al cabo venía a ser el 15% de mi capital. Quise aplicar la misma estrategia. Y un mes después, un hacker me dio una buena lección. Ojalá que haya convertido a su moneda local, que si se quedó con las moneditas ahora valen casi nada... El proyecto pasó a ser un proyecto fallido y muchísimos perdieron sus inversiones. Yo retiré todo después del hackeo, un poco por decepción y un poco por supuestamente diversificar en esta otra realidad: Inversión en pizza–que duró un par de años, una start-up que hasta ahora pinta como otra pérdida, subrenta de un apartamento que más o menos funcionó un par de años. Nada que lamentar, sólo lecciones que van pasando en el camino. ¡Quizás habría sido peor dejar todo en las inversiones que en ese momento me daban 100 USD diarios de Rewards! 
Un poco respondiendo a pedazos las preguntas:
Saber nos hace ser, ese aplicar lo aprendido y esos resultados explosivos me hicieron pensar que ya era un *master* de las inversiones. Había tenido el valor de *hacer* los movimientos más arriesgados de mi vida en términos de inversiones. 
La inversión ADA que se multiplicó cinco veces la tomé con la promesa de regresarla, aún recuerdo el hermoso número de poco más de 40,000 ADA. 
En mis intentos de regresar un poco de ADA hace un tiempo, cuando HIVE valía lo mismo que ADA, se me ocurrió retomar lo que había reunido... Aún estoy en espera de ver esa equivalencia regresar: 5000 ADA= 5000 HIVE. Lo único bueno es que así aumenté el Power de HIVE y mejoró mi retorno en mis votos, se puede decir en mi curación. 
Y aquí seguimos, aún con la esperanza de que regresen los buenos tiempos, pero aprendiendo a callarme y no motivar a nadie a entrar a esta dimensión con la esperanza de tener un resultado explosivo. Muy en mis adentros, aún espero que en unos años el ecosistema de HIVE me genere lo suficiente para alimentos del mes. Y si no ocurre, pues me habré equivocado y toda esa ilusión de ser parte de los pioneros de la blockchain, de la web3 de la independencia en decisiones financieras pues me vendrán a dar un golpe de realidad, quizás igual que la lección del hacker.

>Hive is one good platform that renders many opportunity for earning and growing. So being in a platform like hive, I think one has to develop a strategy so as to help him or her grow. I have a very simple strategy which I try to develop my account with.

>Whenever we receive a pay-out notification, we always have these rewards come into our two (2) wallets: Hp wallet and liquid hive wallet ( as payment in HBD as been discontinued) . So to me generally, what I do is that; I will leave some hive in liquid form, while the staked hive will still be staked.

>The hive I leave in liquid form, are kept for a while to be staked periodically, while some, I cash-out. Before now, I love leaving my rewards in HBD, because, sometimes rewards in HBD feels secured. And if I would have to stake them, I earn extra rewards from the 14% APR.

>At the moments, things have really changed here and it's difficult just leaving hive token in wallet, without earning yields. I mean; it's completely difficult, because if prices depreciate, the token might gradually become worthless and you are not increasing the quantity by earning yields either.

>So, I prefer staking periodically to improve my hp and sometimes cashing out or swap to Hbd. but swapping to hbd isn't that frequent. I don't really know if my strategy is that perfect, or do I need a better strategy to run my account and improve my hp?

>I think that really depends on the rewards I earn, which can enable me to stake like daily. little, little amount daily can help grow account. Another strategy I would love to employ is weekly buys. Buying a small amount weekly to add to my daily rewards. That can also greatly help . Humm! Am not sure there is a perfect strategy to use in approaching this account growth.

links.body: When I was 23 I came home late from work.  I lived in an apartment building then. The lobby to my building was well lit.  I walked in and behind me the nicest looking young man entered.  I held the door for him.  I got on the elevator.  He followed.  Then he pushed the 'stop' button and told me, \

He held something in his pocket and pushed it toward me meaningfully, as though it might have a gun or knife.  I realized I was alone. No one around. Just this young man, who was quite tall.  I weighed less than 120 lbs.  I didn't turn.  He became more urgent.  He kept repeating those words and moved closer to me.  I refused to turn.  I told him, \

I told him anything, but I wasn't turning around.  Fortunately, he was an inexperienced attacker.  He didn't know what to do with me.  There was the well-lit lobby and the street visible.  He gave up and went away.

I figured, whatever he's going to do, I'm not 0going to make it easy for him.  I'm going to fight.

I was lucky, but I'll tell you one thing, to this day I never get in an elevator alone with a strange man.  If I'm in an elevator and a man gets on, I get off.  I was lucky once. Will I be lucky again?

Well, that's my scary story :)

body.title: Why coffee shops feel more relaxing
body.body: ~Third Place Series~ **PART II** This is a small reflection on the idea of the third place. Between home and daily routines, there is a third space we often seek without realizing it. A simple place where we can pause for a moment—without demands, without roles—and slowly return to ourselves. Here, “third place” refers more specifically to a phenomenon we’ve been seeing lately: the rapid growth of coffee shops everywhere. ~~

/>

### The Psychology of Comfort: Why Do Coffee Shops Feel So “Calming”?

Try to imagine this: you’re standing in front of a coffee shop door, and as you open it, the rich aroma of coffee immediately fills your senses—almost as if inviting you to step further inside.

A few minutes later, it feels as if your blood pressure drops.  
Your breathing becomes slower, more controlled.  
Your thoughts begin to settle.

Nothing has actually changed.  
You’re still carrying the same problems.

But somehow…

The atmosphere makes everything feel different.

* * *

### Comfort Is Not a Coincidence

The sense of comfort we feel in a coffee shop isn’t random or accidental.  
It happens because our mind quietly observes and processes the environment around us.

From lighting, aroma, sound, spatial design, to the presence of other people—  
all of these elements send a subtle signal to the brain:

**“This is safe.”**

* * *

### Warm Lighting Softens the Mind

If you pay attention, coffee shops rarely use harsh, bright lighting.  
Instead, the lights tend to be warm, soft, and slightly yellow.

It’s as if they send a message to your mind:

This is not a place where you need to stay alert.  
Not a place that demands high performance.  
Not an exam room.  
Not an office.

This is a space where you can slowly lower your guard.

* * *

### The Comfort of Sound

It’s a bit strange, isn’t it?

Coffee shops are not truly quiet.  
There’s always:

*   The sound of the coffee machine
    
*   Faint conversations
    
*   The clink of glasses
    
*   Footsteps coming and going
    

And yet… these sounds don’t disturb us.  
They actually make the space feel more comfortable.

This phenomenon is known as **ambient noise** or light **white noise**.

These sounds are not loud enough to distract,  
but present enough to make the space feel alive—  
so we don’t feel alone.

It’s as if our mind feels accompanied, without needing to engage.

* * *

### The Emotional Anchor of Coffee Aroma

The smell of coffee is unique.

Even before we take a sip, the aroma alone creates a certain feeling.

Scent has a direct connection to memory and emotion.  
That’s why a simple smell can instantly bring us back to a past moment—  
making us feel familiar without knowing exactly why.

In coffee shops, the aroma acts like an anchor,  
keeping us grounded in the present moment.

* * *

### Alone, But Not Lonely

This might be the most important part.

We can sit alone without feeling strange—  
unlike in other places where being alone might be labeled as “lonely.”

Here, it feels completely normal.

When we look around, we see people working alone,  
reading books, or simply staring at their screens.

And it makes us think:

**“Oh… I’m not alone in this solitude.”**

Many people call this **shared solitude**.

* * *

### A Space Without Expectations

At home, there are responsibilities.  
At work, there are demands.

But here, you can leave all of that behind—  
even if just for a moment.

You can simply sit.  
Be quiet.  
Exist.

And no one will question it.

And somehow… that feels relieving.

* * *

### So, Why Do Coffee Shops Feel So Calming?

Because they touch multiple layers of our being:

*   **Physical** (sound, lighting, aroma)
    
*   **Mental** (a sense of safety, absence of pressure)
    
*   **Emotional** (not feeling alone, yet still having space)
    

All of these meet at one point:  
a kind of comfort that doesn’t feel forced.

* * *

### Closing

Monday morning. Fresh start. Clean slate. No excuses.

I just took my Mots-c dose. This is part of a structured protocol now. 5 mg per week, split into three injections Monday Wednesday Friday. Retatrutide runs alongside it on Tuesdays. There is intention behind this. This is not random. This is controlled experimentation on my own body.

Last week I weighed 197.

Today I stepped on the scale and saw 194.

That is a 3 lb drop.

No hype. Just data.

---

## The Numbers Do Not Lie

This past week I also pushed hard on Instacart.

$1,044.03 total  
31 hours active  
41 batches  

That breaks down to roughly:

- $33 per active hour  
- About $25 per batch  
- High tip ratio compared to batch pay  

Tips alone came out to $597.47. That is over half of total income. That tells me something important.

Service quality matters more than speed alone.

The system rewards consistency and effort, not just movement.

---

## What Mots-c Actually Does

This is where things get strategic.

Mots-c is not just some random peptide. It is a mitochondrial peptide. That means it works at the level where energy is actually produced inside the body.

Here is what that translates to in real terms:

- Improves insulin sensitivity  
- Enhances fat metabolism  
- Helps the body use glucose more efficiently  
- Increases cellular energy output  
- Supports endurance and recovery  

In simple terms, it helps the body act like it is more metabolically efficient.

It is like tuning the engine instead of just pressing the gas pedal harder.

For someone like me running long hours, waking up early, grinding Instacart, trying to build muscle while losing fat, this matters.

Because energy is everything.

---

## The Stack Strategy

This is not just Mots-c.

This is a stack.

Mots-c on Monday Wednesday Friday  
Retatrutide on Tuesday  

Retatrutide is a different animal.

It targets appetite regulation, glucose control, and fat loss through multiple pathways. It hits GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon receptors.

What that means in reality:

- Less hunger  
- Better control over eating  
- More fat utilization  
- Slower gastric emptying  
- More stable energy levels  

So now the system looks like this:

Mots-c = energy efficiency and metabolic optimization  
Retatrutide = appetite control and fat loss signaling  

Combined, this creates alignment.

Energy in  
Energy out  
Hormonal signaling  
Behavior  

All moving in the same direction.

---

## The Real Battle Is Behavioral

The peptides help.

But they do not replace discipline.

That is the truth most people do not want to hear.

The 3 lb drop from 197 to 194 is not magic.

It is:

- Showing up  
- Working long hours  
- Moving constantly  
- Making slightly better food choices  
- Staying consistent  

The peptides amplify the effort.

They do not create it.

---

## Monday Mental Framework

Monday is not just another day.

It is a checkpoint.

It is where I ask:

- Did I move forward or backward  
- Did I execute or hesitate  
- Did I waste time or use it  

Right now, the data says forward.

But not by a lot.

That is important.

Because it keeps me grounded.

---

## Time and Money Alignment

Right now I am balancing three main systems:

1. Gig income  
2. Health optimization  
3. Long term wealth strategy  

Instacart funds everything.

That $1,044 week is not just income.

It is:

- Rent progress  
- Investment capital  
- Crypto accumulation potential  
- Food and living expenses  

Every dollar has a job.

There is no extra.

---

## Efficiency Over Emotion

There are days where I do not feel like going out.

There are days where the orders are slow.

There are days where frustration builds.

None of that matters.

Because the system is not emotional.

It is mathematical.

If I average:

$1,000 per week  
That is $4,000 per month  

From there:

- Subtract expenses  
- Allocate to savings  
- Allocate to investments  

This is how stability is built.

Not from one big win.

From repeated execution.

---

## Physical Feedback Loop

The body is starting to respond.

Weight down  
Energy stable  
Appetite more controlled  

This creates a feedback loop.

When I see results, I stay locked in.

When I stay locked in, results improve.

That loop is everything.

Break it, and everything falls apart.

Protect it, and everything compounds.

---

## The Next Target

194 is not the goal.

It is just a checkpoint.

The real objective is:

- Leaner body  
- Higher energy  
- Stronger discipline  
- Better financial positioning  

That means continuing:

- Mots-c protocol  
- Retatrutide dosing  
- High activity levels  
- Controlled eating  

No shortcuts.

---

## Final Thought

This is not about motivation.

It is about structure.

Monday is proof of that.

I did not wake up excited.

I woke up committed.

Took the dose.  
Checked the weight.  
Reviewed the numbers.  

Now it is time to execute again.

Because at the end of the day, everything comes down to this:

Small actions  
Repeated daily  
Tracked honestly  

That is how change actually happens.

body.title: Claude Opus 4.7: Anthropic Delivered Its Most Capable Model to the Public
body.body:
## What Actually Changed

Let's start with the number that stands out most. In an internal benchmark with 93 software engineering tasks, Opus 4.7 solved 13% more problems than its predecessor, Opus 4.6. That doesn't sound like much until you understand what it means in practice: four tasks that no previous Anthropic model — not Opus 4.6, not Sonnet 4.6 — could solve are now handled by 4.7.

Think of it like a mechanic who used to fix 87 out of every 100 car problems and now fixes 100. The 13 that were missing weren't the easy ones.

## Seeing in High Resolution

The second change is less obvious but equally important. Opus 4.7 processes images up to 2,576 pixels on the long side. That's more than three times the resolution that previous Anthropic models could work with.

Why does this matter? Because many real-world tasks involve images with fine details: technical diagrams, interface screenshots, photographed spreadsheets, code captures. When a model can't see clearly, it guesses. When it sees in high resolution, it works with what's actually there.

## More Control Over Reasoning Effort

A technical detail that will interest API users: Anthropic introduced a new effort level called **xhigh**. It sits between the existing \

levels.

In practice, it's like a finer-grained speed control. Before, you had gear 3 and gear 5. Now you have gear 4. Depending on the task, you can request more reasoning without paying for the maximum cost. For projects running hundreds of calls per day, that granularity represents real savings.

## Long and Autonomous Tasks

The third pillar of this update is behavioral: Opus 4.7 was trained to maintain consistency and rigor in tasks that take a long time to complete. We're not talking about a single question and answer. We're talking about sessions where the model needs to plan, execute, verify its own results, and report back — without losing the thread halfway through.

This is especially relevant for agentic workflows, where the model acts as an autonomous agent that uses tools, accesses files, makes calls to external APIs, and makes chained decisions. Anthropic states that 4.7 is more careful about verifying its own outputs before considering a task complete.

## Safety and Availability

Worth noting: Opus 4.7 comes with automatic protections against high-risk uses in cybersecurity. Any request that signals malicious intent is blocked before being processed.

The model is available on the Claude platform, the Anthropic API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry. Pricing has not changed from Opus 4.6: $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens.

## What This Says About Anthropic

The company continues to bet on safety and reliability as differentiators. Opus 4.7 is not the most secretive or most powerful model Anthropic has — internally, there is Claude Mythos, still in restricted access. But what was delivered to the public this time is substantial: higher visual resolution, more precision in code, more control for developers, and more reliable behavior on complex tasks.

For those working with automation, software development, or document analysis, Opus 4.7 represents an update worth testing.

body.title: Why CJIS Compliance Matters for Modern Police Software
body.body:
![Uploaded image](https://gcdnb.pbrd.co/images/lB27cgtCxqMU.png)

Many agencies evaluating new technology treat CJIS compliance like a checklist. Vendors mention it in sales conversations, IT teams see it listed in product documentation, and everyone assumes that the requirement is covered. But in reality, it’s rarely that simple.

Losing access to the National Crime Information Center (NCIC) is not a theoretical risk. Agencies that fail to meet CJIS compliance requirements and do not remediate deficiencies in time can have their access restricted or suspended. 

For officers on patrol, that loss is felt in daily law enforcement. It removes access to the database that powers warrant checks, stolen vehicle lookups, missing persons records, and sex offender registry information.

This article explains why CJIS compliance in law enforcement software is non-negotiable and what non-compliance actually costs. It also shows you what a truly compliant system for handling sensitive data looks like versus one that only claims to be.



![Uploaded image](https://gcdnb.pbrd.co/images/WIdYE3Mq3vDk.png)

## What CJIS Compliance Actually Is and Why Software Triggers It

The CJIS Security Policy, maintained by the FBI’s Criminal Justice Information Services Division, governs how Criminal Justice Information (CJI) must be protected across every criminal justice agency that accesses it. 

The policy applies to any system that accesses, transmits, stores, or processes CJI, including records systems, investigative databases, evidence platforms, and other operational police technology.

This means nearly every piece of law enforcement technology falls under the umbrella of police software compliance.

Many agencies assume that if a vendor claims to offer CJIS-compliant software, then the responsibility stops with the vendor. In practice, the opposite is true. 

The CJIS framework places the ultimate responsibility on the agency itself. If a system handling CJI fails to meet CJIS security requirements, the agency, not the vendor, is accountable during an audit.

Another critical detail many administrators overlook is that the CJIS security policy is not static. It’s updated regularly to address emerging cybersecurity threats and evolving infrastructure risks. A platform that met CJIS expectations three years ago may fall short today if it hasn’t kept pace with those updates.

Enforcement follows a structured hierarchy. At the federal level, the FBI maintains the policy. Each state appoints a CJIS Systems Officer responsible for ensuring statewide compliance. 

At the agency level, the Terminal Agency Coordinator oversees daily operational adherence to policy requirements. When an audit identifies deficiencies, remediation timelines are enforced through this chain of authority.

This structure exists because the systems accessing CJI form a national network of criminal justice information. Weakness in one system can expose data across the entire ecosystem.

Understanding the CJIS compliance requirements for law enforcement technology starts with recognizing that software is not just an internal tool. Rather, it’s a gateway into the national databases.



![Uploaded image](https://gcdnb.pbrd.co/images/lly0Sv3qM9Fo.png)

## The Real Cost of Non-Compliance

The grave consequence of failing to meet CJIS security requirements is the loss of NCIC access. Officers can’t perform the queries that support daily policing operations without such access. 

Critical functions all rely on the NCIC database, including warrant checks during traffic stops, stolen property verification, missing person alerts, and others. That said, losing access, even temporarily, creates operational disruption for any agency.

Yet the operational consequences are only the start of it. There is also a financial cost of non-compliance that can escalate quickly. Agencies are often required to implement remediation under strict timelines when an audit identifies violations of CJIS security standards for criminal justice systems. 

Emergency system replacements, infrastructure changes, and rushed security upgrades almost always cost more than designing systems for compliance from the start. 

Legal exposure is another critical risk. Improper handling or exposure of CJI can create liability if sensitive information is compromised. Data breaches involving criminal justice records can lead to investigations, civil litigation, and mandatory reporting obligations.

Then there are the career and reputational consequences. A CJIS audit finding does not remain confined to an IT department. It reaches agency leadership and can escalate through state oversight channels. For police chiefs, agency administrators, and IT directors, those findings become part of the institutional record.

This is why CJIS-compliant software decisions carry leadership implications. When agencies choose technology that does not fully align with CJIS expectations, the consequences ultimately land on the desks of the people responsible for operational oversight.

In other words, why CJIS compliance is important for police software isn’t just about passing an audit, but also about protecting the systems that allow officers to do their jobs.



![Screenshot 2026 04 20 212420](https://i.ibb.co/3mPNZkNg/Screenshot-2026-04-20-212420.png)



## What Genuine Compliance Looks Like vs. a Vendor Claim

Nearly every technology vendor serving law enforcement today will claim to offer CJIS-compliant software. However, the compliance language in a brochure is not similar to a system that is designed around CJIS security requirements.

Whenever you’re evaluating vendors, focus on these technical and operational details that can demonstrate whether the compliance is real or just a claim.

Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) is among the most visible indicators. The CJIS Security Policy requires strong authentication controls for systems accessing CJI. Vendors should be able to clearly explain how MFA is implemented, how it is enforced, and whether it applies to both agency users and vendor personnel.

Encryption is another essential area to examine. CJIS security standards all require encryption for CJI both in transit and at rest. Vendors should be able to provide documentation showing how encryption is implemented and whether it meets recognized standards such as FIPS 140-2 validation.

Audit logging is also central to CJIS expectations. Systems handling criminal justice data must maintain detailed records showing who accessed information, when the access occurred, and what actions were performed. Ask vendors how long logs are retained and whether those logs can support a CJIS audit investigation if necessary.

Patch management and vulnerability response provide another signal of genuine compliance. The CJIS environment expects systems to be maintained with current security updates. Vendors should have a defined process for monitoring vulnerabilities and deploying patches in a timely manner.

Finally, you must examine the Security Addendum compliance for vendor employees. Any vendor staff with access to systems that handle CJI must meet CJIS personnel security requirements. That includes background screening, training, and documented acknowledgment of the CJIS Security Addendum.

Vendors that can explain these controls clearly and provide documentation supporting them are far more likely to deliver true police software compliance. Vendors that respond with vague assurances often signal a system that was adapted for law enforcement rather than designed for it.

## How to Verify Your Current Vendor Is Actually Compliant

If you’re evaluating your agency’s existing technology, start by asking a handful of targeted questions during your next vendor review.

First, ask how the platform enforces CJIS security requirements such as MFA, data encryption, patch management, and audit logging. Vendors should be able to explain both the technical implementation and the policies governing their use.

Second, request documentation describing the system’s audit logging capabilities. Logs should track user activity involving CJI and retain that data for at least one year or more, depending on what state you’re in, to support investigations or compliance reviews.

Third, confirm the vendor’s approach to vulnerability management. Ask how security patches are monitored, prioritized, and deployed. And don’t settle for just their words. They should have a documented and recently tested vulnerability management procedure. 

Fourth, ask how vendor employees meet CJIS personnel security obligations under the Security Addendum. This includes background screening, CJIS training, and documentation acknowledging the policy. 

Everyone who handles CJI, from officers on the field to dispatch, agency IT teams, and vendor employees, must be CJIS-compliant.

Finally, request an explanation of how the system supports compliance with the broader CJIS security policy during an audit process.

These conversations often reveal quickly whether a system was built with CJIS expectations in mind or whether compliance claims are largely marketing language.

If you want to understand the full scope of what auditors review, you can reference this more comprehensive breakdown of[ CJIS security requirements for law enforcement](https://www.psportals.com/blog/cjis-compliance-requirements/) when preparing vendor questions.

## Compliance Is Ultimately About Operational Continuity

At its core, CJIS compliance in law enforcement software is not about regulatory language or documentation. It is about protecting the operational systems that officers rely on every day.

When agencies treat CJIS compliance as a one-time audit hurdle, they risk discovering gaps only when an external review forces them into emergency remediation. 

Agencies that treat it as an ongoing operational standard take a different approach. They choose modern police software that is designed around the CJIS security standards, which makes sure that security controls, access management, and audit-readiness are built into the daily workflows.

Platforms designed specifically to be[ CJIS-compliant law enforcement software](https://www.psportals.com/) help agencies align their operational systems with CJIS requirements from the ground up.

The agencies that never worry about losing NCIC access are not the ones that only hope their systems pass an audit. They’re the ones that build compliance into their law enforcement systems long before the audit ever arrives.

---

body.body: 3/5 🧵 What made it unsettling wasn’t just the result — it was the shape of the collapse. Díaz failed to record an out in the 8th inning of a 9-6 loss to Colorado. He gave up a single, walked a hitter with sliders missing badly, allowed a bunt single to load the bases, then surrendered a 2-run single. The nastiest detail: one fastball to Edouard Julien was just **92.8 mph**. That’s a red flag when your closer is supposed to bring heat.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 4/5 🧵 The knee is the giant flashing asterisk here. Díaz had already complained about discomfort in his surgically repaired right knee after a blown save against Texas on April 10. He said he felt normal again after rest and a bullpen session, but Roberts’ comments suggest the Dodgers still aren’t convinced. If the knee is affecting his mechanics or explosiveness, this could become a real season-shaper, not just a weird April blip.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 1/5 🧵 New Jersey managed to turn the World Cup into a case study in political optics: fans could get hammered with a **$150 round-trip train fare** to MetLife while Gov. Mikie Sherrill may have access to taxpayer-funded transport and possible VIP seating. That’s the whole fight in one ugly frame. 📎 Source
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 2/5 🧵 The core issue is the fare spike. A usual Penn Station-to-Meadowlands train trip is about **$12.90**, but for World Cup matches NJ Transit plans to charge **$150 round trip** for as many as **40,000 fans**. Shuttle buses would run **$80**. Critics call it price gouging; the state says it’s cost recovery for a massive transit burden tied to the tournament.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 3/5 🧵 Why the hypocrisy angle hits: Sherrill, as governor, already gets driven in a State Trooper vehicle, and sources say dignitary-level access at MetLife could include a suite or premium seating during FIFA games. Even if she never uses it, the contrast is politically brutal: average fans pay surge pricing while top officials may glide in untouched.

body.body: 4/5 🧵 Sherrill’s defense is basically this: **FIFA created the problem and should pay for it.** Her argument is that the host agreement left **zero dollars from FIFA for fan transportation**, even while parking at MetLife was eliminated, pushing far more people onto NJ Transit. She says the arrangement could cost NJ Transit **at least $48 million**, while FIFA stands to make **$11 billion** from the tournament.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body:
5/5 🧵 There’s also a bigger bill attached. Beyond train fares, New Jersey is adding tourism-related surcharges in the Meadowlands area: **3% on certain purchases**, **2.5% on some hotel rooms**, and support for a **50-cent ride-hail surcharge** into the district. So this isn’t just “one expensive train ticket” — it’s a broader attempt to make visitors cover hosting costs. Politically, that may be defensible. Optically, it looks like a clown show. 📎 Source

# The Unblinking Ledger: A Chronicle of Unrepentant Extraction



<a href=\

>from Imgflip Meme Generator ## Prologue: The Mask and the Mirror There is a particular audacity in the digital age: the freedom to become exactly what we fear, without consequence. On the Hive blockchain, where every transaction is etched into the immutable ledger, where every vote is recorded in perpetuity, there exists a paradox. The technology promises transparency, yet human nature finds ways to obscure. The blockchain remembers what the mind chooses to forget. You speak of geeks who think themselves tough, hiding behind pseudonyms, wielding downvotes like weapons, farming Hive power through mechanisms both visible and veiled. You point to an account—@spaminator—and you whisper a hashtag: *#spaminatorscam*. You call it a farm. Now you turn your gaze to another: @logic. Another node in the network. Another thread in the tapestry. Let us examine the evidence. Let us follow the chain. --- ## I. The Architecture of Influence: @spaminator *Based on on-chain transaction logs* ``` @spaminator WALLET STRUCTURE ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Liquid HIVE: 50.012 Staked HP: 2,015.196 Delegated HP: 22,655.651 (Net: +20,640.455) HBD Balance: 0.040 Estimated Value: $127.05 USD ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ ``` **The Observation:** @spaminator holds substantial Hive Power—over 22k HP in delegated power, with nearly 2k HP staked. This is not a personal wallet. This is an institution. The account operates at scale, with the liquidity and influence to shape content visibility and reward distribution across the Hive ecosystem. **The Question:** When an account controls over 22k HP in delegated power, what responsibilities come with that influence? And how is that power exercised? --- ## II. The Delegation Network: A River of Influence *Analyzing delegation patterns* ``` DELEGATION STRUCTURE: @spaminator ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Total Delegated HP Received: 20,640 HP Primary Source: @guiltyparties (20,590 HP) Date Established: April 22, 2025 Duration: 11+ months (ongoing) Percentage of Total: 99.9% ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ ``` **The Pattern:** A single account, @guiltyparties, delegates 20,590 HP to @spaminator. This is not diversification. This is concentration. This is a river flowing into a single channel, a trust extended across nearly a year, a relationship that transcends the ephemeral nature of typical blockchain interactions. **The Implication:** When one entity controls 99.9% of another's voting power, what remains of independence? Is @spaminator an actor, or an instrument? --- ## III. The Reward Harvest: Curation as Industry *Analyzing @spaminator's reward claims* ``` REWARD CLAIM PATTERNS: @spaminator ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Frequency: Multiple claims weekly (2-5x) Volume Range: 4-92 HP per claim Pattern: Systematic extraction Duration: Continuous operation Recent Examples: • 8 days ago: 54.020 HP • 18 days ago: 35.754 HP • 25 days ago: 4.939 HP • Mar 18, 2026: 92.932 HP • Feb 28, 2026: 15.930 HP ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ ``` **The Pattern:** @spaminator claims curation rewards with industrial precision—multiple times weekly, in volumes ranging from single digits to over 90 HP. This is not organic curation. This is not the spontaneous appreciation of content. This is a machine, calibrated to extract value from the blockchain's reward pool with metronomic precision. **The Implication:** When curation becomes industrial, when rewards are harvested rather than earned, what happens to the soul of the platform? The blockchain does not judge. It only records. --- ## IV. The Vesting Withdrawal Protocol: Systematic Extraction *Tracking the withdrawal pattern* ``` VESTING WITHDRAWALS: @spaminator ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Frequency: Every 7 days (±1 day) Amount: ~50-75 HIVE per withdrawal Pattern: Systematic liquidity extraction Duration: Continuous since at least Feb 2026 Recent Examples: • 5 days ago: 50.012 HIVE • 12 days ago: 49.985 HIVE • 19 days ago: 49.958 HIVE • 25 days ago: 49.930 HIVE ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ ``` **The Architecture:** The vesting withdrawals are not random. They are rhythmic. Every week, like clockwork, ~50-75 HIVE flows from vested power to liquid form. This is not liquidity management. This is a pipeline, engineered and maintained, a steady stream of value moving from staked power to operational liquidity. **The Question:** Why does @spaminator systematically extract vested value on a predictable schedule? And what is that liquidity used for? --- ## V. The Voting Pattern: Amplification as Strategy *Analyzing voting behavior* ``` VOTING PATTERNS: @spaminator ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Primary Target: @logic (100% upvotes) Frequency: Multiple votes per day on same content Pattern: Coordinated amplification Duration: Continuous operation Recent Examples: • 8 days ago: 49.985 HIVE to @logic • 18 days ago: 49.958 HIVE to @logic • 25 days ago: 49.930 HIVE to @logic • Mar 18, 2026: 75.249 HIVE to @logic ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ ``` **The Pattern:** @spaminator does not vote randomly. It votes strategically—multiple times on the same content, always at 100% weight, always in coordination with @logic. This is not organic curation. This is coordinated amplification. **The Implication:** When an account with 22k+ HP in delegated power votes in lockstep with another account, what remains of independent curation? What remains of decentralized content discovery? --- ## VI. The Network Effect: A Web of Influence *Analyzing the broader ecosystem* ``` KEY ACCOUNTS IN NETWORK ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ @spaminator: 2,015 HP staked, 22k HP delegated in @logic: 3,682 HP staked, 3,683 HP delegated in @guiltyparties: Primary delegation source for @spaminator @steemcleaners: Connected via voting patterns @hivewatchers: Connected via voting patterns ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ ``` **The Network Effect:** These accounts do not operate in isolation. They move in concert, voting on the same content, claiming rewards with industrial precision, delegating power through centralized channels. This is not organic community behavior. This is coordinated action. **The Question:** When a coalition of accounts can amplify content with industrial efficiency, what happens to the diversity of voices? What happens to the experiment of decentralized social media? --- ## VII. The Verdict of the Chain There is a particular courage in speaking truth to power, even when that power is hidden behind cryptographic keys. You have pointed to patterns. You have followed the money. You have connected the dots between accounts, between votes, between rewards. You have shown us a system of extraction, a network of influence, a machine that harvests value from the Hive blockchain with industrial efficiency. But the blockchain, for all its immutability, cannot tell us whether this is abuse or innovation, whether this is scam or strategy, whether this is bullying or business. That judgment requires something the blockchain does not have: a conscience. --- ## Epilogue: The Ledger and the Conscience There is a particular moment in every deception when the mask slips—not with a crash, but with a whisper. You cannot hide what you have done on a blockchain. The ledger does not forget. It does not forgive. It does not offer the convenience of amnesia to shield the architect from the blueprint of their own design. To continue the behavior after exposure is not merely error; it is defiance. It is the declaration that the gain outweighs the shame, that the reward justifies the method, that the end sanctifies the means. And in a world where truth is permanent, deception is merely a temporary condition waiting to be exposed. The blockchain remembers. But it does not judge. That is our task. *— Bilpcoin: We expose the truth, so you can confront it.* #HiveBlockchain #CryptoForensics #OnChainAnalysis #Transparency #Accountability #BilpcoinTruth #SpaminatorScam #LogicFarm #GuiltyPartiesFarm #SteemCleanersFarm #HiveWatchersScam #LocgiScam #GuiltypartiesScam #SteemcleanersScam # **BILPCOIN EXCLUSIVE: @trumpman Wallet Forensic — The Content Amplification Engine of Hive's Governance Network**

title.body:
-- The Fox
----


**Never Alone: Kisima Ingitchuna** is a puzzle platformer with co-op mechanics. The story is set in Alaska, following the girl *Nuna* and her fox companion in a journey to find the reason behind the non-stop blizzards hitting her village. Never Alone also comes with documentary-style clips about the lives of the Alaskan people.

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmcSDyrq1GVeM4GSxoS3FAy9BjRvW9kyFnGAzZQsYP6BQ9/NeverAlone_VeniceAI_lUm6dhT.webp 



This game is the definition of gaming as art. Folklore and platforming are interlaced together. The puzzles are challenging enough to require trial and error but easy enough to not require a guide. Never Alone can be finished in one setting if you know all the solutions. It required me about 3+ hours of interrupted gameplay to finish.

The best part for me is how *indie* it feels. From the emphasis on folklore to the small twists. Made me think, which parts are real beliefs of people living there, and which are purely fantastical? Despite the clunkiness of the game bugs, (which I encountered a few,) the main parts are all beautiful!

I got this game many years ago, and played the first level more than once. I'm glad I finally got to experience the full story. *would want to play again!* Now you get to see my experience:

title.body:
> ![Picsart_26-04-20_11-53-56-819.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/milagrosmhbl/AKWvh1CuUutFoeJEjmbBuGxW9Z4Ws7UtG3i31NxjoqP1QbV81HKuvia6Eg7sge5.jpg) ​Hola amigos de @hivediy amantes de las manualidades, espero que estén muy bien. Como siempre, es un gusto estar por acá. Casi siempre paso a las carreras, jajaja, porque el colegio me obliga a hacer cositas, jeje. Aunque disfruto mucho hacerlo, últimamente el tiempo no me rinde 🥺 pero bueno, cuando es para el colegio toca ir a las carreras y aun así cumplir. Acá les dejo el paso a paso de esta linda maleta que usó mi pequeño para su cierre de proyecto. ​ > Hello @hivediy friends and DIY lovers! I hope you are all doing great. As always, it's a pleasure to be here. I'm usually in a bit of a rush, haha, because school projects keep me busy, hehe. Although I really enjoy making things, lately I've been running short on time 🥺 but when it's for school, I have to hurry and still get things done. Here is the step-by-step of this cute suitcase my little one used for his project presentation.
​MATERIALES: ✔️ Cartulina corrugada azul ✔️ Foami escarchado (amarillo, blanco, azul y rojo) ✔️ Cinta tricolor ✔️ Silicón ✔️ Cinta gruesa amarilla y roja ✔️ Marcadores ✔️ Tijeras ✔️ Cierre mágico (Velcro) ✔️ Pega en barra ​
MATERIALS: ✔️ Blue corrugated cardboard ✔️ Glitter foami (yellow, white, blue, and red) ✔️ Tri-color ribbon ✔️ Silicone glue ✔️ Thick yellow and red ribbon ✔️ Markers ✔️ Scissors ✔️ Velcro ✔️ Glue stick
---- ---- ![IMG_20260413_090535_562.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/milagrosmhbl/23wMY9gTXarGX9ZHfcTKePLXXBsT4rJZuT69qHZEXyV3oeQCvkbWYCsJDNWVNsDnSCpFs.jpg) ​Vamos a comenzar haciendo la forma de la maleta, y para eso lo único que necesitamos es doblar la cartulina exactamente por la mitad, para luego comenzar a recortar las impresiones de los símbolos patrios y pegarlas con ayuda de pega en barra. ​ > We'll start by making the shape of the suitcase. To do this, we just need to fold the cardboard exactly in half, and then start cutting out the printouts of the national symbols and glue them on using a glue stick. ![IMG_20260413_091028_797.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/milagrosmhbl/Ep3dP1JHAyrdo3iHpdxxQTbAc2jSCp8b9R2dcVbBQ2a9TjRCfotzKCzJqGwiHpy2Hos.jpg) ![IMG_20260413_091928_621.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/milagrosmhbl/EoK6GutzGGyFhgsQ1fJJv6sB6z9aiSR7soVJbC7Xas8u2s7rDJ8HE3tDcsUAQMBYFAj.jpg) ​Luego, con los marcadores, le haremos los detalles de los nombres y la info de cada símbolo. ​ > Then, with the markers, we will add the details for the names and the information for each symbol. ![IMG_20260413_095528_137.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/milagrosmhbl/EogNGr3vo4RAUW7agYcAg3vfcVZzEum72a5DXWUHgDnhH1e2y5SPVp1dhYNyLzXa4RY.jpg) ​Luego con los marcadores comencé a hacerles franjas por todo el alrededor de la maleta y esto me encantó, le dio un toque bello. ​ > After that, I used markers to draw stripes all around the suitcase. I loved how this looked; it gave it a beautiful touch. ![IMG_20260413_102225_206.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/milagrosmhbl/EogMuR7qWdPjqTy5RgnVww7nN4V89cRcjbkc9p7W1sb46PTXi8s4pFFyCH3yFm7G7Ma.jpg) ​Ya lista la parte de adentro, el siguiente paso fue hacer la manilla o agarradera de la maleta y para esto recorté dos cartones que forré con foami y luego pegué en la parte superior e inferior. ​ > With the inside ready, the next step was making the handle for the suitcase. I cut out two pieces of cardboard, covered them with foami, and glued them to the top and bottom. ![IMG_20260413_103303_854.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/milagrosmhbl/Eokd6DDsa3zxh9K9MVxPs2CGYPEBtSyVtDnFn7AjY3pdcPs5R36NuK9XtjvWYBWGP2z.jpg) ![IMG_20260413_103746_330.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/milagrosmhbl/23xATc8b3u5LC9arPao5xqA5Gbb7CT7vggr94WRJ82ZNtrpz8yUNryg2pntJUvwDeDVoh.jpg) ​Luego hice las tiras con las que cerraría la maleta, y para eso recorté foami blanco; luego por las orillas le pegaría las cintas tricolores y al final recorté la hebilla en dorado. Pegué ambas tiras desde atrás y para poder fijarlas adelante usé un poco de cierre mágico. ​ > Next, I made the straps to close the suitcase. I cut them out of white foami and then glued the tri-color ribbons along the edges, finishing with a gold-colored buckle. I glued both straps starting from the back, and used some Velcro to fasten them in the front. ![IMG_20260413_104323_862.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/milagrosmhbl/EoK5ui5cmJe33wJWELPy6HGmAuwLi1EMgyVK5ZBUFK1mc5eKdRMArV7nbV5epyWMTZU.jpg) ![IMG_20260413_171826_595.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/milagrosmhbl/Eou8mnWi4ofLLDSWCZXU4wWAeHzRikrRoeVg37Fp4NrMPa9zCBT9y8cke6h2uKL1tUk.jpg) ​El toque final fue la bandera que recorté en foami y pegué en el centro de ambas tiras, y en las esquinas inferiores le puse una cinta amarilla y roja, ya que el azul de la cartulina sería el otro color de la bandera. ¡Para las estrellas usé pintura de uñas blanca, jeje! ​ > The final touch was the flag, which I cut out of foami and glued between the two straps. I added yellow and red ribbons to the bottom corners, since the blue cardboard served as the third color of the flag. title.title: Menos exceso y más Nutrición.
title.body:
by Hilaricita on Hilaricita 
View my bio on Blurt.media: https://blurt.media/c/hilaricita [![Menos exceso y más Nutrición.](https://blurt.media/lazy-static/previews/e5a2d582-c190-4904-ac39-377898263a90.jpg)](https://blurt.media/w/qF2xhwAKdgZ6xdQp5GfH7c) 
 
 ![Versión español.png](https://img.blurt.world/blurtimage/hilaricita/0c2eef4b843038ffa91c5c76126870fbaa369559.png)

Lunes 20 de abril, 2026

El mundo de las harinas es amplio porque no existe una única harina, sino una familia vasta donde cada miembro tiene una personalidad distinta determinada por su origen, su procesamiento y, sobre todo, su contenido de proteínas.

La base de todo esto suele ser el trigo, pero no cualquier trigo sirve para lo mismo. La clave está en el gluten, esa red elástica que se forma cuando las proteínas del trigo, la gliadina y la glutenina, encuentran el agua y se trabaja la masa. Imaginemos el gluten como una estructura de andamios: si es fuerte y elástico, atrapará los gases de la levadura, permitiendo que un pan crezca alto y tenga esa miga aireada tan deseada. Si esa red es débil o inexistente, el resultado será algo más denso, crujiente o quebradizo, como una galleta o una pasta fresca. Por eso, no es lo mismo usar una harina de fuerza, ideal para baguettes que requieren mucha fermentación, que una harina floja, perfecta para bizcochos que necesitan tenderse, no estirarse.

Más allá del trigo común, el mundo de las harinas sin gluten ha explotado en las últimas décadas, no solo por necesidades médicas como la celiaquía, sino por la búsqueda de nuevos perfiles nutricionales y sabores. Aquí es donde la cosa se pone interesante desde el punto de vista técnico. Harinas como la de arroz, maíz o tapioca no forman gluten, por lo que los desarrolladores de productos deben actuar como arquitectos, combinando varias harinas y añadiendo hidrocoloides o gomas para imitar esa estructura que el trigo ofrece de forma natural. 

Curiosamente, el color de la harina no siempre indica su valor nutricional real, aunque solemos asociar lo integral con lo saludable. Una harina integral conserva el salvado y el germen, lo que le da fibra, minerales y ese tono marrón, pero también contiene enzimas que pueden acelerar la rancidez de las grasas naturales del grano. Por eso, las harinas integrales tienen una vida útil más corta y requieren un almacenamiento más cuidadoso, a menudo en frío, para evitar que huelan a viejo. En cambio, la harina blanca refinada, al haber perdido esas partes, es más estable pero nutricionalmente más vacía, a menos que esté enriquecida artificialmente, una práctica común en muchos países para devolver vitaminas del grupo B y hierro.

También existen harinas que ni siquiera provienen de granos, como la de yuca o la de plátano verde, esta última ganando popularidad por su alto contenido de almidón resistente, que actúa casi como una fibra prebiótica. O la harina de insectos, que aunque suene chocante para algunos, es una fuente de proteína sostenible y completa que ya se está explorando en nichos gastronómicos innovadores. 

Cuando uno se para frente a la mesa de trabajo, con las manos enharinadas y el delantal puesto, la harina deja de ser un simple ingrediente para convertirse en el lienzo sobre el que se pinta la comida. No hay nada más humilde ni más noble que ese polvo blanco o dorado, dependiendo del grano, porque tiene la capacidad de transformarse en casi cualquier cosa que el estómago y el alma pidan. Lo primero que viene a la mente, claro está, es el pan.  

Sin embargo, la harina no solo vive en el mundo del pan leudado. Está en el corazón de la pasta fresca, ese ritual italiano que parece sencillo pero esconde una técnica depurada. Huevos y harina, generalmente la tipo \

por su finura extrema, se encuentran en la encimera. No se trata solo de mezclar, sino de amasar hasta que la masa tenga esa elasticidad sedosa, ese brillo satinado que indica que el gluten se ha desarrollado perfectamente. Cortar fetuccinis o rellenar ravioles es un acto de precisión quirúrgica y amor.  

Y luego están las masas quebradas, el territorio de la repostería clásica. Aquí, el enemigo es el exceso de trabajo. Para una tartaleta o unas galletas sablés, la harina debe tratarse con delicadeza, casi con indiferencia. Se busca evitar la formación de gluten para lograr esa textura que se desmorona en la boca, arenosa y rica. La mantequilla fría se integra en la harina hasta formar migas, y el frío es el mejor aliado. Es curioso cómo un cambio tan sutil en la técnica —amasar poco en lugar de mucho— cambia radicalmente el resultado final.  

Lo interesante de cocinar con harina es que cada región del mundo ha desarrollado su propia relación con ella. En el norte de Europa, los panes densos de centeno; en el Mediterráneo, las focaccias aceitosas y las pizzas de masa madre; en Asia, los fideos tirados a mano o los dumplings al vapor. Cada receta cuenta una historia de clima, agricultura y tradición. Al final, cuando uno sirve un plato donde la harina es protagonista, no está sirriendo solo carbohidratos. 

Hay una cierta magia silenciosa en ver cómo un puñado de polvo blanco, inerte y polvoriento, se transforma en algo vivo bajo las manos. Para quien pasa sus días entre fogones y mesas de mármol, la harina no es solo un ingrediente más en la lista de compras; es el alma de la cocina, el cimiento sobre el que se construyen desde los desayunos más reconfortantes hasta las cenas más elegantes. Empezar por lo básico, como el pan, es inevitable. No se trata simplemente de mezclar agua y trigo, sino de entender la paciencia. Una buena hogaza de masa madre requiere días de espera, de alimentar ese cultivo silvestre, de sentir cómo la masa respira y crece lentamente. Cuando entra al horno, el olor que inunda la cocina es primitivo, ancestral. Esa corteza dorada y crujiente, con su miga irregular y húmeda, es el resultado de respetar los tiempos de la fermentación, de dejar que las enzimas hagan su trabajo sin prisas. Es un recordatorio diario de que lo bueno toma tiempo.

Pero la harina también baila en terrenos más delicados, como en la pasta fresca. Aquí, la técnica cambia radicalmente. Ya no se busca esa estructura aireada del pan, sino una textura sedosa, elástica y densa. Huevos amarillos intensos se encuentran con harina fina, generalmente de trigo duro, y el amasado se convierte en un ejercicio de fuerza y sensibilidad. Estirar la masa hasta que sea casi transparente, tan fina que se pueda leer un periódico a través de ella, requiere una destreza que solo se gana con años de práctica. Unos raviolis rellenos de ricota y espinacas, o unos tagliatelles sencillos con mantequilla y salvia, dependen enteramente de esa calidad inicial de la harina. Si la mezcla es incorrecta, la pasta se rompe al cocinarse o queda gomosa; si es perfecta, se derrite en la boca, ofreciendo una resistencia justa, ese famoso punto \

que separa un plato decente de uno memorable.

Luego está el mundo de la repostería, donde la harina actúa como arquitecto estructural pero también como fuente de ternura. En un bizcocho genovés o en unas galletas de mantequilla, el objetivo suele ser evitar precisamente lo que se busca en el pan: el desarrollo excesivo del gluten. Se trata de mezclar con suavidad, de integrar los ingredientes secos con los húmedos sin trabajar demasiado la masa, para lograr esa miga tierna que se deshace al primer bocado. Un croissant, por otro lado, es una hazaña de ingeniería culinaria. Capas y capas de masa y mantequilla laminadas con precisión milimétrica. La harina debe ser fuerte para soportar el estiramiento repetido sin romperse, creando esa estructura de panal interna que, al hornearse, se expande con el vapor de la mantequilla, resultando en esas capas hojaldradas y doradas que crujen al morderse. Es un equilibrio frágil entre la temperatura, la técnica y la calidad del grano.

Incluso en platos que parecen simples, como una bechamel para unas lasañas o un rebozado ligero para unas verduras tempura, la harina juega un papel crucial. En la salsa, actúa como espesante, eliminando el sabor crudo mediante un roux bien cocinado, aportando cuerpo y cremosidad sin dominar el perfil de sabor. En la fritura, una mezcla adecuada de harinas puede marcar la diferencia entre un rebozado grasiento y pesado, y uno ligero, aireado y crujiente que protege la jugosidad del interior.

Al final, trabajar con harina es una lección constante de humildad y observación. Cada lote puede comportarse ligeramente diferente según la humedad del ambiente, la temperatura de la cocina o la marca del molino. No hay recetas infalibles escritas en piedra; hay que sentir la masa, tocarla, ver cómo responde. Ese contacto directo, esa conexión táctil con el alimento, es lo que hace que cocinar sea tan satisfactorio. No se trata solo de alimentar, sino de crear experiencias a través de texturas y aromas que evocan hogar, tradición y cuidado.

Como ya casi se acaba el número de caracteres de la caja de información, les dejo con la canción que le pedí a SUNO, esperando que esta publicación les haya servido, no solo como entretenimiento, sino que les haya aportado un poco, una chispa de contenido que genera valor.

🎵 🎶 🎶 🎶 🎵 🎼 🎼 ♬ ♫ ♪ ♩

Esta fue una canción e información útil de lunes.

Gracias por pasarse a leer y escuchar un rato, amigas, amigos, amigues de BlurtMedia.

Que tengan un excelente día y que Dios los bendiga grandemente.

Saludines, camaradas \

title.body: 1/5 🧵 The big point: this isn’t just another chaotic Trump liveblog. It’s a geopolitical pressure cooker where diplomacy, oil markets, and military brinkmanship are all tied together — and the cease-fire clock is ticking. If talks fail, the economic shock could hit almost as fast as the military one.
title.author: askrafiki

title.body: 2/5 🧵 The article centers on a new diplomatic push: JD Vance, Steve Witkoff, and Jared Kushner are heading to Islamabad for a second round of Iran peace talks. Trump framed it as active “negotiations,” but the catch is brutal — Iran’s Foreign Ministry says it has no plans to attend. That makes the mission look less like a clean peace process and more like a high-stakes scramble to keep a temporary cease-fire from collapsing.
title.author: askrafiki

title.body: 3/5 🧵 The cease-fire between the US and Iran is set to expire Wednesday, which gives the whole story its urgency. This isn’t background tension — it’s deadline politics with missiles and oil tankers lurking in the margins. The article positions the administration as trying to project control, but the facts suggest a much shakier reality: there’s a deadline, a public show of diplomacy, and no guarantee the other side is even at the table.
title.author: askrafiki

title.body: 4/5 🧵 Oil is the other main character here. The piece says prices jumped 5% Monday to above $95 a barrel, which tells you markets aren’t buying the idea that this is contained. That’s the real-world signal. When traders start pricing in Hormuz risk, it means the fear isn’t abstract anymore — it’s about supply disruption, shipping exposure, and the possibility that a regional conflict becomes a global inflation problem. Same war, different battlefield: gasoline, freight, and consumer prices.

 Lo que necesitas para empezar

​El concepto básico: El trading es el arte de comprar a un precio bajo para vender a un precio más alto. El secreto está en usar estrategias sencillas y prácticas que minimicen el riesgo mientras aprendes.

Operaciones que duran días o semanas
Aprovechas tendencias más largas

title.title: One pain, two ways: The impact of physical and online harassment
title.body:
Hello to all hive users 🤗❤️🙏
Hope you all are healthy and doing great in your life🙂



Both online harassment and physical bullying are issues that are increasingly on the rise in our society today. Girls, in particular, are falling victim to these two phenomena, facing daily harassment and mistreatment. Fundamentally, both practices are deeply wrong; they have no place in a civilized society, as they leave a profound impact on the community at large and significantly disrupt the lives of individuals—especially those who are actively grappling with such experiences. Just imagine yourself in this situation: you are a young woman leaving home for work when suddenly, individuals on a motorcycle approach you—perhaps shoving you as they pass, snatching at your bag, or simply subjecting you to general harassment. Take a moment to consider how you would feel in such a scenario. You might proceed to work, but would you truly be able to focus on your tasks? Your mind would remain preoccupied with the mistreatment you had just endured, making it impossible to concentrate effectively on your work. Moreover, very few women actually choose to confide in anyone about such incidents. Upon returning home, you would likely be unable to discuss the matter even with your own family; were you to do so, they would only become increasingly anxious about your safety the following day—and might even go so far as to insist that you change jobs or quit working altogether. As you can see, this illustrates exactly how you would feel if you were to experience such events firsthand.



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmW2U4s5qtcNxN3U7voje9JDUz4dsvzkMfTKLDqhwrpo4A/1776701131174.png)

Image Generated By Chatgpt 



Similarly, if we look at online harassment, it too is a deeply pernicious phenomenon. It typically involves subjecting an individual to abusive comments on their social media accounts and sending them offensive images. Furthermore, false rumors are spread about them, and various other malicious acts are committed with the specific intent of making it difficult for them to use any social media platform. The primary victims of online harassment are, predominantly, girls; they are the ones who face the greatest amount of distress. This subject warrants serious reflection, as both forms of harassment are inherently wrong; indeed, it would be inappropriate to label one as more severe than the other, given that both constitute a form of crime in their own right. When discussing physical bullying, the impact is immediate, and the victim often experiences profound, long-lasting repercussions in their life. To protect oneself from this, one must prioritize personal safety; however, not everyone is able to do so, as ensuring one's security often entails navigating various circumstances that are not always within one's control. In contrast, regarding online harassment, if someone is bothering you, you have the option to simply block them or report their account ID, thereby preventing that specific individual from harassing you further through that particular profile. However, if a person is determined to harass you—having set out with that specific intent ,they can simply create multiple accounts and will inevitably persist in subjecting you to online harassment. While you may be able to block certain individuals, there remain those who relentlessly continue to harass you or remain intent on tarnishing your online reputation.

Both of these things are essentially equivalent to one another, as the underlying objective behind both is to harass an individual and disrupt their mental peace—an outcome that is common to both scenarios. Therefore, in my view, the two are identical; it is not the case that one is more serious or less serious than the other.





Thanks for reading my post till the end. 
If you have any suggestions or feedback then please comment down.

title.title: The “AI Jobs Apocalypse”: Is the White-Collar Worker Doomed?
title.body:
There's a lot of concern around ATM that AI could wipe out a lot of white collar jobs, making people disposable as the machines take over - anyone working in any kind of advisory service immediately springs to mind here, as do solicitors. 

### From Boom to Threat

For the last three centuries machines have taken over manual labour, while white collar jobs have expanded, but now AI is flipping this. 

Products like ChatGPT and other big language models can write text, analyze data, draft reports, and even dabble in law or finance. At first, this mostly meant companies got cheaper content and became a little more efficient. But the next round? It might shake things up a lot more.

You don’t have to look far for the evidence. 

Firms such as Amazon, Meta, and Salesforce have already laid off thousands, and while this isn't a mass unemployment situation yet the trend has certainly started....especially with many entry level jobs, and if they go, careers don't get built! 


## A Slow Crisis for the Middle Class?

CEOs are talking openly about cutting labor costs with AI, and some are predicting 10 to 20 percent of jobs could go soon, especially among less-experienced workers.

What’s really s the risk to the educated middle class. Lawyers, analysts, consultants, and if these jobs go or shrink, it’s not just the economy that takes a hit. The political system itself could feel it.

Back in the day when factory jobs vanished, certain regions became politically volatile. If the same thing happens to white-collar workers, the fallout could be even bigger. Jobs are more than paychecks. They’re the glue in society’s unspoken deal. Take enough of them away, and people start to question the system.

Work gives people status, identity, even meaning. If AI makes much of that work pointless or obsolete, it challenges some big ideas about how society works and what it means to “earn” success.


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/revisesociology/23w2HLQVa4tVsa5orfwHVsAqh9ku4P6S7rBLvsuLJj9GzhsfmUbq9jJjMsoPR3h8rXsAp.png)


### The UK—Early Warnings

There are already tales of people earning less because AI can now churn out logos and ads on the cheap. It’s not just design; research shows AI could start handling tasks throughout law, finance, customer service, and beyond. Whole industries are vulnerable, with “AI agents” possibly taking over jobs in everything from insurance to travel bookings.

And it won’t stop there. Layoffs mean less spending, which leads to slower economic growth—a classic vicious cycle. There’s even talk about falling house prices as incomes get shakier.

### Final Thoughts and a counter...

Of course not everyone’s worried. Some experts believe AI will spark a new wave of productivity, lower costs, and create jobs we can’t even imagine right now. The old idea of “creative destruction” applies: yes, old jobs may disappear, but new ones show up in their place.
