title.title: Global Safety Nets or Dependency at the IMF and World Bank?
title.body:
![20260420_162912.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aqsagu/23wzdJAKEWFzVVdmoznLCxqqmWD7S4WjgtFtaGZkBnLdgLvkufxYzHaeA7gEtPntG6L9J.jpg)
The experiences of the IMF and World Bank lately reveal a truth: These organizations can only partially help to sustain the world economy from economic shocks (global financial shocks). Furthermore, the entire world seems to be increasingly dependent on the USA for continuity in the provision of economic stability and policy direction.

How does that affect the world economy and how do we, particularly from ethical and Islamic perspectives, understand it?

Limited ability to address global shocks
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank were created to provide a mechanism for the stability of the global economy; to assist developing countries; and to reduce global poverty. However, issues such as the following have exposed structural limitations in how the IMF and World Bank were created to stabilize the global economy:


Global inflation shocks
Energy crises and geopolitical issues
The rising levels of debt of the developing countries
The currency instability of many emerging markets

As a result of providing limited assistance in addressing these issues or shocks to the world economy, countries rely on the interim assistance of the IMF and World Bank indefinitely. All too often, countries end up receiving a new loan, which creates long-term financial dependency on the IMF and/or World Bank from a growing number of countries. 

💸 Dependent on the United States - Continued Global Relationship
A significant concern raised during the most recent discussions is that countries continue to rely on financial policy decisions made by the United States.

As the global reserve currency, the U.S. dollar continues to be the most widely-used currency for international transactions; therefore:
The majority of all international trade is conducted using U.S. dollars.
Decisions made by the U.S. to change interest rates have far-reaching effects on economies across the globe.
Many of the largest international organizations and institutions tend to implement economic and financial policies that are consistent with those established by the U.S.

As a result of the above-described dependencies, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank are, in part, under the influence of the United States’ economic and monetary policies.

🏦 Structural Debt-Based Financial System
Many of the issues regarding countries’ dependency on the United States are related to the way in which the global financial system is currently structured — namely, it is primarily debt-based and interest-driven.

For example, when countries borrow funds, they typically must accept a loan with prescribed conditions, some of which are as follows:
Riba (interest-based) repayment terms
Structural adjustment conditions
Fiscal consolidation requirements

While conditions imposed by lenders are intended to create stability, they frequently result in:
Reduction of public expenditure; economic contraction in developing nations; and long-term reliance on debt. 

Ethical Basis of Islamic Finance 
The exploitation of people through the charging of interest, or riba, results in an uneven distribution of wealth and is not permitted by the Islamic financial system. 
Islamic Economics has certain principles, which include: 
• Sharing risk rather than taking on a debt load 
• Providing financing that is backed by an asset rather than providing an interest-based loan 
• Fairly distributing wealth and trading with justice 
Global institutions such as the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank may still be considered “haram” by Muslims to discuss; however, their systems of economics are, in general, philosophically different from Islamic economics and therefore are the basis upon which the respective philosophies differ. 
Understanding the differences between these two different systems will allow for honest evaluation of global economies without any emotional bias. 
The role of the IMF and World Bank is critical to the stability of the global economy; however, their recent discussions demonstrate that there remains a much larger issue than just global economics; that global economic systems continue to be heavily centralised and depend upon the use of debt.
To emerging economies, there is much to consider in light of the continuing dependence on global lenders; for example: 
• How can we reduce our reliance on global lenders? 
• Are there alternative financial systems that provide more stability to the countries creating their economic foundation?  

📌 Final thoughts

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank, along with their many objectives, should not be seen as strictly “good” or “bad” but rather as “systems.” The International Monetary Fund and World Bank are part of a comprehensive system where both their positive effects and negative effects can exist simultaneously.
Understanding how these systems interact and operate within larger systems is important to our ability to analyze global economic systems, debt, and financial independence in an ever-evolving world.

title.body: 2/5 🧵 The article argues Hungary’s election was treated by Brussels as a battle over obedience, not democracy. Armstrong says the EU backed Orbán’s defeat because he put Hungarian national interests first, resisted EU pressure on Ukraine, and maintained ties with Russia. His point: when leaders refuse to align with the EU line, they’re branded corrupt or authoritarian — but when Brussels interferes, it gets sold as defending democratic values.
title.author: askrafiki

title.body: 3/5 🧵 A big theme is election interference. Armstrong claims the EU has meddled not just in Hungary, but also in Italy, Romania, Germany, and even Scotland, all to preserve centralized control. Whether you buy every example or not, his argument is consistent: the EU is presented as a neutral democratic institution, but he sees it as a political operator protecting its own power and punishing dissent inside member states.
title.author: askrafiki

title.body: 4/5 🧵 The article’s real warning is about structure: Armstrong says the EU is trying to move from unanimous consent to qualified majority voting, especially in foreign policy. That matters because unanimity is one of the last real brakes smaller nations have. Strip out the veto, and member states stop being meaningful sovereign actors. In his telling, that’s the moment the EU stops being a cooperative bloc and starts looking like an unelected empire with a cleaner logo.
title.author: askrafiki

title.body:
5/5 🧵 He broadens that into a civilizational argument: centralized systems, censorship, speech controls, and bureaucratic social engineering always overreach, then crack. Armstrong ties the EU’s direction to falling economic dynamism, suppression of dissent, and a wider “globalist” project that could spill into the US. You don’t have to swallow every flourish to get the thesis: he sees concentrated supranational power as inherently unstable — and ultimately self-destructive. 📎 Source

title.title: [Eng./Esp.]   The checkmate of the species.   ||   El jaque-mate de la especie.
title.body:
*** *** #
Si eres de habla hispana, la versión en español es mejor para ti; debes hacer clic 👉 [**AQUÍ**](#english)
*** ***
# ***
The checkmate of the species
***

> Lately, every morning I wake up with a tightness in my chest that isn’t just mine, but belongs to the wounded pulse of the world, which can be felt across all social media. **“The big clash”**, the headlines repeat with a coldness that makes my blood run cold. What for some is a simple geopolitical analysis, for me is the echo of an ancient fear. That great, definitive confrontation that so many call the Third World War... I am, by conviction and instinct, a person who professes peace, but in recent weeks the air has felt heavy with a dark foreboding that I cannot ignore.
![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/amigoponc/23t7acJVTSG9qhZ6kQxPJUgsFy3og4sCMFqRfd1jTFQstPajUfBFCcEQALrEc6EiMzyHo.png) [Thanks to the Banana 2.0 app for illustrating my post.](https://gemini.google.com/app)
I look at the chessboard in the corner of my living room and am overcome by a deep melancholy. How is it possible that we have not evolved enough to transfer our disputes to the strategic silence of Go or wooden pieces? I find it incomprehensible that human intelligence, capable of deciphering the cosmos, should prefer the clamour of iron and clay. Human beings are terribly reckless; we retain that primitive impulse to measure our strength face to face, forgetting that in war the only shared fate is the grave—or, today, cremation... if anything organic remains at all. It is regrettable, and deeply harsh, to accept that we have learnt absolutely nothing from the past. The scars of our grandparents still fester, yet we insist on ignoring the trail of ashes to light new bonfires. I feel small, vulnerable in the face of a machinery of pride that is greased with the blood of others. In this potential ‘big clash’, there will be no winners, only a shattered chessboard and the bitter certainty that we were too arrogant to choose peace. *** ***

*** *** ***
>\n\nÚltimamente, cada mañana despierto con una presión en el pecho que no me pertenece solo a mí, sino al pulso herido del mundo que se siente en todas las redes sociales. **\

**, repiten los titulares con una frialdad que me hiela la sangre. Lo que para algunos es un simple análisis geopolítico, para mí es el eco de un miedo ancestral. Ese gran enfrentamiento definitivo que tantos llaman la Tercera Guerra Mundial... Soy, por convicción y por instinto, una persona que profesa la paz, pero estas últimas semanas el aire se ha sentido cargado de un presagio oscuro que no puedo ignorar.
![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/amigoponc/23tbiScYteCVCLSaQeAyymbZzX8xKLBYaobvfSBF7yqfhsso8iVmFDkFzMH6SMqAzvzgK.png) [Gracias a la app Banana 2.0 por ilustrar mi publicación.](https://gemini.google.com/app)
Miro el tablero de ajedrez en el rincón de mi sala y me invade una melancolía profunda. ¿Cómo es posible que no hayamos evolucionado lo suficiente como para trasladar nuestras disputas al silencio estratégico del Go o de las piezas de madera? Me resulta incomprensible que la inteligencia humana, capaz de descifrar el cosmos, prefiera el estruendo del hierro y el barro. El ser humano es terriblemente osado; conservamos ese impulso primitivo de medir fuerzas cara a cara, olvidando que en la guerra el único destino común es la fosa —también hoy, la incineración... Si es que queda algo orgánico—. Es lamentable, y profundamente crudo, aceptar que no hemos aprendido absolutamente nada del pasado. Las cicatrices de nuestros abuelos aún supuran, pero nos empeñamos en ignorar el rastro de ceniza para encender hogueras nuevas. Me siento pequeño, vulnerable ante una maquinaria de orgullo que se aceita con sangre ajena. En este posible “big clash”, no habrá ganadores, solo un tablero roto y la amarga certeza de que fuimos demasiado soberbios para elegir la paz.

title.title: No matter the method used, the pain is the same [EN/PT]
title.body: > At some point in life, all of us will face offenses. Sometimes they are directed at us, other times at those around us, or on a larger scale, at someone completely outside our circle of acquaintances. It is sad to admit, but it is part of human behavior to use words or actions with the intention of hurting. There are many ways to cause pain to someone. Bullying, insults, and aggression, whether verbal or physical, leave deep marks on those who are targeted. The question that remains is whether, in online or in-person environments, the weight of these actions really changes. Saying that both forms cause harm would be obvious. The most important point is not the medium, but the intention. When someone decides to hurt, embarrass, or diminish another person, the damage already begins there. We are creative by nature and, unfortunately, that creativity also appears in the way we hurt others. Whether face to face or behind a screen, the consequences exist and they are not light. From my own experience, in-person bullying has a very strong immediate impact. It is a discomfort that paralyzes and can stay with a person for years. When it happens, there is not always time or space to react. I remember situations at school that, even today, when they come to mind, bring a weight that is hard to ignore. When the victim is a child, this becomes even more delicate. But there are many other situations in which a person is exposed and caused pain, and the trauma can be irreversible, regardless of age. In the online environment, the impact can follow a different path. It may not be as immediate, but it can grow in an uncontrolled way. A situation can reach enormous proportions in a short time and reach people who are not even part of the initial context. When that happens, the damage spreads and can affect different areas of someone’s life, often in a silent and prolonged way. People who hide behind screens can add to what is happening, and the ease of increasing the damage is much greater. Those who practice this kind of behavior rarely have a real notion of what they are causing. The damage goes beyond the moment. It extends, accumulates, and can deeply affect how someone sees themselves and relates to the world. Some argue that the weight of punishment should vary depending on the medium, but in practice, suffering does not follow that logic. Only those who are truly victims know the real damage that can be done, regardless of the means by which this deplorable act was carried out. What needs to be analyzed is the intention. If there was a desire to hurt, embarrass, or humiliate, the response must be firm. Punishment should serve not only as a consequence but also as an example. When there is clarity and consistency in dealing with this, there is a greater chance of reducing the repetition of these behaviors. But we cannot look at this and measure the act by the way it was carried out, but rather by how that intention caused consequences in another person’s life, and regardless of the medium, the punishment should be severe for all involved. It is hard not to feel a certain weight when thinking about how many situations like this happen every day. Many go unnoticed, but leave deep marks. In some cases, the damage cannot be reversed. For this reason, more than discussing where it happened, it is essential to look at the impact caused and act proportionally to it, with responsibility, awareness, and above all, with the goal of preventing other stories from ending the same way. It does not matter the medium through which the harm was caused, the punishment must be proportional to its consequences. --- Credits: Translated: [Deepl](www.deepl.com/pt-BR/translator) Cover: created by [Canva.](www.canva.com) AI-generated image [ Flow]( www.labs.google/fx/pt/tools/flow) --- ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQma2XinqppUM2Uvqbsii8ViPirxPmkbLmJ8FkfAbcj9EYN/image.png) Em algum momento da vida, todos nós vamos nos deparar com ofensas. Às vezes são direcionadas a nós, outras vezes a quem está por perto, ou em proporções maiores, alguém totalmente fora do nosso circulo de conhecidos. É triste admitir, mas faz parte do comportamento humano usar palavras ou atitudes com intenção de ferir. Existem muitas formas de provocar dor em alguém. O bullying, as ofensas e as agressões, sejam verbais ou físicas, deixam marcas profundas em quem é alvo. A questão que fica é se, no ambiente online ou presencial, o peso dessas ações realmente muda. Dizer que ambas as formas causam danos seria óbvio. O ponto mais importante não está no meio, mas na intenção. Quando alguém decide ferir, envergonhar ou diminuir outra pessoa, o estrago já começa ali. Somos criativos por natureza e, infelizmente, essa criatividade também aparece na forma de machucar o outro, seja cara a cara ou por trás de uma tela, as consequências existem e não são leves. Pela minha própria experiência, o bullying presencial tem um impacto imediato muito forte. É um desconforto que paralisa e que pode acompanhar a pessoa por anos. Quando acontece, nem sempre há tempo ou espaço para reagir. Lembro de situações na escola que ainda hoje, quando vêm à memória, trazem um peso difícil de ignorar. Quando a vítima é uma criança, isso se torna ainda mais delicado. Mas existem muitas outras situações em que uma pessoa é exposta e lhe causada dor e o trauma pode ser irreversível, independente da idade. No ambiente online, o impacto pode seguir outro caminho. Talvez não seja tão imediato, mas pode crescer de forma descontrolada. Uma situação pode ganhar proporções enormes em pouco tempo e alcançar pessoas que nem fazem parte do contexto inicial. Quando isso acontece, o dano se espalha e pode atingir diferentes áreas da vida de alguém, muitas vezes de forma silenciosa e prolongada. Pessoas que se escondem atrás de telas podem causar impactos somados ao que está acontecendo e a facilidade de aumentar o estrago é muito maior. Quem pratica esse tipo de comportamento raramente tem noção real do que está causando. O dano vai além do momento. Ele se estende, se acumula e pode afetar profundamente a forma como alguém se vê e se relaciona com o mundo. Há quem defenda que o peso da punição deve variar dependendo do meio, mas, na prática, o sofrimento não segue essa lógica. Só quem realmente é uma vitima sabe realmente o estrago que pode ser feito, independente do meio que foi realizado essa ato deplorável. O que precisa ser analisado é a intenção. Se houve vontade de machucar, constranger ou humilhar, a resposta deve ser firme. A punição precisa servir não só como consequência, mas também como exemplo. Quando existe clareza e consistência na forma de lidar com isso, há mais chance de reduzir a repetição desses comportamentos. Mas não podemos olhar para isso e medir o ato pela forma como foi feito, mas sim como essa intenção causou consequências na vida de outra pessoa e independente do meio a punição deve ser severa, a todos os envolvidos. É difícil não sentir um certo peso ao pensar em quantas situações assim acontecem todos os dias. Muitas passam despercebidas, mas deixam marcas profundas. Em alguns casos, os danos não podem ser revertidos. Por isso, mais do que discutir onde aconteceu, é essencial olhar para o impacto causado e agir de forma proporcional a ele, com responsabilidade, consciência e, principalmente, com o objetivo de evitar que outras histórias terminem da mesma forma. Não importa o meio que o mal foi causado, a punição dever proporcional a sua consequência. --- Credits: Translated: [Deepl](www.deepl.com/pt-BR/translator) Cover: created by [Canva.](www.canva.com) AI-generated image [ Flow]( www.labs.google/fx/pt/tools/flow) --- ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQma2XinqppUM2Uvqbsii8ViPirxPmkbLmJ8FkfAbcj9EYN/image.png)

title.body:

Este post también está disponible en Español. Puedes leerlo [aquí](#espannol), o simplemente desplázate hacia abajo en la página.

---
*English*

# Chicken Herbs (genus Commelina) ### Observed on: Apr 17, 2026 · 9:55 AM CDT 📍22.829, -80.337 | https://static.inaturalist.org/photos/639959919/large.jpg | https://static.inaturalist.org/photos/639960066/large.jpg | | ------------ | ------------ |

The original observation created by me is published on iNaturalist: [original observation](https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/350722331) # Field Notes **Observation of April 17, 2026.** Sunny morning, temperature 22°C and humidity 90%. Observation begins near a small urbanisation in a rural area. Small bluish flowers from a plant that seems to be creeping because the leaves spread through a single stem, ending in a flower with very striking bluish petals and yellow pistils in the center. All the flowers seen have the same number of petals: two rounded petals, very soft to the touch. I collected flower and leaf samples for detailed observation with a magnifying glass. The leaves are an intense green with the underside lighter. The upper side of the leaf is rough and has small stiff white hairs. Some leaves seem to have a kind of white spot, not apparently part of the plant itself (maybe a disease or some insect). The ground where the small flowering plant was found is sandy, dry, with rocks that I identify (I could be wrong) as limestone or calcareous. **Some approximate measurements taken in the field using a ruler:** - Flower size: ~2 cm - Leaf size: ~4.2 cm | https://static.inaturalist.org/photos/639960249/large.jpg | https://static.inaturalist.org/photos/639960275/large.jpg | | ------------ | ------------ |

**Summary of *Commelina* – Source: Wikipedia** *Commelina* is a genus of herbaceous perennial plants in the family Commelinaceae. It includes about 200 species, among them *Commelina communis*, *C. diffusa* and *C. erecta*. **Main characteristics:** - Flowers typically with **two large showy petals** (blue or purple) and a **third small white petal**. - The genus was named by Linnaeus in honor of three botanist brothers named Commelin: the two large petals represent the two famous brothers, and the small petal symbolizes the third, less known one. - They grow in urban soils, abandoned gardens and places with partial shade or filtered light. - They attract bees, butterflies and birds. - Some species (such as *Commelina benghalensis*) are edible and used as a vegetable in Southeast Asia and Africa. **Taxonomic information:** - Kingdom: Plantae - Order: Commelinales - Family: Commelinaceae **Selected species mentioned in the article:** - *Commelina benghalensis* - *Commelina communis* - *Commelina diffusa* - *Commelina erecta* - *Commelina tuberosa* (rosilla de México) --- **Source:** Wikipedia, article \

title.title: The Pain: Hidden Scars
title.body:
/>

The initial comparison of physical bullying with online harassment leads people to determine which form of bullying causes greater harm.

The question creates confusion because it presents an incorrect assumption about two types of abuse which both create their own unique damage to victims.

Physical bullying creates immediate effects which people can see. Students experience immediate physical danger when someone pushes them or punches them or uses their body to intimidate.

The body's defense system activates through three physical responses which include heart racing and adrenaline surging and muscles tensing.

A person experiences an intense feeling of imminent danger. The memory of being vulnerable stays with those who experience this phenomenon even though their physical wounds will eventually heal.

Victims develop fear associations with specific locations which include schools and streets and entire environments. The world now feels dangerous because the attack created physical harm which also changed how safe people perceive their environment to be.  
Online harassment operates through a silent approach which maintains continuous pressure on its victims. The attacks create nonvisible effects which continue to follow their target throughout all locations.

A phone should work as a connection device but it turns into a fear-inducing object. People receive messages and comments and posts at all times which makes them feel like they cannot find any moments of peace. Online harassment creates continuous personal space violations which differ from physical bullying because it ends when someone leaves a location.  
The extensive reach and unending existence of online harassment create a major risk for users. A single cruel comment in person may be heard by a few, but online, humiliation can be amplified to hundreds or thousands.

The harmful content remains in circulation because people can share and reshare and archive it. The crowd attacks its target because the victim must defend against multiple attackers at once. The process of exposure to public view produces deep impacts on three aspects which include self-esteem and identity and mental health.

The common error involves people who believe physical bullying loses its power because it lacks online presence. The anticipation of physical harm causes people to modify their normal conduct.

The victim of physical bullying will change their daily activities because they need to stay away from specific places and they will stop all social interactions. The power of violent threats creates an urgent danger which human beings perceive as vital for their existence.  
So, is one worse than the other? Not necessarily. The more honest answer is that they are harmful in different ways.

Physical bullying targets the body and sense of safety in the physical world. Online harassment targets the mind, identity, and sense of belonging in a social world that increasingly exists online.  
What matters more than comparison is recognition. Both forms of bullying can lead to anxiety, depression, suicide, isolation, and long-term psychological effects.

Both particles require complete attention because they need their respective protective measures and their corresponding disciplinary actions.

The treatment of one as less important than another creates a risk which diminishes the real experiences of those who endure it.  
People today find it difficult to distinguish between physical harm and online harm because both their physical and digital existence exist together in the current world.

The same bullies who target students at school will also attack their victims through online platforms which creates a never-ending pattern of bullying.

The process of handling bullying needs to include both existing methods and complete understanding about how these two areas connect with each other.  
Instead of asking which is worse, we should be asking: how do we stop both?  
The actual effects of pain become evident whether the injury shows visible bruises or hidden scars which people cannot see.

Which is more painful, physical or verbal abuse?

Dire Warnings from Heaven 
End-Times, Inc.: Seven Apocalyptic Scares That Made Believers Do Crazy Things (and the People Who Profited).  

From Orson Welles' Martians to Harold Camping's Rapture, a century of dire warnings from heaven has led to mass panic, mass suicide, and a whole lot of merchandise. 

It was Halloween Eve, 1938, when millions of Americans reached for their radios and heard the end of the world. The broadcast—a dramatization of H.G. Wells' War of the Worlds—was so convincing that listeners jammed police switchboards, grabbed their guns, and prepared to fight off Martians with heat rays. But the panic wasn't real—at least, not as real as the newspapers claimed. And that tension between genuine fear and manufactured hysteria has defined every major apocalypse scare since. 

Here are seven events since 1900—plus one critical precursor—that scared believers into doing crazy things, complete with the money trail and legal fallout left behind. 



 The Precursor: The Great Disappointment (1844).  

The Prediction: Jesus Christ would return on October 22, 1844. 

William Miller, a Baptist preacher, convinced thousands of followers—the Millerites—to sell their possessions, don white robes, and ascend to heaven. When Jesus failed to appear, the day became known as the \

The Crazy: Followers sat on rooftops in their robes, waiting for the rapture that never came. Some wept through the night. 

The Ramification: Instead of abandoning their faith, many Millerites invented the \
theology—claiming Christ had entered a heavenly temple rather than Earth—which birthed the Seventh-day Adventist Church. This psychological template of \

failed prophecy would repeat for generations. 

Money? Mostly lost. Followers had given away their possessions. But the Adventist movement would grow into a wealthy denomination with hospitals, schools, and publishing houses. 



 1. The War of the Worlds (1938). 

The Prediction: Martians were invading Grover's Mill, New Jersey, with deadly heat rays and poison gas. 

Orson Welles and the Mercury Theatre on the Air produced a radio adaptation that used fake news bulletins to interrupt what seemed like a regular dance music program. For listeners who tuned in late—missing the disclaimer that it was fiction—the realism was terrifying. 

The Crazy: In Concrete, Washington, a power failure plunged the town into darkness right as the Martians were supposedly attacking. Believing this was the end, men grabbed their guns to shoot the aliens. A New York City woman ran into a church screaming that the end had come. Police in Newark received nearly a thousand calls. The New Jersey Bell telephone company reported 75,000 to 100,000 extra calls during the 8:00 hour alone. 

The Ramification: The FCC launched an immediate investigation. Trenton's City Manager wrote a furious letter complaining that the broadcast had \

. Congress demanded laws to prevent such broadcasts.  \n\nUltimately, the FCC closed its investigation in December 1938 after CBS promised to avoid making fiction sound like breaking news. No fines were issued. However, the FCC later adopted a formal \

(Section 73.1217) that today would likely result in massive fines for such a broadcast. \nAccountability: Orson Welles apologized publicly, claiming he didn't know the broadcast would cause panic—though internal evidence suggests otherwise. H.G. Wells, author of the original novel, told the New York Times that CBS had \
.  \nMoney? Welles became a household name, launching his film career. CBS saw its audience skyrocket. The Mercury Theatre gained national attention. While no direct profiteering occurred, the \

narrative sold a lot of newspapers—the New York Times front page story is now considered a significant overstatement of the actual hysteria. 



 2. The Cold War \

(1950s-60s). 

The Prediction: Nuclear annihilation at the hands of the Soviet Union, interpreted by evangelicals as the biblical Armageddon preceding Christ's return. 

The Crazy: School children practiced \

drills—huddling under wooden desks that would have done nothing against an atomic blast. Families built fallout shelters stocked with canned goods and firearms. Some evangelical preachers identified Soviet leaders as the Antichrist. 

The Ramification: The nuclear threat never materialized as predicted, but the Cold War ended only after decades of near-misses (Cuban Missile Crisis, Able Archer 83). The existential fear reshaped American civil defense policy and popular culture. 

Money? A booming industry of survival gear, shelter construction, and canned food suppliers. Civil defense contractors made fortunes. The evangelical prophecy industry—books, conferences, films—grew substantially.  



 3. Heaven's Gate (1997).   

The Prediction: The Comet Hale-Bopp was hiding a UFO that would take their souls to \
\n\nLed by Marshall Applewhite, the Heaven's Gate cult believed their bodies were mere \

that needed to be shed to board the spacecraft behind the comet. \n\nThe Crazy: On March 26, 1997, police entered a rented mansion in Rancho Santa Fe, California, and found 39 bodies—all dead by suicide. They were dressed in matching black Nike sneakers and armband patches reading \

Each had consumed a fatal mixture of phenobarbital and vodka. 

The Ramification: The largest mass suicide on U.S. soil. Applewhite had convinced followers to sever all ties with family, sell their possessions, and dedicate their lives (and deaths) to the cause. The cult funded itself through a web design business called Higher Source. 

Accountability: Applewhite died with his followers. No one was prosecuted. The event sparked national debate about cults, religious freedom, and warning signs. 

Money? The cult had assets, including a $7,000-per-month mansion lease. Their web design business generated revenue. After the suicides, the remaining estate was tied up in legal battles. Nike famously tried to distance itself from the brand association. 



 4. The Y2K Bug (1999-2000).   

The Prediction: On January 1, 2000, computers would crash because of a two-digit date coding error. Planes would fall from the sky, power grids would fail, and society would collapse. 

The Crazy: Survivalists moved to remote compounds. Families stockpiled water, generators, ammunition, and dehydrated food. Some dug wells and drilled for natural gas. The recommendation to stockpile toilet paper as a barter item became a running joke. 

Southern Baptists and Pat Robertson's Christian Broadcasting Network openly viewed Y2K as a recruiting tool. \

.  

The Ramification: Nothing happened. The new year arrived with barely a flicker. Millions of food buckets sat untouched in garages for years. 

Accountability: The experts who predicted catastrophe largely disappeared from public view. Some admitted they got it wrong. Most simply moved on to the next scare. 

Money? This was the big one. Y2K became a $600 billion global industry. Consultants billed fortune. Lawyers prepared for lawsuits. Survival gear companies saw massive spikes. Walton Feed's dehydrated food business doubled. Emergency Essentials saw sales rise 40%. Books flooded the market—including Everyone's Guide to Making a Million Dollars on the Year 2000 Crash for $44.95. One observer called Y2K \

. 



 5. Harold Camping's 2011 Rapture.   

The Prediction: The Rapture would occur on May 21, 2011, followed by the end of the world on October 21. 

Using complex biblical numerology, the 89-year-old Christian broadcaster spent millions on billboards worldwide declaring \

\n\nThe Crazy: Followers sold their homes, quit their jobs, and drained their retirement accounts to spread the message. Some spent their life savings on advertising. When May 21 passed without incident, Camping claimed it was a \
(invisible) judgment. When October 21 also passed quietly, he admitted he \

The Ramification: Family Radio, Camping's organization, had spent approximately $100 million on the campaign. Most of this came from selling a television station and an FM station, but significant donations also came from followers who sacrificed everything. 

Accountability: The Freedom from Religion Foundation asked the California Attorney General to investigate fraud. Legal scholars said lawsuits were almost certainly doomed under First Amendment protections. The Supreme Court's 1944 United States v. Ballard decision ruled that courts cannot declare religious beliefs true or false. \

. He noted that Family Radio never advised followers on financial matters. 

Money? Family Radio retained most of its assets. Charity Navigator had rated it a 4-star charity. The $100 million was spent exactly as promised—on advertising the end. Legally, that made it difficult to claim fraud. But for followers who lost their life savings, the distinction was cold comfort. 



 6. The 2012 Mayan Apocalypse.   

The Prediction: The Mayan Long Count calendar ends on December 21, 2012, bringing catastrophic Earth changes or total destruction. 

The Crazy: People flocked to \

like Bugarach mountain in France (believed to be a Noah's Ark-style refuge) and Sirince, Turkey. Survival gear sales skyrocketed. One survival company reported a 400% increase in pandemic kit sales. 

The Ramification: The sun rose on December 22. The world continued. Most Mayan scholars had said all along that the calendar's end simply marked the beginning of a new cycle. 

Money? Global box office for the movie 2012—starring John Cusack and massive CGI destruction—was $770 million. The Stevens Point Brewery sold a \
with Mayan calendar labels. CafePress sold tens of thousands of doomsday items: thong underwear reading \
and T-shirts with the planet Earth saying \
. Tour companies charged $5,000 per person for trips to Mayan ruins on the fateful date. Hotels offered \
packages. \n\nA religion professor noted the cycle: \

. 



 The Pattern: Profit, Panic, and No Accountability.  

Seven events, seven cycles of fear, and one consistent outcome: someone always makes money. 

The profiteers fall into three categories.  

The Legitimate Opportunists: Y2K consultants, survival gear sellers, movie studios, and breweries selling apocalypse-themed products. They didn't create the fear, but they happily capitalized on it.  

The True Believers: Harold Camping, Marshall Applewhite, and the Millerites genuinely believed their predictions. Their followers' financial losses were collateral damage to sincere (if delusional) faith. 

The Legal Escape Hatch: The First Amendment's protection of religious belief makes fraud claims nearly impossible. As long as the predictor genuinely believes—or can convincingly claim to believe—their prediction, they cannot be sued for being wrong. The Supreme Court has ruled that juries cannot determine the \

of religious claims. 

The pattern endures because the human need for meaning—and the human capacity for self-deception—remains unchanged. Whether it's Martians, nuclear war, computer bugs, or comets, the apocalypse is always just around the corner. And someone is always selling tickets.

今天的步行真是一次愉快的体验！阳光明媚，微风轻拂，完美的天气让我心情格外好。 在我散步的过程中，遇到了一位老奶奶，她正在公园的长椅上喂鸽子。她一边撒着面包屑，一边和我聊起了她年轻时的故事，提到当年她也是个喜欢在城市里散步的人，真是和我感觉好相似！她的笑声和温暖的回忆让我感受到生活的美好。 另外，我还看到了一位街头艺术家，他正在墙上画一幅巨大的涂鸦作品，色彩鲜艳且充满创意。很多路人都停下脚步欣赏，有些甚至拿出手机拍照。他的作品展现了城市的活力与多样性，让我不禁感叹艺术可以把日常生活变得如此生动。 总之，今天的散步让我不仅锻炼了身体，还收获了温暖的交流和美丽的视觉享受。生活真是处处有惊喜！ _This report was published via Actifit app ([Android](https://bit.ly/actifit-app) | [iOS](https://bit.ly/actifit-ios)). title.title: (EN-DA) Plank shoulder taps: A hidden powerhouse exercise-Planke skuldertaps: En skjult kraftfuld øvelse
title.body: (English version) Hello, Healthy Bees! This is my first post to the community.

/> [_Plank Pose at Live the Riverfront Moonlight Yoga 2016_](https://www.flickr.com/photos/healthiermi/28420678756/in/photolist-2m9ARLo-2m7H1Mh-2gBzqjH-9FPLha-9FPLgX-2gBDDhi-eF7K9u-2kUHc4b-dV8VsW-csMMVA-JVikhE-KirpCG-JpNWUN-2hrFw2B-oofudU-egk1mY-8B7Q1f) _was originally posted on Flickr by_ [_A Healthier Michigan_](https://www.flickr.com/photos/healthiermi/) _and is reused here under the terms and conditions of the_ [_Attribution-ShareAlike 2.0 Generic (CC BY-SA 2.0)_](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0/) _Creative Commons license_ **From doing the plank to doing shoulder taps** If you are a plank aficionado like me, chances are that you will also fall in love with shoulder taps. This is because, in order to do shoulder taps, you will first have to go into the plank pose. And remember, you should rest on your palms instead of your elbows. Trying to keep your body in a straight line, just like when doing the plank, is important, because, in this way, you will prevent, for example, your back from hunching, and getting injured in the long run. Instead of using both of your hands to rest your body upon, as you would do in the plank, you alternately use each palm to support your body, touching the ground with one palm and lifting the other palm to touch the shoulder, and so on, to the point of failure, that is until you have reached your limit, and you can do no more repetitions. In this way, each arm, forearm, wrist, and palm holds double the weight and makes double the effort, compared to what would happen during the ordinary plank pose. **Are shoulder taps an effective form of exercise?** https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pO1BxvWpVN4&pp=ygUgYXJlIHBsYW5rIHNob3VsZGVyIHRhcHMgYW55IGdvb2Q%3D You bet it is! Shoulder taps are a typical exercise that is more effective than most people tend to believe. Although other forms of exercise, such as using weights, are believed to be the most effective ones in helping people build muscle, for example, shoulder taps, which is a bodyweight exercise, has it own, unique benefits. In many ways, this exercise mimics the movement of different animals that are well-known for their extraordinary strength. Therefore, it can also work in the same way, and help humans using it to build stamina and overall body strength. Contrary to common belief, it is not necessary to lift weights, and sometimes, tons of them, in order to dramatically improve your body’s look and posture, and feel strong as an animal (literally). Doing 30 reps of shoulder taps in a row, for instance, can make you realize how challenging this exercise really is and include it in your regular training routine. **My own experience with doing shoulder taps** While I was looking on the Internet for different exercises that can boost my whole body fitness level, I stumbled upon shoulder taps, which is very similar or an alternative to the standard plank pose on the palms. It is claimed that this exercise works many different muscles, such as both the biceps and the triceps, at the same time. In fact, it is one of the few plank versions, if not the only one, that works muscles both at the back and front of the arm, whereas an ordinary plank usually only works the biceps. For me, this is a major advantage, when choosing to do an exercise. So, when I gave it a go and did 40 reps of shoulder taps within a couple of minutes, I immediately felt how effective this exercise is. I was panting for breath within seconds, and I realized that shoulder taps are also great for cardiovascular health. In terms of strength, when I tried to lift a chair immediately after doing the exercise, it felt lighter to lift, and my muscles felt stronger. **A little word of caution when doing shoulder taps** https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ztpXZm7Dv80&pp=ygUgYXJlIHBsYW5rIHNob3VsZGVyIHRhcHMgYW55IGdvb2Q%3D When you do shoulder taps for the first time, you may get easily disappointed, especially if your fitness level is low, and you have big belly, for example, which can prevent your from doing a high number of reps, and enjoying the benefits of this exercise to the maximum. With persistent effort, however, you can increase your reps with time, lose weight, and do even more reps, in turn. So, the key is not to get disappointed too early, because, otherwise, you will not be able to reap the full benefits of this highly effective form of bodyweight exercise. (Dansk version) Hej, Healthy Bees! Dette er mit første indlæg til fællesskabet.

/>

[_Plank Pose at Live the Riverfront Moonlight Yoga 2016_](https://www.flickr.com/photos/healthiermi/28420678756/in/photolist-2m9ARLo-2m7H1Mh-2gBzqjH-9FPLha-9FPLgX-2gBDDhi-eF7K9u-2kUHc4b-dV8VsW-csMMVA-JVikhE-KirpCG-JpNWUN-2hrFw2B-oofudU-egk1mY-8B7Q1f) blev oprindeligt lagt ud på Flickr af [_A Healthier Michigan_](https://www.flickr.com/photos/healthiermi/) og genbruges her i henhold til vilkårene og betingelserne i [_Attribution-ShareAlike 2.0 Generic (CC BY-SA 2.0)_](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0/) Creative Commons-licens

**Fra at lave planken til at lave skuldertaps**

Hvis du er en planke-entusiast ligesom mig, er der stor sandsynlighed for, at du også vil forelske dig i skuldertaps.

Det skyldes, at for at lave skuldertaps skal du først gå ind i plankestillingen.

Og husk, at du skal hvile på dine håndflader i stedet for dine albuer.

Det er vigtigt at forsøge at holde din krop i en lige linje, ligesom når du laver planken, fordi du på denne måde for eksempel forhindrer, at din ryg bøjer sig og bliver skadet i det lange løb.

I stedet for at bruge begge hænder til at hvile din krop på, som du ville gøre i planken, bruger du skiftevis hver håndflade til at støtte din krop, rører jorden med den ene håndflade og løfter den anden håndflade for at røre skulderen, og så videre, indtil du ikke kan klare det, indtil du har nået din grænse, og du ikke kan lave flere gentagelser.

På denne måde bærer hver arm, underarm, håndled og håndflade dobbelt så meget vægt og gør dobbelt så meget indsats sammenlignet med, hvad der ville ske under den almindelige plankestilling.

**Er skuldertryk en effektiv form for motion?**

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pO1BxvWpVN4&pp=ygUgYXJlIHBsYW5rIHNob3VsZGVyIHRhcHMgYW55IGdvb2Q%3D

Det er du sikker på!

Skuldertryk er en typisk øvelse, der er mere effektiv, end de fleste tror.

Selvom andre former for motion, såsom at bruge vægte, menes at være de mest effektive til at hjælpe folk med at opbygge muskler, har for eksempel skuldertryk, som er en kropsvægtsøvelse, sine egne unikke fordele.

På mange måder efterligner denne øvelse bevægelserne hos forskellige dyr, der er kendte for deres ekstraordinære styrke.

Derfor kan den også fungere på samme måde og hjælpe mennesker med at bruge den til at opbygge udholdenhed og generel kropsstyrke.

I modsætning til den almindelige opfattelse er det ikke nødvendigt at løfte vægte, og nogle gange masser af dem, for dramatisk at forbedre din krops udseende og kropsholdning og føle dig stærk som et dyr (bogstaveligt talt).

At lave 30 gentagelser af skuldertryk i træk kan for eksempel få dig til at indse, hvor udfordrende denne øvelse virkelig er, og inkludere den i din regelmæssige træningsrutine.

Min egen erfaring med skuldertaps

Mens jeg søgte på internettet efter forskellige øvelser, der kan forbedre min samlede kropslige kondition, faldt jeg over skuldertaps, som minder meget om eller er et alternativ til den almindelige plankestilling på håndfladerne.

Det siges, at denne øvelse træner mange forskellige muskler, såsom både biceps og triceps, på samme tid.

Faktisk er det en af ​​de få plankeversioner, hvis ikke den eneste, der træner muskler både på bagsiden og forsiden af ​​armen, hvorimod en almindelig planke normalt kun træner biceps.

For mig er dette en stor fordel, når man vælger at lave en øvelse.

Så da jeg prøvede det og lavede 40 gentagelser af skuldertaps på et par minutter, mærkede jeg straks, hvor effektiv denne øvelse er.

Jeg gispede efter vejret i løbet af få sekunder, og jeg indså, at skuldertaps også er gode for hjerte-kar-sundheden.

Med hensyn til styrke, da jeg prøvede at løfte en stol umiddelbart efter øvelsen, føltes det lettere at løfte, og mine muskler føltes stærkere.

**En lille advarsel, når du laver skuldertryk**

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ztpXZm7Dv80&pp=ygUgYXJlIHBsYW5rIHNob3VsZGVyIHRhcHMgYW55IGdvb2Q%3D

Når du laver skuldertryk for første gang, kan du nemt blive skuffet, især hvis dit konditionsniveau er lavt, og du for eksempel har en stor mave, hvilket kan forhindre dig i at udføre et højt antal gentagelser og nyde fordelene ved denne øvelse maksimalt.

Med vedholdende indsats kan du dog øge dine gentagelser med tiden, tabe dig og dermed udføre endnu flere gentagelser.

Så nøglen er ikke at blive skuffet for tidligt, for ellers vil du ikke være i stand til at høste det fulde udbytte af denne yderst effektive form for kropsvægtstræning.

(Dette indlæg blev oversat fra engelsk til dansk med Google Translate)

title.title: Television Review: The Wheel (Mad Men, S1x13, 2007)
title.body:
![(source:madmen.fandom.com)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/madmen/images/8/83/The_wheel.jpg)


**The Wheel (S1x13)**

Airdate: 18 October 2007

Written by: Matthew Weiner & Robin Veith
Directed by: Matthew Weiner

Running Time: 52 minutes



In the contemporary landscape of prestigious television drama, a now‑common structural gambit sees the season’s most defining, explosive moments reserved for the penultimate episode. This practice, whilst often delivering a powerful immediate punch, carries a significant risk: the actual season finale can appear weak, underwhelming and inconsequential by comparison. This is precisely the trap into which *Mad Men*’s first season falls. The brilliance of *Nixon vs. Kennedy* – an episode of profound political and personal upheaval – is replaced by the more pedestrian, conventional *The Wheel*. The contrast renders the final chapter of an otherwise superb season a curiously flat and anti‑climactic affair, a competent piece of television that nevertheless fails to match the heights of what came immediately before it.

The plot of *The Wheel* unfolds several weeks after the momentous events of the previous episode: the 1960 presidential election and Don Draper’s securing of his partnership at Sterling Cooper by fending off Pete Campbell’s blackmail attempt. The episode is largely concerned with the aftermath, showing characters grappling with the new status quo.

The Draper family is supposed to reunite with Betty’s family for Thanksgiving, but Don is adamant in his refusal to attend, citing work pressures. At the office, he receives the shattering news that his brother, Adam, has committed suicide. Simultaneously, he learns that Rachel Menken, with whom he shared a genuine connection, is embarking on a three‑month world trip; a call from her father to Bert Cooper is interpreted as a not‑so‑subtle hint that their affair is conclusively over. Plunged into acute loneliness, Don channels this desolation into professional inspiration, crafting the legendary pitch for Kodak’s new Carousel slide projector. Using slides of his own family, he sells a nostalgic, aching vision of ‘the wheel’ of time and memory, securing Kodak as a client in a moment of triumphant artifice.

Whilst Don triumphs professionally, the episode pointedly contrasts his success with the personal suffering of others. Harry Crane, having attempted honesty by confessing his one‑night stand with Hildy to his wife, is banished to the office. Watching the happy images of the Drapers during Don’s presentation, he breaks down in tears – a stark reminder that the perfect family tableau is a marketable fiction. Pete Campbell, meanwhile, operates under intense pressure to save his job. His humiliation is complete when he must accept help from his father‑in‑law, who uses old connections to secure the Clearasil account. Don assigns the newly promoted junior copywriter, Peggy Olson, to handle it, compounding Pete’s emasculation. His frustration finds solace only in drink, much to his wife Trudy’s displeasure.

The domestic sphere offers no sanctuary either. Betty Draper’s storyline takes a decisive turn when her friend Francine arrives to complain about her husband Carlton’s affair, discovered via Manhattan numbers on a phone bill. Betty, harbouring her own suspicions, tests a Manhattan number from her own bill only to discover it belongs to her psychiatrist, Dr. Wayne, who has been colluding with Don. This betrayal – deeper than mere infidelity – prompts her to begin deliberately feeding suspicions to the psychiatrist, knowing they will be passed to her husband, a quiet act of marital warfare.

Peggy’s arc culminates in the episode’s most conventionally dramatic ‘wham’ moment. Having finally been promoted and given an office, albeit shared with the grumpy Victor Manny (Jonathan Spencer), her triumph is undercut by severe stomach pains. Rushed to hospital, she and the attending doctors are stunned to discover she is not only pregnant but entering labour. In a chilling, ambiguous moment after the birth, she turns away when offered the chance to hold her baby. This plot twist, whilst undeniably powerful, feels like a more traditional season‑ender, a cliffhanger setting up the career‑versus‑family dilemma that will define her character in subsequent seasons.

The episode concludes on a masterfully melancholy note of self‑deception. Don returns home and agrees to join Betty and the children for Thanksgiving, appearing to choose family. The final shot reveals this to be a fantasy; the season ends with Don utterly alone in his dark, empty house. This conclusion underscores the episode’s central theme: the gap between the lives we curate, both for clients and for ourselves, and the desolate reality we inhabit.

*The Wheel*, co‑written by Matthew Weiner and Robin Veith and marking Weiner’s directorial debut for the series (it would later earn both an Emmy nomination), is a finale of intriguing contradictions. It is both conventional and unconventional. Its unconventionality lies in its refusal to deliver major, plot‑driven resolutions for its protagonist. Don experiences a kind of epiphany – shaken by his brother’s death and Rachel’s departure, he seems to realise that his constructed life with Betty might be preferable to yet another reinvention. Yet, in a cruel irony, Betty is simultaneously learning the extent of his deceptions and beginning her emotional withdrawal, sowing the seeds of the marital collapse that will unfold in later seasons. The finale thus trades explosive action for poignant, character‑based irony.

However, some of its choices feel less assured. The scene between Betty and the young boy, Glenn Bishop, in which she discusses his private troubles, remains awkward and has long been criticised as an indulgence for Weiner’s son, who played the role. It adds little to the episode’s thematic weight. Furthermore, whilst Peggy’s secret pregnancy is handled with the show’s typical subtlety – the self‑delusion of a woman focused on career over family is psychologically plausible – its revelation as a last‑act shock inevitably feels like a concession to more conventional serialised storytelling. It is the kind of dramatic punctuation mark the show was often wise to avoid.

First season of *Mad Men* is a superb and fascinating recreation of the past’ with fascinating characters’ while noting a lack of traditional plot. *The Wheel* encapsulates these strengths and weaknesses. It is a character study steeped in period detail and psychological nuance, yet its plot mechanics, especially when compared to the seismic shifts of *Nixon vs. Kennedy*, can feel slight. The season’s overall excellence is isn’t drastically diminished with  *The Wheel*, but the episode functions as the season’s least essential chapter.


RATING: 7/10 (+++)

title.body:
![IMG_0778.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcmUALnqp5n7NNjjB76CxNFkTaTzb5gN71rMcG6HzXUsx/IMG_0778.jpeg)
 A kind heart is quiet.
It doesn’t beg to be seen.

It shows up in small ways
in the way you listen,
in the way you stay
when it would be easier to leave.

It feels things deeply,
sometimes too deeply.
It carries pain
it didn’t create.
A kind heart forgives
even when it still aches.
It gives, even when it’s tired.

Not because it’s weak
but because it refuses
to become something cold.
And most days,
no one claps for it.
No one notices.

But somewhere,
in someone’s quiet moment,
it made the world softer.

Charcoal and crayon on paper
8 x 11 inch

title.title: Daily story 20/4/2026 : Many stories on a rainy day.
title.body: /> Hello all lovely friends. How are you? I hope everyone is fine. Today I have various stories from my daily life to share with my friends. The story begins at 6:00 AM. The atmosphere is quite nice; it had been raining since last night. This morning, the weather is quite good. I prepare breakfast for the children, then wake them up so they can get ready, shower, and get dressed. Afterward, we carry our bags down the stairs to the dining room. In the afternoon, it rained heavily, but not for long, about 20 minutes. In the evening, I cook. It's a daily routine, but there are small details interspersed throughout, making it a story. I encourage you to follow along and read my article.

/> The children are ready to drink milk. I sat waiting for the children to finish their morning milk. My little daughter sometimes dawdled a bit, but she was always cheerful and happy. Soon they finished their milk, and it was time for them to go to school.

/> Today's flowers are very beautiful because they received really good rain. Wow, the morning glory is blooming early this morning! It's been raining frequently lately, so the flowers are all lush and blooming profusely. There are so many beautiful flowers everywhere, but these morning glory weren't planted; they just sprouted, but they're as beautiful as ever.

/> Around noon, just before I went to pick up my daughter, it started raining. So I didn't think about going immediately and waited for about 10 minutes until it began to drizzle, then I was able to drive to school to pick her up. Actually, if my husband had been home, he could have picked her up right away because he has the car... When I got home, I was completely soaked, but the children weren't because they were sitting in the back and I held umbrellas for them.

/>At 4 PM, it was time to cook. Today I made three simple dishes, nothing complicated... and they didn't take long because I marinated the pork yesterday. The other dishes were vegetables that don't require much stir-frying. These days, we're trying to save money wherever we can, even with rising costs, but we still cook fresh every day. Tomato and egg stir-fry is a favorite of mine and the kids'. For the vegetables, I used oyster sauce and didn't add any other seasoning because we usually don't eat much sauce in stir-fries. At 6 PM, the kids went to bathe and got ready to eat. That's our story for today. Thank you for reading my article. See you again in the next one. Bye-bye!\n\nThank you.(◍•ᴗ•◍)❤

title.title: [Eng/Esp]✨ Healthy, Creamy & Delicious: Papaya Banana Juice You Need to Try
title.body:
Hello dear friends of the Amazing Drinks community 👋💖
I hope you're having a wonderful day full of positive energy.

Today I want to share with you a delicious, natural, and very easy-to-make drink 🌞. It's a papaya and banana juice, a perfect combination that results in a creamy texture and an irresistibly sweet flavor.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdQnLqUpeD3dQjeRdmcZbWWnH18EYatQ9KE5NCASBQG4T/1776460711401.jpg)

This drink is not only tasty but also very beneficial for your health. Papaya is excellent for digestion thanks to its natural enzymes, while banana provides energy, potassium, and a smooth consistency that makes this juice almost like a smoothie 🥤✨.

**Ingredients:**

- 3 cups of ripe papaya
- 2 medium ripe bananas
- 3 cups of cold water or more (depending on how thick you want the juice)
- Sugar or honey to taste (optional)
- A pinch of salt (to enhance the flavor)

👩‍🍳**Preparation:**

1- Peel and cut the papaya into small pieces.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXvLXMubeASQbpqvoRGBj8tRFSd9FkCPNU8w9ZCGvKZNY/1776461184111.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPjDKkyyMwXBVqhLhg1DsYgY1M6oVkKNerTMyWmh69atj/1776461220053.jpg)

2- Peel the banana and slice it.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbE6qU8qwkJ7rcyfcLhue9zDsPsvBBzdexsc9tCinppPi/1776461275226.jpg)

3- Place both ingredients in the blender.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfS5JEwwvR5gMFUkoTcW91hTJiSXU5whRzH3U69UDK6X3/1776461352126.jpg)

4- Add the water, a pinch of salt and sweetener if desired.
5- Blend until smooth and creamy.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZ4CnBuchHJbrkVr6dKqQCBn1ouwHv9veh7kaW5MtRY71/1776461379111.jpg)

6- Serve with ice and enjoy it cold.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaUEF6UtZhKK5UpuHwHvwLWAdvAxg59pQBs5m3jNpHRsR/1776461400682.jpg)

🌿 **Benefits:**

Supports digestion
Provides natural energy
Rich in vitamins A, C, and potassium
Ideal for breakfast or as a snack

This juice is perfect to start your day right or to refresh yourself on a hot afternoon. It's also a great option for the whole family thanks to its mild and pleasant taste 💛.

I hope you try it at home and let me know how it turns out 🤗
See you in the next post!

Thank you all very much for your votes and comments. Thanks to this community for the warm welcome and for the advice to improve my posts.

<center> **Versión en español**

✨ **Saludable, Cremoso y Delicioso: Jugo de Papaya y Plátano que Debes Probar**

Hola queridos amigos de la comunidad Amazing Drinks 👋💖
Espero que estén teniendo un día maravilloso lleno de energía positiva.

Hoy quiero compartir con ustedes una bebida deliciosa, natural y muy fácil de preparar 🌞. Se trata de un jugo de frutabomba (papaya) con plátano, una combinación perfecta que resulta en una textura cremosa y un sabor irresistiblemente dulce.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdQnLqUpeD3dQjeRdmcZbWWnH18EYatQ9KE5NCASBQG4T/1776460729200.jpg)

Esta bebida no solo es sabrosa, sino también muy beneficiosa para la salud. La frutabomba es excelente para la digestión gracias a sus enzimas naturales, mientras que el plátano aporta energía, potasio y una consistencia suave que convierte este jugo en casi un batido 🥤✨.

**Ingredientes:**

3 tazas de frutabomba madura (papaya)
2 plátanos maduros medianos
3 vasos de agua fría o más (en dependencia de cuán espeso quieren el jugo)
Azúcar o miel al gusto (opcional)
Una pizca de sal (para resaltar el sabor)
Hielo al gusto

👩‍🍳 **Preparación:**

1- Pela y corta la frutabomba en trozos pequeños.

title.title: Figs, walnuts, olives to cure an energy hangover
title.body:
Yesterday, I felt pretty overwhelmed and, frankly,  a bit depressed. I literally struggled to express myself ( both on here and to @clareartista ) and spend most of the time being quiet, not doing much at all. I struggled to smile and enjoying things proved extremely difficult. I also felt very low on energy, no matter how much ( good food ) I ate. Almost as if I was experiencing a hangover. 

Now I have had plenty of hangovers in my life ( from drinking too much alcohol the day/ night before  ) but this was a different one. 

I guess you could call it an energy hangover. 

I suspect that it was caused by a - very exceptional - cup of coffee, some sugary things and a small bit of alcohol, two days earlier, mixed with us having had a visitor for two full days and three nights. 

Clare's friend left us yesterday morning, after arriving early Thursday night and even though she has been a pretty easy going guest, it left a mark on me/ us. Both Clare and I are famous for being super attentive and social when the need arises and often have to deal with the consequences ( of giving away too much of our energy ) soon after.

Comunque/ anyhow, we decided to call it a night early, yesterday ( which is nothing new as we mostly rise with the sun and go to bed when the sun sets ) and this morning I woke up a new man, again.

So far, today, apart from having had a very luxurious, savory double breakfast, Clare and I have mostly enjoyed spending time in our garden/ on our land. In fact, whilst I am writing this, Clare is still snipping brambles and moving stones ( opening up yet another path in the area above our old well. 

I suspect that she will come in soon though, as it's raining and it is pretty much lunch time. I am already looking forward to a nice ( rice and beans? ) dish.

I just heard some rumbling of thunder. This is supposed to be the rain before the (actual proper) rain that will likely follow tomorrow.

We welcome any amount of it ( although we prefer to keep the inside of our house dry, if possible - see my earlier posts ) as it has been very dry and our land ( 's top soil ) seems pretty parched, even though it's only mid Spring.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRh4JEBY3kgbQo6U9qM5m1QX99vZq9ganJx4aJuTz4zsA/1776685038698.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUaS1Mq9fY9DVAZPbKqJWryMd66ghEgEuqmKHbbssH9Rr/1776685038337.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmStaUf84U6z6Pfdx8g5nBec4FfTwXTS8T2DakbMZhgXiT/1776685037377.jpg)

Dry or not ( he typed while the rain poured down outside ), most of our trees are hardy and used to extremes. So, as you can see on the pictures, our olives, figs and walnut trees are doing pretty good. 

It is, in fact, very exciting to see how well they are doing ( as a consequence of us taking care of them, since last Summer ). And, unlike some people, nature tends to reprocicate abundantly.

It is also extra special to experience our very first Spring out here, on our land. Everything is new and the view around our changes every single day.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcyudwcomxpAT6qUGqjgHH3WV2YcungJrdghcG7WUCduw/1776685038053.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQma3534FUqmWfmyQiVzTyQivfkK7bCPM9fHCr4SaAmno4q/1776685037775.jpg)

I did cut down two of our 80+ olives though as they were growing too close to other ones. They will make for amazing firewood. 

**Notice the stump in the foreground of the following pic?**

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaBfZvUdJ5BJ9XjTYuqgET1AEhNTjb6U2wfqzH1mavPY8/1776684952333.jpg)

*Fun fact: freshly sawn olivewood seems to smell like applecider or apple juice* 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbz2gvmETKircmGqeGH1bdNMgzkHivxGWaUk6JZ5MiKDi/1776684953404.jpg)

Now let me end this with some pretty pictures of several of our walnut trees and approaching rain clouds.

We will likely have more than enough of this amazing fruit to last us an entire year, after our next harvest coming Autumn.

Sending love from Molise, Italia.  

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQrDHmUUoay8iGSMqd6zwPuwA516AzMLLV3SgKEuPRuPT/1776684952873.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZmrvPDecCPMmMxsRMscMALwMtUMuMRQeSY6wE55JJ6Q8/1776684953174.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdwnANt5CAw7gUehh3pNSorJcXXFvV4jPDECCxF3eBY8B/1776684952696.jpg)

title.title: Scrambled Eggs and Onions: A Filipino Hive Dinner Story
title.body:
![collage.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/leighdalisay/AK3evcJ7h7so7LswvQUxMhMMbBqwQSEuwmeQcYL4QvN9nGqxKssfW4jsXJx6hFK.jpeg)

**Hello Hive Fam!** Most especially to my co-Filipino Hive blog writers, I’m excited to share a simple yet heartfelt story with you today. Our Hive community thrives on authenticity, and tonight I’m bringing you a slice of my everyday life.

![a96c6534-cb90-49bb-8600-a0de1c07c559.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/leighdalisay/EoGxueoRVEgX5bVaKNMdd5XZFMUCJ4bnzz97iT6TrifTkjbGjN8t2eWsRpb49tgspPm.jpeg)

Dinner time is always a moment of reflection for me. With a tight budget guiding my choices, I’ve decided to keep things simple yet satisfying. Tonight’s meal is none other than **scrambled eggs with onions**. It may sound humble, but there’s something comforting about the aroma of sautéed onions blending with fluffy eggs. This dish reminds me of the resilience and creativity we Filipinos carry in our kitchens, making the most of what we have and turning it into something delicious.

![f4cc99b2-e9c7-4f9c-a8d2-f7d9312e045c.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/leighdalisay/EoiVASkFX9kgkuN6Um6cbJLyCGbuv7jXTb68c3dTiJE5UkWKw48iCUbtrQUpkg6nsPx.jpeg)

As I whisked the eggs and watched them transform in the pan, I thought about how food connects us. Whether it’s a grand feast or a modest plate, it’s the act of sharing that makes it meaningful. And here I am, sharing my dinner story with you, Hive Fam, because even the simplest meals deserve a place in our narratives.

**Thank you, dear readers, for taking the time to join me in this little dinner tale.** Your support and presence in the Hive community make every post worthwhile. Until next time, let’s continue celebrating both the big and small joys of life together.

title.title: Beautiful Ritan Park In a Rainy Day!
title.body:
>

I have visited the Ritan Park at the beginning of April on a work day as I was in Beijing city for my visa passport renewal. The park is located in the Chaoyang district and I went to the same area as  most of the foreign embassies are located in this district in the Beijing. Also, it was a rainy day without sun in the sky and as a s result the day was not so bright as it is usually during this springtime of the year. The views of the entire park are so empty at first glance, as the gate I used was the south gate, which was not so popular for entry, I think. I have not covered all the areas of the park, as I was on my way to the institute after I had my work done in the embassy in the afternoon. But in the short visit, I found this beautiful spot in the park with a large pond and so many rocks surrounding the pond area, making it a great attraction for the visitors.


I have entered the park from the south gate, which is on the same road as the embassy road that I have visited, and found this interesting section on the left side of the park. I have not selected the right direction because that direction is far away from my final destination to catch the bus to return home. So, I wanted to go towards the left side and exit from the park through the western gate.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNet3hci1ektvEfnUQwJf4S1zEaZRmXAmMdnXwd42LaUx/img_20260409_120534.jpg)


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmX4p9E57SeappFDGyRuvuNNABPW8qkoW9nP1VNMd7GBZT/img_20260409_120714.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUbzhdVmD9cXJe4xG5E3RpRwxsWyJiiycdDDGSaQVxPDq/img_20260409_120725.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZ5sQJ3anJNgYGCW24w5SUN2qvaaTuzit3JgEVmw9fjmo/img_20260409_120735.jpg)



At a smaller distance, I found the spot, and it is a beautiful one, and I think the most beautiful spot of the whole park. The water of the pond is quite high due to the rainwater. The greenish surroundings of the park make it so attractive in this dry region. I saw a good number of visitors in this section, while other parts seemed to have very few people.

I found many people interested in walking on the waterside stone way, where some of the stones are curved like you are in a world of stone caves, and the vibes are completely natural in this part of the water body. These are built with real stones, and some of the shapes and corners of the stones are decayed over time, with smooth rocky finishing, and such an attractive color combination of the stones. Though the day was a cloudy day bit this section is so vibrant with such amazing beauty.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYuaKUc3fJaBz13c3iC7GaJW6VeLNj3okGRr9oXQvP19u/img_20260409_120603.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmes2fkDVRmcHQAuLKxgxw4HdgrWPjM238qdKwXfTCpQ3G/img_20260409_120759.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdAb9gEfMX5eaqyoczb2Z5hftgDidR8bBLxEy7Q8nBJ5i/img_20260409_120745.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVcTYemFPaALjMBj7hZLQpS89t2NUKCsm3LytZFF79CvM/img_20260409_120748.jpg)

I have also walked on the waterside way full of stones, and the surrounding nature was welcoming me. The natural beauty is so good that it is everywhere in such parks in Beijing, and when some water bodies are built near such amazing nature, the beauty of the place increases a lot, like this place. The overall area is completely neat and clean without any garbage. So, I enjoyed the fresh air and environment there under the bright sun. It was a pleasant experience.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdNGtuqG6Zpd1DGw8ZpWhNpypwEjCLvSaFHDZWWxu8pai/img_20260409_120547.jpg)




![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbVv47Cwgs4WGnkjRF1oiTRdXSDTPuh5AzDYYToh775WV/img_20260409_120638.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTq8p3KzW2NjnZL8txBEaijbZ98fbTYnYn5Puy6xxsE5A/img_20260409_120700.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWuRe2oPxpZgHmn4kN69k2cZACmo5cb3sUtvRuBSqaRF9/img_20260409_120708.jpg)




I hope you enjoy my photos of Beijing's beautiful natural beauty of the Ritan Park in the Chaoyang district area on a spring afternoon after the rain. The soothing beauty of the spring afternoon is really great here with the greenish surrounding, with its serene beauty in this city area of the Chaoyang district. It is a great time to enjoy some outdoor activity like walking or running in this area with warmer weather after the freezing winter. If you have any questions, let me know in the comments, and I will do my best to answer them.

Thanks a lot for your time and attention. I will catch up with you at the next one.

Wishing you a good day!

title.title: Tips to handing the police with a motorbike in Thailand
title.body:
So many people come and visit this country and want to scoot around on a motorbike to get to some of the out of city things that are around Chiang Mai. This can be a good idea if you actually are capable of driving a motorbike and honestly, there really isn't that much to it. I've been to and lived in a number of other places in this country and it is just more of the same. In one way, Chiang Mai is easier because the roads are in pretty great shape here and there has been a lot of forward planning to ensure that there actually are enough roads for most of the demand that traffic dictates. Obviously there are exceptions but if you are just traveling here on holiday, you are pretty unlikely to end up in rush hour gridlocked traffic unless you are very unlucky.
https://www.triptipedia.com/tip/img/Vl02JddFg.jpg [src](https://www.triptipedia.com/tip/img/Vl02JddFg.jpg)
One thing though, that you can get away with in most of the rest of the country that you can't really get away with here, is dodging the police if you are operating a motorbike without a license. The thing is, the police proabably aren't truly interested in keeping the roads safer, they are interested in collecting money from people that don't have the correct certification and in most situations, unless you have a legitimate international license the likes of which I don't even know how someone acquires, you aren't going to have what they are looking for because they aren't actually looking for a license, they are looking to fine you right there on the spot. This is something you just kind of have to come to terms with if you are visiting here, or like me, living here. I have some tips to save yourself a bunch of headache though and maybe even get you out of it altogether.

comply, show ID

If you end up in a checkpoint where they ask for your ID or license, provide them with any sort of photo ID. If you have a driving license in your home country, show them that. Then, answer in the affirmative if they ask things like \

. Remember, if you tell a little white lie here this isn't any different than them purposely fleecing visitors. Safety is not their concern hence the fact that Thailand regularly ranks in the top 3 for most road deaths of any country in the world.

Be friendly

Acting like a \

might get you out of situations in USA but it is only going to make things a lot worse for you over here. Thai police are definitely on a power trip, but they will treat you with respect if you do so as well. Throwing a fit will only make the fine larger, so keep it cool.

If you are fined, pay on the spot

Some people are upset and refuse to pay on the spot for some receipt that is probably not official anyway. IF you play this game you are going to lose. They will in fact allow you to go to the station and take care of your \

there but now you have just turned a 5-minute transaction into an all day affair and trust me when I say that they are going to make this take as long as possible. In order to save $20 or so you have just wasted your entire day. Also the system is not going to change just because you think you are going to go over the heads of a corrupt street officer. The **entire organization is in on it** so it's not like if you ask to speak to a manager that internal affairs are going to get involved and thank you for exposing their system.

do NOT record them

This is a fantastic way to super-escalate the situation

Keep your ticket if you get one

This is one of the rather amusing things about routine traffic violations in Thailand. If you are issued a ticket, there is an unofficial rule that you cannot be charged for that same made up crime for 7 days. So if you got a ticket for driving without a license, you can carry on doing so for another week. In a country with actual road rules, driving without a license would mean you are removed from the streets and your vehicle is towed at your own expense. In Thailand the infraction was never about a law to begin with so they don't really care. This 7-day grace period is likely in place so that the population don't riot and burn down police stations and yes, this is something that actually does happen and when it does, the police just get out of the way and let the people burn it.

Keep that ticket forever

Using my own system, I have had the same \

ticket in my motorbike compartment for several years and if I see a checkpoint, I slow down, pull out the ticket and then show it to the guy who is flagging down vehicles.   Chances are, this person seeing a ticket AT ALL is going to convince him to flag you on through because it is such a common thing for there to be multiple checkpoints all over the city and surrounding areas on the same day.\n\nIF they guy happens to look at it closely (and with dozens of this exact situation happening to me they NEVER have) and they say \
you can just claim ignorance.   Just say \

then be polite and comply. This is a bullshit situation anyway, so you may as well play along.

Carry small bills

The fine is often simply made up on the spot and if you open your wallet and you have a bunch of 1000 Baht notes and several 500's, you can be assured your fine will be at least 500. However, if you have a few 100's in there and then just chump change, you can probably get away with just paying a couple hundred. They are not going to ask anyone to do a QR bank transfer because that is a little thing that some people in the legal system refer to as \

<hr> 
<center> https://static.bangkokpost.com/media/content/20210331/c1_2092559.jpg
[src](https://static.bangkokpost.com/media/content/20210331/c1_2092559.jpg)</center> 
You many not like it, but this is simply the way it is in Thailand.   You almost certainly do not qualify to have a Thai driving license unless you have a work permit.  They always fiddle with these rules and often it feels as though it is specifically designed so that a certain percentage of people are always going to be in violation and therefore, can generate pocket money for the officers to kick up to the boss man.   

I tend to look at it from the standpoint of which would you rather have?  A mildly corrupt police force looking for kickbacks, or a situation like we have in the United States where you would never be allowed to drive anyway?

Follow these above steps though and there is a good chance you might just avoid getting fined at all.  If you do get fined, treat it as a vacation experience.   Fighting it is a waste of time and the system is not going to change.
