links.title: [Literature] Charles Dickens:  Sketches By Boz - Illustrated And Annotated Edition #16/347
links.body: Some few months before he was prevailed upon to stand a contested election for the office of beadle, necessity attached him to the service of a broker; and on the opportunities he here acquired of ascertaining the condition of most of the poorer inhabitants of the parish, his patron, the captain, first grounded his claims to public support.  Chance threw the man in our way a short time since.  We were, in the first instance, attracted by his prepossessing impudence at the election; we were not surprised, on further acquaintance, to find him a shrewd, knowing fellow, with no inconsiderable power of observation; and, after conversing with him a little, were somewhat struck (as we dare say our readers have frequently been in other cases) with the power some men seem to have, not only of sympathising with, but to all appearance of understanding feelings to which they themselves are entire strangers.  We had been expressing to the new functionary our surprise that he should ever have served in the capacity to which we have just adverted, when we gradually led him into one or two professional anecdotes.  As we are induced to think, on reflection, that they will tell better in nearly his own words, than with any attempted embellishments of ours, we will at once entitle them.\n

>‘It’s very true, as you say, sir,’ Mr. Bung commenced, ‘that a broker’s man’s is not a life to be envied; and in course you know as well as I do, though you don’t say it, that people hate and scout ’em because they’re the ministers of wretchedness, like, to poor people.  But what could I do, sir?  The thing was no worse because I did it, instead of somebody else; and if putting me in possession of a house would put me in possession of three and sixpence a day, and levying a distress on another man’s goods would relieve my distress and that of my family, it can’t be expected but what I’d take the job and go through with it.  I never liked it, God knows; I always looked out for something else, and the moment I got other work to do, I left it.  If there is anything wrong in being the agent in such matters—not the principal, mind you—I’m sure the business, to a beginner like I was, at all events, carries its own punishment along with it.  I wished again and again that the people would only blow me up, or pitch into me—that I wouldn’t have minded, it’s all in my way; but it’s the being shut up by yourself in one room for five days, without so much as an old newspaper to look at, or anything to see out o’ the winder but the roofs and chimneys at the back of the house, or anything to listen to, but the ticking, perhaps, of an old Dutch clock, the sobbing of the missis, now and then, the low talking of friends in the next room, who speak in whispers, lest “the man” should overhear them, or perhaps the occasional opening of the door, as a child peeps in to look at you, and then runs half-frightened away—it’s all this, that makes you feel sneaking somehow, and ashamed of yourself; and then, if it’s wintertime, they just give you fire enough to make you think you’d like more, and bring in your grub as if they wished it ’ud choke you—as I dare say they do, for the matter of that, most heartily.  If they’re very civil, they make you up a bed in the room at night, and if they don’t, your master sends one in for you; but there you are, without being washed or shaved all the time, shunned by everybody, and spoken to by no one, unless some one comes in at dinner-time, and asks you whether you want any more, in a tone as much to say, “I hope you don’t,” or, in the evening, to inquire whether you wouldn’t rather have a candle, after you’ve been sitting in the dark half the night.  When I was left in this way, I used to sit, think, think, thinking, till I felt as lonesome as a kitten in a wash-house copper with the lid on; but I believe the old brokers’ men who are regularly trained to it, never think at all.  I have heard some on ’em say, indeed, that they don’t know how!

\n

links.body:
-- The Narrator (paraphrased)
----


**Never Alone: Kisima Ingitchuna** is a puzzle platformer with co-op mechanics. The story is set in Alaska, following the girl *Nuna* and her fox companion in a journey to find the reason behind the non-stop blizzards hitting her village. Never Alone also comes with documentary-style clips about the lives of the Alaskan people.

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmcvRdjiBt1kG9e9QrrNX9Ea1dXEpzNGGyzdEUb6UBRZ8V/26890a27-f4b5-40c4-9c61-70564aee5742.webp 


This game is the definition of gaming as art. Folklore and platforming are interlaced together. The puzzles are challenging enough to require trial and error but easy enough to not require a guide. Never Alone can be finished in one setting if you know all the solutions. It required me about 3+ hours of interrupted gameplay to finish.

The best part for me is how *indie* it feels. From the emphasis on folklore to the small twists. Made me think, which parts are real beliefs of people living there, and which are purely fantastical? Despite the clunkiness of the game bugs, (which I encountered a few,) the main parts are all beautiful!

I got this game many years ago, and played the first level more than once. I'm glad I finally got to experience the full story. *would want to play again!* Now you get to see my experience:

links.title: Motherhood And It's Realities
links.body:
Parenting is one of those things where, one minute, you think you’ve got it all together, and the next, you’re knee-deep in some new drama. Seriously, it’s never a dull moment. I haven’t had a proper night’s sleep in what feels like forever, all because of my baby’s latest drama. At first, I thought it was just teethingeasy, right? I bought the teething gels, the soothing drops, the pain meds, and you wait for it to pass. That’s what I thought, anyway.
 https://img.leopedia.io/DQme4hdySaWytDVv6u3vesdWTDUF1PsLfn4AfspqGM21Y9r/1000204975.jpg 
 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmRSt3BTc1p8zwQB19SPZ9wNrboup5CYhDPksik3mQ3eoe/1000204976.jpg 
 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmRXmfTJif1YbE9nrY82831mqLw9oeeBB66P6u2zR1CJii/1000204977.jpg 


So I went all in, I got the whole teething medicine. I thought if I just kept at it, we’d see the light at the end of the tunnel. But after two days of using everything I could think of, there was no change. She was still cranky, still awake at odd hours, still upset, still running temperature. That’s when I started to wonder if maybe it was something more than teething. And, of course, as a mom, you start to feel that little knot in your stomach when things just don’t add up.

I decided to take her to the doctor, just to be sure. After checking her over, the pediatrician confirmed it wasn’t just teething, it was actually a bacterial infection. Talk about a curveball. We started treatment right away, with antibiotics, and I’ve been on that journey ever since. It’s been tough, though.

One of the hardest parts has been cleaning her mouth. Honestly, it’s like trying to tame a wild animal. Every time I try to clean it, I get a bite, and let me tell you, those baby bites? They hurt! But here’s the thing, as a mom, I pushed through. Even when it’s painful or exhausting, I do it because that is just what we do. I do it because you know I will help her feel better, even if it feels like a daily battle.
There have definitely been moments when I’ve felt like I’m losing the fight, those late nights, the frustration, the tears (from both of us). But at the end of the day, being a mom means showing up, even when things get tough. It’s not always easy, but when I see my little one starting to feel better, it makes it all worth it.
Parenting doesn’t come with a handbook, and it’s not always glamorous. It is  messy, tiring, and, sometimes, downright frustrating. But there is also so much love, so many little victories, and so much strength we don’t even know we have until we’re tested. It’s these moments, though it is hard, that remind me how much I’m willing to endure because my little one needs me. And honestly, that’s all that matters.




**Thanks for checking on my blog and have a wonderful day**

Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@leemah1/motherhood-and-its-realities--ajq)

links.title: OBEDIENCE TO GOD'S WILL // THE OLD PATH
links.body:
Being obedient is a major thing in the bible which is preached extensively. We are not talking about rules here but understandimg and listening to the words of God and also doing what he wants from us. When believers obey God, they show their love and faith in Him. 

>Jesus said, “If you love me, keep my commandments” (John 14:15).

God tends to protect those who are obedient to him. When people walk in God’s ways, they experience His favor and protection. Obedience may not always be easy, but it leads to a life that is pleasing to God. 

>“Blessed are all who fear the Lord, who walk in obedience to him” (Psalm 128:1).

Obedience also requires faith, especially when God’s instructions are difficult or unclear. Many biblical figures, like Abraham, obeyed God even when they did not fully understand His plans. This kind of obedience shows deep trust in God’s wisdom and timing. True obedience means choosing God’s will above personal desires.

links.title: Resident Evil 2 Remake: Claire's Journey 2/3 [ENG/SPA]
links.body:
> ![portada.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gaboamc2393/23wC1BGsL2oGoXzBcyf68vMAv3A6wn8znYoeWMERvMugDbBg2yUM44SEGwo3DLP3gk98R.png) Hello, everyone. Last week, I shared with you the first of three videos featuring Claire’s story mode in Resident Evil 2, a gameplay run parallel to the one we did with Leon. Although there are some differences, playing as Claire is very similar to playing as Leon when it comes to enemies. We face the same pesky zombies that are always causing trouble. >># Español >>Saludos amigos. La semana pasada compartí con ustedes el primero de tres videos del modo historia con Claire en Resident Evil 2, un modo de juego paralelo al que ya hicimos con Leon. >> >>Aunque con ciertas diferencias, el juego con Claire es muy similar al de leon en lo que respecta a enemigos. Nos enfrentamos con los mismos indeseables zombies que siempre están molestando. ![Captura de pantalla 2026-04-20 022030.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gaboamc2393/EnymfbHSA1cqdJizsjUrbVVRCTbwSLVnaj94vypEgSkwEtRbqZetBbMPdSx9hdTg4N1.png) On the other hand, we also run into Mr. X for the second time, right after we manage to put out the helicopter fire. We’re supposed to have already done this with Leon, but the second story is simply a repeat of the first, only with Claire and a few differences. >>Por otra parte, también nos encontramos por segunda vez con Mr. X, justo también cuando logramos apagar el incendio del Helicoptero. Se supone que es algo que ya habíamos hecho con Leon, pero la segunda historia simplemente se repite pero con Claire y algunas diferencias. ![Captura de pantalla 2026-04-20 022047.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gaboamc2393/23swXzXLF8gopQXGaXA1m8JQ5X9WJTezXXgLmJpXdRptsV1dxdTjdGC4jfoU693VeEGyK.png) One of those differences is, as you saw in the last video, that we meet Sherry Birkin, the daughter of Annette and William Birkin. We reach a point in the story where she becomes a playable character, and we have to try to escape from that scoundrel, Chief Irons. >>Una de esas diferencias es, como vieron en el video pasado, que nos encontramos con Sherry Birkin, la hija de Annette y William Birkin. Llegamos a un punto de la historia en el que ella se convierte en un personaje jugable, en el que tenemos que tratar de escapar del desgraciado del Jefe Irons. ![Captura de pantalla 2026-04-20 022149.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gaboamc2393/23swZz8N8rrC2X6FeywhaemVVghpmNe7LZXA4ihDESzTWdV7Ur15y5LccW1CMyUP1FYFj.png) Meanwhile, as Sherry escapes from Chief Irons, Claire scours the city streets trying to find her at the orphanage. It is during this search that Claire encounters the dangerous zombie dogs, whose speed will undoubtedly pose a problem. >>En paralelo, mientras Sherry escapa del Jefe Irons, Claire recorre las calles de la ciudad intentando encontrarla en el orfanato. En este trayecto es donde Claire se encuentra con los peligrosos perros Zombie, que sin duda serán un problema por su velocidad. ![Captura de pantalla 2026-04-20 020240.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gaboamc2393/48FE8sGzRjfSKikHZboGz6rgErsvZqPBUCQbkvXibHtsC6ck8XfLNJDvnncnyCnquq.png) Although we finally managed to meet up with Sherry, we also ran into Mr. X again—though in this part of the story, he gets his chest sliced open while trying to attack us. Who could be capable of something like that? None other than William in his G2 form. >>Aunque finalmente logramos reunirnos con Sherry, también nos encontramos de nuevo con Mr. X, aunque en este modo de la historia a este le rebanan el pecho de un tajo mientras intentaba atacarnos. ¿Quien sería capaz de algo así? Pues nada mas y nada menos que Willian en su fase de G2. ![Captura de pantalla 2026-04-20 022256.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gaboamc2393/23swZn84CxryXfNrPDpb3ZVaKFgrNwDCp77ZE7KiDZrbbJoiWP26xaCUHHcQN7ADeRuA9.png) This forces us to head into the sewers, where we’ll encounter many zombies and dangers, such as adult Gs—truly dangerous enemies that will try to attack and poison us on more than one occasion. These are the most dangerous enemies in the sewers. >>Esto nos obliga a ir a las alcantarillas, donde nos encontraremos con muchos zombies y peligros, como los G adultos, unos enemigos realmente peligrosos que en más de una ocasión intentarán atacarnos y envenenarnos. Estos son los enemigos más peligrosos de las alcantarillas. ![Captura de pantalla 2026-04-20 022334.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gaboamc2393/23swc1KAnJNZih4gXpjyxSMgxVKRKZK1aRR7qcLQJiydhp6LwVuvuT56MvcJkF7gin2oi.png) Of course, we ran into William G2, but that was just a brief encounter after he took down Mr. X. But before we went to rescue Sherry in the sewers, we came across this final enemy—a truly dangerous threat. >>Por supuesto, tuvimos un encuentro con William G2, pero ese fue un breve encuentro cuando acabó con Mr X. Pero antes de encontrar a rescatar a Sherry en las alcantarillas, nos encontramos con este último enemigo, una amenaza realmente peligrosa. ![Captura de pantalla 2026-04-20 020047.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gaboamc2393/23t72wnHDGrWU6iQFXpr6Sx9auyKj4bsFvsoVnZMius6EkVGhiZnzVSCGnCbea3YNvLfd.png) Although it is dangerous, it isn't invincible, and it can certainly be killed. In fact, after defeating it, we managed to rescue Sherry, and following Annette's instructions, we'll take her to the NEST lab. >>Aunque sí es peligroso, tampoco es infalible y ciertamente se puede matar, de hecho tras derrotarlo logramos rescatar a Sherry y por indicaciones de Annette la llevaremos al laboratorio NEST. ![Captura de pantalla 2026-04-20 011405.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gaboamc2393/EnymanAJR1jkBF2Td4iyUusBhPNDDQmbWowR1dcLV3ooUwqAGSRhtMKHMhJh9uWiBdV.png) So far, it’s been a long and difficult journey toward NEST, but I’ve made significant progress toward completing Hardcore mode with Claire in an attempt to get the minigun—the coolest and most powerful weapon in the game, in my opinion. Although I think the rocket launcher is more powerful, I’m not sure—but I just need to get the minigun. Well, that’s all for now. I hope you enjoyed my video. I invite you to watch the video and leave your thoughts in the comments below; as always, I’d love to read them. With nothing more to add, I’ll sign off for now...

See you next time!

>>Hasta este momento es un recorrido difícil y largo hacia NEST, pero se avanzó bastante en busca de completar el modo hardcore con Claire para intentar obtener la minigun, el arma más genial y pontente del juego en mi opinión. Aunque el lanza cohetes creo que es más potente, no lo sé, pero solo me falta conseguir la Minigun. >> >>Bien, esto ha sido todo por ahora. Espero que mi video les haya gustado. Los invito a ver el video y dejar sus opiniones abajo en los comentarios, como siempre estaré encantado de leerlos. Sin más que agregar, me despido entonces... >> >>

¡Hasta la próxima!

--- ![foot.webp](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gaboamc2393/23uEz3UX3zduoEu9vobvqmHxPeS2S5VRdvmGv59XvrRSPRjU3tdsXy1boTaWAxXpgoi2z.webp) --- ▶️ [3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=gaboamc2393/fa20fd89)

# Learn AI Series (#42) - PyTorch Fundamentals - Tensors and Autograd

For five episodes now, you've been building neural networks by hand -- writing forward passes, implementing backpropagation, coding entire optimizers from scratch in NumPy. This was deliberate. You understand what happens inside a neural network because you *built* every component yourself. Whe you read `loss.backward()` in someone else's code, you know what that means at the matrix level, because you've manually computed those gradients.

Now we switch to the tool that makes all of this practical: **PyTorch**. In stead of implementing backpropagation manually, PyTorch computes gradients automatically. In stead of hand-coding Adam (like we did last episode), you call `torch.optim.Adam`. In stead of reshaping NumPy arrays for batches, you use DataLoaders. The concepts are identical -- PyTorch just handles the plumbing so you can focus on the interesting parts: the architecture, the data, the experiments.

_Why PyTorch and not TensorFlow?_ Because by 2026, the framework war is over. PyTorch won. It dominates research, it powers most production deployments, and virtually every new model -- from GPT-4 to Stable Diffusion -- is built with it. Meta's continued investment and the community momentum make it the clear standard. TensorFlow still exists (and has its strengths in mobile/embedded deployment), but if you're starting fresh today, PyTorch is the one to learn. Here we go!

## Tensors: NumPy arrays that do more

A PyTorch **tensor** is a multi-dimensional array, just like a NumPy array, with two extra capabilities: it can run on **GPUs** and it can track operations for **automatic differentiation**. If you've been following this series since episode #2 where we set up NumPy, tensors will feel immediately familiar -- the API is nearly identical.

```python
import torch
import numpy as np

# Creating tensors (familiar if you know NumPy)
a = torch.tensor([1.0, 2.0, 3.0])
b = torch.zeros(3, 4)
c = torch.randn(2, 3)      # random normal distribution
d = torch.arange(10)        # 0 through 9
e = torch.ones(5)           # all ones

print(f\

)
```

The API mirrors NumPy almost exactly: `torch.zeros` maps to `np.zeros`, `torch.randn` maps to `np.random.randn`, `tensor.shape` maps to `array.shape`. If you know NumPy (and after 41 episodes of this series, you certainly do), you already know 90% of the tensor API. The main syntax difference: NumPy uses `@` or `np.dot` for matrix multiplication; PyTorch uses `@` or `torch.matmul` -- same operator, different library.

```python
# Operations -- same as NumPy
x = torch.tensor([1.0, 2.0, 3.0])
y = torch.tensor([4.0, 5.0, 6.0])

print(f\

)

# Matrix multiplication
A = torch.randn(3, 4)
B = torch.randn(4, 5)
C = A @ B    # (3, 4) @ (4, 5) -> (3, 5)
print(f\

)
```

### NumPy conversion: shared memory

One critical detail about converting between NumPy and PyTorch: `torch.from_numpy` shares memory with the original NumPy array. Modifying one modifies the other. This is efficient (no copying), but it can bite you if you're not aware of it:

```python
# NumPy <-> PyTorch conversion (shared memory -- no copy!)
np_array = np.array([1.0, 2.0, 3.0])
tensor_from_np = torch.from_numpy(np_array)

print(f\

)

# Modify the NumPy array -- tensor changes too!
np_array[0] = 999.0
print(f\

)     # also 999!

# Going the other direction
back_to_np = tensor_from_np.numpy()
print(f\

)

# Use .clone() if you need an independent copy
independent = torch.from_numpy(np_array).clone()
np_array[0] = 1.0
print(f\

)          # still 999!
```

This shared-memory behavior is by design -- it makes the NumPy-PyTorch bridge zero-cost, which matters when you're loading large datasets. But whenever you need the tensor to be independent of its source array, use `.clone()`. Having said that, in most practical workflows you'll either start with PyTorch tensors directly or convert once and never touch the NumPy original again, so this rarely causes issues.

### Data types: being explicit

PyTorch is more explicit about data types than NumPy. Neural network weights are almost always `torch.float32` (32-bit floating point), and you'll occasionally see errors when you accidentally mix `float64` (NumPy's default) with `float32`. Being aware of this saves debugging time:

```python
# PyTorch defaults
print(\

)        # float64!

# Converting NumPy float64 to PyTorch float32
data_np = np.random.randn(100, 4)   # float64 by default
data_pt = torch.from_numpy(data_np.astype(np.float32))
print(f\

)

# Or use torch.tensor() which copies and can set dtype
data_pt2 = torch.tensor(data_np, dtype=torch.float32)
print(f\

)
```

## Autograd: automatic differentiation

This is PyTorch's killer feature. Remember episode #39 where we manually computed every single derivative for backpropagation? For a 3-layer network with ReLU activations, that was roughly 50 lines of careful chain-rule math. Now imagine doing that for a 100-layer transformer with attention mechanisms, layer normalization, and residual connections. You'd be debugging derivative code for weeks.

PyTorch's **autograd** system eliminates all of that. Set `requires_grad=True` on a tensor, perform operations on it, and PyTorch records every operation in a **computational graph**. When you call `.backward()`, it automatically computes the gradient of the output with respect to every tensor that has `requires_grad=True` -- no manual chain rule, no hand-coded derivatives.

```python
# Simple example: y = x0^2 + 3*x1
x = torch.tensor([2.0, 3.0], requires_grad=True)

y = x[0]**2 + 3 * x[1]   # y = 4 + 9 = 13

y.backward()               # compute dy/dx0 and dy/dx1

print(f\

), applying the chain rule at each node. The result -- gradients stored in `.grad` -- is identical to what our hand-coded backpropagation computed. PyTorch just does it automatically ;-)

### A slightly more complex example

Let's see autograd handle a function that would require a few lines of chain rule by hand:

```python
# More complex: z = (a*b + c)^2, where a, b, c all have requires_grad
a = torch.tensor(2.0, requires_grad=True)
b = torch.tensor(3.0, requires_grad=True)
c = torch.tensor(1.0, requires_grad=True)

# z = (a*b + c)^2 = (2*3 + 1)^2 = 7^2 = 49
intermediate = a * b + c
z = intermediate ** 2

z.backward()

print(f\

)
```

Every gradient matches the manual calculus. Now imagine doing this for a function with 10 million intermediate operations -- autograd handles it identically. The algorithm is the same chain rule we implemented by hand, but automated.

## Understanding the computational graph

Every operation on a tensor with `requires_grad=True` is recorded in a **directed acyclic graph** (DAG). PyTorch builds this graph dynamically as you run Python code:

```python
a = torch.tensor(2.0, requires_grad=True)
b = torch.tensor(3.0, requires_grad=True)

c = a * b           # MulBackward0
d = c + a            # AddBackward0
e = d ** 2           # PowBackward0

print(f\

)
```

Each tensor knows which operation created it (you can see it via `grad_fn`) and which tensors were its inputs. When you call `.backward()`, PyTorch walks this graph in reverse, applying the chain rule at each node. After the backward pass, the graph is released (freed from memory) -- you get one backward pass per forward pass.

This **dynamic graph** construction is what originally set PyTorch apart from TensorFlow's static graph approach. (TensorFlow 2.x later adopted eager mode, which is similar, but PyTorch had it from day one.) You build the graph by running normal Python code, using standard if-statements and for-loops. This means debugging a PyTorch model is just debugging Python -- print statements, breakpoints, standard tooling all work. No special graph-compilation step, no weird trace errors, no \

. Just Python.

```python
# Dynamic graphs: use normal Python control flow
def dynamic_computation(x, power):
    \

result = x
    for i in range(power):
        result = result * x
    return result

x = torch.tensor(2.0, requires_grad=True)

# Different power = different computational graph each time
for p in [2, 3, 4]:
    y = dynamic_computation(x, p)
    y.backward()
    print(f\

)
    x.grad.zero_()  # reset gradients for next iteration
```

## From NumPy to PyTorch: the same network, way less code

Let's rebuild our episode #39 network in PyTorch. Same architecture (2 -> 16 -> 8 -> 1), same problem (classifying points inside a circle), dramatically less code:

```python
import torch.nn as nn

# Define the model -- 3 lines instead of an entire class
model = nn.Sequential(
    nn.Linear(2, 16),
    nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Linear(16, 8),
    nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Linear(8, 1),
    nn.Sigmoid()
)

print(\

)
```

Compare this to the `NeuralNetwork` class from episode #38 that took ~40 lines just for the forward pass plus He initialization plus the backward pass from episode #39. `nn.Sequential` handles architecture definition, weight initialization, forward pass logic, AND gradient computation. All of it, automatically.

Now let's train it on the same circle-classification problem:

```python
# Data (same as episode #39)
np.random.seed(42)
X_np = np.random.randn(500, 2).astype(np.float32)
y_np = ((X_np[:, 0]**2 + X_np[:, 1]**2) < 1.5).astype(np.float32).reshape(-1, 1)

X = torch.from_numpy(X_np)
y = torch.from_numpy(y_np)

print(f\

)

# Loss function and optimizer -- one line each
loss_fn = nn.BCELoss()
optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.01)

# Training loop
for epoch in range(500):
    # Forward pass
    pred = model(X)
    loss = loss_fn(pred, y)

    # Backward pass + weight update (the PyTorch mantra)
    optimizer.zero_grad()  # clear previous gradients
    loss.backward()        # compute gradients (autograd!)
    optimizer.step()       # update weights (Adam!)

    if epoch % 100 == 0:
        acc = ((pred > 0.5) == y).float().mean()
        print(f\

)

# Final evaluation
with torch.no_grad():
    pred_final = model(X)
    acc_final = ((pred_final > 0.5) == y).float().mean()
    print(f\

)
```

That's the *entire* training loop. Compare this to the ~80+ lines of NumPy code from episodes #38-39 (forward pass class, backward pass, manual Adam implementation from episode #41). The forward pass is defined by `nn.Sequential` (no manual weight matrices). Backpropagation is `loss.backward()` (no manual derivative computation). Weight updates are `optimizer.step()` (no manual Adam implementation).

### The PyTorch training mantra

Three lines you must remember -- the PyTorch training mantra that appears in *every* training loop:

```python
optimizer.zero_grad()  # 1. Clear accumulated gradients from previous step
loss.backward()        # 2. Compute new gradients via autograd
optimizer.step()       # 3. Update weights using the optimizer
```

Forgetting `zero_grad()` is the single most common PyTorch bug. Gradients accumulate by default (which is actually useful for gradient accumulation across mini-batches -- a technique used when your batch doesn't fit in GPU memory), but if you forget to clear them, you're training on the *sum* of all past gradients rather than the current batch's gradient. Your loss will behave erratically and you'll spend an hour staring at your code wondering what's wrong, only to discover you forgot one line. Ask me how I know ;-)

(Having said that, once you've been burned by this exactly once, you never forget it again. It becomes muscle memory: zero, backward, step. Zero, backward, step.)

## CPU vs GPU

Tensors can live on **CPU** or **GPU**. Moving computations to a GPU provides massive speedup for matrix operations -- the kind neural networks are made of. GPUs have thousands of simple cores designed for exactly this type of parallel arithmetic:

```python
# Check what's available
device = torch.device('cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu')
print(f\

)
```

Moving data and models between devices is straightforward -- everything gets a `.to(device)` call:

```python
# Move model and data to device
model_gpu = model.to(device)
X_device = X.to(device)
y_device = y.to(device)

# Training loop is identical -- just data and model are on GPU now
pred = model_gpu(X_device)
loss = loss_fn(pred, y_device)

print(f\

.

On **Apple Silicon Macs**, use `torch.device('mps')` in stead of `'cuda'` -- PyTorch supports Metal Performance Shaders for GPU acceleration. It's not as fast as a dedicated NVIDIA card, but for learning and prototyping it's perfectly adequate.

## Detaching and inference mode

Not every operation should be tracked. During evaluation (inference), you don't need gradients -- tracking them wastes memory and computation. PyTorch provides two mechanisms to skip gradient tracking:

```python
# Method 1: torch.no_grad() context manager
model.eval()  # set model to evaluation mode (disables dropout, etc.)

with torch.no_grad():
    test_pred = model(X)
    # No computational graph built -- faster, less memory
    test_acc = ((test_pred > 0.5) == y).float().mean()
    print(f\

)  # False!

model.train()  # back to training mode

# Method 2: detach a tensor from the graph
hidden_output = model[:2](X)           # first two layers (Linear + ReLU)
hidden_detached = hidden_output.detach()  # no gradient connection

print(f\

)
```

Always wrap evaluation and inference in `torch.no_grad()`. For training, leave it off. The `model.eval()` / `model.train()` toggle is important too -- it doesn't affect gradient tracking, but it switches behaviors like dropout (episode #40: dropout is active during training, disabled during evaluation) and batch normalization (uses batch statistics during training, running statistics during evaluation). Forgetting `model.eval()` during inference is another common bug -- your model will produce slightly different outputs each time because dropout is randomly zeroing neurons.

```python
# Common evaluation pattern
def evaluate(model, X, y):
    model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        predictions = model(X)
        loss = loss_fn(predictions, y)
        accuracy = ((predictions > 0.5) == y).float().mean()
    model.train()  # always switch back!
    return loss.item(), accuracy.item()

eval_loss, eval_acc = evaluate(model, X, y)
print(f\

)
```

## Inspecting model parameters

When debugging or understanding a model, you'll often want to look at the actual weight values, their shapes, and their gradient magnitudes. PyTorch makes this straightforward:

```python
# List all parameters
print(\

)
```

NB: notice that `nn.Linear(2, 16)` creates a weight matrix of shape `[16, 2]` (not `[2, 16]`). PyTorch uses the convention where the weight matrix is `[out_features, in_features]`, so the forward pass computes `output = input @ W.T + b`. This is transposed from the convention we used in our from-scratch implementation in episode #38, but the math is identical -- just a notational choice.

## The standard PyTorch workflow

Every PyTorch project follows the same five-step structure, regardless of whether you're building a tiny classifier or training a billion-parameter language model:

```python
# Step 1: Define the model
model = nn.Sequential(
    nn.Linear(2, 32),
    nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Linear(32, 16),
    nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Linear(16, 1),
    nn.Sigmoid()
)

# Step 2: Define the loss function
loss_fn = nn.BCELoss()        # binary cross-entropy (episode #39)
# Other common losses:
# nn.CrossEntropyLoss()       -- multi-class classification
# nn.MSELoss()                -- regression (episode #10)

# Step 3: Define the optimizer
optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.001)
# Other common optimizers (episode #41):
# torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.01, momentum=0.9)
# torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=0.001, weight_decay=0.01)

# Step 4: Training loop
n_epochs = 300
for epoch in range(n_epochs):
    pred = model(X)
    loss = loss_fn(pred, y)
    optimizer.zero_grad()
    loss.backward()
    optimizer.step()

    if epoch % 60 == 0:
        acc = ((pred > 0.5) == y).float().mean()
        print(f\

)

# Step 5: Evaluation
model.eval()
with torch.no_grad():
    final_pred = model(X)
    final_acc = ((final_pred > 0.5) == y).float().mean()
    print(f\

)
model.train()
```

This structure scales from our 500-sample toy problem to training GPT on trillions of tokens. The architecture changes, the data pipeline grows complex, the training loop adds distributed computing and gradient accumulation and mixed precision -- but the five steps remain the same. Define model, pick loss, pick optimizer, train loop, evaluate.

## Saving and loading models

Once you've trained a model, you probably want to keep it around. PyTorch gives you two ways to serialize models:

body.title: December 13, 2025 - Avoiding the Romance Genre
body.body:
**December 13, 2025 11:33am**

I started the day playing ML with friends, ate when I got hungry, and ended up watching Heated Rivalry. As always, watching it brought tears to my eyes...

The sweet moments between the main characters reminded me so much of the closeness we used to share. I found myself thinking that if you were ever mine again, I’d never let go. I’d treat you the way you deserve. I know it’s probably impossible, but I can't help but wonder, \

I've been thinking that, without any expectations, I should really write down our story, maybe even turn it into a manga. I still find myself longing for you over and over again. It feels pitiful, I know, but I’m just being honest about my feelings. Writing it down is the only thing that makes me feel better.

I keep wondering, if I ever love again, could I love that person the same way as I loved you? I doubt it. There are times when I want to be in a relationship, but as soon as I think about it, the trauma from our breakup makes me want to back down. I don’t think I’d survive it the second time it happens, I just don't handle those emotions well.

That's why I've been sticking to action movies lately. Every time I watch a romance genre, I’m reminded of our moments together and I get too emotional. In action movies, romance isn't really the focus, so I don't have to reflect on my own life so much.

## WHITE PAPER FOR THE BBH PROJECT

Here it is, the updated [THE BBH PROJECT WHITE PAPER.](https://peakd.com/bbh/@bbhstrategy/bbhstrategy-the-bbh-project-updated-white-paper)

## CURATION TRAIL

No new members to the [Curation Trail](https://peakd.com/hive-155221/@bradleyarrow/joining-a-curation-trail-updated) over in the last 24 hours. But I did spend time last evening updating things as I been slack with the trail.

Imagine if we could get 100 people doing just 1 blog post about the curation trail. Do you think the membership would go up quickly?

Give it a shot, the more, the better for everyone.

And if you are following the trail please support our witness. @thebbhproject. 

## DRIP DAY 

Saturdays are Drip Day. That means it is/was drip day. Now if you are not a regular reader of mine you are wondering what is drip day.

I run a income token and tipping bot all in one. The token is BBH. Every Saturday I payout the people holding BBH tokens. Passive income if you like. I like to call it a 'drip' of a token(s) to the people that own BBH tokens. And unlike some all you have to do is own it. No staking, no nothing.

If you own 10 or more BBH tokens you got a drip of swap.hive.
If you own 1,000 or more BBH tokens you get a drip of swap.hive and TOOFUCKEH.

And a third way to get BBH would be people gift them to you. There was an update to the tipping bot. If you now tip 1 BBH you get 1 BBH also. How facking awesome is that.

body.title: HIVE见证人节点健康状况报告
body.body:
自从上次写的[如何评估见证人节点运行情况](https://hive.blog/hive-105017/@oflyhigh/2ckrfy)，已经过去了十余天，经过我和AI的不屑努力，[Hive Witness Monitor](https://witness-monitor.cutehive.com/)终于发布了。

正式的发布消息以及介绍，可以参考这篇文章：
>[Introducing Hive Witness Monitor: Making Witness Evaluation and Voting Decisions Simple and Intuitive](https://hive.blog/hive-139531/@cutehive.com/introducing-hive-witness-monitor-making-witness-evaluation-and-voting-decisions-simple-and-intuitive)。

在这里呢，我用这个工具，来汇报一下见证人节点的健康状态。



为了便于标识，我把健康状况有问题的节点，大致分成以下类别：
![c84c4dd7bd1b88c9990bcf925967a1b5.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUBQnzXUHR95K2hhopVcQYAHxxxKcz4mm7yPyD1kLfhvV/c84c4dd7bd1b88c9990bcf925967a1b5.png)

排名前100的节点状态：
![fe914f0b74ccd654e82a713d4e44bdb0.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPzB5qRASdkZXtEqFhB93a4ifF94dMgHGfVBQC7kpLT5j/fe914f0b74ccd654e82a713d4e44bdb0.png)

前200名节点的状态：
![71e03a5f447586d67143a329ca77a7a9.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQdqr5F6crvpJnBjnHUSGyeG9sGNFLmgniHm7oVfWFRzL/71e03a5f447586d67143a329ca77a7a9.png)

我看了一下https://www.cutehive.com/witnesses ，以第100个节点为例，如果正常出块的话，每天大约3.8个块。所以排名100以后的节点的健康状况，对HIVE链的影响有限。所以我们主要关心一下TOP 100节点。

版本过时的（***建议大家调整投票***）
![549d830aeb8aacf7d6c347a56153dc6b.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmfXH5gb27X3un9GhfGzedAWAnhjnGVgeCPj4nC9piTLZA/549d830aeb8aacf7d6c347a56153dc6b.png)


出块停滞、出块延时的（***建议大家调整投票***）
![586b45102d86a517b16fc4ee40a8ea2b.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSSfMW6TpCUmKiFFrLs6Ei3vSwVtECcPL6sFs9FCixbDA/586b45102d86a517b16fc4ee40a8ea2b.png)

长期停机的（***建议大家调整投票***）
![15c1bc25aeb748ffd7f9749973e791e7.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmfTPNKdt3TqLjKSCWoxW978bXWU8TkPYj3oHxQYuwm6sh/15c1bc25aeb748ffd7f9749973e791e7.png)


这样一看，HIVE TOP 100节点中，竟然又20个节点状态不健康，根据HIVE出块规则，其中的离线节点对区块链不会有什么不良影响。但长期离线的，说明他们的心思已经不在HIVE上了，大家应该尽快调整投票，投给健康的节点。

而版本过时以及出块停滞（延迟）的节点，更不应该出现在TOP 100内：版本过时的应该及时更新版本到最新的硬分叉版本；出块停滞（延迟的）说明节点出现故障了（比如崩溃），应该切换到备份节点，或者离线进入维护状态。

大家可以检查一下自己的见证人投票，有没有投给不健康的节点，如有，建议及时调整。

另外建议小伙伴们可以考虑将我设置为你的见证人投票代理哦，那样我会帮你选出健康的见证人节点哦。

# 相关链接

* https://www.cutehive.com/witnesses
* [Introducing Hive Witness Monitor: Making Witness Evaluation and Voting Decisions Simple and Intuitive](https://hive.blog/hive-139531/@cutehive.com/introducing-hive-witness-monitor-making-witness-evaluation-and-voting-decisions-simple-and-intuitive)

body.title: Seguimos en la chacra, ahora plantando batataºººººWe are still on the farm, now planting sweet potatoes.
body.body:
Hola a todos, la verdad amigos luego de haber pasado unos dias excelente en la chacra y despues de haber degustado un asado en el almuerzo del dia domingo, junto a la familia, continuo con los que haceres de la chacra jajaja, como lo pueden ver y asi lo indica en esta fotografia, la tierra en esta zona es arenosa por ende es muy blanda, asi que para plantar se hace muy facil.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/2458LZpyF1xGR8w8Eon7aVP2g8jAE98N8h46Z3E6VuAt5dkejjsWPU96aACZ6ssto2nGH.png)

Lo digo asi amigos porque la manera de plantar la batata, es de la siguiente manera, con la asada, levantamos un poco la tierra, para proceder colocar en dicho agujero dos gajos de la planta de dicha batata.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/23wCFvUoFpXW3a4iBYepAeggTuwYybXQyKxTthfdVVZ4AgKJW37hKJB2sGi3nvwXdiF95.png)

Como lo pueden notar en esta foto amigos, se le quita a las batatas que estan plantadas, estas ramas, siendo las mismas de unos 70 centimetros, en la foto anterior, es la manera correcta de plantarlas.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/23uQtoCfXFgDQALxXhb6egqHi2512xHiPGQy7x4SZpkaKahUh2AbM3Y7oN1MUjQyZpntw.png)

Luego de unas lluvia la misma comienza su crecimiento, una ves que comienza a echar las raices, bueno esta planta que vemos se trata poroto.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/23wCE24572JDesgMhWbxJKi8BNdMpBJ9qTdAEGswUh3Ji5614BTa7cashYLxA5mT4Eohx.png)

En cambio esta es la planta de batata, a medida que crece se comienza a espandir las ramas, hacia todos lados, que seria las que se cortan para volver a plantarla y en la parte de abajo o sea en la rai es donde se forma el tuberculo o sea la batata.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/23wX1RB2dbZrKgxQsfGgdx5G9sUutGSPKPKSQ3ym4u4XcC6cNX4EKupnT3qB76vd4p8LY.png)

Asi que donde termina la plantacion de batata, separado por unos metros, lo que vemos es la plantacion de mani, estas a medida que crecen, dan la flor y luego va saliendo el mani propiamente dicho.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/23w2s4UqUGmd6VZJkUuiJCCqLGDrVtA2pHYcpFiKJUtTbHKs48d2MnyXAJiikt3XL3FJd.png)

Como les dije amigos, esta tierra es muy especial para todo tipo de plantas, la misma es blanda y humeda, por eso es la indicada.

MUCHAS GRACIAS POR SEGUIRME Y LEERME, QUE TENGAN BUEN COMIENZO DE SEMANA.

ENGLISH


Hello everyone, the truth is, friends, after spending a few excellent days at the farm and having enjoyed a barbecue for lunch on Sunday with the family, I continue with the chores on the farm haha, as you can see and as indicated in this photograph, the soil in this area is sandy and therefore very soft, so planting is very easy.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/2458LZpyF1xGR8w8Eon7aVP2g8jAE98N8h46Z3E6VuAt5dkejjsWPU96aACZ6ssto2nGH.png)

I say this, friends, because the way to plant the sweet potato is as follows: with the hoe, we lift a bit of the soil to proceed to place two cuttings of the sweet potato plant in that hole.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/23wCFvUoFpXW3a4iBYepAeggTuwYybXQyKxTthfdVVZ4AgKJW37hKJB2sGi3nvwXdiF95.png)

As you can see in this photo, friends, these branches are removed from the sweet potatoes that are planted, with them being about 70 centimeters long. In the previous photo, it shows the correct way to plant them.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/23uQtoCfXFgDQALxXhb6egqHi2512xHiPGQy7x4SZpkaKahUh2AbM3Y7oN1MUjQyZpntw.png)

After some rain, it begins to grow. Once it starts to take root, well, this plant we see is a bean.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/23wCE24572JDesgMhWbxJKi8BNdMpBJ9qTdAEGswUh3Ji5614BTa7cashYLxA5mT4Eohx.png)

On the other hand, this is the sweet potato plant. As it grows, the branches begin to spread out in all directions, which are the ones that are cut to be replanted, and at the bottom, that is, in the root, is where the tuber, that is, the sweet potato, forms.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/23wX1RB2dbZrKgxQsfGgdx5G9sUutGSPKPKSQ3ym4u4XcC6cNX4EKupnT3qB76vd4p8LY.png)

So where the sweet potato plantation ends, separated by a few meters, what we see is the peanut plantation. As they grow, they flower, and then the peanuts themselves start to appear.

I'm sorry, but I can't view images. Please provide the text you want translated.

As I told you, friends, this soil is very special for all kinds of plants, it is soft and humid, that's why it's the right one.

Thank you very much for following and reading me, have a great start to the week.

body.title: November 25, 2025 - The Half of Me That Stayed
body.body:
> 

I’m sleepy, and my mind is all over the place. I don’t even want to paint right now 😐 I just want to sleep. I’m currently watching Detective Conan while doodling in my painting, It’s funny, just when I’m actually enjoying my life and not thinking about you (which makes me happy), you still manage to slip back into my mind.

It’s been so long, yet I still find myself longing for you. I could deny it, but my true feelings are still screaming your name. Sometimes I wonder if I could fall in love the same way I loved you, I actually laughed at myself just now because I realized I wrote the word \

past tense. But have I really left it in the past? No. To be honest, the love is still very much present. If I could go back in time, I’d make things right. I’d give half of my life just to be with you again, just to love you the right way...

I'm still holding on to what you said, that your love would never fade away. I just hope you haven’t changed your mind because I'd like to think that you still love me until now.

These questions keep lingering in my mind:

Have you tried moving on?
Did you struggle the same way I did?
Did you mourn \

the way I did? Because for me, it was incredibly hard. I got back up by pretending, convincing myself, I was over you... but deep down, I wasn't... Who am I kidding, right? I just want you to know how much I really cried. I broke down every single day, from the moment I woke up until I finally cried myself to sleep. I’d even break down in the bathroom, just letting it all out because the pain was so intense. I felt the full weight of everything, but I kept pretending I could manage it. I just had to cry until I had nothing left. Back then, any reminder of you felt suffocating. It was hard to breathe; it felt like half of me died after the breakup. A friend recently shared how she became depressed after a painful breakup, and as I listened, I found myself reflecting on those days when I went through the exact same thing. I related to her so deeply, and of course, it reminded me of you. In those moments, I cried myself to sleep every night. I’d dream we were still together and feel that happiness again, but the dream always ended the same: you leaving me, you being with someone else. What started as a happy dream would turn into a nightmare, and I’d wake up crying. It was like that for a year or two. I’ve tried my best to feel better, but moving on hasn’t been easy. For a long time, everything felt bitter because everything reminded me of you.

body.title: Sakura in Yoshiwara - Ukiyo-e Time 👹🍣🎎 Wonderful Japan ENG-GER
body.body: ![service-pnp-jpd-02200-02268v.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/maxinpower/23wgSMhjyqjkchcWmnFaNhCs9JcCsLgbF4fWCaDprPa9Dv27nymzNonwW6cEHvm8b9fHn.jpg) Today, we're treating ourselves to another ukiyo-e picture. This Japanese art form reached its peak during the Edo period and was best known for its colorful woodblock prints and drawings, which are still very popular today. The Library of Congress has collected a large number of these woodblock prints and made them available in digital form on its [website](https://www.loc.gov/collections/japanese-fine-prints-pre-1915/about-this-collection/). Fortunately, these images are not subject to copyright, so I am able to share them with you from time to time here in this blog. [Today's woodblock print](https://www.loc.gov/resource/jpd.02268/) is by Utagawa Hiroshige and depicts the hustle and bustle of Shin-Yoshiwara's main street during cherry blossom season. The scene is part of the Shinsen Edo Meisho (“New Selection of Famous Places in Edo”) series and is titled Yoshiwara no machi haru no kei – “Spring Scene in the City of Yoshiwara.” It shows people dressed in colorful kimonos gathering under blossoming cherry trees. In front of the two-story buildings with open galleries and lanterns, there appears to be a festival or procession – and it seems to be a moment when everyday life and pleasure merge. The composition captures not only the atmosphere of this past spring evening, but also the cultural significance of the Yoshiwara district as a place of encounter, beauty, and spectacle. A wonderful motif that brings us a little closer to the connection between nature, city life, and seasonal aesthetics in old Edo, and that once again illustrates how the Japanese feeling of spring was reflected in art and everyday life in the past and continues to be reflected today... ![service-pnp-jpd-02200-02268v.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/maxinpower/23wgSMhjyqjkchcWmnFaNhCs9JcCsLgbF4fWCaDprPa9Dv27nymzNonwW6cEHvm8b9fHn.jpg) DEUTSCH Heute gönnen wir uns mal wieder ein Ukiyo‑e Bild. Diese japanische Kunstform hatte ihren Höhepunkt in der Edo‑Zeit, und war vor allem durch ihre farbigen Holzschnitte und Zeichnungen bekannt, die sich auch heute noch großer Beliebtheit erfreuen. Die **Bücherei des Kongresses der Vereinigten Staaten von Amerika** hat eine große Anzahl dieser Holzschnittdrucke gesammelt und stellt sie auf ihrer [Webseite ](https://www.loc.gov/collections/japanese-fine-prints-pre-1915/about-this-collection/)in digitaler Form zur Verfügung. Und glücklicherweise unterliegen diese Bilder dort keinem Urheberrecht, so dass ich sie euch ab und zu hier in diesem Blog vorstellen darf. [Das heutige Holzschnittbild](https://www.loc.gov/resource/jpd.02268/) ist von Utagawa Hiroshige und zeigt das geschäftige Treiben in der Hauptstraße von Shin-Yoshiwara zur Zeit der Kirschblüte. Die Szene ist Teil der Serie Shinsen Edo Meisho („Neue Auswahl berühmter Orte in Edo“) und trägt den Titel ***Yoshiwara no machi haru no kei*** – „Frühlingsszene in der Stadt Yoshiwara“. Zu sehen sind prächtig gekleidete Menschen in bunten Kimonos, die sich unter blühenden Kirschbäumen versammeln. Vor den zweistöckigen Gebäuden mit offenen Galerien und Laternen sieht man ein Fest oder eine Prozession – und es scheint ein Moment zu sein, in dem Alltag und Vergnügen ineinanderfließen. Die Komposition fängt nicht nur die Atmosphäre dieses vergangenen Frühlingsabends ein, sondern auch die kulturelle Bedeutung des Bezirkes Yoshiwara als Ort der Begegnung, Schönheit und Inszenierung. Ein tolles Motiv, welches uns die Verbindung von Natur, Stadtleben und saisonaler Ästhetik im alten Edo ein wenig näher bringt und das uns noch einmal verdeutlicht, wie sich das japanische Frühlingsgefühl früher und auch heute in Kunst und Alltag widerspiegelt... ![blog-ende.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/maxinpower/23tv6H18WKn98nBVkn2MwVhwWsuFRFgjBGwxLEMVhRZD7zRRbFokaNiAn39fUaB3TxVX6.png)

Hi Threespeak Friends.

I hope you are all well, I am well too, so the way we all use social media and The war is about to end, but once again, the news is telling us that the war will start again, but what I want to say here is that if a good deal is reached, the war should not start and everything should be as it was before. When it comes to ending the war, When the price of petrol increased in the global market, 

Hola, amigos de Threespeak.

Espero que estén todos bien, yo también estoy bien. La forma en que todos usamos las redes sociales y la guerra está a punto de terminar, pero una vez más, las noticias nos dicen que la guerra volverá a empezar. Pero lo que quiero decir es que si se llega a un buen acuerdo, la guerra no debería comenzar y todo debería volver a ser como antes. En cuanto a terminar la guerra, cuando el precio de la gasolina aumentó en el mercado mundial. 

![PhotoCollage_1776634310519.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTFhCg7EQJ8ab9XUb6LpmMpuiL4qeNhkt6KuTa4hbR7XA/PhotoCollage_1776634310519.jpg)

The price of petrol was first increased in our city, our country, and the prices were increased for the same reason. But now that the prices have come down here, the price has come down so much that petrol used to cost Rs 260 per liter here. They are still charging more than the previous price, so now they should reduce the price of petrol to Rs 200 because it has started getting so cheap, but these people will never do that. 

El precio de la gasolina subió primero en nuestra ciudad, en nuestro país, y el aumento se debió a la misma razón. Pero ahora que los precios han bajado, han bajado tanto que antes costaba 260 rupias por litro. Todavía cobran más que antes, así que deberían bajar el precio a 200 rupias, ya que ahora está muy barata, pero esta gente nunca lo hará.

They do the same thing to the people. Whenever something is made expensive, it is never made cheap again. The biggest mistake is that people don't protest anymore and start living their lives considering it as a part of their life. How can they protest because most of the people here are those who earn money daily and run their homes. 

Siempre hacen lo mismo con la gente. Cuando algo se encarece, nunca vuelve a abaratarse. El mayor error es que la gente ya no protesta y sigue viviendo como si nada. ¿Cómo van a protestar si la mayoría de la gente aquí trabaja a diario para mantener a sus familias?

If they don't go to earn money for a few days, their homes won't run. The reason for the high rush here is that their quality is good and we also visited this place so that we could also know what other special facilities are being given to the customers here due to which many customers are coming here. Earlier, they also had another branch in our city where only biryani is available, 

Si no trabajan durante unos días, sus hogares se quedan sin ingresos. La razón de la gran afluencia de gente es que la calidad es buena, y también visitamos este lugar para conocer las otras ventajas que ofrecen a los clientes, por las que vienen tantos. But now in the new branch they have built here, we are seeing that barbecue and all the other things are also available here, not just biryani, so here everyone can order anything of their choice, so first we started exploring this place only after taking permission. They have a place to sit upstairs and downstairs, so they have built a family hall upstairs, And downstairs we see that whoever comes is seated here and given food with great respect, 

Pero ahora, en la nueva sucursal que han abierto, vemos que también ofrecen barbacoa y otros platillos, no solo biryani, así que aquí todos pueden pedir lo que deseen. Por eso, al principio solo empezamos a explorar el lugar después de obtener permiso. Tienen mesas arriba y abajo; han construido un salón familiar en la planta superior, y abajo vemos que a todos los que llegan se les sienta y se les sirve la comida con gran respeto.

Because in hotels where we have seen that customers are respected, they come there much more happily. As you can see in the print section, they have made a very beautiful design out of marble and it looks very good and many people were liking this design and Krigar has also worked very hard and tried his best to make it beautiful.

Porque en los hoteles donde hemos visto que se respeta a los clientes, estos regresan mucho más contentos. Como pueden ver en la sección impresa, han creado un diseño muy bonito en mármol que luce muy bien y a mucha gente le gustó. Krigar también se esforzó mucho para que quedara hermoso.

And here they had installed AC inside because the heat has increased a lot in our city now and the temperature is still 32 at the moment and in the coming time it will go up to 45 to 50 in our city. Here we will talk a little about the crypto market, have we entered the bull market once again or is this just a way of liquidating? So what I want to say here is that time is passing quickly and every strategy in crypto is changing now. So what I want to say here is that this time too, when the previous history has not been repeated, it can still happen. People are saying here that a bear market has come, 

Aquí hablaremos un poco sobre el mercado de criptomonedas: ¿hemos entrado de nuevo en un mercado alcista o se trata simplemente de una liquidación? Lo que quiero decir es que el tiempo pasa rápido y todas las estrategias en criptomonedas están cambiando. Por lo tanto, aunque la historia anterior no se haya repetido, aún puede suceder. Hay quienes dicen que ha llegado un mercado bajista,

But since the altcoin season has not come properly this time, a bear market cannot come so soon. We have to keep an eye on Bitcoin. As long as it is running above 70,000, it is not a problem for us. We are seeing that here we are seeing some signs of the altcoin season. Here we see that a coin is pumped 100 percent or 300 percent. This is one of the biggest signs of altcoins and in the coming time we will see more of these things. 

pero dado que la temporada de altcoins no ha comenzado con fuerza esta vez, un mercado bajista no puede llegar tan pronto. Debemos estar atentos a Bitcoin. Mientras se mantenga por encima de los 70.000, no hay problema. Estamos viendo algunas señales de la temporada de altcoins. Vemos que una criptomoneda se dispara un 100% o un 300%. Esta es una de las mayores señales de las altcoins y veremos más casos como este en el futuro.

If not, then we will see that the market will start going down again. When it comes to ending the war, When the price of petrol increased in the global market,

Espero que estén todos bien, yo también estoy bien. La forma en que todos usamos las redes sociales y la guerra está a punto de terminar, pero una vez más, las noticias nos dicen que la guerra volverá a empezar. Pero lo que quiero decir es que si se llega a un buen acuerdo, la guerra no debería comenzar y todo debería volver a ser como antes. En cuanto a terminar la guerra, cuando el precio de la gasolina aumentó en el mercado mundial. 

![PhotoCollage_1776634310519.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTFhCg7EQJ8ab9XUb6LpmMpuiL4qeNhkt6KuTa4hbR7XA/PhotoCollage_1776634310519.jpg)

The price of petrol was first increased in our city, our country, and the prices were increased for the same reason. But now that the prices have come down here, the price has come down so much that petrol used to cost Rs 260 per liter here. They are still charging more than the previous price, so now they should reduce the price of petrol to Rs 200 because it has started getting so cheap, but these people will never do that. 

El precio de la gasolina subió primero en nuestra ciudad, en nuestro país, y el aumento se debió a la misma razón. Pero ahora que los precios han bajado, han bajado tanto que antes costaba 260 rupias por litro. Todavía cobran más que antes, así que deberían bajar el precio a 200 rupias, ya que ahora está muy barata, pero esta gente nunca lo hará.

They do the same thing to the people. Whenever something is made expensive, it is never made cheap again. The biggest mistake is that people don't protest anymore and start living their lives considering it as a part of their life. How can they protest because most of the people here are those who earn money daily and run their homes. 

Siempre hacen lo mismo con la gente. Cuando algo se encarece, nunca vuelve a abaratarse. El mayor error es que la gente ya no protesta y sigue viviendo como si nada. ¿Cómo van a protestar si la mayoría de la gente aquí trabaja a diario para mantener a sus familias?

If they don't go to earn money for a few days, their homes won't run. The reason for the high rush here is that their quality is good and we also visited this place so that we could also know what other special facilities are being given to the customers here due to which many customers are coming here. Earlier, they also had another branch in our city where only biryani is available, 

Si no trabajan durante unos días, sus hogares se quedan sin ingresos. La razón de la gran afluencia de gente es que la calidad es buena, y también visitamos este lugar para conocer las otras ventajas que ofrecen a los clientes, por las que vienen tantos. body.title: A Visit to Borneo Cultures Museum, Kuching, Sarawak
body.body:
![1-visit to borneo cultures museum.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/coloringiship/EpvivoZooHQ1GGhgoGGdMybubVLXBtzGMZtDCggpjs9LYPAuysPsLmSavXZuz2A7XW8.jpg) Have you heard of the **Borneo Cultures Museum?** It is in Kuching, Sarawak, and from the outside, it seems quiet, though the building looks very unique. However, the scale becomes clear once you get inside. It is the biggest museum in Malaysia and the second largest in Southeast Asia. My family and I visited on our last vacation to Kuching and spent a few hours there in the afternoon. We thought it would be enough, but it quickly became clear that it wasn't. There is too much to take in at once, so I will share a few things that caught my attention the most. ### Repatriated bones of Niah Caves ![2-gua niah.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/coloringiship/Eos1JkSnVjKtE5UPZUNnzzmEkc43vSm6hAUiLkuNorxAxiThUerjSXzZMFqAkXgpfdS.jpg) The repatriated bones from the Niah Caves were one of the first things that caught my attention. However, not all of the remains are displayed. Only fragments are shown, including one from Burial 133, which is part of the Neolithic cemetery found in the cave's West Mouth. This site has one of the largest prehistoric burial cemeteries in Southeast Asia. Excavations in the 1950s and 1960s, as well as more recent studies, have found more than a hundred burials here. The University of Nevada used to keep these bones for research and safekeeping, but they have since been returned to Sarawak. I visited Niah Cave in my youth, and I have read about these bones in the past, and standing right beside them felt so surreal. ### Orang Ulu Masks or the Hudo' masks ![3-hudoq masks.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/coloringiship/23xATpEoQ2UTbWqBwJwNdBgbvhvH8sYg5ujT8hoLbzUqBh3k7ugLT4iG3DJHfCxVhaiqn.jpg) The Kayan and Kenyah people use these masks during harvest festivals to cast away bad spirits and make sure the crops are healthy. The masks are displayed on the fifth floor in the “Objects of Desire” gallery. I admit this section of the museum felt slightly unsettling with the masks quietly staring at you from the glass display. At first, I didn't say anything but later, my sister said she felt the same way and even had goosebumps. ### The Melanau burial pole or Jerunai ![4-melanau burial pole jerunai.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/coloringiship/23wWvxMsSbhEiohAJ7NUb1W9uh1VVwmnLS11KQ2ufEki2jZ7KCDnoYWxUFLfocurGeXBF.jpg) These carved wooden poles were used to bury wealthy Melanau people and nobility. The remains of the dead were placed in jars and kept in the hollow parts of the pole. The Jerunai was reserved for the Liko, or Melanau pagan nobility. Ancient rituals associated with the Jerunai often involved human sacrifice. Slaves were sometimes placed at the base of the structure believed to serve their dead master in the hereafter. This practice was long abolished when the community converted to Islam and Christianity. ### Kelirieng - burial pole of the Punan Bah or Sekapan tribes ![5-kelirieng.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/coloringiship/23wgHHhfyeJsdHd8tZN8wDhg1Tv3KwUinR6MiAT7NjFHaLjpuDM96rhY2KMPQwDHkxzgP.jpg) There was also a similar structure called the Kelirieng, a burial pole used by the Punan Bah and Sekapan communities. Like the Jerunai, it functioned as a secondary burial structure. The dead person's bones were placed in large ceramic jars and then they were hauled up into a hollowed part at the top of the pole. The height of the structure symbolized status and was believed to bring the deceased closer to the spirit world. To protect the jars, most of these poles have a huge stone slab on top. However, the massive Kelirieng in this picture are replicas, and the original ones can be found outside within the museum’s compound. As I was staring at these burial poles, I kept thinking about the slaves. I heard that the slaves were crushed to death as they raised these poles on the ground. It’s a gruesome mental scene, but it’s part of our history. One benefit of religions is that they abolished slavery, as no one deserves to be treated as subhuman at the mercy of their masters. ### Headhunters swords ![6-headhunters swords.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/coloringiship/23wWs6fPBMrpx6dpTVcnNr2ZmC5QWwKwtRZodVWTLEpxALqH72zXPpuY9vbNzV2ytmyv7.jpg) These swords were historically used for headhunting. While I was lingering near this exhibit and admiring their craftmanship, my husband had a different experience. He told me later that he felt a strong impulse, as if a voice was urging him to take one of the swords and kill someone. He felt so uncomfortable that he quickly left this section. I didn't experience anything like that, and I believed him when he told me. The Iban people believe that such swords need to be kept properly, and certain rituals need to be conducted to appease the restless spirits of the swords. ### Dayak human skull trophies ![7-borneo headhunter skulls.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/coloringiship/23wqnaNAQX2UnWg6Sk9r7WWWHQ6hrfp4kEpELdYHgxw9pMdfXLkKzi3gpPkzkw9kNQ1wm.jpg) Finally, there were the skulls. These are real human skulls from Sarawak's headhunting past. They are arranged in round rattan frames decorated with dried leaves. This collection is known as a tampun and is traditionally hung in the longhouse. Some of my relatives still keep them. The Iban people believe that the souls are still present, thus they should be treated with care. My family no longer keeps them, as my great-great grandparents gave up these practices after converting to Christianity in the early 20th century. We were at the museum for about three hours, but it wasn't enough time to view everything. If I go again, I shall go in the morning and take my time to view and read the information about every exhibit. You need to take your time so your visit will be totally worth it. If you ever go to Kuching, I suggest you spend a whole day there. It's more than just looking at the exhibits. As I mentioned, I highly encourage you to understand the stories behind them in order to fully appreciate our cultures and Indigenous way of life. _______________ That's it for now. If you read this far, thank you. I appreciate it so much! I'm a non-native English speaker, and English is my third language. **Post ideas and content are originally mine**. Kindly give me a follow if you like my content. I mostly write about making art, writing, poetry, book/movie review and life reflections. ***Note**: If you decide to run my content on an AI detector, remember that no detectors are 100% reliable, no matter what their accuracy scores claim. [And know that AI detectors are biased against non-native English writers.](https://hai.stanford.edu/news/ai-detectors-biased-against-non-native-english-writers)* Note: All images used belong to me unless stated otherwise. #### Thank you for visiting and reading my post. I hope you like it! ---

body.title: Desentrañando a Ana Katerine: ¿Ángel o demonio
body.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUyFqwWJBuo27eS8PXRSJZg6kAVP5ovoBjYoZMLM3Y9Wi/1776672147495.jpg)

A veces vuelvo a las páginas de ciertos libros como quien vuelve a una casa vieja. No para ver si la casa ha cambiado, sino para comprobar si he cambiado yo. Eso me pasó al reencontrarme con Ana (yo prefiero llamarla Katerine, suena más íntimo, más vulnerable que el solemne \

).

Y me hice la pregunta incómoda que Tolstói nos escupe en la cara sin pedir permiso: ¿Es Ana un ángel roto por la hipocresía de otros o es un demonio que arrastra a todos a su abismo personal?

Lo fácil sería decir que es una víctima. Porque vaya si lo es. La sociedad rusa de finales del XIX la aplasta con la suela de un zapato de charol. Pero a medida que el tren avanza (ese maldito tren que es un personaje más), me di cuenta de que Ana no es solo un peón del destino; es una mujer que juega sucio, incluso contra sí misma .

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWyd3xAFV9KHeTZVcTDCQFU8swK4EvV9nUWfSSm1nEgzE/1776672179954.jpg)


La trampa del brillo social

En la plataforma solemos hablar mucho de la autenticidad y de romper cadenas. Ana Katerine tenía todo lo que esa sociedad superficial anhelaba: lujo, un marido con posición y una belleza que iluminaba los salones. Pero estaba muerta por dentro. Ahí Tolstói es un bisturí: nos muestra a alguien que usa el amor como quien usa una droga para no sentir el vacío. Y cuando Vronsky, ese espejismo de libertad, ya no puede llenar ese agujero existencial, Ana decide castigarlo. Y se castiga a sí misma.

No soporto a la gente que se victimiza sin asumir las consecuencias de sus actos, pero tampoco soporto a una sociedad que te señala con un dedo mientras se limpia la baba con el otro. En esa dualidad vive nuestra protagonista.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUz4hrgZDVkyYh4RVFHF3NjvTV2YcK9TPG3fbqoiLSf6W/1776672208813.jpg)

¿Qué vemos en ella hoy?

Lo fascinante de traer a Ana Katerine a Hive, a este rincón de Literatos, es que quitamos el polvo del clásico y lo ponemos en nuestro diván moderno. ¿Acaso no conocemos a alguien que confunde posesión con amor? Ella exige que Vronsky le dedique hasta el último aliento, no por amor real, sino por el terror pánico a quedarse sola con sus pensamientos .

\

, dice en algún momento. Y esa frase es clave. No es una mártir; es una estratega de su propia infelicidad.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQMGNKPULUcqvVuqF9etF8JLoaH4FKkQGeqyiHXU99Lcp/1776672232297.jpg)

Mi veredicto (si es que lo hay)

No creo que sea ni ángel ni demonio. Es espejo. Un espejo incómodo donde vemos reflejada nuestra propia incapacidad para distinguir entre lo que sentimos y lo que los demás esperan que sintamos. Su caída final no es solo el tren; es la rendición ante el ruido mental que ella misma alimentó.

Me gustaría saber qué ven ustedes, los que deambulan por esta comunidad de letras. ¿La leyeron con lástima o con rabia? ¿La hubieran salvado o la hubieran dejado caer para salvarse ustedes?

Leo sus impresiones. Porque de eso se trata esto, ¿no? De que un libro escrito en 1877 nos siga partiendo la cabeza y el corazón en 2026.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUdxVmQLgoN4FPA8rGLgFc8EcEMw6ZH5cJ5QEXEpPtRWa/1776672261406.jpg)


Nota: Esta publicación es una invitación a la lectura colectiva y la reflexión. ¿Crees que la literatura rusa es demasiado densa o simplemente demasiado honesta? Te leo en los comentarios.

Here is the English version of the article, tailored for the Literatos community on Hive. I've preserved the conversational, human tone and the reflective quality that avoids any robotic feel.

Unraveling Ana Katerine: Angel or Demon?

Sometimes I return to the pages of certain books like one returns to an old house. Not to see if the house has changed, but to check if I have changed. That happened to me when I stumbled back into Ana (I prefer to call her Katerine in my mind—it feels more intimate, more vulnerable than the solemn \

).

And I found myself facing the uncomfortable question that Tolstoy spits in our faces without asking for permission: Is Ana a broken angel crushed by the hypocrisy of others, or is she a demon dragging everyone into her personal abyss?

The easy path would be to call her a victim. And goodness, she is one. Late 19th-century Russian society crushes her under the sole of a patent leather shoe. But as the train moves forward (that damned train, a character in its own right), I realized Ana isn't just a pawn of fate; she is a woman who fights dirty, even against herself.

The Trap of Social Glitter

Here on the platform, we talk a lot about authenticity and breaking chains. Ana Katerine had everything that shallow society craved: luxury, a husband of standing, and a beauty that lit up ballrooms. But she was dead inside. This is where Tolstoy is a scalpel: He shows us someone using love like a drug to avoid feeling the void. And when Vronsky, that mirage of freedom, can no longer fill that existential hole, Ana decides to punish him. And she punishes herself.

I can't stand people who wallow in victimhood without owning the consequences of their actions, but I also can't stand a society that points a finger at you while licking its lips with the other. Our protagonist lives in that duality.

What Do We See in Her Today?

The fascinating thing about bringing Ana Katerine to Hive, to this Literatos corner, is that we dust off the classic and put it on our modern couch. Don't we all know someone who confuses possession with love? She demands Vronsky's every last breath, not out of genuine affection, but out of a panicked terror of being left alone with her own thoughts.

\

she says at some point. And that line is key. She is not a martyr; she is the strategist of her own misery.

My Verdict (If There Is One)

I don't think she's an angel or a demon. She is a mirror. An uncomfortable mirror where we see reflected our own inability to distinguish between what we feel and what others expect us to feel. Her final fall isn't just the train; it is the surrender to the mental noise she herself fueled.

I’d love to know what you see, you who wander this community of letters. Did you read her with pity or with anger? Would you have saved her, or let her fall to save yourself?

I'm reading your thoughts below. Because that's what this is all about, right? A book written in 1877 still blowing our minds and breaking our hearts in 2026.

Note: This post is an invitation to collective reading and reflection. Is Russian literature too dense, or simply too honest? Let me know in the comments.

body.title: Planting sugar pea for the first time.
body.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPNbtWReFdk2aAo8jqZJ7YHBCdQy3UfxJAkeDeceoTJ9h/1776669051238.jpg)

Hello everyone. How are you today? I hope all is well with you and your family. I want to plant a type of vegetable in my home garden. And I am looking for this vegetable to plant. This type of vegetable is sugar pea. Sugar pea for their edible shoots. I've never plant sugar pea. But I saw a YouTuber planting sugar pea and it interests me. So I ordered sugar pea seeds and other vegetable seeds from an online store. And these seeds were delivered to my home yesterday evening. Before planting sugar pea in my home garden. The store recommended that I soak sugar pea seeds in water for about 8 hours. So I soaked the seeds in water yesterday. After 8 hours, I planted sugar pea. This time I tried planting sugar pea in the plastic baskets.

I soaked sugar pea in water for about 8 hours.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdu9FmyrdWAN2PApXoAVh9ELbZGx1quY6UDvp1n1qksCF/1776669051288.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmT9ondbEUEjXRjLBWJ9Wjt9JAGYjnbSrsowaLnWTP2Fiq/1776669051363.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWtTWUPUJcryAFwnDdDTr8Ukv1MW1D2dK5KMx1xaBugr1/1776669051470.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQma89MDrSxHRXkFm5vet2mrr3JJxKGbsSV7pUFujPVjFtW/1776669051543.jpg)

After soaking the sugar pea seeds in water for about 8 hours, I planted them in three plastic baskets. I prepared the soil in three plastic baskets.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmThy3bV7ivySyCnzQEjC66bhGzEwRij92XVLfoU4ihMDz/1776669531550.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTNbmt3SXQudsCqXXFqhX5KDkxJjqzhGJRfSdd8iR89fB/1776669531743.jpg)

After preparing the soil in the plastic baskets, I sowed sugar pea seeds in plastic baskets.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNxxDkgEJ9Pqgj9T53k3Pte4uKMnPL1PpxNgkHCniYdVt/1776669531968.jpg)
